issues.locator: Proposition 7.4.10, ‘Moreover’ part and proof, p. 117, in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 112
issues.printed: For a second sufficiently regular character κ^1, the source identifies L(φ_κ) with L(φ_{κ^1}) using Theorem 7.1.1's isomorphisms 𝕋 ⥲ 𝕋_{K^p,κ,O_π} ⥲ 𝕋_{K^p,κ^1,O_π}, localized at π. The proof attributes this to Lemma 7.4.9 and an expansion of the definitions.
issues.correction: An argument is needed that the elements built at weights κ and κ^1 agree: one must show that the Gorenstein isomorphisms G_r and the identifications Ŝ_{r,V} ≅ 𝕋_{r,κ} ⊗ Î_π at different weights are specializations of the single Λ-adic isomorphisms of Hypothesis 7.3.2 and §7.3.4, and that φ_{r,κ}, φ_{r,κ^1} are specializations of the same Λ-linear measure.
issues.reason: Lemma 7.4.9 concerns change of level at fixed weight and gives the existence of L(φ_κ) as an inverse limit; it says nothing about comparing weights. The comparison is the heart of the construction of a two-variable (Hida-family) p-adic L-function. Defence: it is a standard consequence of Λ-adic duality once all identifications are chosen Λ-adically (as §7.3.4 does), so the gap is expository. Independent check: Quotation checked on p. 117 (v5): Proposition 7.4.10's 'Moreover, if κ^1 is a second sufficiently regular character, then L(φ_κ) and L(φ_{κ^1}) are identified with respect to the identifications 𝕋 ⥲ 𝕋_{K^p,κ,O_π} ⥲ 𝕋_{K^p,κ^1,O_π} of Theorem 7.1.1', with 'PROOF. This is a consequence of Lemma 7.4.9 and follows by unwinding the definitions.' Lemma 7.4.9 (p. 117) only says that ι_r^* is the trace map K_{r+1} → K_r at a FIXED weight κ, i.e. it gives the compatibility in r that makes L(φ_κ) ∈ lim_r 𝕋_{r,κ} ⊗ I_{π^♭} ⊗ I_π well defined. It says nothing about changing weight. L(φ_κ) is obtained from φ_{r,κ} ∈ Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r,V}, S^ord_{r,−V}) through the chosen isomorphisms 𝕋_{r,κ} ⊗ Î_π ≅ Ŝ^ord_{r,V}, 𝕋̂_{r,κ} ⊗ I_{π^♭} ≅ S^ord_{r,−V} (§7.3.4, Proposition 7.3.5) and G_r. These choices are unique only up to units of 𝕋_{r,κ} and automorphisms of Î_π, and p. 115 admits 'These isomorphisms depended on certain choices'. So L(φ_κ) = L(φ_{κ^1}) needs the weight-κ and weight-κ^1 isomorphisms to be specialisations of one Λ-adic isomorphism. The paper never supplies this. §7.3.4 fixes the Λ-adic isomorphism only for lim_r S^ord_κ(K_r,O) at one weight κ. Proposition 7.3.5 asserts isomorphisms for every (κ^1,r^1) with commutative diagrams for change of level only, with no compatibility across weights. Theorem 7.1.1 identifies Hecke algebras, not the modules of forms. The missing input is Hida's Λ-adic control for the modules ((33)–(34)) together with choosing all finite-level isomorphisms and G_r as specialisations of the Λ-adic ones (for G_r this is how Hypothesis 7.3.2 reads). With the measure φ fixed (Lemma 7.4.2, same φ for every ρ), the claim then does follow by unwinding. So the gap is expository and the result is standard, but it is needed for Lemma 7.4.14 and for Propositions 7.4.13 and 7.4.15 (specialisation at λ ∈ X(κ,r,R) for any sufficiently regular κ). Versions: v4 p. 112 identical; v2/v3 Proposition 7.2.13 same, with proof citing Lemma 7.2.12. Reach: the proof (of Proposition 7.4.10’s weight independence, hence of Propositions 7.4.13, 7.4.15).

issues.correction: L_φ(h) = ⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r} = Vol(I^0_{r,V})^{-1} ∫_{G(Q)Z_G(R)\G(A)} [h(g),φ(g)]·||ν(g)||^{−a(κ)} dg, by (136)–(137). The product of the two volumes is the normalization for the doubled group G_3 used in Proposition 9.1.7.

By (125), I^0_{r,−V} = δ_p^{-1}Ī^0_{r,V}δ_p has the same volume, so the printed formula is off by the factor Vol(I^0_r)^{-1}, a non-unit rational number depending on r. The lemma calls itself ‘just a restatement of (133)’, which has no volume at all. Defence: Proposition 9.1.7 applies the formula ‘doubled’, i.e. on G_3 ⊂ G_1 × G_2, where a product of two volumes is natural; the printed G_1 version seems to anticipate that. Whether Proposition 9.1.7/Corollary 9.1.8 carry the correct factor is not settled here. Independent check: Quotation checked on the page image (p. 121). Lemma 7.5.2 (p. 120) defines L_φ(h) := ⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r}. By (136)–(137) (p. 94), ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r} = Vol(I^0_{r,V})^{-1}⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ = Vol(I^0_r)^{-1}∫_{G(Q)Z_G(R)\G(A)}[φ(g),φ'(g)]·||ν(g)||^{−a(κ)}dg. By (125), I^0_{r,−V} = δ_p^{-1}Ī^0_{r,V}δ_p has the same volume as I^0_{r,V}, so the printed value is Vol(I^0_r)^{-1} times the correct one, an r-dependent non-unit. issues.locator: §8.1, Corollary 8.1.2, p. 122, in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 117
issues.printed: The source presents Corollary 8.1.2 as a p-adic counterpart of Corollary 4.4.9's final part. Assuming the preceding proposition's hypotheses, it claims differential operators … for every κ† ≤ κ satisfying θ(κ, χ) = Σ_{κ†≤κ} res_3 ∘ θ(κ, κ†) ∘ θ^hol(κ†, χ).
issues.correction: Add a proof: θ(κ,χ), θ^hol(κ†,χ) and θ(κ,κ†) are the p-adic operators attached to the polynomials p(r̃,s̃), P^hol(κ†,χ) and δ(κ,κ†) ∈ U(p_3^+) ⊂ Sym(p_4^+) underlying Corollary 4.4.9 and Proposition 8.1.1(d); the polynomial identity underlying Corollary 4.4.9 transfers because the assignment polynomial ↦ p-adic operator is multiplicative and commutes with res_3 for elements of U(p_3^+) (with a reference, e.g. to [EFMV18]).
issues.reason: No argument is given, and it is an input to Proposition 8.1.3 (hence to Corollary 8.2.4 and the Main Theorem). Defence: the p-adic operators are attached to the same polynomials as the C^∞ ones (Proposition 8.1.1(a), (d)), so polynomial identities transfer; this is routine in Eischen's framework. Independent check: p. 122: Corollary 8.1.2 is introduced only by 'The following corollary is the p-adic version of the last part of Corollary 4.4.9' and has no proof; it is used as the first step of the proof of Proposition 8.1.3 (p. 123), hence feeds Corollary 8.2.4. Corollary 4.4.9 (p. 73) is an identity D(κ,χ) = Σ δ(κ,κ†)∘D^hol(κ†,χ) of C^∞ operators with δ(κ,κ†) ∈ U(p_3^+), derived from the (g,K)-module decomposition and holomorphic projection. The mechanism for transfer is indicated in the proof of Proposition 8.1.1(d) ('one lets θ^hol(κ,χ) be the differential operator on p-adic modular forms attached to the same polynomial'), but the transfer of the identity additionally needs that the assignment polynomial ↦ p-adic differential operator is compatible with composition and with restriction res_3 to G_3 (δ(κ,κ†) acts on G_3, while the formula applies θ(κ,κ†) on G_4 before res_3), which is neither stated nor referenced. The statement is surely correct and the missing argument routine in Eischen's framework, so this is a minor expository gap. (The symbol θ(κ,λ) and the domain V_χ(G_4,…) in the statement are misprints for θ(κ,κ†) acting on V(G_4,K^p,O); that is recorded separately, sourceIssues E126.) v4 p. 117 is identical.

issues.locator: §8.1, proof of Proposition 8.1.3, p. 123, last sentence ('Part (1) above now follows from …') and the proof of Lemma 8.1.4, in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 117
issues.printed: The source equates κ† < κ with positivity of the p-adic valuation of ∏_{w,j} κ′^{,−1}·κ^{†,′}(t_{w,j}). It then derives Part (1) from commutation between the ordinary projector and the differential operators.
issues.correction: State and justify (or cite) the commutation U_{w,j,κ}∘θ(κ,κ†) = θ(κ,κ†)∘(|κ'^{−1}κ†'(t_{w,j})|_p U_{w,j,κ†}) on p-adic forms (together with res_3∘θ(κ,κ†) = θ_3(κ,κ†)∘res_3); in Lemma 8.1.4 read 'κ† < κ implies that ∏_{w,j}κ'^{−1}κ†'(t_{w,j}) has negative p-adic valuation (so its |·|_p is a positive power of p)', with κ' = κ_norm as in (30), not 2.6.11.
issues.reason: On p-adic modular forms the (unnormalised) U-operators do not commute with the differential operators on the nose (for elliptic forms U_pθ = pθU_p); the needed statement is that they commute after the weight-dependent normalisations |κ′(t)|_p^{−1}, i.e. that the power of p produced by θ(κ, κ†) is exactly the ratio of normalising factors used in Lemma 8.1.4 — this is asserted, not checked. The 'equivalence' in Lemma 8.1.4 is also more than true in general: the valuation is one linear functional (pairing with the strictly dominant cocharacter ∏_j t_{w,j}), positive on κ − κ† when κ† < κ, but not conversely. Defence: the conclusion (the κ† < κ terms are killed by e_κ) is the standard 'ordinary projection kills θ-images' phenomenon and is correct. Independent check: p. 123 (zoomed). Part (1) of the proof of Proposition 8.1.3 is dispatched by 'the ordinary projector commutes with the differential operators', together with Lemma 8.1.4. What is needed is e_κ∘θ(κ,κ†) = θ(κ,κ†)∘lim U_{p,κ}^{N!}, where on weight-κ† forms U_{p,κ} = ∏|κ'^{−1}κ†'(t_{w,j})|_p U_{w,j,κ†}, i.e. that the p-adic U-operators and θ(κ,κ†) commute up to exactly the ratio of weight normalisations (for elliptic forms U_pθ = pθU_p, so 'commutes' is only true after renormalisation). This is asserted without proof or reference; it also requires moving res_3 past θ(κ,κ†). The first reading's second point (the 'equivalence' is more than true) is minor: only the implication is used, and within the index set κ† ≤ κ of Corollary 8.1.2 the converse is harmless. I found one more slip in the same proof, which supports the verdict: if the p-adic valuation of y = ∏κ'^{−1}κ†'(t_{w,j}) is e > 0 as printed, the scalar |y|_p = p^{−e} has p-adic norm p^{e} > 1, so 'Thus U_{p,κ} has p-adic norm strictly less than 1' does not follow; the argument needs v_p(y) < 0 (equivalently, the rational number |y|_p has positive valuation). A sample computation with p⁺-weights e_{σ,i} + e_{σc,j} in the κ_norm coordinates of p. 129 does give v_p(y) = j − (n − i + 1) < 0. Also 'κ' defined as in 2.6.11' is a wrong cross-reference: 2.6.11 defines the twist κ' = (κ_0 + a,(κ_{σ,i})), whereas the normalisation is by κ_norm as in (30) (cf. p. 98 'κ' related to κ as in (30)'). The conclusion (e_κ kills the κ† < κ terms) is the standard phenomenon and is correct. v4 p. 117 is identical.

issues.locator: §8.2, Theorem 8.2.2, p. 125 (and the identification of sections on p. 124), in arXiv v5; present in v4 as Theorem 5.4.1 at pp. 84–85 (without the Y^class_H qualifier)
issues.printed: Theorem 8.2.2, called the Eisenstein Measure theorem, is derived using the p-adic q-expansion principle and coefficients described in [Eis14, Section 3], with [EFMV18, Theorem 7.2.3] as an analogue. It asserts existence of a measure Eis_{a,b} satisfying ∫ χ̃ψ·ρ^υ Eis_{a,b} = θ^{(κ,a,b)}(G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ}) for (χ, c = ψ·ρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H.
issues.correction: Give the proof, or a precise reference for general signature: define Eis_{a,b} by the q-expansion coefficients of G_{k,ν,F} for the §4.3 Schwartz data at p (checking the Kummer congruences, Lemma 5.1.3) together with the action of θ^{(κ,a,b)} on q-expansions [EFMV18], and verify that the §4 sections f(χ,c), including the 'minor changes' at p of §4.3.1, are the sections underlying G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ}.
issues.reason: The theorem is only 'obtained', with a pointer to a similar theorem; in the definite case it is [Eis15, Theorem 20] (Remark 8.2.3), but for general signature neither cited source states it, and the identification of the Eisenstein series of the §4 sections with (a normalisation of) G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} is asserted on p. 124 without verification. Defence: the construction is standard (Katz–Hida–Eischen) once q-expansions are known, and [EFMV18, Thm 7.2.3] is the analogous statement. Independent check: Quotation checked on the page image (p. 125). The theorem is only 'obtained', with a pointer to a result that is 'similar'. The first reading's 'neither cited source states it for general signature' is too strong. The arXiv version of [EFMV18] (1511.06771, Theorem 7.2.4 there) constructs a signature-dependent measure μ_{G'} on X_p × T(Z_p) for the sections F_{χ_u,ψ}(x,y) = χ_u(x)φ_ζ(N(x)ᵗy). What is genuinely unverified is the step connecting that measure to the data of this paper. §4.3.1 (p. 49) says the Siegel–Weil section at p agrees with that of [Eis15, Eis14] only 'with a few minor changes'. Yet p. 124 and Remark 8.2.1 assert without argument that the Eisenstein series of the §4 sections f(χ,c) is (a normalization of) G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ}. Also, θ^{(κ,a,b)} is applied on G_4 before restriction, not res∘Θ^κ as in [EFMV18]. So the Kummer-congruence/q-expansion argument for these modified sections, and the matching of sections, are left to the reader. p. 85 claims the existence 'is proved in [Eis15, Eis12]; see Theorem 8.2.2'. That holds in the definite case (Remark 8.2.3) but not literally in general. Versions: v4 Theorem 5.4.1 (pp. 84–85) is the same apart from the Y^class_H qualifier.
searched: arXiv:1602.01776 v1 (February 2016), v2, v3 and v4 at the same place: v4 Theorem 5.4.1 (p. 84–85) identical except that v5 adds 'whenever (χ, c = ψ·ρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H'.

issues.locator: §8.2, proof of Corollary 8.2.4, p. 126, in arXiv v5 (the proof is new in v5; v4 Corollary 5.4.3, p. 85, has no proof)
issues.printed: The proof compares Theorem 8.2.2 against Definition 5.3.2. Using the translation in Remark 8.2.1, it reduces this task to comparing how e_κ ∘ res_3θ^{(κ,a,b)} and e_κ ∘ ∘D^hol(κ, χ) act, and invokes Proposition 8.1.3 to finish.
issues.correction: Also verify the remaining requirements of Definition 5.3.2: the local sections of G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} at v ∉ S, v ∈ S, v | p and ∞ are those prescribed; the normalising factor D(n, K, 𝔟, p, k) of [Eis15, Prop. 13] matches D_S(χ) (or D(χ)) of (108) as required in the last bullet; and the shift (1, χ) condition (109).
issues.reason: Only the differential-operator part of the last bullet of Definition 5.3.2 is addressed; the normalisations and local-section conditions are left to 'the translation mentioned in Remark 8.2.1'. Defence: these are bookkeeping facts about Eischen's construction. Independent check: Quotation checked on the page image (p. 126). The local-section bullets of Definition 5.3.2 hold by the choice made on p. 124 ('We choose f(χ,c) to be a factorizable Siegel section meeting the conditions of Definition 5.3.2'). They transfer to G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} only through the identification discussed in sourceIssues E130 (overlap). What the proof leaves out is the rest of the last bullet. That bullet requires e_κ∫(χ,c)dEis = D^S(χ)·e_κ∘res_3E_{f(χ,c)}, whereas Remark 8.2.1 says the Eisenstein series is normalized by D(n,K,𝔟,p,k) of [Eis15, Prop. 13]. The equality of these factors (or the passage between normalized and unnormalized measures) is not checked. Nor is the claimed shift (1,χ) of (109). The proof reduces everything to Proposition 8.1.3 'bearing in mind the translation mentioned in Remark 8.2.1'. The conclusion is standard bookkeeping, but it is not supplied. Versions: new in v5 (v4 Corollary 5.4.3 has no proof).

issues.locator: §8.3.1, proof of Lemma 8.3.2, p. 129 (display 'β_x/β^x(t) = …', the definition of θ, the formula for θ(diag), the chain of inequalities, and the definition of m_i), in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 120
issues.correction: β_x(t)/β^x(t) = |κ_norm(xtx^{−1}t^{−1})|_p δ_w(xtx^{−1}t^{−1})^{1/2}; the invariant character is θ = |κ_norm|_p δ_w^{1/2} (equivalently its inverse |κ_norm|_p^{−1}δ_w^{−1/2}, which is what the θ(diag) display computes); m_i = −Σ_{σ,𝔭_σ=𝔭_w}(κ_{σc,i−a_w} − a_w) for i > a_w; θ(diag(t)) = ∏_i |t_i|_p^{m_i + e_i/2} with e_i = n+1−2i (i ≤ a_w), 2i−n−2a_w−1 (i > a_w), so the t_{a_w}-exponent is m_{a_w} + (b_w−a_w+1)/2 and the t_n-exponent m_n + (b_w−a_w−1)/2; the chain reads m_1 + (n−1)/2 > ⋯ > m_{a_w} + (b_w−a_w+1)/2 > m_n + (b_w−a_w−1)/2 > ⋯ > m_{a_w+1} + (1−n)/2. Also 'Weil group' should be 'Weyl group'.
issues.reason: With β = |κ_norm|_p^{−1}δ_w^{−1/2}α and β_x = |κ_norm|_p^{−1}δ_w^{−1/2}α^x, one gets β_x(t)/β(xtx^{−1}) = (|κ_norm|_p^{−1}δ_w^{−1/2})(t)/(|κ_norm|_p^{−1}δ_w^{−1/2})(xtx^{−1}) = (|κ_norm|_pδ_w^{1/2})(xtx^{−1}t^{−1}), the inverse of the printed value (harmless: a p-adic unit iff its inverse is). The printed θ = |κ_norm|_pδ_w^{−1/2} would have exponents m_i − e_i/2, which need not be distinct (e.g. m_1 = m_2 + 1 makes the t_1- and t_2-exponents equal), so the regularity argument needs the corrected θ; the displayed θ(diag) is in fact the corrected character (up to inversion) with the δ-exponent misprints of the previous issue, and the misprinted constants (b_w−a_w)/2, (b_w−2−a_w)/2 differ from the correct ones by the same 1/2, so every inequality of the chain is unaffected (m_{a_w} + (b_w−a_w+1)/2 > m_n + (b_w−a_w−1)/2 ⇔ m_{a_w} ≥ m_n). The t_n-exponent (a_w−2−b_w)/2 in θ(diag) is inconsistent even with the chain. Index: κ_{σc} has b_w entries and the κ_norm formula just above uses κ_{σc,j} for t_{a_w+j}. Defence: the logic (unit ⇒ trivial ⇒ θ^x = θ ⇒ x = 1 by regularity) is sound with the corrected character, and (166) (read as κ_{σ,a_σ} + κ_{σc,b_σ} ≥ n) gives m_{a_w} ≥ m_n. Independent check: Checked on 300-dpi zooms of p. 129 (and p. 126 for δ_w, B_w). With β = |κ_norm|_p^{-1}δ_w^{-1/2}α, β_x = |κ_norm|_p^{-1}δ_w^{-1/2}α^x and β^x(t) = β(xtx^{-1}) (by analogy with α^x), the α-factors cancel and β_x(t)/β^x(t) = |κ_norm(xtx^{-1}t^{-1})|_p·δ_w(xtx^{-1}t^{-1})^{1/2}: the printed value is its inverse (harmless, a unit iff its inverse is). The invariant character is therefore |κ_norm|_pδ_w^{1/2} (or its inverse), not the printed θ = |κ_norm|_pδ_w^{-1/2}; the printed θ has exponents m_i − e_i/2, which coincide at t_1,t_2 when m_1 = m_2 + 1 (a_w ≥ 2), so it would not be regular. Root count for B_w (A upper, D lower triangular) gives δ_w exponents e_i = n+1−2i (i ≤ a_w) and 2i−n−2a_w−1 (i > a_w), i.e. b_w−a_w+1 at t_{a_w} (p. 126 prints b_w−a_w, cf. sourceIssues E131) and b_w−a_w−1 at t_n. The κ_norm display σ(t_{a_w+j})^{−κ_{σc,j}+a_w} gives m_i = −Σ(κ_{σc,i−a_w} − a_w) for i > a_w (printed κ_{σc,i} is out of range for i > b_w). The θ(diag) display, |∏t_i^{m_i+e_i/2}|_p^{-1}, is exactly |κ_norm|_p^{-1}δ_w^{-1/2}, i.e. the corrected character up to inversion, with the t_{a_w} exponent inheriting the δ_w misprint and the t_n exponent (a_w−2−b_w)/2 wrong under any reading (the chain itself has (b_w−2−a_w)/2). All constants in the chain are off by the same 1/2 on the relevant comparison, so the inequalities are unaffected: m_{a_w}+(b_w−a_w+1)/2 > m_n+(b_w−a_w−1)/2 ⇔ m_{a_w} ≥ m_n, which is Σ_σ(κ_{σ,a_w}+κ_{σc,b_w}−n) ≥ 0, i.e. (166). 'Weil group' should be 'Weyl group'. The logic (unit ⇒ trivial ⇒ θ^x = θ ⇒ x = 1) is sound with the corrected character. v4 p. 120 is identical.

issues.locator: §8.3.5, pp. 131–132, normalisation of the anti-ordinary Hecke operators, in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 122
issues.printed: The source normalizes its Hecke operators as u^−_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p U^−_{w,j} on p. 131, and as u^{GL,−}_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} U^{GL,−}_{w,j} on p. 132.
issues.correction: p. 131: u^−_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} U^−_{w,j} (the same scalar as u_{w,j} and u^{GL,−}_{w,j}).
issues.reason: (170) and (171) use ⟨u^{GL,−}_{w,j}φ, φ′⟩_w = ⟨φ, u^GL_{w,j}φ′⟩_w; since [I t^{−1} I] is the adjoint of [I t I] for the invariant pairing, this holds exactly when both operators carry the same scalar |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1}; with the p. 131 normalisation the identity is off by |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{2}. Case for the defence: for n = 1 the p. 131 normalisation makes 'anti-ordinary' coincide with 'ordinary', in line with Lemma 9.0.1, so the authors may intend a different weight normalisation on the anti-holomorphic side; the paper does not make this explicit, and the local analysis of §8.3.5 is written with the p. 132 convention. Independent check: Zoomed pp. 131–132. p. 131: 'u^−_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p U^−_{w,j}'; p. 132, in the next sentence of the same paragraph: 'u^−_{w,j} acts on π_p^{I_r} = ⊗π_w^{I_{w,r}} via the action of the Hecke operator u^{GL,−}_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1}U^{GL,−}_{w,j}'. U^−_{w,j} = I_r t^{−1}_{w,j} I_r and U^{GL,−}_{w,j} = I_{w,r}t^{−1}_{w,j}I_{w,r} are the same operator (t^+_{w,j} has trivial similitude component, (23)), so the two normalisations differ by |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^2 and contradict each other. The p. 132 one is the one the proofs need: for the G_w-invariant pairing π_w × π_w^∨, (1/vol I)∫_{ItI}⟨π(x)v,v'⟩dx = ⟨v,[It^{−1}I]v'⟩, so [It^{−1}I] on π_w is exactly adjoint to [ItI] on π_w^∨ = (π^♭)_w (the ||ν||^{a(κ)} twist in (141) only affects μ_p); (170)/(171) (⟨u^{GL,−}φ,φ'⟩ = ⟨φ,u^{GL}φ'⟩ with u^{GL} = |κ_norm(t)|_p^{−1}U^{GL}, p. 127) hold only if both carry the same scalar |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1}, and only then does 'anti-ordinary' correspond to ordinarity of π^♭_w for the weight κ, as Lemma 8.3.6(i) asserts. p. 131 copies the shape of the §6.6 convention U^−_{w,j,κ} = |κ'(t_{w,j})|_pU^−_{w,j} (p. 98), which there is used with the Serre-dual subscript κ^D (e^−_{κ^D}, p. 101), but applies it to the holomorphic weight κ of π^♭. The global definition of anti-ordinarity (p. 132, e^−·φ = φ) uses the p. 131 operator, so the slip is in a definition, but the intended meaning is fixed by p. 132 and (170). v4 p. 122 is identical.

issues.locator: §8.3.5, proof of Lemma 8.3.6(i), pp. 132–133 (induction on j after (170), and 'as in the preceding proof' after (171)), in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 123
issues.printed: The proof takes a maximal joint eigenspace V_{j−1} ⊂ π_w^{∨,I_{w,r}} for u^GL_{w,1}, …, u^GL_{w,j−1}, with eigenvalues a(1, r), …, a(j−1, r). Commutativity of the u^GL_{w,j}s is used to extend (170) to every φ ∈ V_{j−1}. It then asserts a nonzero maximal eigenspace V_j ⊂ V_{j−1} for u^GL_{w,j}, with eigenvalue a(j, r).
issues.correction: Work with joint generalised eigenspaces: ℓ = ⟨φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, ·⟩_w satisfies ℓ∘(u^GL_{w,i} − a(i,r)) = 0, hence vanishes on every generalised u^GL_{w,i}-eigenspace for eigenvalues ≠ a(i,r); so ℓ ≠ 0 on the joint generalised eigenspace W_{j−1} for (a(1,r), …, a(j−1,r)); u^GL_{w,j} preserves W_{j−1} and u^GL_{w,j} − a(j,r) is not surjective there, so W_j ≠ 0; finally commuting operators on W_n have a common eigenvector.
issues.reason: The step needs ℓ|_{V_{j−1}} ≠ 0, which is not shown and can fail for true eigenspaces: on ℂ² with u = [[a,1],[0,a]], ℓ(x,y) = y satisfies ℓ∘(u − a) = 0 but vanishes on the eigenspace ℂe_1. Defence: the conclusion is standard linear algebra and holds by the corrected argument. Independent check: p. 132–133: after (170), the first step is justified (ℓ = ⟨φ^{a-ord}_{w,r},·⟩_w is non-zero on π_w^{∨,I_{w,r}} since the pairing of I-invariants is perfect, and ℓ∘(u − a) = 0 forces u − a to be non-surjective, hence a is an eigenvalue). The induction step 'the identity (170) holds for all φ ∈ V_{j−1}. In particular, there is a non-zero subspace V_j ⊂ V_{j−1} which is an eigenspace for u^{GL}_{w,j} with eigenvalue a(j,r)' needs ℓ|_{V_{j−1}} ≠ 0, which is not shown and fails in general for true eigenspaces: on C² with u = [[a,1],[0,a]] and ℓ(x,y) = y one has ℓ∘(u − a) = 0 but ℓ vanishes on ker(u − a) = Ce_1 (checked). The conclusion is nevertheless true (the first reading's generalized-eigenspace argument works; in fact V_{j−1} ∩ W_j ≠ 0 where W_j is the joint generalized eigenspace), so this is a gap in the argument, not an error. v4 p. 123 is identical.

issues.locator: §8.5, proof of Lemma 8.5.3, p. 139 ('The remaining claims of the lemma are consequences of the definition of Q[π′, χ]'), in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 129
issues.printed: The source places the quotient ⟨φ_{r′}(v_S, π′), φ_{r′}(v^♭_S, (π′)^♭)_χ⟩_{π′,χ} / Vol(I^0_{r′,V} ∩ I^0_{r′,−V}) in R·Q[π′, χ]. It attributes the other assertions of the lemma to how Q[π′, χ] is defined.
issues.correction: In Lemmas 6.7.1 and 6.7.6 and in the normalization of the orthogonal complement before Definition 6.7.2 (pp. 104–106), replace Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r}) by Vol(I^0_{r,V} ∩ I^0_{r,−V}). Lemma 8.5.3 and the Main Theorem then hold as stated.
issues.reason: I^0 ∩ ᵗI^0 (diagonal mod p^r) contains I ∩ ᵗI (≡ 1 mod p^r) with index ∏_w #T_w(𝒪_w/p^r), which is divisible by p for r ≥ 2; so 'value in R·Q[π′, χ]' with the §6.7 normalisation requires an extra divisibility that is not addressed. Moreover, by Lemma 8.4.9 the pairing of the trace-compatible anti-ordinary vectors grows like Vol(I^0 ∩ ᵗI^0), so a period defined with Vol(I ∩ ᵗI) would depend on r, contradicting 'these periods are independent of r ≫ 0 … (see also Lemma 8.4.9)' (p. 105) — which suggests §6.7 intends I^0. Defence: with I^0 in §6.7 the claims are indeed immediate from the definitions. Independent check: The inconsistency is real (checked on pp. 104, 106, 137–139, 145). §6.7 normalizes the periods by Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r}): five occurrences, in Lemmas 6.7.1 and 6.7.6 and before Definition 6.7.2, all without superscript 0 (zoomed image of p. 104). Everything downstream uses I^0: Remark 4.6.2, Lemma 8.4.9, Lemma 8.5.3, Proposition 9.1.7 and the Main Theorem's Ω_{π′,χ} = ⟨φ,φ^♭_χ⟩_χ/(Vol(I^0_{r^1,V} ∩ I^0_{r^1,−V})·Q[π′,χ]). The index [I^0 ∩ ᵗI^0 : I ∩ ᵗI] = ∏_w #T_w(O_w/p^r) is divisible by p for r ≥ 2. So, taken literally, for lattice vectors the ratio in Lemma 8.5.3 lies in (∏#T_w(O_w/p^r))^{-1}·R·Q[π′,χ], not in R·Q[π′,χ]. Likewise Ω is neither p-integral nor r^1-independent, contrary to the last sentence of Main Theorem 9.2.2. With I^0 in §6.7, everything is consistent. The paper's own claim (p. 105) that the periods 'are independent of r ≫ 0 … (see also Lemma 8.4.9)' only holds with the I^0 normalization of Lemma 8.4.9. So the fault is a notational slip in §6.7 (a dropped superscript 0), not a missing argument in Lemma 8.5.3, whose 'consequences of the definition' are then immediate. Versions: same in v4 (§6.7 with Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r}); I^0 elsewhere).

issues.reason: Complex conjugation replaces the U_{w,j}-eigenvalues by their complex conjugates, and for a fixed embedding incl_p: Q̄ → Q̄_p complex conjugation need not preserve p-adic absolute values (e.g. for n = 1 a CM Hecke character of infinity type z^k with p split: one of χ(ϖ_w), χ(ϖ_w)‾ is a p-adic unit and the other is not). Since π̄ ≅ π^∨ ⊗ (similitude twist) by essential unitarity, the first sentence is essentially equivalent to the conclusion; the weight normalisations (κ_norm for π̄ versus π) are not discussed. Defence: the lemma is presented as reassurance and is not used — §9 assumes anti-ordinarity and the Main Theorem assumes ordinarity separately.

issues.locator: §9.1.6, proof of Proposition 9.1.7, p. 143, in arXiv v5; present in v4 at p. 133
issues.printed: The proof sets [G_3] = G_3(ℚ)Z(ℝ)\G_3(𝔸), dg^χ_2 = χ(det(g_2))^{−1}dg_2. Doubling Lemma 7.5.3 gives = 1/(Vol(I^0_{r,V})Vol(I^0_{r,−V})) ∫_{[G_3]} D(κ, m, χ_0)E^holo_{f(χ_0,ψρ^υ)}((g_1, g_2), m) φ′(g_1)φ′^♭(g_2) ||ν(g_1)^{a(κ)}|| dg_1 dg^χ_2. It claims the equality by comparison with (179) and the zeta integral definition.
issues.correction: Spell out the comparison: Lemma 7.5.3 has the factor ||ν(g)^{−a(κ)}|| (sign of the exponent flipped here) and is over G(ℚ)Z_G(ℝ)\G(𝔸); the zeta integral I(φ, φ′, f, s) (p. 142) has no ν-factor and is over Z_3(𝔸)G_3(ℚ)\G_3(𝔸). The central characters and the ||ν||^{±a(κ)} twist (π^♭ = π^∨ ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)}) have to be reconciled to identify the two integrals.
issues.reason: The 'comparison' is asserted in one line although the two integrals differ by a character of the centre and by the integration domain. Defence: these are normalisations of the twist by the similitude character, presumably absorbed into the identification of π^♭ with π^∨ ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)}; the final formula is unaffected up to such a normalisation. Independent check: Quotation checked on the page image (p. 143). The 'comparison' is a single sentence, but the two integrals visibly differ. (a) The doubled Lemma 7.5.3 carries ||ν(g_1)^{a(κ)}||, with the sign of the exponent opposite to Lemma 7.5.3's ||ν(g)^{−a(κ)}|| (p. 121). (b) It is integrated over G_3(Q)Z(R)\G_3(A), while the zeta integral I(φ,φ′,f,s) (p. 142; (51), p. 45) is over Z_3(A)G_3(Q)\G_3(A), with χ^{-1}(det g_2) and no ν-factor. (c) The proof uses E^holo_{f(χ_0,ψρ^υ)}, while the statement has f^holo(χ_u,ψρ^υ). Matching requires tracking the central characters and the twist π^♭ = π^∨ ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)} (141). A quick check of Z(R)-invariance suggests the forms alone require ||ν||^{−a(κ)}, not +a(κ), unless the Eisenstein series compensates. None of this is written. The final formula is presumably right up to such normalizations, so this is a gap in the proof. The volume factor itself is consistent (see sourceIssues E125). Versions: v4 p. 133 same.

issues.locator: §9.2, Main Theorem 9.2.2 (and Corollary 9.2.1), statement, pp. 144–145, in arXiv v5; present in v4 at pp. 133–134 ('for any π′ congruent to π')
issues.printed: The source asserts the displayed equality for the result of evaluating L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭), taking any classical character χ = ||•||^m χ_u : X_p → R^× and every π′ ∈ S(K_{r^1}, κ^1, π), with some r^1.
issues.correction: '… for any classical χ = ||•||^m χ_u with m ≥ n and any π′ ∈ S(K_{r^1},κ^1,π) with κ^1 sufficiently regular (and satisfying (166)) such that (χ,ψρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H, i.e. κ^1_σ ∈ C_3(χ_σ) for all σ, with ρ, ρ^υ determined by κ^1 and χ via (95), (97) …'
issues.reason: The interpolation formula is derived from Proposition 9.1.7, which assumes (χ, ψρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H and m ≥ n; I_∞(χ, κ^1) (Proposition 4.5.6) and the local computations at p are only available for such pairs. The Main Theorem quantifies over all classical χ and all π′ in the family, with only the preceding sentence 'Let the algebraic characters κ, ρ, ρ^υ determine one another, relative to a given χ, as in (95) and (97)' hinting at the constraint. Defence: 'classical' may be read as 'the pair (χ, κ^1) is classical', i.e. lies in Y^class_H; and the anti-ordinarity is a stated standing assumption of §9 (p. 140). Independent check: Quotation checked on the page images (pp. 144–145). The interpolation formula comes from Proposition 9.1.7 and Corollary 9.1.8, which assume (χ,ψρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H and m ≥ n. It also relies on Proposition 7.4.15, which needs λ ∈ X(κ,r,R) with κ sufficiently regular, and on Proposition 8.5.1/Lemma 8.5.3 (κ satisfying (166)). 'Classical χ' in the paper means only that χ is the p-adic avatar of an algebraic Hecke character (§5.3.1, p. 83). The sentence before the theorem ('Let … κ, ρ, ρ^υ determine one another, relative to a given χ, as in Inequalities (95) and Equation (97)') arguably imposes κ^1_σ ∈ C_3(χ_σ), i.e. the Y^class_H condition. It does not impose m ≥ n or the regularity of κ^1, and the theorem quantifies over all classical χ and all π′ ∈ S(K_{r^1},κ^1,π). So the stated range exceeds what is proved. Whether the formula holds outside it (e.g. m < n) is not addressed, hence 'gap'. The anti-ordinarity clause of the first reading's correction is unnecessary: it is a stated standing assumption of §9 (p. 140). Versions: v4 pp. 133–134 same ('for any π′ congruent to π').

issues.citation: Ellenberg–Venkatesh–Westerland, "Homological stability for Hurwitz spaces and the Cohen-Lenstra conjecture over function fields", Annals of Mathematics 183 (2016), no. 3
issues.reviewReason: Confirmed. Located verbatim on p.733: "…which is to say that both the upper limit δ+ and the lower limit δ− in Theorem 1.2 are equal to 1." In Theorem 1.2 δ± are the upper and lower densities of the imaginary quadratic extensions of F_q(t) whose ℓ-part of the class group is isomorphic to the fixed A; distinct A give disjoint events, so the δ for different A sum to at most 1 and none can equal 1 (Theorem 1.2 itself gives c_ℓ/|Aut A|, e.g. 0.560 for ℓ=3, A trivial). Remark 7.9 on p.769 confirms δ± are the lim sup and lim inf in n at fixed q, so no reading of the printed sentence makes it true. The intended statement is presumably that each density equals the Cohen–Lenstra mass — i.e. that the ratio, not the density, is 1 — and the correction's refusal to derive anything from the sentence as printed is the right instruction.

Without that restriction the combinatorial A has simplices in every dimension while the geometric A has dimension n−1, and the homeomorphism asserted in Proposition 5.6 could not hold.

issues.reviewReason: Confirmed, and the enumeration reproduces exactly. Case (i) of the proof of Lemma 8.4 (p.772) asserts that for A' ≆ A × Z/ℓZ "any such lift f̃ is surjective, and the set of lifts is a principal homogeneous space under Hom(X,Z/ℓZ)" — in particular nonempty. Take ℓ=3, A = C3², A' = X = C9×C3 with π(x,y) = (x mod 3, y) (kernel of order 3, and A' ≆ A×C3, so case (i) applies), and f(x,y) = (y, x mod 3). A lift must send the order-3 generator (0,1) into π⁻¹(1,0) = {1,4,7}×{0}, all of whose elements have order 9, so no lift exists at all. Enumerating: |Sur(X,A)| = 48, of which exactly 12 lift and 36 do not. The aggregate conclusion (8.4.1) still holds here — |Sur(X,A')| = |Aut(C9×C3)| = 108 ≥ (ℓ−1)·48 = 96 — which is why the finding is recorded against the proof and not the statement.

The proof of Corollary 3.5 (Achter–Pries p.14) reads "Since the composition M_{Z_ℓ}(H̃_g⊗k) ↪ Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ) → Sp_{2g}(Z/ℓ) is surjective, a standard group theory argument (e.g., [29, 1.3]) shows that M_{Z_ℓ}(H̃_g⊗k) ≅ Sp_{2g}(Z_ℓ)", and [29] is Vasiu, Manuscripta Math. 112 (2003), 325–355 — the very source recorded as a prerequisite. Vasiu's own Theorem 1.3 matches the correction's scope: condition (a) is q ≥ 5, and condition (b) at q = 3 demands Lie_{F_3}(H) ∩ K_2 ≠ {0} for every normal PGL_2 or SL_2 subgroup H of G_k — vacuous for Sp_{2g} with g ≥ 2, but a real hypothesis for Sp_2 = SL_2; Vasiu adds that "most of the extra assumptions of b) to d) were known to be needed before". The conclusion of Corollary 3.5 is not in doubt, which is why the finding is a gap.

The proof of Lemma 2.3 (Achter–Pries p.5) concludes that the branch functor β°_γ ⊗ C : M̃^{γ,°}_G ⊗ C → M̃^°_{0,r} ⊗ C "is an isomorphism", and §2.2 says explicitly that the same letters denote the representing stacks. That is precisely the correction offered, and item 131 of this extraction keeps the μ_2 stabiliser.

issues.reason: Over a connected affine base with a nontrivial line bundle L, take S to be its additive vector group inside the reductive group GL(O⊕L), as the off-diagonal unipotent subgroup Hom(O,L). Then Lie(S)=L is locally free of rank1 but not free. For a concrete affine base, a nonprincipal invertible ideal over Z[sqrt(−5)] supplies L.

issues.citation: Ellenberg–Venkatesh–Westerland, "Homological stability for Hurwitz spaces and the Cohen-Lenstra conjecture over function fields", Annals of Mathematics 183 (2016), no. 3
issues.reviewReason: Confirmed. Vasiu §2.2 (PDF p.4) says "We now assume that S is a smooth group scheme over R. So Lie(S) is a free R-module of rank equal to the relative dimension of S." The standing base is only a connected affine Spec(R) (§1, p.2: "A reductive group scheme F over a connected affine scheme Spec(R)…"), not a local ring, and over such a base Lie(S) is finite locally free but need not be free: for an invertible non-free R-module L the vector group S = Spec(Sym_R(L^∨)), which is the off-diagonal unipotent subgroup Hom(O,L) of GL(O⊕L), is smooth of relative dimension 1 with Lie(S) = L. As the finding notes, the applications run over W(k), where projective modules are free, so nothing downstream is affected.

issues.locator: Abstract, p. 729, and the paragraph after Theorem 1.2, p. 730 (published version; the arXiv v4 PDF has the same abstract, p. 1)
issues.printed: The abstract asserts existence of Q = Q(A) such that for q greater than Q a positive proportion of quadratic extensions of F_q(t) have ℓ-primary class group isomorphic to A. After Theorem 1.2, it says that for q > Q0(ℓ) among imaginary quadratic extensions over F_q(t), positive proportions have class numbers divisible by ℓ and indivisible by ℓ, respectively.
issues.correction: What the paper proves is these statements for q > Q with q ≢ 1 (mod ℓ), q odd and prime to ℓ, as in Theorem 1.2 and E11. For q ≡ 1 (mod ℓ) the paper says only that 'the method of proof still works' and yields a different distribution, and it gives no argument; that case is not proved there.
issues.reason: Theorem 1.2 (p. 730) is stated 'as q → ∞ with q ≢ 1 (mod ℓ)', and its proof, through Proposition 8.3 and Theorem 8.8, needs moments tending to 1 and ℓ ∤ q(q − 1). The abstract and the sentence 'In particular, for q > Q0(ℓ), …' drop the congruence. The moment-one argument does not carry over as written. Take A = (Z/ℓ)², k = 1, g ≥ 2 and q ≡ 1 (mod ℓ). The multiplier-q coset GSp_q(V) of V = Jac[ℓ] is then Sp(V) itself. The Sp(V)-orbits on Sur(V, A), which are the ordered pairs of independent covectors, are classified by the value of the alternating pairing on the pair (Witt), and all ℓ values occur. So there are ℓ Frobenius-stable orbits, each stable under −I, where the case q ≢ 1 (mod ℓ) has one. For ℓ = 3, g = 2 they have 80·24 = 1920 and 80·27 = 2160, 2160 elements. Proposition 8.3 therefore does not apply, and the paper supplies no replacement. This does not show that the positive-proportion statements fail when q ≡ 1 (mod ℓ): the modified distribution (Garton's thesis, [30]) may still have positive masses. The paper does not prove it.
issues.known: new: no correction found. The arXiv listing's abstract for v4 (1 December 2015) reads 'for q greater than Q and not congruent to 1 modulo l', but the v4 PDF, the published abstract and the paragraph after Theorem 1.2 do not carry the congruence.

issues.locator: Published p. 106, the last display of the introduction; compare §7, p. 148
issues.printed: The source calls (E,∇), an irreducible flat connection whose determinant L is torsion, cohomologically rigid when [(E,∇)] is both isolated and reduced in M_dR(X,L,r). It asserts equivalence with H¹_dR(X,(End(E),∇)) = 0 and uses this to motivate the terminology.
issues.correction: H¹_dR(X,(End⁰(E),∇)) = 0, the trace-free endomorphisms, as §7 (p. 148) writes it: "Recall that an irreducible connection (E,∇) with determinant L on X over C is called cohomologically rigid if H¹(X,End⁰(E,∇))=0". ("equivalent to vanishing of … = 0" is also one "vanishing" too many.)
issues.reason: M_dR(X,L,r) is the moduli of connections with the determinant fixed, so its Zariski tangent space at an irreducible point is H¹_dR(X,End⁰(E,∇)) — which is exactly what p. 148 says. In characteristic zero the trace splitting gives End(E) = End⁰(E) ⊕ O_X as flat bundles, so H¹_dR(X,(End(E),∇)) = H¹_dR(X,End⁰(E,∇)) ⊕ H¹_dR(X,(O_X,d)) and the second summand is H¹(X,C), of dimension b₁(X). For every X with b₁(X) > 0 — every curve of positive genus, and every variety the paper is really about — the printed condition therefore holds for no connection at all, and the notion it defines would be empty. Read on the rendered page: the display carries an underlined "End" with no superscript.

issues.citation: Esnault–Groechenig, "Rigid connections and F-isocrystals", Acta Mathematica (2020)
issues.reviewReason: Confirmed. The introduction on p.106 prints 'An irreducible flat connection (E,∇) with torsion determinant L is called cohomologically rigid, if [(E,∇)] is a reduced isolated [point of] M_dR(X,L,r). This is equivalent to vanishing of H¹_dR(X,(End(E),∇)) = 0', with the full endomorphism bundle, while §7 on p.148 writes 'an irreducible connection (E,∇) with determinant L on X over C is called cohomologically rigid if H¹(X, End⁰(E,∇)) = 0'. On a fixed-determinant moduli space the trace-free version is the right one, so the introduction's End(E) should be End⁰(E).

issues.locator: Theorem 2.17 and its proof, published pp. 117–119 (especially p. 118, line 8, and p. 119, lines 4–6)
issues.printed: The source claims at most one a∈A_{Z′,r}(S) has the property because a and b are monic. It then obtains the desired a∈A_{Z′,r}(S) by invoking uniqueness for a^{p^d}=b in Sym^• Ω¹_{Z′×S/S}[λ].
issues.correction: Both claims fail as soon as S is non-reduced, and so does the essential-image half of the statement of Theorem 2.17. The invariant that is canonical is the one the proof has just built: the characteristic polynomial of the Morita-reduced Higgs sheaf π′_*F, which is independent of the splitting because F is unique up to unique isomorphism. Theorem 2.17 should require of M that this reduced invariant equal a, rather than only that M be supported on Z′_a with π′_*M of characteristic polynomial a^{p^d}; the descent of a should be deduced from that canonicity, not from uniqueness of p^d-th roots.
issues.reason: Sym^• Ω¹_{Z′×S/S}[λ] is a commutative F_p-algebra, so x ↦ x^{p^d} is a ring endomorphism of it, and it is injective only when the algebra is reduced. Witness for the two printed claims (r=2): let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, Z′ an elliptic curve over k with a nowhere-vanishing ω ∈ H⁰(Z′,Ω¹), and S = Spec k[ε]/(ε²). Then a = λ² + εω² and a₀ = λ² are distinct monic elements of A_{Z′,2}(S) with a^{p} = λ^{2p} + ε^pω^{2p} = λ^{2p} = a₀^{p}, so b = λ^{2p} has two monic degree-2 roots. Witness for the statement (r=3, d=1): take a = λ³ + εω²λ and a₀ = λ³, again with a^p = a₀^p. Since a vanishes on the zero section, Z′ ×_k S ⊂ Z′_a, so the D_{Z′}-module M of the constant family (F^*V,∇_can) with V of rank 3 — whose p-curvature is zero — is scheme-theoretically supported on Z′_a, and π′_*M is locally free of rank 3p with characteristic polynomial λ^{3p} = a^{p}. M therefore satisfies every condition on the right-hand side of Theorem 2.17 for this a, while the connection it corresponds to has Hitchin invariant a₀ ≠ a: the asserted equivalence of groupoids fails. Over reduced S the printed argument is correct and nothing changes. The correspondence is applied over non-reduced bases exactly where it matters — the Artinian deformations in the proof of Proposition 3.5, and the divided-power thickenings of Appendix A — so the repair is needed, but no main theorem depends on the defective half: §3 uses the equivalence C_a supplied by [OV, Corollary 2.9] for an OV-admissible a, and the forward assignment (E,∇) ↦ (χ_dR(E,∇),M) is unaffected.

issues.citation: Esnault–Groechenig, "Rigid connections and F-isocrystals", Acta Mathematica (2020)
issues.reviewReason: Confirmed at the locator. Page 118 prints 'It is clear that there is at most one such a ∈ A_{Z′,r}(S) with this property, since a and b are monic polynomials', in the construction of the degree-r factor a of b with M scheme-theoretically supported on Z′_a. issues.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.5, published p. 127, lines 5–10
issues.printed: The source says construction of (E_{T_t^{(m−1)}},∇_{T_t^{(m−1)}}) makes χ_dR((E_{T_t^{(m−1)}},∇_{T_t^{(m−1)}})) a morphism T_t^{(m−1)} → A′. It concludes that this factors through A′(m−1), but through no A(k−1) with k<m.
issues.correction: Only the first half is automatic. Truncating an arbitrary deformation at order m−1 can lower the order of its Hitchin invariant, or destroy it; the truncation order has to be chosen so that a non-factoring jet survives, and what the contradiction needs is only that the restriction not factor through A′(D′−1). Since the order required is not bounded by m, the interaction with the standing hypothesis p−1 > R(r,m) has to be re-examined — which is why a uniform bound on the length of a rigid component is the real content here. (A(k−1) is also printed without its prime.)
issues.reason: Counterexample to the inference, with A′ = A¹ = Spec k[u]: take m = 4, T = Spec k[t]/(t⁹) and χ: u ↦ t². Then χ does not factor through A′(3) = Spec k[u]/(u⁴), since χ^*(u⁴) = t⁸ ≠ 0, so T satisfies the hypothesis of the paragraph; but its restriction to T_t^{(3)} = Spec k[t]/(t⁴) has χ^*(u²) = t⁴ = 0, so it factors through A′(1), that is through A′(k−1) with k = 2 < 4 = m, contrary to the printed conclusion. With T = Spec k[t] and χ: u ↦ t^m the restriction to T_t^{(m−1)} is the constant map to 0. The proof of Proposition 3.5 is a proof by contradiction, and this is the step that produces the contradicting Higgs deformation, so the gap is in the load-bearing part of the argument; the conclusion of Proposition 3.5 is not in doubt.

issues.locator: Definition 5.2, published p. 139, together with Lemma 5.6 and its proof, p. 141
issues.printed: The source defines Def_ϱ: Art_F → Sets by assigning to a finite-dimensional commutative local F-algebra A the isomorphism classes of continuous ϱ′: Γ→GL(r,A) for which some finite extension F′/F and F-morphism A→F′ give (ϱ′)_{F′}≃ϱ_{F′}. It calls ϱ rigid when B∈Art_F corepresents Def_ϱ. The proof of Lemma 5.6 claims that completing M_B(X/C,det(ϱ),r)⊗_Z F_p formally at [ϱ] represents Def_ϱ̂(F_q).
issues.correction: Def_ϱ must be the fixed-determinant deformation functor — the same convention as everywhere else in the paper — namely the isomorphism classes of continuous ϱ′ with det ϱ′ = det ϱ. Otherwise Definition 5.2 does not define the notion Lemma 5.6 and Theorem 5.4 use.
issues.reason: As literally defined the functor is the unrestricted one, and it is never corepresented by an Artinian algebra once b₁(X) > 0. Twisting ϱ′ = ϱ⊗χ by a continuous character χ: Γ → 1+m_A is a deformation of ϱ for every A ∈ Art_F, and for p > r distinct characters give non-isomorphic twists (an isomorphism ϱ⊗χ ≅ ϱ forces χ^r = 1 on determinants, and 1+m_A is a p-group). The character functor A ↦ Hom_cont(Γ,1+m_A) is corepresented by the completed group algebra F_q[[Γ^ab ⊗ Z_p]] ≅ F_q[[x_1,…,x_b]] with b = b₁(X), so it acts freely on Def_ϱ and forces the hull of Def_ϱ to have dimension at least b₁(X). For X a curve of genus g ⩾ 1 no absolutely irreducible ϱ would then be rigid, and Lemma 5.6 — whose right-hand side is the completion of the moduli space M_B(X/C,det(ϱ),r) with the determinant fixed — would be false. With the fixed-determinant reading both statements are correct and this is plainly what is meant.

issues.locator: Proof of Proposition A.2, published p. 154, lines 12–14
issues.printed: The source places m^*θ−r^*θ ∈ Ker(H⁰((Z′_a)_p, Ω¹_{(Z′_a)_p/Spec k[t]/(t−1)^p}) → H⁰(Z′_a, Ω¹_{Z′_a})). It infers that m^*θ−r^*θ is supported on Z′_p ↪ T^*Z ×_k G′_m, taking Z′ ↪ T^*Z′ as the zero-section.
issues.correction: The support assertion does not follow and is false as stated. What has to be established is that the class φ(m^*θ−r^*θ) is pulled back from a neighbourhood of the zero section on which D_{Z′} splits — a Brauer-class computation, not a support statement. The symbol Z′_p also has to be disambiguated: Remark A.1 defines V_n = V ×_k Spec k[t]/(t−1)^n, a thickening in the group direction, whereas the appeal to [OV, Corollary 2.9] in the last line needs the infinitesimal neighbourhood of the zero section inside T^*Z′. ("T^*Z ×_k G′_m" is a misprint for T^*Z′ ×_k G_m.)
issues.reason: m is the conic action, so m^*θ = tθ and r^*θ = θ and hence m^*θ − r^*θ = (t−1)θ. Writing ε = t−1, which satisfies ε^p = 0 on (Z′_a)_p, and θ = ξ dx in local coordinates, the section is εξ dx. It does lie in the displayed kernel, because it dies at ε = 0; but it is non-zero at every point where ξ is invertible and ε^{p−1} ≠ 0, so its support is the closure of the locus where θ ≠ 0, not a thickening of the zero-section {ξ = 0}. The two thickenings occurring in the step — the p-th neighbourhood in the t-direction and a neighbourhood of the zero section in the fibre direction — are different schemes. Proposition A.2 carries Theorem A.4, Remark A.5 and Corollary A.7; the appendix is itself presented as an alternative route to Theorem 1.4, which §§2–7 prove independently, and Question A.8 records that its scope is deliberately limited.

issues.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1, published p. 146, lines 3–5
issues.printed: The source uses Lemma 5.11 to obtain infinitely many primes p admitting a good closed point s∈S, and concludes that the Kodaira–Spencer class is zero throughout X_S.
issues.correction: Apply Lemma 5.11 after inverting a non-zero coefficient of gr(∇_S) — equivalently, after shrinking S — which its own proof allows, since the finitely generated ring R₁ ⊂ C chosen there may be enlarged at will and Cassels's theorem then sends the adjoined inverse to a p-adic unit. Infinitude of residue characteristics on its own does not give the density the deduction needs.
issues.reason: The good points of Lemma 5.11(c) are closed points of S of pairwise distinct residue characteristics, and such a family need not meet every non-empty open subset of a positive-dimensional arithmetic base: in Spec Z[t] the closed points (p,t), p prime, realise every residue characteristic and all lie in V(t), where the non-zero section t vanishes. The vanishing of a section at all of them therefore does not make it zero. What is true, and is what the proof needs, is this: gr(∇_S) is a section of a coherent sheaf on the integral scheme X_S, so it is non-zero if and only if it is non-zero on the generic fibre; if gr(∇_C) ≠ 0 there is a non-empty open V ⊂ S over which it is non-zero, and a good point inside V contradicts the vanishing established for every good s. The rest of the proof is unaffected: on the reduced fibre X_s the identity gr(∇_s) = ω·id together with nilpotency does force ω = 0.

Vanishing of gr(∇_s) at the good points of infinitely many fibres does not by itself give vanishing on X_S; the repair the correction records — invert a non-zero coefficient of gr(∇_S), that is shrink S, which Lemma 5.11's own proof allows — is what makes the deduction work.

issues.locator: Remark 2.16(a) and (b), published pp. 116–117
issues.printed: In (a), the source identifies A_{Z′,r}(k) with the space consisting of degree-r sections of H⁰(Z′, Sym^• Ω¹_{Z′}[λ]). In (b), for a∈A_{Z′,r}(S), it defines Z′_a ⊂ T^*Z′×_kS by the ideal sheaf generated by θ^r+a₂θ^{r−2}+…+(−1)^r a_r inside (π′×_k Id)_*O_{T^*Z′×_kS} = (Sym^• T_{Z′})⊗_k O_S.
issues.correction: In (a): the space of *monic* degree-r sections whose λ^{r−1}-coefficient vanishes — an affine space over A_{Z′,r}(k) — or, kept linear, the degree-r sections whose λ^r- and λ^{r−1}-coefficients both vanish. In (b): that section lives in H⁰(T^*Z′×_kS, (π′×Id)^* Sym^r Ω¹_{Z′}), as the display on p. 117 correctly states, and for dim Z′ > 1 the ideal is the one generated by its components.
issues.reason: A degree-r section of Sym^• Ω¹_{Z′}[λ] is ⨁_{i=0}^{r} H⁰(Z′,Sym^i Ω¹_{Z′})·λ^{r−i}, which contains the i = 0 summand k·λ^r and the i = 1 summand H⁰(Z′,Ω¹_{Z′}); (2.5) defines A_{Z′,r} as ⨁_{i=2}^{r}, the paper having just noted that "the definition above omits the i=1 term, since our Higgs fields are trace-free by assumption". The two spaces are therefore never equal: for Z′ = P¹ one has H⁰(Sym^iΩ¹) = 0 for all i ⩾ 1, so A_{Z′,r}(k) = 0 while the degree-r sections are k·λ^r ≠ 0. Part (b) itself uses the corrected description, its element being monic with no λ^{r−1} term. This is the remark the authors introduce with "Since it is central to our approach, we give a more detailed description", which is why the imprecision is worth recording rather than passing over.

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.5, published p.140; arXiv v4 p.30
issues.correction: Retain χ^r=1, hence χ takes values in μ_r(K), since K is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. The generic deformation is rho⊗χ⁻¹ over K. Its moduli point is closed, so the entire DVR map has constant image, contradicting a nonconstant deformation. Triviality of χ is unnecessary.
issues.reason: Trace equality after reduction imposes no condition on χ(g) where Tr rho(g)=0. For Q₈ use A=diag(i,−i) and B=[[0,1],[−1,0]], generating an irreducible determinant-one representation, with χ(A)=1 and χ(B)=−1. Conjugation by A intertwines rho and rho⊗χ, so this constant family satisfies the displayed isomorphism although χ≠1 and χ²=1. The trace is ±2 on ±I and zero elsewhere. Thus the inference in the proof is false, while the lemma survives the constant-moduli-point argument.

issues.printed: The source specifies the type as A_n.
issues.correction: For a unitary group arising from a vector hermitian form, impose the required rational-versus-real Witt-index equality separately.
issues.reason: Over L=Q(i), the hermitian form diag(1,−1,1,−3) is a hyperbolic plane plus an anisotropic plane: 3 is not a norm from Q(i), because its 3-adic valuation is odd. (Keeping t_N − t_H and reversing the semistability inequality — Kedlaya's convention — would repair §2.1.2 and is the convention §2.5 actually uses (Remarque 2.38(ii), Théorème 2.42(ii): deg ∆(D) = deg D with deg = v_p of the Frobenius), but it does not repair §5: Proposition 5.6(i) and Théorème 5.7(i) need deg = t_H − t_N.)
issues.reason: With the Préface's own convention (semistable means µ(D′) ≤ µ(D) for strict subobjects, slopes of the HN filtration decreasing), 'weakly admissible = semistable of slope 0' would require t_N(D′) ≤ t_H(D′) for subobjects, the opposite of Fontaine's t_H(D′) ≤ t_N(D′). Check: for a non-split crystalline extension 0 → Q_p(1) → V → Q_p → 0 (Kummer class of a unit), D = D_cris(V) is admissible, but its φ-stable line D″ of slope 0 has t_N(D″) = 0 and t_H(D″) = −1 (Fil^0 D_K is not K·D″ since V is non-split), so deg(D″) = t_N − t_H = 1 > 0 = µ(D) and D would not be 'faiblement admissible'. Likewise deg E(D) = t_H(D) − t_N(D) (E(D, φ) has slopes minus the Frobenius slopes, Remarque 4.8, and the modification by Fil adds t_H), so Proposition 5.6(i) 'deg(E(D)) = deg(D)' and Théorème 5.7(i) 'Si µ(D) > 0, alors dim V_st(D) = +∞' are false as printed: for D = K_0e, φ = 1, weight −1 (Fil^{−1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0) one has µ(D) = t_N − t_H = 1 > 0, but E(D) = O(−1) and V_st(D) = 0. Internal check: the Préface's own proof of Proposition 5.6(i) derives the degree for the trivial filtration from Remarque 4.8 (O(λ) ↔ Ĕ(−λ)), which gives deg E(D) = −t_N(D), whereas §2.1.2 gives deg(D) = t_N(D) for the trivial filtration. Proposition 2.15 (hypothesis t_H = t_N) is unaffected.

issues.locator: Préface §2.3.3 (proof that B_e is principal), p. 19, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The proof asserts that t^{k+d} r ∈ U_{k+d} maps to zero in t^k B+dR, from which it deduces t^{k+d} r ∈ t^r U_d and deg r ≤ d. It then claims to have obtained (u0/t^d) a − (v0/t^d) b in I with degree < d.
issues.correction: … a une image nulle dans B_dR^+/t^kB_dR^+, et donc t^{k+d}r ∈ t^k U_d (with d = deg b) … ; the element of I of degree < d is (u_0/t)a − (v_0/t)b = t^{−(d+1)}(a_0u_0 − b_0v_0) (a_0 = t^d a, b_0 = t^d b). (In the first case, 'I contient t^{1−d}u′' should read t^{1−d}b′.)
issues.reason: In the division step r is the remainder, so 't^r' is meaningless; t^{k+d}r ∈ U_{k+d} ∩ t^kB_dR^+ = t^kU_d gives deg r ≤ d. In the second case the printed element (u_0/t^d)a − (v_0/t^d)b = t^{−2d}(a_0u_0 − b_0v_0) satisfies φ = p^{1−d}, so it is not in B_e (nor in I) as soon as d ≥ 2; since a_0u_0 − b_0v_0 ∈ U_{d+1} maps to 0 in B_dR^+/t², it lies in t²U_{d−1}, and (a_0u_0 − b_0v_0)/t^{d+1} = t^{−1}(u_0a − v_0b) ∈ I is nonzero of degree ≤ d − 1. (Also d = deg b is not introduced in the division paragraph.)

issues.locator: Préface Exemple 2.23(ii), p. 21, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source claims that V = Qp t ⊕ Qp a, where a = log[1 + p^♭], is a two-dimensional sub-Qp-representation of U.
issues.correction: Take a = log[(1+p)^♭] (a compatible system of p-power roots of the principal unit 1 + p, or of any u ∈ 1 + m_K with log u ≠ 0); then σ(a) = a + c(σ)t with c the Kummer cocycle, V is G_K-stable, θ(a) = log(1 + p) ≠ 0 and U ⊗ V → B_2 is surjective.
issues.reason: x ↦ log[x] is a G_K-equivariant Z_p-linear isomorphism from (1 + m_{C^♭}, ×) onto a lattice of U (Théorème 3.11(ii) for E = Q_p), so V is G_K-stable iff σ(1 + p^♭) lies in the Q_p-saturation W of ε^{Z_p}(1 + p^♭)^{Z_p} for all σ. Write ℓ(u) = v_{C^♭}(u − 1). For u ∈ W, ℓ(u) ∈ {p^m} ∪ {p^m/(p−1)} (m ∈ Z) when p is odd (ℓ((1+p^♭)^{p^kα_0}) = p^k, ℓ(ε^{p^jβ_0}) = p^{j+1}/(p−1), these never coincide for p odd, and ℓ(u^{p^n}) = p^nℓ(u)). Take σ ∈ G_{K(μ_{p^∞})} with σ(p^♭) = ε^{p^s}p^♭ (s ≥ 0, possible by Kummer theory); then w = σ(1 + p^♭)/(1 + p^♭) = 1 + (ε^{p^s} − 1)p^♭/(1 + p^♭) has ℓ(w) = p^{s+1}/(p−1) + 1 = (p^{s+1} + p − 1)/(p−1), which is neither of the form p^m nor p^m/(p−1) (m ∈ Z): p^{s+1} + p − 1 ≡ −1 (mod p) cannot equal (p−1)p^m or p^m for m ≥ 1, and is too large for m ≤ 0. Hence w ∉ W and V is not G_K-stable (p odd).

issues.locator: Préface §3.1.1–3.1.4, Théorème 3.1(ii) and Théorème 3.8(ii), pp. 32–35, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: In (ii), the source asserts that a slope λ of NPx with multiplicity d admits a1 , . . . , ad ∈ OC^♭ with vC^♭(ai ) = −λvp (π) and a factorization x = (π − [a1 ]) · · · (π − [ad ])y with y ∈ AE.
issues.correction: With NP_x defined at the integer abscissae k (§3.1.1) the factor π − [a] has slope −v_{C^♭}(a), so the condition should be v_{C^♭}(a_i) = −λ; alternatively define NP_x with abscissae k·v_p(π) (the Legendre dual of v_r). The two agree only when v_p(π) = 1, i.e. E/Q_p unramified. Similarly v_r = inf_k(v(x_k) + k r v_p(π)) has slopes in v_p(π)·N, not 'pentes entières'; and in §3.1.4 the multiplicity of λ ∈ −I should be ∂_g v_{−λ}(x) − ∂_d v_{−λ}(x).
issues.reason: Example: E = Q_p(p^{1/2}), π = p^{1/2}, v_p(π) = 1/2, x = π − [π^♭] (a generator of Ker θ_E). NP_x joins (0, v(π^♭)) = (0, 1/2) to (1, 0): slope λ = −1/2 of multiplicity 1. The theorem would give a_1 with v(a_1) = −λ·v_p(π) = 1/4; but any factorisation x = (π − [a_1])y with y ∈ A_E forces y to be a unit (NP_y is constant) and θ_E(π − [a_1]) = 0, i.e. a_1^♯ = π, so v(a_1) = v_p(π) = 1/2. Also v_r(x) = min(1/2, r/2) has slope 1/2 ∉ N.

issues.printed: The source gives the identities u([a]) = [a], u(Vπ x) = (π/π′) Vπ′ (F^{fE′/E −1} u(x)) and u(F^{fE′/E} x) = F u(x).

For y = V_π x one gets W_{fn}(V_π x) = π W_{fn−1}(x) for n ≥ 1 (and 0 for n = 0), while W′_n((π/π′)V_{π′}z) = π W′_{n−1}(z). issues.locator: §1.5.1, p. 66, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source calls the function concave and claims that, for convex ϕ, the inverse Legendre transform recovers it by ϕ(x) = sup{L (ϕ)(λ) − λx | λ ∈ R}.
issues.correction: The inversion formula holds for ϕ convex and lower semicontinuous (in general sup_λ{L(ϕ)(λ) − λx} is the lower semicontinuous hull of ϕ).
issues.reason: Counterexample: ϕ(0) = 1, ϕ = 0 on ]0, 1], ϕ = +∞ elsewhere, is convex and not identically +∞; L(ϕ)(λ) = min(0, λ) and sup_λ{min(0, λ) − λ·0} = 0 ≠ 1 = ϕ(0). The polygons to which the formula is applied (Newton polygons, which take a finite value at their left endpoint and are +∞ before it) are lower semicontinuous, so nothing later is affected.

issues.locator: Proposition 1.6.16, démonstration, p. 73, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source invokes concavity to claim, when n ≥ N and r2 ≤ r ≤ r1, that vr (xn ) ≤ vr1 (x) + (r − r1 )∂g vr1 (x) ≤ vr2 (x) + (r1 − r2 )|∂d vr2 (x)|.
issues.correction: The first inequality is correct, the second is not. Take instead A = v_{r_1}(x) + (r_1 − r_2)|∂_g v_{r_1}(x)| (an upper bound for the affine middle term on [r_2, r_1]), or choose N so that also v_{r_2}(x_n) = v_{r_2}(x) and ∂_d v_{r_2}(x_n) = ∂_d v_{r_2}(x) and use concavity at r_2: v_r(x_n) ≤ v_{r_2}(x) + (r − r_2)∂_d v_{r_2}(x) ≤ v_{r_2}(x) + (r_1 − r_2)|∂_d v_{r_2}(x)|.
issues.reason: Counterexample to the second inequality: E = F_q((π)), F algebraically closed, a ∈ F with v(a) = 11.2, x = π^5 + [a]π^{−3}, so v_r(x) = min(5r, 11.2 − 3r); with r_2 = 0.5, r_1 = 1.5 one has v_{r_1}(x) = 6.7, ∂_g v_{r_1}(x) = −3, v_{r_2}(x) = 2.5, ∂_d v_{r_2}(x) = 5, and at r = r_2 the middle term is 6.7 + 3 = 9.7 > 7.5 = v_{r_2}(x) + (r_1 − r_2)|∂_d v_{r_2}(x)|. The proof only needs some finite uniform upper bound A for v_r(x_n) on [r_2, r_1], which either repair supplies; the statement of Prop. 1.6.16 is unaffected.

issues.reason: N_n(z) = sup_{m≤n}|z_m| is not bounded by |z|_0 = q^{−v_π(z)} ≤ 1: e.g. z = [a] with |a| > 1 has |z|_0 = 1 and N_n(z) = |a|. The bound needed is N_n(z) ≤ sup_m |z_m| = |z|_1, which is finite for z ∈ B^b, and then the argument goes through unchanged. issues.locator: Lemme 1.7.2, p. 81, and Proposition 1.7.3, p. 82, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: Lemma 1.7.2 asserts |ι(f )|ρ = ‖f‖ρ̌ for ρ ∈ [0, 1], using the embedding ι : B^b_K ↪ B^b_F.
issues.correction: For ρ = q^{−r} ∈ ]0, 1[: |ι(f)|_ρ = ‖f‖_{ρ̌}^r (the two norms are equal only up to the power r = −log_q ρ; the cases ρ = 0, 1 are correct as stated). Likewise in Prop. 1.7.3, ‖f‖_ρ = |ι(f)|_{ρ̌}^{r} for ρ = q^{−r}.
issues.reason: By Lemme 1.7.1, |ι(f)|_ρ = sup_k |a_k|_ρ q^{−k} = sup_k q^{−r v_π(a_k) − k} = (sup_k q^{−v_π(a_k) − k/r})^r = ‖f‖_{ρ̌}^r, since ‖·‖ is normalized by |π_E| = q^{−1} and ρ̌ = q^{−1/r}. Concretely f = X gives |ι(X)|_ρ = |[π_F]|_ρ = q^{−1} but ‖X‖_{ρ̌} = ρ̌ = q^{−1/r}; f = π_E gives ρ = q^{−r} versus q^{−1}. The norms define the same topologies, so the topological conclusions of §§1.7.2–1.7.3 (completions, Fréchet structures) survive; the 'isometric' identifications must be read up to this power.

issues.locator: Proposition 1.7.3, démonstration, pp. 82–83, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source says the Newton polygon of π_ε equals +∞ precisely on ] − ∞, 0[. It assigns the slope ((q−1)/q^{n+1}) v(ε − 1) = 1/((q−1)q^{n+1}) to [n, n + 1], n ∈ N.
issues.correction: The two sides disagree (v(ε − 1) = v(π_F) = 1). For E = Q_p the slope on [n, n+1] is (p − 1)/p^{n+1}; for a general E|Q_p with absolute ramification index e the positive slopes of Newt([ε] − 1) are (p − 1)/(e p^m), m ≥ 1, each with multiplicity e, and in equal characteristic [ε] − 1 = [π_F] has no positive slope. The needed bound still holds: |π_ε/T − 1|_ρ < 1 as soon as −log_q ρ exceeds the first slope, which is ≤ (q − 1)/q.
issues.reason: The printed right-hand side 1/((q−1)q^{n+1}) contradicts the left-hand side (q−1)/q^{n+1} (checked in the PDF content stream: both fractions are typeset as printed). The value is also q- rather than p-based: for E = Q_p, at the zero of ϕ^{−n}(u_ε) the element (ε^{1/p^{n+1}})^♯ is a primitive p-th root of unity ζ, and |ζ − 1| = |p|^{1/(p−1)} = q^{−λ/(p−1)} with |ζ − 1| = |ε − 1|^{1/p^{n+1}} = q^{−1/p^{n+1}}, giving λ = (p−1)/p^{n+1}; for E|Q_p one has v^E_r = v^{Q_p}_{er} (|p|_ρ = ρ^e), which rescales slopes by 1/e and multiplicities by e (so for E = Q_q unramified of degree f > 1 the slopes are (p−1)/p^m, not (q−1)/q^m); in characteristic p, [ε] − 1 = [ε − 1] = [π_F]. The conclusion of Prop. 1.7.3 remains true under its hypothesis ρ > q^{−q/(q−1)}, because that hypothesis gives −log_q ρ̌ > (q−1)/q ≥ (p−1)/(ep).

issues.reviewReason: p. 83 image: 'a pour pente (q−1)/q^{n+1} v(ε−1) = 1/((q−1)q^{n+1}) sur l'intervalle [n, n+1]'. With v(ε−1) = v(π_F) = 1 the two sides differ. Independent check for E = Q_p: π_ε = Π_{m≥1} u_m, u_m = Σ_{i<p}[ε^{i/p^m}] primitive of degree 1 with u_m ≡ (ε^{1/p^m}−1)^{p−1} mod p, so Newt(u_m) has the single slope (p−1)/p^m, giving slope (p−1)/p^{n+1} on [n,n+1] (the left-hand side, for q = p). The needed bound: v_r(π_ε − T) = v_r(p·(…)) with first Teichmüller coefficient of valuation 1/p (Witt sum [1]+[π_F]), so > 1 = v_r(T) iff r > (p−1)/p ≤ (q−1)/q; the proposition's hypothesis suffices. issues.locator: §1.7.3, p. 83 (after Proposition 1.7.3), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source deduces that for I ⊂ [0, q^{−1/(q−1)}], BI describes holomorphic functions on lim_{←n,ϕ} D_{ϕ^n(I)ˇ}. It imposes boundedness near the radius |X| = 1 when 0 ∈ I (equivalently 1 ∈ Ǐ).
issues.correction: The range should be the one given by Prop. 1.7.3, I ⊂ [0, q^{−(q−1)/q}[ (for E = Q_p: I ⊂ [0, p^{−(p−1)/p}[).
issues.reason: Prop. 1.7.3 and its proof give ‖f‖ ↔ |ι(f)| only for ρ < q^{−(q−1)/q} (in the B-variable). For q ≥ 3 one has q^{−(q−1)/q} < q^{−1/(q−1)}, and the identification fails in between: for E = Q_p, p ≥ 3, ρ = p^{−r} with 1/(p−1) ≤ r < (p−1)/p, the Newton polygon of π_ε (value 1 at 0, slopes (p−1)/p, (p−1)/p², …) gives v_r(π_ε) = 1/p + r < 1 = v_r([π_F]), so |ι(X)|_ρ ≠ |[π_F]|_ρ and the annulus attached to ρ is not D_{ρ̌}. For p = 3, r = 1/2: v_r(π_ε) = 5/6.

issues.locator: Proposition 4.2.1(2), p. 156 (and its use in Proposition 4.4.5, p. 169), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source asserts the bijection L_{d,h} : m_F^d ⥲ (B_E^+)^{ϕ_E^h=π_E^d}, given by (x_0, . . . , x_{d−1}) ↦ Σ_{i=0}^{d} Σ_{n∈Z} [x_i^{q^{−nh}}] π_E^{nd+i}.
issues.correction: The sum over i must have d terms. Either Σ_{i=0}^{d−1} with arguments (x_0,…,x_{d−1}), or Σ_{i=1}^{d} with arguments (x_1,…,x_d). Proposition 4.4.5's formula (x_0,…,x_{d−1}) ↦ π^{−d}L_{d,h}(x_{d−1}^{q^{d−1}},…,x_1^{q},x_0) is correct only for the second convention (i-th argument, i = 1,…,d, weighted by π^{nd+i}); with the first convention it must read π^{−d}L_{d,h}(x_0^{q^h}, x_{d−1}^{q^{d−1}},…,x_1^{q}).
issues.reason: The printed sum involves x_d, which does not exist. The proof of Prop. 4.4.5 computes the map as Σ_{i=0}^{d−1}Σ_{n∈Z}[x_i^{q^{−nh+i}}]π^{nd−i}; rewriting nd − i = (n−1)d + (d−i) shows this equals π^{−d}Σ_{j=1}^{d}Σ_n[y_j^{q^{−nh}}]π^{nd+j} with y_d = x_0 and y_{d−i} = x_i^{q^i}, i.e. π^{−d}L_{d,h}(y_1,…,y_d) = π^{−d}L_{d,h}(x_{d−1}^{q^{d−1}},…,x_1^q,x_0) in the 1-indexed convention. (Both conventions do define bijections onto (B^+)^{ϕ^h=π^d}.)

issues.locator: Proposition 4.6.14(1), p. 187, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: Proposition 4.6.14 asserts that every bounded subset of M(A) is compact for a topological K-algebra A.
issues.correction: Every bounded subset of M(A) is relatively compact (its closure is bounded and compact); equivalently every closed bounded subset is compact.
issues.reason: The text itself notes that a subset of a bounded set is bounded, and M(A) with the weak topology is Hausdorff (distinct valuations differ on some f). For A = K⟨T⟩ (a spectral Banach algebra; M(A) is the compact Berkovich closed disc and every subset is bounded, U = the unit ball), the subset {x : |T(x)| < 1} is bounded but not closed, hence not compact. No proof is given ("On vérifie facilement").

issues.locator: Proposition 4.6.14(3), p. 188, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source describes A ↦ A^sp as right adjoint to the inclusion of spectral algebras into topological K-algebras whose spectra are countable unions of bounded sets.
issues.correction: A ↦ A^sp is a left adjoint (reflector) to the inclusion: Hom(A^sp, B) = Hom(A, B) for spectral B, with unit A → A^sp.
issues.reason: A continuous f: A → B with B spectral pulls bounded sets back to bounded sets, so ‖f(a)‖_{Ω'} = ‖a‖_{f^*Ω'} and f extends uniquely to A^sp → B: this is left adjointness. It is not a right adjoint: for B = K⟨T⟩ and A = K[ε] (ε² = 0, Banach), Hom(K⟨T⟩, K[ε]) = {T ↦ a + bε : |a| ≤ 1, b ∈ K} while Hom(K⟨T⟩, A^sp = K) = {a : |a| ≤ 1}.

issues.locator: Exemple 4.6.10, p. 186, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source defines a_{α,β} = lim_{n→+∞} (p^n choose p^n(1 − α), p^n(1 − β), p^n(α + β − 1)) and calls it a p-adic integer of valuation 1 − inf{v_p(α), v_p(β), v_p(α + β)} when p ≠ 2 and α ≠ 1 or β ≠ 1.
issues.correction: By Legendre, v_p(a_{α,β}) = (s_p(p^n(1−α)) + s_p(p^n(1−β)) + s_p(p^n(α+β−1)) − 1)/(p−1) for n large (s_p = base-p digit sum). This is always ≥ −inf{v_p(α), v_p(β), v_p(α+β)}, with equality e.g. whenever α + β = 1; there is no closed formula of the printed form.
issues.reason: Counterexamples with p odd: (α, β) = (1/p, 1 − 1/p) gives a_{α,β} = lim binom(p^n, p^{n−1}), of valuation 1 (Kummer), while the printed formula gives 1 − (−1) = 2; (α, β) = (1, 0) gives a_{α,β} = 1, of valuation 0, while the formula gives 1. issues.locator: Exemple 5.5.2.6, p. 218, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source sets rg(E , ϕ) = longOX,η (Eη ) and deg(E , ϕ) = long(coker(Φ)). For a C-morphism u : (E , ϕ) −→ (E', ϕ') that becomes an isomorphism generically, it claims deg(E', ϕ') = deg(E , ϕ) + (deg(σ) − 1) long(coker(u)) ≥ deg(E , ϕ), with equality precisely when u itself is invertible.
issues.correction: With deg = length(coker Φ) one has deg(E', φ') = deg(E, φ) − (length(σ^*coker u) − length(coker u)) ≤ deg(E, φ), where length(σ^*coker u) = deg(σ)·length(coker u) when σ induces isomorphisms on the residue fields of closed points; the HN axiom of §5.5.1 holds for deg(E, φ) := −length(coker Φ) provided moreover length(σ^*k(x)) ≥ 2 for every closed point x (true in the Breuil–Kisin case R = W(k)[[u]], k perfect, σ(u) = u^p) (and likewise deg(M, φ) := −length_R M/R·φ(M) in the reformulation over a 2-dimensional regular local ring, p. 219).
issues.reason: u ∘ Φ = Φ' ∘ σ^*u as maps σ^*E → E', all injective with finite-length cokernels, so length(coker Φ) + length(coker u) = length(coker σ^*u) + length(coker Φ') = deg(σ)·length(coker u) + length(coker Φ'). Explicit counterexample: X = Spec k[[z]], k perfect, σ = Frobenius on k with σ(z) = z^p (finite flat of degree p); E = k[[z]] with φ(x) = z^{p−1}σ(x), E' = k[[z]] with φ'(x) = σ(x), u = multiplication by z. Then u is a generic isomorphism, not an isomorphism, length(coker u) = 1, deg(E) = p − 1, deg(E') = 0 < deg(E), whereas the printed formula gives deg(E') = 2(p − 1). The equality clause also fails without a residue-field hypothesis, whatever the sign: for k of characteristic p with [k : k^p] = p, X = Spec k[[z]] and σ = Frobenius on k with σ(z) = z (finite flat of degree p), E = E' = k[[z]], φ = φ' = σ and u = multiplication by z is a generic isomorphism, not an isomorphism, with length(coker Φ) = length(coker Φ') = 0.

issues.citation: Fargues and Fontaine, "Courbes et fibrés vectoriels en théorie de Hodge p-adique", Astérisque 406 (2018)
issues.reviewReason: Page image p. 254 matches the quote. Checked independently: (i) Définition 6.2.11 normalises Π^−(b) by ϕ(Π^−(b)) = bΠ^−(b); the proof of Lemme 6.2.12 (p. 250) uses ϕ(D) = Σm(y)[ϕ(y)] with y = (ξ) ↦ (ϕ(ξ)) (consistent with ‖·‖∘ϕ = ‖·‖^q and Π^− ∈ A having support near 1), gets D' + D = ϕ(D) and hence div Π^−(b) = Σ_{n<0}ϕ^n(div b), which does not contain y. (ii) The ideal meant is {x ∈ A : ϕ^n(x) ∈ y_1⋯y_d (product of the ideals (a_i) of A) ∀n ≥ 0}; n = 0 already forces x ∈ y_1⋯y_d, so its generator must vanish at the y_i. (iii) Cyclotomic check, independent of divisor conventions: E = Q_p, Q = (1+X)^p − 1, [ε]_Q = [1+ε] − 1, u_ε = (T^p − 1)/(T − 1) with T = [(1+ε)^{1/p}] (= [1+ε^{1/p}] in characteristic p, as printed in Exemple 6.4.2); Π^−(u_ε) = T − 1 = [ε^{1/q}]_Q satisfies ϕ(T−1) = u_ε(T−1) (p. 253). θ_y(u_ε) = 0 forces θ_y(T) to be a root of 1+X+⋯+X^{p−1}, i.e. a primitive p-th root of unity ζ ≠ 1, so θ_y(T − 1) = ζ − 1 ≠ 0: Π^−(u_ε) ∉ y, hence it cannot generate an ideal contained in y. The generator is ϕ(Π^−) = u_εΠ^− = [1+ε] − 1, which is Fontaine's [25] Prop. 5.1.3 generator [ε] − 1. Correction right; kind error / affects a stated result right. Additionally the theorem needs the orbit hypothesis of Théorème 6.4.1 (recorded as E211).

issues.locator: no 6.1.3 (totally ramified change of E), p. 244, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source takes a totally ramified extension E'|E with uniformizers π_{E'}, π_E and defines the one-dimensional E-space L_{π_{E'},π_E} = {x ∈ W_{O_E}(k)_Q | ϕ(u)π_E = uπ_{E'}^{[E':E]}}. It asserts a canonical isomorphism ⊕_{d≥0} P_{E,π_E,d} ⊗_E L^{⊗d}_{π_E,π_{E'}} ⥲ P_{E',π_{E'},[E':E]•}.
issues.correction: Take L = {u ∈ W_{O_{E'}}(F̄_q)_Q : ϕ(u)π_E = uπ_{E'}^{[E':E]}}, a 1-dimensional E'-vector space, and the isomorphism ⊕_{d≥0} (P_{E,π_E,d} ⊗_E E') ⊗_{E'} L^{⊗d} ⥲ P_{E',π_{E'},[E':E]•}, x ⊗ u^{⊗d} ↦ u^d x — as in Proposition 4.1.8 (p. 155), which takes u ∈ W_{O_{E'}}(F̄_q)^×. (Also: the set is written with x but the condition with u, and the subscripts of L are swapped between the two displays.)
issues.reason: For u ∈ W_{O_E}(k)_Q = Ĕ one has ϕ(u)/u ∈ Ĕ, while π_{E'}^{[E':E]}/π_E ∈ O_{E'}^×; since E'|E is totally ramified, Ĕ ∩ E' = E inside W_{O_{E'}}(k)_Q, so the printed set is {0} unless π_{E'}^{[E':E]}/π_E ∈ E, which fails for general choices (e.g. replacing π_{E'} by π_{E'}(1 + π_{E'})). Moreover the left side of the displayed isomorphism is only an E-vector space tensored over E, while the right side is an E'-vector space containing P_{E,π_E,d} ⊗_E E'. The later use (proof of Théorème 6.5.2(2)) only needs the corrected form.

issues.locator: proof of Proposition 7.8.1, p. 273, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source proves point (1) by the method of 7.3.1 and derives point two by applying (1) to E(π^{1/2}), following the proof in 7.3.1.
issues.correction: Prove point (1) in the twisted form: for d > 1 and continuous characters ψ, χ, (B_{F̂̄}^{ϕ=π}(ψ))^{G_F} ⊗ (B_{F̂̄}^{ϕ=π^d}(χ))^{G_F} → (B_{F̂̄}^{ϕ=π^{d+1}}(ψχ))^{G_F} is surjective (same Koszul argument with two G_F-twisted sections s, t of degree 1 without common zero, using H^1(G_F, B^{ϕ=π^{d−1}}(χψ^{−1})) = 0 from Proposition 7.1.2). Then over E' = E(π^{1/2}), with P' = P_{F,E',π^{1/2}}: P'_4(χ_1χ_2) = P'_1(χ_1)·P'_3(χ_2) = P'_1(χ_1)·P'_1·P'_2(χ_2) ⊂ P'_2(χ_1)·P'_2(χ_2), which is point (2).
issues.reason: Point (1) as stated only involves the untwisted factor B_F^{ϕ=π}. Applied over E' it gives P'_4(χ_1χ_2) = P'_1·P'_1·P'_2(χ_1χ_2) ⊂ P'_2·P'_2(χ_1χ_2), i.e. point (2) for the pair (1, χ_1χ_2), not for (χ_1, χ_2): nothing in (1) moves the character χ_1 onto a separate factor. In the proof of 7.3.1 all characters are trivial, so the same trick works there but does not transfer. The fix is routine, but the step as written does not follow.

issues.locator: proof of Proposition 7.9.1, p. 276, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source handles π/[b] by considering π/(L(εb^{−1/p^n})/L(ε))^{p^n} for n ≫ 0.
issues.reason: By formula (2), L(εb^{−1/p^n})/L(ε) = [b^{−1/p^n}](1 + v) with ‖v‖_I ≤ α, so its p^n-th power is ≈ [b^{−1}] = 1/[b]. Hence π·(…)^{p^n} ≈ π/[b] and lies in B_e (its only denominator is t^{p^n} = L(ε)^{p^n}), whereas the printed π/(…)^{p^n} ≈ π[b] (the wrong element) and has denominator L(εb^{−1/p^n})^{p^n}, which is not a power of t, so it is not in B_e. Compare the parallel treatment of [a]/π via (1/π)(L(εa^{1/p^n})/L(ε))^{p^n}. The printed '/' was checked in the PDF content stream.

issues.locator: §7.5 and proof of Proposition 7.5.1, p. 269, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source takes a finite degree extension E'|E and uses B_{E'} = B_E ⊗_E E' to claim M(Y_{E'}) = M(Y_E) ⊗_E E', hence M(Y_{E'}/ϕ^Z) = M(Y_E/ϕ^Z) ⊗_E E'.
issues.correction: B_{E'} = B_E ⊗_{E'_0} E' with E'_0 the maximal unramified subextension (§1.6.2), so B_{E'} = B_E ⊗_E E' only for E'|E totally ramified. For the unramified part (which needs F_{q'} ⊂ F) B_{E'} = B_E with ϕ_{E'} = ϕ_E^{[E'_0:E]}, and M(Y_{E'}/ϕ^Z) = M(Y_E)^{ϕ^f = Id} = M(Y_E/ϕ^Z) ⊗_E E'_0 must be obtained by Galois descent (Hilbert 90 as in Proposition 4.1.7), not from a tensor identity for B.
issues.reason: By the paper's own §1.6.2 (pp. 70–71): 'lorsque E'|E est non-ramifiée, B_{E,I} = B_{E',I} mais ϕ_{E'} = ϕ_E^{[E':E]}'. If E'|E is unramified of degree f > 1 and F ⊃ F_{q^f}, then E' ⊂ W_{O_E}(F)_Q ⊂ B_E, so B_E ⊗_E E' ≅ B_E^f is not a domain and M(Y_E) ⊗_E E' ≅ M(Y_E)^f is not a field, contradicting B_{E'} = B_E and M(Y_{E'}) = M(Y_E). The final identity for ϕ-invariants and Proposition 7.5.1 remain true, but the step (and the equality B_{E'}/(ξ) = B_E/(ξ) ⊗_E E' used next in the proof) needs this reduction.

issues.locator: §7.8 (definition of ϕ-Mod_B), p. 271, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)

issues.correction: … et ϕ un isomorphisme ϕ-linéaire de M (i.e. ϕ-linear with ϕ^*M → M bijective), as in the definition of ϕ-Mod_A in Chapter 11 (p. 356: 'ϕ : M ⥲ M un isomorphisme ϕ_E-linéaire').

issues.locator: Proposition 10.1.1, proof, p. 314, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source places θ(t') in H^0(G_K, C(χ^{−1})) and invokes Tate ([60]) for its vanishing when χ has infinite order. It then concludes t' ∈ ker θ, so t' is a Q_p-multiple of t and x = ∞. It next assumes, for a contradiction, that χ has finite order.
issues.correction: Split according to whether χ(I_K) is infinite or finite. If χ(I_K) is infinite, Tate gives H^0(G_K, C(χ^{−1})) = 0 and the argument goes through. If χ(I_K) is finite, choose K'|K finite with χ|_{I_{K'}} = 1 and run the second argument with G_{K'} replaced by the inertia group I_{K'} = Gal(K̄|K'^{nr}): ε' ∈ (1+m_F)^{I_{K'}} ⊂ F^{I_{K'}} = (K̂'^{nr})^♭ = k̄_K, contradicting 0 < |1−ε'| < 1 (K̂'^{nr} is still discretely valued).
issues.reason: Tate's vanishing C(χ)^{G_K} = 0 requires χ(I_K) infinite (so stated in the atlas node PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tate-sen-theorem), not merely χ of infinite order. When k_K is finite, an unramified χ with χ(Frob) = u ∈ Z_p^× of infinite order has H^0(G_K, C(χ^{−1})) ⊇ {c ∈ K̂^{nr} : Frob(c) = uc} ≠ 0 (Lang's theorem on O_{K̂^{nr}}^×), so the first case does not conclude, and such χ is not of finite order, so the second case does not apply. The statement of Prop. 10.1.1 is unaffected (it follows from the corrected case split).

issues.locator: Proposition 10.6.18(2), p. 350, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: Part 2 asserts that, when (d, h) ≠ (1, 1), the Bloch-Kato exponential δ : K −→ H^1(G_K, χ^d_{LT_h}) is an isomorphism.
issues.correction: 2. Si (d, h) ≠ (1, 1), l'exponentielle de Bloch-Kato δ : K −→ H^1_g(G_K, χ^d_{LT_h}) est un isomorphisme (which is what the following sentence 'toute Q_{p^h}-représentation … de de Rham … est cristalline' asserts).
issues.reason: Prop. 10.6.17(2) gives ker(u_*) = 0, i.e. (by the corrected display of p. 349) δ: K ≅ H^1_g; it says nothing about ker(θ_*) = coker(δ: K → H^1). For h ≥ 2 the printed statement is false: take K = K̂_0^{nr} = W(F̄_p)[1/p] (algebraically closed residue field, K ⊃ Q_{p^2}), h = 2, d = 1, V = χ_{LT_2}. Since V^{I} = 0 for the inertia group I = G_K of K' = Q_{p^2}, inflation–restriction embeds H^1(G_{K'}, V), of Q_p-dimension ≥ [K':Q_p]·dim_{Q_p} V = 4 by Tate's Euler characteristic formula, into H^1(G_K, V)^{Frob}; if δ: K → H^1(G_K, V) were a (Frobenius-equivariant) isomorphism, H^1(G_K, V)^{Frob} ≅ K^{Frob} = Q_{p^2} would have Q_p-dimension 2.

issues.reviewReason: p. 350 image: '2. Si (d,h) ≠ (1,1), l'exponentielle de Bloch-Kato δ : K → H^1(G_K, χ^d_{LT_h}) est un isomorphisme. En d'autres termes, toute Q_{p^h}-représentation … de de Rham … est cristalline.'
