issues.locator: no 10.6.5.4, pp. 352–353, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The proof deduces surjectivity of exp^*_V from the perfect pairings and injectivity of exp_{V^*(1)}. It also claims that weak admissibility of (D^*, ϕ, Fil^•D^*_K), applied to the sub-isocrystal (D^*)^{ϕ=p} ⊗_{Q_p} K_0 of D^*, gives Fil^1(D^*)^{ϕ=p} = (D^*)^{ϕ=p}.
issues.correction: The equality Fil^1(D^*)^{ϕ=p} = (D^*)^{ϕ=p} (equivalently injectivity of exp_{V^*(1)}, surjectivity of exp^*_V and dim H^2(G_K,V) = dim D^{ϕ=p^{−1}}) does not follow from weak admissibility and fails for some filtrations allowed by 'Soit donc Fil^•D_K une telle filtration'. It holds if, when the slope is −1, one chooses Fil^•D_K with all jumps equal to −1 (Fil^{−1}D_K = D_K, Fil^0D_K = 0; weakly admissible since t_H = t_N for every sub-isocrystal), so that Fil^1D^*_K = (Fil^0D_K)^⊥ = D^*_K; for slope ≠ −1 both sides are 0.
issues.reason: Weak admissibility only gives t_H(D'_K) ≤ t_N(D') for sub-isocrystals D' (an upper bound), whereas Fil^1D'_K = D'_K needs all jumps of D'_K to be ≥ 1. Counterexample: K = Q_p(√p) (K_0 = Q_p), D = Q_p^2 with ϕ = p^{−1}·Id (isoclinic of slope −1), Fil^{−2}D_K = D_K ⊋ Fil^{−1} = Fil^0 = K·(1, √p) ⊋ Fil^1 = 0. Every sub-isocrystal is a line ℓ = Q_p·w, ℓ_K ∩ Fil^0 = 0, so t_H(ℓ) = −2 ≤ −1 = t_N(ℓ) and t_H(D) = −2 = t_N(D): weakly admissible, with Fil^iD_K = 0 for i > 0. But (D^*)^{ϕ=p} = Q_p^2 and Fil^1D^*_K = (Fil^0D_K)^⊥ = K·(√p, −1) meets Q_p^2 only in 0. Accordingly H^2(G_K,V) = H^0(G_K,V^*(1))^∨ = 0 while dim D^{ϕ=p^{−1}} = 2; dim H^1(G_K,V) = [K:Q_p]·2 = 4 = dim(D^{ϕ=p^{−1}} ⊕ D_K/Fil^0D_K), so α is an isomorphism, β = exp^*_V = 0 is not surjective onto Fil^0D_K ≅ K, and exp_{V^*(1)} is not injective. Prop. 10.6.16 itself is proved independently via Prop. 10.6.17.

issues.citation: Fargues and Fontaine, "Courbes et fibrés vectoriels en théorie de Hodge p-adique", Astérisque 406 (2018)
issues.reviewReason: pp. 352–353 images: 'La perfection des accouplement précédents couplée à l'injectivité de exp_{V^*(1)} montrent que exp^*_V est surjectif' and 'Utilisant la faible admissibilité de (D^*, φ, Fil^•D^*_K) appliquée au sous-isocristal (D^*)^{φ=p} ⊗_{Q_p} K_0 de D^* on vérifie que Fil^1(D^*)^{φ=p} = (D^*)^{φ=p}'. Weak admissibility only bounds t_H of sub-isocrystals from above; D's jumps are ≤ 0 so D^*'s are ≥ 0, which does not force jumps ≥ 1. I rechecked the counterexample: K = Q_p(√p) (K_0 = Q_p), D = Q_p^2, φ = p^{−1}·Id, Fil^{−2} = D_K ⊋ Fil^{−1} = Fil^0 = K(1,√p) ⊋ Fil^1 = 0; t_H(D) = −2 = t_N(D), each sub-isocrystal is a line Q_p·w with Kw ≠ K(1,√p) (√p ∉ Q_p), so t_H = −2 < −1 = t_N: weakly admissible, and it satisfies Lemme 10.6.20's conclusion. D^* has φ = p·Id, (D^*)^{φ=p} = Q_p^2, Fil^1D^*_K = (Fil^0D_K)^⊥ = K(√p, −1), which meets Q_p^2 in 0. So H^2(G_K,V) = H^0(G_K,V^*(1)) = 0, dim H^1(G_K,V) = 4 = dim D^{φ=p^{−1}} + dim_{Q_p} D_K/Fil^0 D_K, α (injective) is an isomorphism, β = exp^*_V = 0 is not onto Fil^0D_K ≅ K; consistently exp_{V^*(1)} = 0. The fix (all jumps −1 when the slope is −1) is weakly admissible (t_H(D') = −dim D' = t_N(D') for all D') and gives Fil^1D^*_K = D^*_K. Prop. 10.6.16 still holds (the map into H^1_g is an isomorphism in the example). Error in the alternative proof, affects the proof. Checked on the page image.

issues.locator: Proof of Lemme 11.1.6 (second assertion: k_F arbitrary, λ ≠ μ), p. 362, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The proof uses B(λ)^∨ = B(−λ) and claims that B(−λ) ⊗ B(µ) decomposes into ϕ-modules each isomorphic to B(µ − λ). It therefore reduces the task to H^1(B(ν)) = 0 for every ν ∈ Q.
issues.correction: For arbitrary k_F, B(−λ) ⊗ B(µ) is only isoclinic of slope µ − λ (a twisted form of a sum of B(µ−λ)); one should prove H^1 = 0 for every ϕ-module of the form D ⊗_L B(ν) with D isoclinic of slope 0 and ν ≠ 0 — which the d > 0 and d < 0 arguments give verbatim, and which is exactly the generalisation (5) the authors state in the proof of Théorème 11.1.8.
issues.reason: Take k_F = F_q (so L = E and φ_E is the identity on E), λ = −1/2, µ = 1/2. On L(1/2) ⊗ L(1/2) = E^4 the E-linear φ is M ⊗ M with M = [[0,π],[1,0]]; (M⊗M)^2 = π^2 and tr(M⊗M) = (tr M)^2 = 0, so L(1/2) ⊗ L(1/2) ≅ (E, π)^2 ⊕ (E, −π)^2 and ℬ(1/2) ⊗ ℬ(1/2) ≅ ℬ(1)^2 ⊕ (ℬ, −πφ)^2. But (ℬ, −πφ) ≇ ℬ(1) = (ℬ, πφ): reducing an isomorphism to the residue field L = E would give u ∈ E^× with −πu = πφ(u) = πu. So the asserted decomposition fails; the conclusion of the lemma is still true.

issues.reviewReason: p. 362 image: quote exact. Checked the counterexample: k_F = F_q, L = E with trivial φ_E, L(1/2) has matrix M = [[0,π],[1,0]], M⊗M squares to π² and has trace 0, so it is diag(π,π,−π,−π); (ℬ,−πφ) ≇ ℬ(1) because an isomorphism u would reduce to ū ∈ E^× with −ū = ū. So ℬ(1/2) ⊗ ℬ(1/2) is not a sum of ℬ(1). The conclusion survives: every isoclinic V of slope ν is a direct summand of (V ⊗ L(−ν)) ⊗ L(ν) = D ⊗ L(ν) with D of slope 0 (trace splitting of 1 → End L(ν)), and H^1(D ⊗ ℬ(ν)) = 0 for ν ≠ 0 by the printed d > 0 / d < 0 arguments using a φ-stable lattice of D. Error in the proof, correctly classified.

issues.locator: Proof of Théorème 11.1.8 (k_F not necessarily algebraically closed), p. 365, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source identifies D_λ = End(B(−λ)) = End(L(−λ)) as the division algebra over E with invariant λ. It then asserts the canonical isomorphism of ϕ-modules over B given by M ⥲ Hom_{D_λ⊗B}(B(−λ), M ⊗ B(−λ)).
issues.correction: Both claims need F_{q^h} ⊂ k_F (in particular they hold for k_F algebraically closed, where D_λ ⊗_E L ≅ M_h(L) and Morita theory applies). For general k_F the Morita step must be replaced, e.g. by first extending scalars to a field containing F_{q^h} and descending, or by working with the isoclinic slope-λ part directly.
issues.reason: Let k_F = F_q, λ = d/h with h ≥ 2 (e.g. λ = 1/2). Then L = E, φ_E is trivial on E, and L(−λ) = E^h with E-linear φ the companion matrix C of x^h − π^{−d}; End(L(−λ)) = E[C] ≅ E[x]/(x^h − π^{−d}), a commutative field of degree h (totally ramified since (d,h) = 1), not the central division algebra of invariant λ (dimension h^2). Moreover ℬ(−λ) is free of rank one over D_λ ⊗_E ℬ = ℬ[C], so Hom_{D_λ⊗ℬ}(ℬ(−λ), M ⊗ ℬ(−λ)) ≅ M ⊗_ℬ ℬ(−λ) has ℬ-rank nh ≠ n = rank M; the claimed isomorphism with M is false. The theorem itself (every φ-module over B^+ comes from an isocrystal) is not contradicted.

issues.locator: Proof of Théorème 11.1.8, p. 365 (filtration of M ⊗ B(−λ)), author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The source takes isoclinic isocrystals (U_i)_{1≤i≤r} whose slopes increase strictly with i. It claims Hom(U_i ⊗_L B, U_j ⊗_L B) = 0 for i > j, and concludes that the action preserves Fil^• = ⊕_{i≥•} U_i ⊗_L B.
issues.correction: With slopes increasing in i, Hom(U_i ⊗_L B, U_j ⊗_L B) = 0 when i < j, and the D_λ-stable filtration is Fil_• = ⊕_{i≤•} U_i ⊗_L B (equivalently keep 'i > j' and ⊕_{i≥•} but order the slopes decreasingly).
issues.reason: Hom(U_i ⊗ B, U_j ⊗ B) = H^0(U_i^∨ ⊗ U_j ⊗ B) is H^0 of a module isoclinic of slope µ_j − µ_i. Here B is the ring ℬ = B^{b,+}/𝔭 of §11.1. With the chapter's convention A(n) = (A, π^nφ), H^0(ℬ(n)) = ℬ^{φ=π^{−n}}: it vanishes for n > 0 (H^0(ℬ(n)) = H^0(B^+(n)) by Proposition 11.1.3, and (B^+)^{φ=π^{−n}} = 0) but H^0(ℬ(−1)) = ℬ^{φ=π} ≅ P_1 ≠ 0 (§11.1.2). So Hom(ℬ(1), ℬ(0)) ≠ 0, i.e. nonzero maps go from larger to smaller slopes, and for µ_i > µ_j (i > j) the Hom need not vanish. The argument only needs some D_λ-stable filtration with graded pieces U_i ⊗ B, which the corrected filtration provides.

issues.locator: Proof of Proposition 11.2.7, p. 371, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The proof assumes I ⊄ J, J ⊄ I and sup(I) < sup(J), and uses lemma 11.2.6 to write f = a + b, a ∈ B_{I^+}, b ∈ B_{I^−}. From B_{I^−} ⊂ B_{I∪J} it deduces a ∈ B_{I^+} ∩ B_J. It then cites proposition 1.6.23 for B_{I^+} ∩ B_J ⊂ B_{I∪J}.
issues.correction: Puisque B_{I^+} ⊂ B_{I∪J} on a donc b ∈ B_{I^−} ∩ B_J. Mais d’après la proposition 1.6.23 on a B_{I^−} ∩ B_J ⊂ B_{I∪J}.
issues.reason: B_K ⊂ B_{K'} iff K' ⊂ K (the text itself uses B_I ⊂ B_{I∩J}). Under the stated normalisation inf I < inf J ≤ sup I < sup J, one has I ∪ J = [inf I, sup J] ⊄ [0, sup I] = I^−, so B_{I^−} ⊄ B_{I∪J}, whereas I ∪ J ⊂ [inf I, 1] = I^+. Also Proposition 1.6.23 describes B_K for 0 ∈ K (1 ∉ K), which applies to I^−, not to I^+. With the roles of a and b interchanged the argument is correct.

issues.locator: Lemme 11.2.10, statement and proof, p. 372, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The lemma takes Banach E-algebras B_1, B_2, A with maps B_1 → A and B_2 → A inducing a surjection B_1 ⊕ B_2 → A. For Z ∈ GL_n(A), it asserts that some identity neighbourhood in GL_n(A) consists of matrices XZYZ^{−1}, where X ∈ GL_n(B_1) and Y ∈ GL_n(B_2).
issues.correction: Add the hypothesis that the tangent map M_n(B_1) ⊕ M_n(B_2) → M_n(A), (U, V) ↦ U + ZVZ^{−1}, is surjective (true for Z = 1, and in the application of Proposition 11.2.12 because Z = Z'DZ'' with Z', Z'' ∈ GL_n(B_{I_1∪I_2}) and every ratio of diagonal entries of D is a unit of B_{I_1∩I_2} factoring as w_1w_2, w_i ∈ B_{I_i}^×, so B_1 + (d_i/d_j)B_2 = w_1(B_1 + B_2) = A). The proof's appeal to Lemme 11.2.11 silently uses this surjectivity.
issues.reason: Counterexample: A = E⟨T, T^{−1}⟩, B_1 = E⟨T⟩, B_2 = E⟨T^{−1}⟩ (B_1 ⊕ B_2 → A surjective), Z = diag(T, T^{−1}). For ε ∈ E^×, Z_ε = [[T, 0],[ε, T^{−1}]] satisfies L Z_ε R = [[0, −1/ε],[ε, 0]] with L = [[1, −T/ε],[0, 1]] ∈ GL_2(B_1), R = [[1, −T^{−1}/ε],[0, 1]] ∈ GL_2(B_2), so Z_ε ∈ GL_2(B_1)GL_2(B_2). But Z ∉ GL_2(B_1)GL_2(B_2): if X^{−1}Z = Y with X^{−1} = [[a,b],[c,d]] over B_1, then aT, cT ∈ B_2 ∩ T·B_1 = 0 forces a = c = 0, contradicting invertibility. Hence Z_εZ^{−1} → 1 as ε → 0 but Z_εZ^{−1} ∉ GL_2(B_1)·Z·GL_2(B_2)·Z^{−1}. (Tangent map: the (2,1)-entry of its image is B_1 + T^{−2}B_2, which misses T^{−1}.)

issues.locator: Proof of Proposition 11.2.12, pp. 373–374, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The proof invokes density of B_{I_1∪I_2} in B_{I_1∩I_2} to choose Z ∈ M_n(B_{I_1∪I_2}) ∩ GL_n(B_{I_1∩I_2}), making UZ^{−1} arbitrarily near the identity of GL_n(B_{I_1∩I_2}). Using proposition 11.2.7 and lemma 11.2.10, it claims X ∈ GL_n(B_{I_1}) and Y ∈ GL_n(B_{I_2}) exist with UZ^{−1} = XZYZ^{−1}.
issues.correction: One needs a neighbourhood in Lemme 11.2.10 that is uniform for all Z close to U (or a different route, e.g. Kedlaya's: approximate U on one side by a matrix invertible over the bounded ring so that the remaining factor is close to 1, then use the Z = 1 factorisation; cf. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/matrix-approximation-and-factorization). The proposition itself is true (Kiehl-type gluing).
issues.reason: The neighbourhood produced by Lemme 11.2.10 depends on Z (through ‖Z‖, ‖Z^{−1}‖ and the norm of a section of (U,V) ↦ U + ZVZ^{−1}, which here depends on the factorisation of the units d_i/d_j of the Smith form of Z), while Z is chosen after, and depending on, how close UZ^{−1} must be to 1. No bound uniform in Z is given, so 'aussi proche que l’on veut' does not ensure that UZ^{−1} lies in the neighbourhood attached to Z; uniformity would follow from surjectivity of the tangent map at U itself, which is equivalent to what is being proved.

issues.locator: Proof of Proposition 11.2.24, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017)
issues.printed: The proof takes λ = d/h, (d, h) = 1, as the largest Dieudonné-Manin slope of (V̂, ϕ), and claims a lattice Λ ⊂ V exists with ϕ^h(Λ) ⊂ π^dΛ. It makes (V, ϕ) an extension of ⊕_i E^†(µ_i) by E^†(λ)^r, r ≥ 1, with µ_i < λ for every i. It reduces Ext^1(E^†(µ), E^†(λ)) = 0 for λ > µ to vanishing of the cokernel of Id − π^{−d}ϕ^h : E^† → E^† when d > 0 and h ≥ 1.
issues.correction: λ must be the SMALLEST slope; then µ_i > λ for all i, and one needs Ext^1(E^†(µ), E^†(λ)) = 0 for µ > λ, which reduces to coker(Id − π^{−d}ϕ^h) = 0 with d/h = µ − λ > 0 (as displayed). Even so corrected the argument does not close: the step through Lemme 11.2.25 fails for non-bijective φ, and Proposition 11.2.24 itself is false as stated (see the separate issues on Lemme 11.2.25 and Proposition 11.2.24).
issues.reason: (i) A lattice with ϕ^h(Λ) ⊂ π^dΛ forces every slope to be ≥ d/h, so λ is the smallest slope (as in the parallel proofs of Théorèmes 11.1.7 and 11.1.8). (ii) With the chapter's convention (E^†(n) = (E^†, π^nϕ)), Ext^1(E^†(µ), E^†(λ)) = H^1(E^†(λ−µ)) = coker(Id − π^{d'}ϕ^{h'}) with λ − µ = d'/h'; the displayed map Id − π^{−d}ϕ^h is the case λ − µ < 0. (iii) The printed claim is false: for F algebraically closed, 0 < |ϖ| < 1, Ext^1(E^†(0), E^†(1)) = coker(Id − πϕ on E^†) ∋ [ϖ^{−1}] is nonzero, since the unique solution in ℰ of y − πϕ(y) = [ϖ^{−1}] is y = Σ_{k≥0} π^k[ϖ^{−q^k}], and sup_k |ϖ|^{−q^k}ρ^k = ∞ for every ρ > 0, so y ∉ E^†.

issues.locator: Lemme 1.6.8, p. 71, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017); page image checked
issues.printed: The source takes ρ ∈ [0, 1] and asserts |.|_{E′,ρ^{1/e_{E′|E}}} = |.|_{E,ρ} ⊗ |.|_{E′,ρ^{1/e_{E′/E}}}. Its proof calls the case ρ = 0 immediate.

issues.reason: By Déf. 1.4.7, |·|_{E,0} = q^{−v_{π_E}} and |·|_{E′,0} = q′^{−v_{π_{E′}}} with q′ = q^f and π_E = unit·π_{E′}^e. For x = π_E: |π_E|_{E′,0} = q^{−ef} while |π_E|_{E,0} = q^{−1}, so the equality fails whenever [E′:E] > 1 (and the tensor product of |·|_{E,0} with |·|_{E′,0} is not even defined, the two disagreeing on E′_0 ∋ π_E). For ρ ∈ ]0,1[ the formula is consistent (|π_E| = ρ on both sides) provided the same absolute value on F is used for E and E′ (§1.1 writes |·| = q^{−v} with q = q_E, which would change it to |·|^f for E′). Classified as an error in a stated result for consistency with E43 (the printed equality of norms in the statement is false at ρ = 0 when [E′:E] > 1), though only a normalization: the norms are equivalent and nothing downstream (Prop. 1.6.9, which uses only the topology) is affected.

issues.locator: Théorème 2.5.1 (2), p. 128, and Théorème 3.5.1 (2), p. 145, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017); page image checked
issues.printed: The source states that otherwise B_I is a principal ideal ring with |Y_I| ⥲ Spm(B_{I∖{0}}). Theorem 3.5.1 (2) likewise asserts |Y_{F,I}| ⥲ Spm(B_{I∖{0}}).
issues.correction: |Y_{I∖{0}}| (= |Y_I|) ⥲ Spm(B_I): the index I∖{0} belongs on Y, not on B.
issues.reason: For 0 ∉ I the two readings agree. For I = [0, ρ] (compact, 0 ∈ I, not {0}), B_{I∖{0}} = B_{]0,ρ]} has maximal ideals that are not of the form ker θ_y: take z_i ∈ m_F with v(z_i) → +∞ and pairwise distinct points y_i = ([z_i] − π) ∈ |Y_{]0,ρ]}| (‖y_i‖ = |z_i| ≤ ρ for i large), and f_n = ∏_{i≥n}(1 − [z_i]/π) ∈ B^+ ⊂ B_{]0,ρ]} (§2.6), with div(f_n) = Σ_{i≥n}[y_i] (Prop. 2.7.3). Since f_n = (1 − [z_n]/π)f_{n+1}, J = ∪_n B_{]0,ρ]}f_n is an ideal; it is proper (f_n(y_n) = 0, so no f_n is a unit), so lies in a maximal ideal m; if m = ker θ_y then f_n(y) = 0 for all n, i.e. y ∈ {y_i : i ≥ n} for all n, impossible. So |Y_I| → Spm(B_{I∖{0}}) is not surjective. What the proofs give (Thm 2.4.10 and Lemme 2.5.2, cf. Thm 2.5.3 and Cor. 2.5.4) is that the non-zero primes of the PID B_I are the ker θ_y, y ∈ |Y_{I∖{0}}|.

issues.locator: Proposition 11.2.24, statement, p. 378, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017); page image checked
issues.printed: The source asserts that completion ϕ-Mod_{E†} −→ ϕ-Mod_ℰ is an equivalence of categories, and therefore applies Dieudonné-Manin classification to ϕ-Mod_{E†}.
issues.correction: Only a filtration descends (Kedlaya [45] Prop. 5.11): every (V, ϕ) ∈ ϕ-Mod_{E†} has a unique filtration by saturated sub-ϕ-modules with isoclinic graded pieces of strictly decreasing Dieudonné–Manin slopes (each a direct sum of E†(λ) when F is algebraically closed). The completion functor is essentially surjective and an equivalence on isoclinic objects, but not fully faithful, and ϕ-modules over E† are not in general direct sums of E†(λ).
issues.reason: Let c ∈ F with |c| > 1 (any F, e.g. algebraically closed) and V = E†e_1 ⊕ E†e_2 with ϕ(e_1) = e_1 + [c]e_2, ϕ(e_2) = πe_2 (matrix of determinant π, so V ∈ ϕ-Mod_{E†}). A fixed vector xe_1 + ye_2 needs ϕ(x) = x, so x ∈ E, and y − πϕ(y) = [c]x. In ℰ, Id − πϕ is injective (π-adic valuation) and the solution for x = 1 is ŷ = Σ_{k≥0} π^k[c^{q^k}]. Since |c^{q^k}|ρ^k → ∞ for every ρ > 0, ŷ ∉ E† (Prop. 1.6.23). So V^{ϕ=Id} = 0, whereas V̂ = ℰ(e_1 + ŷe_2) ⊕ ℰe_2 ≅ ℰ(0) ⊕ ℰ(1) has a fixed vector. Hence Hom(E†(0), V) = 0 → Hom(ℰ(0), V̂) ≅ E is not surjective (completion is not full), and V ≇ E†(0) ⊕ E†(1), the only candidate sum of standard objects with those slopes, which would have fixed vectors. Equivalently, the class of [c] in Ext^1(E†(0), E†(1)) = coker(Id − πϕ on E†) is nonzero (cf. E183 (iii)). Kedlaya [45], §5.3 (arXiv math/0110124), says explicitly that the Dieudonné–Manin classification 'does not descend to Γ_con in general'; his Prop. 5.11 is the descending filtration and Cor. 5.12 the isoclinic case. The later uses in §11.4 (essential surjectivity of ϕ-Mod_{E†} → ϕ-Mod_ℛ, isoclinic equivalence) survive with the corrected form.

issues.locator: Lemme 11.2.25, statement and proof (equation (7)), p. 379, author copy courbe.pdf (16 avril 2017); page image checked
issues.printed: The source takes a finite-rank free O_{E†}-module Λ with a semilinear endomorphism ϕ and asserts a bijection Λ^{ϕ=Id} ⥲ Λ̂^{ϕ=Id}. It subsequently chooses X ∈ O_ℰ^n satisfying (7) ϕ(X) = AX.
issues.correction: Assume ϕ bijective on Λ (matrix A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†})). Then a fixed vector satisfies X = Aϕ(X), i.e. ϕ(X) = A^{−1}X, and the printed argument applies to A^{−1} (after rescaling the basis so that A^{−1} mod π ∈ M_n(O_F)).
issues.reason: With A the matrix of ϕ (ϕ(e_j) = Σ_i a_ij e_i, as on p. 360), ϕ(Σx_je_j) = Σ_j x_je_j means Aϕ(X) = X, not (7); with the correct equation the estimate becomes ‖X‖_{k,ρ_0^q} ≤ ‖X‖_{k,ρ_0}^q, which bounds nothing. The statement is false: Λ = O_{E†}e_1 ⊕ O_{E†}e_2, ϕ(e_1) = e_1 + [c]e_2, ϕ(e_2) = πe_2, c ∈ F with |c| > 1. In Λ̂, e_1 + (Σ_{k≥0} π^k[c^{q^k}])e_2 is ϕ-fixed. In Λ, a fixed vector xe_1 + ye_2 has x ∈ O_E and y = [c]x + πϕ(y), whose only solution in O_ℰ is x·Σπ^k[c^{q^k}], not in O_{E†} unless x = 0, and then y = πϕ(y) forces y = 0. So Λ^{ϕ=Id} = 0 ≠ Λ̂^{ϕ=Id} ≅ O_E. Here ϕ is injective but not bijective (det A = π). The lemma is applied in Proposition 11.2.24 to π^{−d}ϕ^h, which is not bijective in general, and this is where that proof breaks (the same V is a counterexample to the proposition).

issues.locator: Chapter I, §I.10, Theorem I.10.1, p. 37, first sentence (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The assertion requires the order of π_0 Z(G) to be indivisible by ℓ, and takes a small stable ∞-category C that is Λ-linear. It equates two data: an exact monoidal functor Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(C)^{BW_E^I}, linear over Rep_Λ(Q^I) and functorial in the finite set I; and an action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)_Λ/Ĝ) that is Λ-linear and compactly supported.
issues.correction: Let C be a small idempotent-complete Λ-linear stable ∞-category (as in Theorem X.0.1).
issues.reason: Theorem X.0.1 (p. 339), its discretized form Theorem X.0.2 (p. 340) and the rational Theorem X.1.1 (p. 341) all assume C idempotent-complete. The proof of X.1.1 begins 'for any L-linear idempotent-complete small stable ∞-category C, giving an exact L-linear functor Rep_L((H ⋊ Q)^I) → C is equivalent to giving an exact L-linear functor … Perf((H ⋊ Q)^I) → C'. The integral case uses that Perf(Z¹/Ĝ) is generated by Rep(Ĝ) only under cones and retracts (Theorem VIII.5.1). Without the hypothesis the printed equivalence is false. Example: G = 𝔾_m, q ≥ 3, and Λ containing μ_{q−1} with ℓ ∤ q − 1. Then Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ) = Hom(E^×/(1 + 𝔪_E), 𝔾_m) ≅ 𝔾_m × μ_{q−1} is a disjoint union of q − 1 copies of 𝔾_{m,Λ}, with trivial Ĝ-action. Let D = Perf(Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)/Ĝ) with its tautological action. Let C ⊂ D be the full subcategory of objects whose K_0-class lies in the image H of K_0(Rep Ĝ). By Thomason's theorem C is a dense stable subcategory. H is a subring containing every class [V ⊗ 𝒪], so the exact monoidal functors Rep(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I → End_Λ(D)^{BW_E^I} given by the tautological action preserve C and restrict to such functors for C. Suppose a compactly supported action of Perf(Z¹(W_E, Ĝ)/Ĝ) on C induced these restricted functors. It would extend to the idempotent completion D, and by the uniqueness in Theorem X.0.1 it would be the tautological action. Then 𝒪_{Z_0} = 𝒪_{Z_0} ⊗ 𝒪, for a connected component Z_0, would lie in C. It does not, because every class in H has the same rank on all q − 1 components while [𝒪_{Z_0}] does not. So these functors on C come from no action, contrary to the printed equivalence. Every application in the paper is to D_lis(Bun_G, Λ)^ω, which is idempotent-complete, so nothing downstream is affected.

issues.printed: For point (i), the proof takes X = X_2 ×_{X_1} X_3 and maps f_i : U_i → X_i. It claims local spatiality for the diamond U = (U_1 ×_{X_2} U_2) ×_{U_2} (U_2 ×_{X_2} U_3), citing representability of ∆_{X_2} by locally spatial diamonds.

issues.reason: With X = X_2 ×_{X_1} X_3 the maps are X_2 → X_1 ← X_3, so there is no map U_1 → X_2 and U_1 ×_{X_2} U_2 is undefined. issues.citation: Fargues and Scholze, "Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence" (arXiv:2102.13459)
issues.reviewReason: Checked in the TeX of the proof of Proposition VI.3.1 (p. 203): 'Bijectivity … on geometric points follows from the Iwahori decomposition.' Neither the Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition nor the Iwahori factorisation of a compact open subgroup gives this. Anschütz–Gleason–Lourenço–Richarz (arXiv:2201.01234, proof of their Theorem 5.2) cite FS Proposition VI.3.1 and prove the analogous bijectivity by the Iwasawa decomposition. Kind misprint and affects nothing both stand.

issues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.2.2.2, Proposition VIII.2.11(ii) (p. 284), its proof and the following paragraph (p. 285) (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: Item (ii) asserts that, for n = f_{E′/E} and W_{E′} = ker(W_E → Out(Ĝ)), ℓ does not divide q^{en} − 1 for any exponent e of Ĝ. The proof describes m homogeneous polynomials whose degrees are root-system exponents, identifies the largest exponent of Ĝ with the Coxeter number h of G, and gives ℓ > q^{hn} − 1 as a sufficient condition.
issues.correction: Replace 'exponent' by 'degree' (degree of a basic invariant polynomial, d_i = m_i + 1) throughout: (ii) should read 'q^{dn} − 1 is not divisible by ℓ for any degree d of a fundamental invariant of Ĝ'. The largest degree is h, which is consistent with the rest of the paragraph.
issues.reason: The proof needs, for each basic invariant P_i of degree d_i, that P_i(v) = P_i(q^n v) = q^{n d_i} P_i(v) forces P_i(v) = 0, i.e. that q^{n d_i} − 1 is a unit in L. The proof itself says the invariants have 'degrees the exponents'. The claim 'supremum of the exponents = Coxeter number h' also holds only for degrees, since standard exponents m_i = d_i − 1 have maximum h − 1. So the paper consistently uses 'exponent' to mean 'degree', which is not the standard meaning. Read with standard exponents, (ii) does not imply what the proof needs, and the two conditions are incomparable. Example: Ĝ = G₂ (split, so n = 1), q = 5, ℓ = 3. The exponents are 1 and 5; 5 − 1 = 4 and 5⁵ − 1 = 3124 are prime to 3, so the printed (ii) holds. But 3 is a bad prime for G₂, contradicting the first step of the proof ('ℓ is very good'), and for the degree-6 invariant 5⁶ − 1 = 15624 = 3·5208, so the key step fails. With degrees (2, 6), 3 divides 5² − 1 = 24, so ℓ = 3 is correctly excluded. Conversely, for G₂ with q = 3 and ℓ = 11 the degree condition holds (3² − 1 = 8, 3⁶ − 1 = 728) while the exponent condition fails (11 divides 3⁵ − 1 = 242). The degree condition excludes bad primes and torsion primes: ℓ − 1 divides some degree whenever ℓ is not very good, and q^{ℓ−1} ≡ 1 mod ℓ. So the result is correct under the paper's own usage but misstated in standard terminology.

issues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.4, proof of Theorem VIII.4.1, p. 292 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source claims cartesianness, directly from the definitions, for the pullback diagram associated to any g : I → J. Its rows are O(Ĝ\(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^I/Ĝ) →Θ^I Map(W^I, End(id_𝒞)) and O(Ĝ\(Ĝ ⋊ Q)^J/Ĝ) →Θ^J Map(W^J, End(id_𝒞)).
issues.correction: … induced by pullback along g, commutes.
issues.reason: What follows from the definitions and is used later ('Applying now functoriality for pullback under I ⊔ I → I', 'still satisfying compatibility with pullback') is that the square commutes. It is not a pullback square in general. For example, for g : {1,2} → {1} the right vertical map's kernel is typically far larger than the image of the left kernel under Θ, e.g. when End(id_𝒞) = Λ. So 'cartesian' is a slip for 'commutative'.

issues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.5.3, remark after Theorem VIII.5.15 (p. 302) and proof of Theorem VIII.5.15 (p. 303) (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source extends the Donkin property of Levi subgroups to centralizers of regular semisimple elements. In the proof, it assumes Θ inner and identifies H with the centralizer of a regular semisimple g ∈ G, whose image ḡ ∈ G_ad has order p.
issues.correction: '… generalized to the statement that centralizers of semisimple elements (of order prime to ℓ in G_ad) define Donkin subgroups' and 'H is the centralizer of some semisimple element g ∈ G (with ḡ ∈ G_ad of order p)'.
issues.reason: If Θ = Int(g) has prime order p ≠ ℓ, then g^p is central, so g is semisimple and H = G^Θ = Z_G(g). But g need not be regular: e.g. every Levi subgroup, and the non-Levi groups listed on p. 311 (A₂ ⊂ G₂, A₄×A₄ ⊂ E₈, …), arise this way. For simply connected G, the centralizer of a regular semisimple element is a maximal torus, and the Donkin property for a torus is trivial. So the remark as printed is true but vacuous and would not generalize the Levi case, while the sentence in the proof is false in general. The proof only uses that a maximal torus of G through g lies in H, which holds for any semisimple g. So the argument and theorem are unaffected; the word 'regular' should be deleted in both places.

issues.locator: Chapter I, §I.6, p. 29, paragraph on the constant term functors CT^± (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source identifies CT+ with the classical Satake transform, described as integration over orbits of the unipotent radical of U+.
issues.correction: … of integrating along orbits under the unipotent radical U⁺ of P⁺.
issues.reason: U⁺ is itself the unipotent radical of the parabolic P⁺ introduced in the same paragraph ('P⁺, P⁻ ⊂ G … two opposite parabolics, with common Levi M'); a unipotent group is its own unipotent radical, so the phrase as printed is circular. The classical Satake transform integrates over U⁺(E)-orbits. U⁺ is not otherwise defined in Chapter I.

issues.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.3, proof of Theorem II.2.6: the estimate (II.2.1), p. 65, and the last paragraph of the proof, p. 66 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source bounds the norm of φ^{−1}(w₁) by that of [ϖ]^{(N−1)/q}π^{M−N+1}, namely q^{−(N−1)/q−rM+rN−r} in B_{R,[r,q]}, and claims a bound q^{−M−1} for sufficiently large M. From w₂ ∈ π^M W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)⟨[ϖ]/π⟩^m, it bounds the norm of A^{−1}w₂ by that of π^{−N′}π^M, namely q^{rN′−rM} in B_{R,[r,q]}, again claiming q^{−M−1} for sufficiently large M.
issues.correction: With the conventions of Proposition II.1.16 (rad = log|[ϖ]|/log|π|, Y_{S,[r,q]} = {|π|^q ≤ |[ϖ]| ≤ |π|^r}) and the normalization ||[ϖ]|| = 1/q, one has |π| = q^{−1/ρ} at radius ρ, so ||π^k||_{B_{R,[r,q]}} = q^{−k/q} for k ≥ 0, not q^{−rk}. The two bounds become q^{−M/q} and q^{(N′−M)/q}, both larger than q^{−M−1}; the printed exponents are those of the reciprocal convention |π| = |[ϖ]|^ρ. The claimed estimate (II.2.1) is itself false as stated, so the proof does not establish global generation as written; the theorem is [KL15, Proposition 6.2.4] and stands, but the quantitative step must be redone (for example following [KL15]). For A = π^N·Id the choice v_i = Σ_j π^{Nj}[ϖ^{Mq^{−j}}]e_i works when (N/r + 1)/(q − 1) ≤ M ≤ (N − q)/(q − 1), i.e. with N made large by twisting and M chosen in a window, not with M large.
issues.reason: Counterexample to (II.2.1): E = 𝔽_q((π)), S = Spa C, A = π^N·Id with N > 0 (so N′ = N, qN > N′), w = π^M e₁ ∈ π^M W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)⟨([ϖ]/π)^{±1}⟩^m. Every v with (φ − A)v = w is v = c e₁ + h with c = π^M/(1 − π^N) ∈ E and h ∈ ker(φ − π^N) = H⁰(X_C, 𝒪(N))^m. Writing h = Σ h_iπ^i, φ(h) = π^N h gives h_i^q = h_{i−N}; if |h_M| = 1 then |h_{M−kN}| = 1 for all k ≥ 0 and h cannot converge on Y_{C,[1,q]}, so |h_M| ≠ 1 and the π^M-coefficient of v has absolute value ≥ 1. Hence ||v||_{B_{C,[r,q]}} ≥ sup|π|^M = q^{−M/q} > q^{−M−1} for every M ≥ 1 and 1 < r ≤ q. The same computation on φ^{−1}(w₁) = [ϖ]^{(N−1)/q}π^{M−N+1} gives q^{−M/q}, not the printed q^{−(N−1)/q−r(M−N+1)}.

issues.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.3, proof of Theorem II.2.6, p. 66, second display (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: Using qN > N′, the source asserts φ(A^{−1}w₂) ∈ π^{−N′}[ϖ]^{Nq}π^M W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)⟨[ϖ]^q/π⟩^m ⊂ π^{M+1}W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)⟨([ϖ]/π)^{±1}⟩^m.
issues.correction: φ(A^{−1}w₂) ∈ π^{−N′}[ϖ]^{Nq}π^{M−N}W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)⟨π/[ϖ], [ϖ]^q/π⟩^m, which lies in π^{M+1}W_{𝒪_E}(R⁺)⟨([ϖ]/π)^{±1}⟩^m when (q − 1)N > N′, not qN > N′. Since N ≤ N′, twisting (N, N′) ↦ (N + n, N′ + n) achieves (q − 1)N > N′ only for q ≥ 3; in general one splits w at the power K of [ϖ]/π with (N′ + 1)/(q − 1) ≤ K ≤ 1 + (N − 1)q/(q − 1), which exists after twisting because qN − N′ grows with n.
issues.reason: w₂ ∈ [ϖ]^Nπ^{M−N}W⟨[ϖ]/π⟩ (as printed just above), so φ(w₂) ∈ [ϖ]^{qN}π^{M−N}W⟨[ϖ]^q/π⟩, and φ(A^{−1}) ∈ π^{−N′}W⟨π/[ϖ], [ϖ]^q/π⟩ because A^{−1} ∈ π^{−N′}W⟨π/[ϖ]^{1/q}, [ϖ]/π⟩. On Y_{S,[1,1]} (|π| = |[ϖ]|) the product has size |π|^{M + (q−1)N − N′}. N ≤ N′ because A·A^{−1} = 1 and 1 ∉ π·W⟨([ϖ]/π)^{±1}⟩. The printed factor π^M drops π^{−N}.

issues.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.3, proof of Proposition II.2.7 (GAGA), p. 67, first sentence (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source calls the construction of f : (X, 𝒪_X) → X^alg formal and independent of assumptions. For g ∈ P_n, it asserts an isomorphism g|_U : 𝒪_U ≅ 𝒪_U(n) on U = D(g) ⊂ X, where g is nonvanishing. Varying g, it glues these to a locally ringed space morphism (X, 𝒪) → X^alg.
issues.correction: The chart maps D(g) → D₊(g) are formal and glue to a morphism ⋃_g D(g) → X^alg; this union is all of X because 𝒪_X(n) is globally generated for large n, which is a hypothesis of the proposition.
issues.reason: For an arbitrary line bundle the D(g), g ∈ P_n with n > 0, need not cover X: for X = ℙ¹ and 𝒪_X(1) replaced by 𝒪(−1), P = ⊕ H⁰(𝒪(−n)) is concentrated in degree 0 and ⋃ D(g) is empty (cf. Stacks 01XS). The accepted restructuring RS-20 (research/blueprint/restructure/RS-20.result.json) records the same point and places the global morphism after global generation, in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness. The result is unaffected since the hypothesis holds.

issues.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.1, first paragraph, p. 58 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source claims uniqueness up to isomorphism of a 1-dimensional formal group G over 𝒪_Ĕ carrying an 𝒪_E-action whose two actions on Lie G agree. It identifies G = G_LT as the Lubin–Tate formal group of E.
issues.correction: … with action by 𝒪_E, such that the two induced actions on Lie G coincide and G is π-divisible of 𝒪_E-height one (i.e. [π]_G is an isogeny of degree q) …
issues.reason: Without a height condition uniqueness fails: the formal additive group Ĝ_a with 𝒪_E acting through 𝒪_E → 𝒪_Ĕ is 1-dimensional with equal Lie actions, and [π](X) = πX is not an isogeny on the special fibre; 1-dimensional formal 𝒪_E-modules of any 𝒪_E-height h ≥ 1 exist over k and lift. The next sentences pin down the intended object by the Dieudonné module M = W_{𝒪_E}(k), F = σ/π, which has height one.

issues.locator: Chapter II, §II.2.5, end of the proof of Theorem II.2.19, p. 75 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The proof invokes Proposition II.2.5 (i)–(ii) to split 0 → 𝒪_{X_C}(λ) → ℰ → ⊕_{λ′≤λ} 𝒪_{X_S}(λ′)^{n′_{λ′}} → 0 after another pro-étale cover, declaring the argument complete.
issues.correction: By Proposition II.2.5 (ii)–(iii), the extension 0 → 𝒪_{X_S}(λ) → ℰ → ⊕_{λ′≤λ} 𝒪_{X_S}(λ′)^{n′_{λ′}} → 0 can be split after a further pro-étale cover.
issues.reason: The obstruction lies in Ext¹(𝒪(λ′), 𝒪(λ)) = H¹(X_S, 𝒪(λ − λ′)^{⊕}) with λ − λ′ ≥ 0: it vanishes on affinoids for λ′ < λ by II.2.5(iii) and pro-étale locally for λ′ = λ by II.2.5(ii). Part (i) concerns negative slopes and is not used. The family is over S, so 𝒪_{X_C} should be 𝒪_{X_S}.

issues.locator: Chapter IV, §IV.4.3, Lemma IV.4.26, p. 146 (statement), and the same sign in Lemma IV.4.25, p. 145 (statement), its proof, p. 146, the proof of Proposition IV.4.24, pp. 144–145, and the proof of Proposition IV.4.29, p. 149 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: Lemma IV.4.26 asserts surjectivity of φ − π^{−d} : I_{[1,q]} → I_{[1,1]}. For i ≠ r_j, Lemma IV.4.25 gives f_i = φ(g_i) − g_{i+1}; it also gives f_{r_j} = φ(g_{r_j}) − π^{−d_j} g_{r_{j−1}+1}. In B_{C,[1,1]}[T_1, …, T_r]/(T_1, …, T_r)^2, the Proposition IV.4.24 proof uses α_{r_j} ≡ π^{−d_j} T_{r_{j−1}+1}.
issues.correction: Replace π^{−d} by π^{d} throughout: Lemma IV.4.26 should read "the map φ − π^{d} : I_{[1,q]} → I_{[1,1]} is surjective"; in Lemma IV.4.25, f_{r_j} = φ(g_{r_j}) − π^{d_j} g_{r_{j−1}+1} (and f = φ^r(g) − π^{d} g in its proof); in the proofs of Propositions IV.4.24 and IV.4.29 the linear terms are α_{r_j} ≡ π^{d_j} T_{r_{j−1}+1}, with α′_{r_j}(0, …, 0) ≡ α_{r_j}(0, …, 0) + π^{d_j} ε_{r_{j−1}+1} − φ(ε_{r_j}) and α_{r_j}(0, …, 0) = φ(ε_{r_j}) − π^{d_j} ε_{r_{j−1}+1}. The Dieudonné module φ(e_{r_j}) = π^{−d_j} e_{r_{j−1}+1} of Lemma IV.4.25 is right; the error is in translating it into the H^1 equation and the coordinate gluing.
issues.reason: FS's convention is H^0(X_S, O_{X_S}(1)) = H^0(Y_S, O_{Y_S})^{φ=π} (p. 60), and in the proof of Proposition II.2.5(iii), p. 62, H^1(X_S, O(n)) = 0 for n > 0 is shown by proving "φ − π^n : B_{R,[1,q]} → B_{R,[1,1]} is surjective". So on B the kernel and cokernel of φ − π^{−d} are H^0 and H^1 of O(−d), not O(d), while the proof of Lemma IV.4.26 ("By the snake lemma and the vanishing H^1(X_S, O_{X_S}(d)) = 0 ... equivalent to the surjectivity of H^0(X_S, O(d)) → H^0(X_{S_0}, O(d))") and the lead-in to Lemma IV.4.25 ("vanishing of H^1(X_S, E) for E of positive slopes") are about O(d). The printed Lemma IV.4.26 is false: take E = F_q((π)), d = 1, C the completed algebraic closure of F_q((ϖ)), S = Spa C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S_0 = V(T) ≅ Spa C (Zariski closed), f = ϖ^{−1}T ∈ I_{[1,1]}. Writing g = Σ g_i π^i with g_i ∈ R, (φ − π^{−1})(g) has coefficients g_i^q − g_{i+1}. Convergence as i → −∞ forces g_i = 0 for i ≤ 0, and then g_1 = −ϖ^{−1}T and g_{k+1} = g_k^q, so |g_{k+1}| = |ϖ|^{−q^k}, and Σ g_i π^i diverges on Y_{S,[1,q]}. The same f with a factor π (f = ϖ^{−1}Tπ ∈ I^+_{[1,1]}) contradicts the printed Lemma IV.4.25 for r = 1. Geometrically, with the printed linear term a section t of Z near s satisfies t_{i+1} = φ(t_i), φ(t_{r_j}) = π^{−d_j} t_{r_{j−1}+1}, i.e. is a section of a bundle of negative slopes, contradicting the positivity of s^*T_{Z/X_S}. With π^{d_j} every step goes through: H^1 of the positive bundle vanishes, and the snake-lemma argument of the printed proof proves the corrected Lemma IV.4.26.

issues.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.2, proof of Proposition VI.2.4, first paragraph, pp. 198–199 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source gives Fil^i_Ξ(R^♯)^n = (ξ^iΞ ∩ B^+_dR(R^♯)^n)/(ξ^iΞ ∩ ξB^+_dR(R^♯)^n) as finite projective R^♯-modules, with rank counting occurrences of −i in k_1, …, k_n. It then lifts e_{n_{i−1}+1}, …, e_{n_i} to f_{n_{i−1}+1}, …, f_{n_i} ∈ ξ^iΞ ∩ B^+_dR(R^♯)^n.
issues.correction: Fil^i_Ξ(R^♯)^n is finite projective of rank #{j : k_j ≤ −i}. The filtration is decreasing (Fil^{i+1} ⊂ Fil^i), and its graded piece Fil^i/Fil^{i+1} has rank the number of occurrences of −i. Accordingly, the basis vectors lifted at step i are e_{n_{i+1}+1}, …, e_{n_i}: those in Fil^i but not in Fil^{i+1}, for which k_j = −i.
issues.reason: Take Ξ = ⊕_j ξ^{k_j}B⁺_dR, the lattice [μ] itself. Then ξ^iΞ ∩ B⁺_dR^n = ⊕_j ξ^{max(k_j+i,0)}B⁺_dR, whose image modulo ξ is spanned by the e_j with k_j ≤ −i. For example n = 1, k_1 = 1, i = −2: Fil^{−2} = R^♯ has rank 1, but −i = 2 does not occur among the k_j. Read with graded pieces, the argument works unchanged, including g_j = ξ^{-i} f_j = ξ^{k_j} f_j.

issues.locator: Chapter VI, §VI.10, last paragraph, p. 234 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source defines Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ̂^p) = lim←_n Rep_{W_E}(ℤ/nℤ) as continuous W_E-representations on finite free modules over ℤ̂^p = lim←_n ℤ/nℤ.
issues.correction: Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ̂^p) = lim←_n Rep_{W_E}(ℤ/nℤ), the category of compatible systems of continuous representations of W_E on finite projective ℤ/nℤ-modules; equivalently, of continuous representations of W_E on ℤ̂^p-modules M = ∏_{ℓ≠p} M_ℓ with each M_ℓ finite free over ℤ_ℓ (i.e. ∏_{ℓ≠p} Rep^cont_{W_E}(ℤ_ℓ)).
issues.reason: Rep_{W_E}(ℤ/nℤ) consists of representations on finite projective ℤ/nℤ-modules (§VI.9). The system (ℤ/nℤ ⊗_{ℤ̂^p} ℤ_ℓ)_n with trivial action is compatible, and each term ℤ/ℓ^{v_ℓ(n)}ℤ is a direct factor of ℤ/nℤ, hence finite projective. Its limit ℤ_ℓ is projective but not free over ℤ̂^p = ∏_{ℓ′≠p} ℤ_{ℓ′}. Systems with ℓ-ranks r_ℓ unbounded in ℓ have limit ∏_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^{r_ℓ}, which is not even finitely generated. So the inverse limit is strictly larger than the representations on finite free ℤ̂^p-modules. The construction of ℋ_G and Ǧ over ℤ̂^p and the proof of Theorem VI.11.1 (which reduces to ℤ_ℓ by the Chinese remainder theorem) are unaffected.

issues.locator: Chapter VII, §VII.2, proof of Proposition VII.2.3, p. 254 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source places F_i ⊗^L G_j in degrees −1 and 0, citing global dimension 1 for Ẑ^p.
issues.correction: 'as Ẑ^p has weak (Tor-)dimension 1', or 'as F_i and G_j are killed by some n prime to p, so that the derived tensor product is computed over the direct factor ∏_{ℓ | n} Z_ℓ of Ẑ^p, a finite product of discrete valuation rings'.
issues.reason: Ẑ^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ does not have global dimension 1. The element x = (ℓ)_ℓ is a non-zero-divisor and a non-unit, and Ẑ^p/x = ∏_{ℓ≠p} F_ℓ. In this von Neumann regular ring the ideal I = ⊕_ℓ F_ℓ is projective (a sum of idempotent-generated ideals) but not a direct summand (it is not finitely generated), so the module M = (∏F_ℓ)/I has projective dimension exactly 1 over Ẑ^p/x. Kaplansky's change-of-rings theorem gives pd_{Ẑ^p} M = 2. What the proof needs is still true. Ẑ^p is a Bézout ring whose principal ideals (x) ≅ e·Ẑ^p are projective, so it is semihereditary and has weak dimension 1. In any case constructible sheaves killed by n prime to p are modules over the hereditary direct factor ∏_{ℓ|n} Z_ℓ. So the conclusion that F_i ⊗^L G_j lies in degrees [−1, 0] holds; only the stated reason is false.

issues.locator: Chapter VIII, §VIII.2.2.1, paragraph before Definition VIII.2.6, p. 282, and its reuse before Theorem VIII.2.7, p. 283 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source cites [ML95, Theorem X.3.1] for HH^2(B/A) = Ext^1_B(L_{B/A}, B), identifies this with Exalcom_A(B, B) via [Gro64, Chap.0, Sec. 18.4], and concludes HH^2(B/A) = H^1(L^∨_{B/A}). On p. 283 it uses H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) = HH^2(B/A) → Ext^2_B(N, N) to claim a natural graded O(Sing_{X/S})-algebra structure.
issues.correction: There is a natural (injective) map Ext^1_B(L_{B/A}, B) = Exalcom_A(B, B) → HH^2(B/A), sending a commutative square-zero extension of B by B to the same extension viewed as an associative one; it is not an isomorphism in general. On p. 283 read 'Using the map H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) → HH^2(B/A) → Ext^2_B(N, N)'.
issues.reason: Counterexample: A = k a field, B = k[x, y]. B is smooth over k, so L_{B/k} ≅ Ω_{B/k} is free of rank 2 and Ext^1_B(L_{B/k}, B) = 0; but the Koszul resolution of B over B ⊗_k B gives HH^2(B/k) ≅ Hom_B(Λ^2 Ω_{B/k}, B) ≅ B ≠ 0 (Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg), e.g. B[ε] with xy − yx = ε is a nonsplit first-order associative deformation. [ML95, Theorem X.3.1] identifies HH^2 with all singular (associative) extensions, while [Gro64, 0_IV 18.4] concerns commutative ones, so the two cited identifications do not compose. The later text only uses a map H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) → Ext^2_B(N, N): its image lies in the image of HH^•(B/A), which graded-commutes with Ext^•_B(N, N), so Sym^•_B H^1(L^∨_{B/A}) = O(Sing_{X/S}) still acts, and μEnd(N), Definition VIII.2.8, Theorems VIII.2.7 and VIII.2.9 and Corollary VIII.2.10 are unaffected.

issues.printed: The proof reduces connectivity in the good filtration t-structure to connectivity of RΓ(H, X ⊗ ∇^H_{w′λ_j}) for w′ ∈ W_j and j < i. It asserts RΓ(H, ∇^H_{wλ_i} ⊗ ∇^H_{w′λ_j}) = 0 and, using the definition of X, restates the requirement for m > 0 as H^m(H, ∇_{λ_i}|_H ⊗ ∇^H_{w′λ_j}) = 0.
issues.correction: Test against the duals of these weights: it suffices that RΓ(H, X ⊗ ∇^H_μ) is connective for the H-dominant μ = −w_0^H(w′λ_j), j < i, w′ ∈ W_j (equivalently, Ext^m_H(Δ^H_{w′λ_j}, X) = 0 for m > 0). For these, RΓ(H, ∇^H_{wλ_i} ⊗ ∇^H_μ) = RHom_H(Δ^H_{w′λ_j}, ∇^H_{wλ_i}) = 0 does hold (different W-orbits), and the argument continues with λ_j replaced by −w_0λ_j, ending with H^m(G, Ind_H^G 1 ⊗ ∇_{λ_i} ⊗ ∇_{−w_0λ_j}) = 0. The induction then needs −w_0λ_j to come before λ_i, so the enumeration should be stable under λ ↦ −w_0λ in this sense, e.g. by increasing ⟨λ + ρ, λ + ρ⟩, which also satisfies the printed condition on the weights of ∇_{λ_i}.
issues.reason: RΓ(H, ∇^H_μ ⊗ ∇^H_ν) = RHom_H(Δ^H_{−w_0^H μ}, ∇^H_ν) is L in degree 0 when ν = −w_0^H μ, so the asserted vanishing fails whenever −w_0λ_i = λ_j with j < i. Example in the proof's own setting: G = SL_3, p ≥ 3 a prime ≠ ℓ, Θ = Int(diag(1, ζ, ζ^2)) with ζ a primitive p-th root of unity, so H = G^Θ is the diagonal torus T (the centralizer of a regular semisimple element, as the proof says). The enumeration 0, ω_1, ω_2, … satisfies the printed condition. For i = 2, j = 1, take wω_2 = −ε_1 and w′ω_1 = ε_1: RΓ(T, ∇^T_{−ε_1} ⊗ ∇^T_{ε_1}) = RΓ(T, L) = L ≠ 0. The reduction to these test objects is also not what the weight argument gives. H^m(H, X ⊗ ∇^H_μ) = Ext^m_H(Δ^H_{−w_0^H μ}, X) can be nonzero only if −w_0^H μ lies below a weight of X, i.e. μ ∈ W·{−w_0λ_0, …, −w_0λ_{i−1}}. That set differs from W·{λ_0, …, λ_{i−1}} when −1 ∉ W (types A_n with n ≥ 2, D_n with n odd, E_6). The repaired argument proves the same theorem. Proposition VIII.5.17's proof reuses 'the arguments with highest weights in the proof of Theorem VIII.5.15' (p. 309) and needs the same repair.

issues.locator: Chapter IX, Definition IX.0.4, p. 319, and §IX.4, Definition/Proposition IX.4.1, p. 327; same wording in Proposition I.9.1, p. 34 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source asserts a unique φ_A : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ Q that is a semisimple L-parameter. For every excursion datum (I, V, α, β, (γ_i)_{i∈I}), it requires A = T_1(A) → T_V(A) → T_V(A) → T_1(A) = A to act by the scalar represented by L → V → V → L.
issues.correction: Then there is a semisimple L-parameter φ_A : W_E → Ĝ(L) ⋊ Q, unique up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation, such that … (as in Corollary VIII.4.3: 'there is, up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation, a unique semisimple L-parameter').
issues.reason: For g ∈ Ĝ(L), the conjugate parameter gφ_Ag^{-1} gives the scalars β∘(gφ_A(γ_i)g^{-1})_i∘α = β∘diag(g)∘(φ_A(γ_i))_i∘diag(g)^{-1}∘α = β∘(φ_A(γ_i))_i∘α. This holds because α : 1 → V|_Ĝ and β : V|_Ĝ → 1 are equivariant for the diagonal Ĝ. So every conjugate satisfies the defining identities, and literal uniqueness fails as soon as the Ĝ(L)-orbit of φ_A has more than one point (e.g. G = GL₂ and φ_A = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ₁ ≠ χ₂). The proof invokes Proposition VIII.3.8, whose (i) is 'Semisimple L-parameters … up to Ĝ(L)-conjugation', and Corollary VIII.4.3 (pp. 292–293) states the conjugacy qualifier. The intended meaning is clear, so this is a misprint.

issues.locator: Chapter IX, §IX.6.3, proof of Proposition IX.6.3, p. 332 (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The source claims that restricting F_n → W to maps through W′ leaves the colimit unchanged, giving Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ ←∼ colim_{(n,F_n→W′)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ ≅ colim_{(n,F_n→W′)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ′))^{Ĝ′} = Exc(W′, Ĝ′).
issues.correction: Apply the Shapiro isomorphism termwise over the W-indexed diagram: Exc(W, Ĝ) = colim_{(n,F_n→W)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n, Ĝ))^Ĝ ≅ colim_{(n,F_n→W)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_n ×_W W′, Ĝ′))^{Ĝ′} → colim_{(m,F_m→W′)} 𝒪(Z¹(F_m, Ĝ′))^{Ĝ′} = Exc(W′, Ĝ′). The last map is induced by the functor (F_n → W) ↦ (F_n ×_W W′ → W′), and one must show that this functor is cofinal. For example, every F_m → W′ factors through F_n ×_W W′ for F_n = F_m ∗ F_k, with the generators of F_k sent to coset representatives of W/W′. Restricting the index category to maps F_n → W with image in W′, as printed, does not compute Exc(W, Ĝ).
issues.reason: Counterexample to both printed isomorphisms. Take E′/E unramified quadratic, G′ = G_m and G = Res_{E′/E} G_m, so that Ĝ = G_m × G_m, with W acting through W/W′ ≅ Z/2 by swapping the factors and W′ acting trivially. For F_n → W′ one has Z¹(F_n, Ĝ)⫽Ĝ = Hom(F_n, G_m²) = G_m^{2n}, while Z¹(F_n, Ĝ′)⫽Ĝ′ = G_m^n. So the middle colimit is, up to universal homeomorphism, the ring of functions on Hom(W′, G_m²) and the right one that on Hom(W′, G_m): the printed '≅' fails. The printed '←∼' is induced by restricting cocycles, Z¹(W, Ĝ)⫽Ĝ ≅ Hom(W′, G_m) → Hom(W′, G_m²), χ ↦ (χ, χ∘Int(σ)) for σ ∈ W ∖ W′ (Shapiro). This is a closed immersion that is not an isomorphism, so the ring map is surjective but not injective. The identification Exc(W, Ĝ) ≅ Exc(W′, Ĝ′) in the statement is not affected: it follows from the Shapiro isomorphism and the cofinality argument above, which the proof does not give.

issues.locator: Chapter II, §II.3.1, proof of Proposition II.3.1, p. 76, paragraph beginning 'First, we handle the case that S = Spa(K, K⁺)' (arXiv v4)
issues.printed: The proof reduces to ensuring that the extension pulled back to ℰ^{≥λ} does not split. It claims that splitting lifts ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} to ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{X_S}, which slopes force to vanish. It defines W′_1 ⊂ W_1 by taking the fibre at S_1^♯ of ℰ^{≥λ} ⊂ ℰ, and concludes that a quotient W_1 → K_1^♯ nonzero on W′_1 suffices.
issues.correction: The extension pulled back is 0 → 𝒪_{X_S} → 𝒪_{X_S}(1) → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} → 0. So the pullback to ℰ^{≥λ} splits exactly when ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} lifts to a map ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{X_S}(1), not to 𝒪_{X_S}. By slopes such a lift vanishes only when λ > 1. For 1/r < λ ≤ 1 the quotient W_1 → K_1^♯ must be chosen so that the induced map ℰ^{≥λ} → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} does not lift to 𝒪_{X_S}(1); a nonzero restriction to W′_1 is not enough. Over a complete algebraically closed field such a choice exists. For ℱ = (ℰ^{≥λ})^∨ ⊗ 𝒪(1), of slope 1 − λ ≥ 0, H¹(ℱ) = 0, so the evaluation map H⁰(ℱ) → ℱ|_{S_1^♯} has cokernel H¹((ℰ^{≥λ})^∨) ≠ 0 (slope −λ < 0). The proof must add this choice, and an argument that it can be made over the non-algebraically-closed perfectoid fields it also treats.
issues.reason: Counterexample to the printed sufficiency claim: r = 2, S = Spa(C, C⁺), ℰ = 𝒪(1), so n = d = m = 1 and ℰ^{≥λ} = ℰ with λ = 1 > 1/2. Here W_1 = 𝒪(1)|_{S_1^♯}, and the cokernel term of 0 → 𝒪 → 𝒪(1) → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} → 0 is canonically 𝒪(1)|_{S_1^♯}. Take the quotient W_1 → K_1^♯ to be this identification; it is nonzero on W′_1 = W_1. Then ℰ → 𝒪_{S_1^♯} is the quotient map of the sequence itself, the pulled-back extension splits, and ℰ_1 ≅ 𝒪 ⊕ 𝒪(1) has a slope 0 < 1/2. Rescaling the quotient by c ∈ C^♯ ∖ E, i.e. outside the image of End(𝒪(1)) = E, gives a nonsplit extension of 𝒪(1) by 𝒪 of rank 2 and degree 1. That is 𝒪(1/2), as the proposition predicts, so the gap is in the argument, not the statement. The passage is a leftover from v1–v3, which pulled back 0 → 𝒪(−1) → 𝒪 → 𝒪_{S♯} → 0 for slopes ≥ 0. There the lift goes to 𝒪_{X_S} and vanishes by slopes because λ > 0.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), the proof of Proposition 6.3, case r = 0

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Proposition 2.4, equation (2.3), p. 11 (published; arXiv v6 identical)
issues.correction: ν(S_{{0,...,n},f,(γ_0,γ_1,...,γ_n)}) = f((ρ_ν(γ_0), ρ_ν(γ_1), ..., ρ_ν(γ_n))). Equivalently, keep the right-hand side and make the subscript of S equal to (γ_0γ_n, ..., γ_{n−1}γ_n, γ_n).
issues.reason: The relations of §2.2.2 are incompatible with the printed formula. Take G = G_m split, so Ĝ = G_m and ^LG^alg = Ĝ × Γ, and let f(g_0,g_1) := ĝ_0ĝ_1^{−1} on the Ĝ-components. This f is invariant under left and right diagonal translation. Relation (iii) with ζ: {0,1} → {∗} gives S_{{0,1},f,(γ,γ)} = S_{{∗},f^ζ,γ} with f^ζ = 1, and relation (ii) makes this 1. The printed (2.3) gives instead ν(S_{{0,1},f,(γ,γ)}) = f(ρ_ν(γ²), ρ_ν(γ)) = χ(γ), where ρ_ν = (χ, id). Now take any character χ: Γ → k^× with χ ≠ 1. The assignment S_{I,f,(γ_i)} ↦ f((χ(γ_i),γ_i)_i) respects relations (i)–(v), so it is a character ν of Exc. Applying the printed (2.3) with (γ_0,γ_1) = (γ,1) forces ρ_ν = (χ, id), and applying it with (γ,γ) forces χ = 1. So no ρ_ν exists, and Proposition 2.4 as printed is false. For split G the printed right-hand side equals f(ρ(γ_0), ..., ρ(γ_{n−1}), 1), which does not depend on γ_n. The corrected formula satisfies relations (iii)–(v), as one checks directly. With h(g_0,...,g_{n−1}) := f(g_0,...,g_{n−1},1), it is the pseudocharacter identity of BHKT19 §4, Θ_n(h)(γ_1,...,γ_n) = h(ρ(γ_1),...,ρ(γ_n)), taken at γ_iγ_n^{−1}. The proof of Lemma 2.7 ('use (2.3)') and all later uses need only the corrected form. Checked on the page image of p. 11 and in the arXiv v6 TeX, which has the same formula. Searched: the arXiv version list (v1–v6, the last saying 'to appear in Forum Math Pi'); BHKT19 §4, which states Theorem 4.5 for pseudocharacters and not in this form. No correction found.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Lemma 2.7, p. 12
issues.printed: The source asserts the existence of φ^*: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → Exc(Γ, ^LH^alg) as a homomorphism. In the Proposition 2.4 description of spectral k-points, an input ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, Ĥ(k)) has image φ ∘ ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, Ĝ(k)).
issues.correction: … sends ρ to the semisimplification (φ∘ρ)^{ss}, the unique semisimple parameter with the same excursion character as φ∘ρ. This equals φ∘ρ when φ∘ρ is semisimple, in particular for φ = φ_BC (see the next finding).
issues.reason: By Proposition 2.4 the k-points of Spec Exc are semisimple parameters, and ν∘φ^* sends S_{I,f,(γ_i)} to f((φρ(γ_i))_i), which depends only on (φ∘ρ)^{ss}. In characteristic p, φ∘ρ need not be semisimple. Take H = PGL_2 and G = PGL_{p+1} split, with φ = Sym^p × id: SL_2 × Γ → SL_{p+1} × Γ, which is admissible. Let ρ have image SL_2(F_p), which is irreducible on k^2 and so semisimple; Γ = Gal(F^s/F) for a suitable global function field of characteristic ≠ p admits such a surjection, by Igusa (the mod p monodromy of the Legendre curve is SL_2(F_p)). Sym^p(k^2) contains the Frobenius twist span(x^p, y^p) as an SL_2(F_p)-submodule with no invariant complement. A linear-algebra check over F_p for p = 3, 5, 7 finds no equivariant retraction. So φ∘ρ lies in the stabiliser of a 2-plane but in no Levi of it, and is not semisimple. The lemma is used only for φ = φ_BC, where its statement holds once φ_BC is shown to preserve semisimplicity.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6, pp. 2–4 (proved as Theorem 6.26, Theorem 6.21, §6.3 and Theorem 5.13), with Definition 2.8, p. 13
issues.printed: Theorem 1.2 asserts φ_BC ∘ ρ_π ≅ ρ_{Π^(p)}. Theorem 1.4 identifies semi-simple L-parameters by ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π. Theorem 1.6 declares φ_BC ∘ ρ automorphic.
issues.correction: Add the lemma (new coverage item) that φ_BC ∘ ρ is semisimple whenever ρ is. With it, the character identities the proofs establish give the stated isomorphisms. An example is χ_π ∘ φ_BC^* = χ_{Π^{(p)}} in Theorem 6.21.
issues.reason: Each proof ends with an equality of excursion characters, which by Proposition 2.4 identifies ρ_Π with (φ_BC∘ρ_π)^{ss}. The statements need φ_BC∘ρ_π itself to be semisimple, and the paper never addresses this; the previous finding shows it fails for general admissible φ. It holds for φ_BC. ρ(Γ_E) is normal in ρ(Γ), so it is completely reducible (Bate–Martin–Röhrle, Invent. Math. 2005, Theorem 3.10). If ψ = φ_BC∘ρ lies in an R-parabolic P_λ, λ = (λ_s)_s, of ^LG = Ĥ^{Hom_F(E,F^s)} ⋊ Γ̄, then P_{λ_{s_0}} contains ρ(Γ_E) and hence has a Levi L_0 containing it. Transporting L_0 to s by ρ(γ) with γs_0 = s is independent of γ because ρ(Γ_E) ⊂ L_0, and gives a Levi of P_λ containing ψ(Γ). So the stated results are correct, but their proofs omit this step.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), §2.1.3, the sentence after Proposition 2.1 and equation (2.1), p. 9
issues.printed: The source chooses χ̃: Gal(F^s/F) → Ĝ(k) lifting χ, possibly obtained using a square root of the cyclotomic character mod p, and claims this yields ^LG^alg ∼→ ^LG^geom through (g, γ) ↦ (g χ̃(γ^{−1}), γ).
issues.correction: Require χ̃ to be a homomorphism lifting χ whose values are fixed by act^alg. An example is χ̃ = 2ρ̂ ∘ ε, where ε is a square root of cyc_p and 2ρ̂, the sum of the positive coroots, is a cocharacter of Ĝ fixed by every pinned automorphism.
issues.reason: Using act^geom(γ) = act^alg(γ) ∘ Ad_{χ(γ)}, one computes that (2.1) is multiplicative exactly when act^alg(γ)(χ̃(γ′)) = χ̃(γ′) for all γ, γ′. Counterexample for an arbitrary lift: G = U_3 attached to a quadratic extension, Ĝ = GL_3, where the pinned outer automorphism acts on the centre by inversion. Let χ̃ = ρ̂∘cyc_p, where ρ̂ = (1,0,−1) is a cocharacter of GL_3 fixed by that automorphism. Let ζ: Gal → k^× = Z(Ĝ)(k) be a character with ζ(γ′)² ≠ 1 for some γ′, and put χ̃′ = χ̃ζ. Then χ̃′ still lifts χ, but whenever γ acts by the outer automorphism, the images of (1,γ)(1,γ′) and of (1,γγ′) differ by ζ(γ′)². Only square-root lifts are used (Definition 2.8), so no result is affected.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), §2.4.2, relation (v), p. 12
issues.printed: The source calls δ_W: 𝟙 → W ⊗ W^* the natural counit; it calls ev_W: W^* ⊗ W → 𝟙 the natural unit.
issues.correction: δ_W is the unit (coevaluation) and ev_W the counit (evaluation) of the duality between W and W^*.
issues.reason: For the adjunction (−⊗W) ⊣ (−⊗W^*), the unit X → X⊗W⊗W^* is built from δ_W and the counit Y⊗W^*⊗W → Y from ev_W, and likewise for (W^*⊗−) ⊣ (W⊗−). No adjunction has a counit 𝟙 → W⊗W^*. With these roles, (2.8) is correct: ⟨ξ⊗ev_W, (g,g′,g″)(δ_W⊗x)⟩ = ⟨ξ, g g′^{−1} g″ x⟩, which matches relation (iv) of §2.2.2. Checked on the page image.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Lemma 4.16, p. 26
issues.printed: Lemma 4.16 assumes simple connectivity of every stratum Y_λ and existence of every parity sheaf E(λ, L) for Y_λ ∈ S. It concludes Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y; O) ⊗_O k ≅ Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y; k).
issues.correction: State the lemma for the non-equivariant categories: Parity^0_S(Y;O) ⊗_O k ≅ Parity^0_S(Y;k). This is all §4.6.3 uses to define BC^(p). A σ-equivariant version holds only on a subcategory whose Hom-lattices M satisfy H^1(⟨σ⟩, M) = 0 and whose objects lift, e.g. the additive closure of the image of Nm. Lemma 4.24 should be stated on such a subcategory.
issues.reason: Counterexample: Y = pt with trivial σ (or the base-point stratum Gr^0_G of Gr_G, whose L^+G⋊σ-equivariant local systems are O[Z/p]-lattices, since the component group of the stabiliser is Z/p). Then σ-equivariant normalized parity sheaves are O[σ]-lattices in degree 0. For I the augmentation ideal, Hom_{O[σ]}(O, I) = I^σ = 0 (the invariants of O[σ] are O·N and ε(N) = p ≠ 0), while Hom_{k[σ]}(k, I ⊗ k) ≠ 0, because the nonzero k[σ]-module I ⊗ k (the augmentation ideal of k[σ]) has nonzero fixed vectors. So reduction is not full. For p ≥ 5 it is also not essentially surjective: the indecomposable O[Z/p]-lattices for unramified O are O, I and O[σ], of ranks 1, p−1 and p, so the Jordan block k[σ]/(σ−1)^2 is not a reduction. The proof's claim that 'all k-local systems on strata lift to O since they are trivial' fails for σ-equivariant local systems on σ-stable strata. Also, the σ-equivariant stratification is not JMW: Ext^2_σ(O,O) = H^2(Z/p;O) = O/p is not free. The σ-equivariant form is used only in Lemma 4.24, where the unlabeled arrow 'exists by the universal property of the categorical tensor product'. Same text in arXiv v6.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Proof of Lemma 4.14, pp. 24–25
issues.printed: The source says a finite L^+G-equivariant filtration of F allows the lemma to be verified on its associated graded, provided that graded object meets the hypotheses. It claims such a filtration exists because Gr^λ_G decomposes as a product of spaces homogeneous under a finite type quotient of L^+H, with graded object a direct sum of F_1 ⊠ … ⊠ F_p for F_i ∈ P_{L^+H}(Gr_H; O).
issues.correction: In the case used (§4.6.3: F a normalized O-parity sheaf, p odd and good) no filtration is needed. F is a direct sum of E(λ_1) ⊠ … ⊠ E(λ_p): an external product of parity sheaves on Gr_G = Gr_H^p is parity, and it is indecomposable since its endomorphism ring is the tensor product of local rings with residue field k. F' = E(λ_1) ⋆ … ⋆ E(λ_p) is parity [JMW16, Theorem 1.5], so its stalks and costalks have O-free cohomology. Nm of a direct sum differs from the sum of the Nm's by induced (free) pieces. The tensor-induction count then applies to H^*(F'_x)^{⊗p} by Künneth; the Koszul signs are harmless for p odd. For F as general as the lemma states, a proof is missing.
issues.reason: Nm is not additive. A filtration of F gives only a σ-stable filtration of Nm(F) with graded pieces Nm(gr_i F) and induced pieces, and i^* is not t-exact, so the stalk cohomology of i^*Nm(F) is tied to the graded pieces only through long exact sequences. Kernels and cokernels of maps between O-free trivial O[σ]-modules need not be O-free (p: O → O has cokernel O/p, whose odd Tate cohomology is k ≠ 0, exactly what (*) must exclude). The text also does not show that the pieces F_1 ⊠ … ⊠ F_p have O-free stalks and costalks. Nor does it show that the convolution F' has O-free stalk cohomology, which the basis-counting step needs. The homogeneity of Gr^λ_G, offered as the reason for the filtration, does not give one.

issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), §4.6.3, p. 26 (last paragraph) and Definition 4.18, p. 27
issues.printed: The source invokes Lemma 4.16 to claim a unique factorization of L ∘ Psm ∘ Nm through Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G; k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H; k). It describes BC^(p) as Frob-semilinear over k and proposes to linearize it.
issues.correction: Add the lemma that Psm ∘ Nm is additive and Frobenius-semilinear on morphisms (proposed as a new coverage item): Psm Nm(f+g) = Psm Nm(f) + Psm Nm(g) and Psm Nm(a f) = a^p Psm Nm(f). The mixed terms of Nm(f+g) form free σ-orbits whose sums are transfers, which factor through induced objects and vanish in the Tate category. Hence L ∘ Psm ∘ Nm kills p·Hom and factors through F as a Frob-semilinear functor.
issues.reason: Nm is not additive on morphisms: Nm(a f) = a^p Nm(f) and Nm(f+g) ≠ Nm(f) + Nm(g). A functor out of Parity^0(Gr_G;O) factors through the full, essentially surjective reduction F (non-equivariant Lemma 4.16) only if it identifies f with f + p·h. Lemma 4.16 is a statement about the source category alone and gives nothing of the kind. §A.3 proves only the object-level isomorphism BC(F ⊕ F') ≅ BC(F) ⊕ BC(F'), and it already presupposes BC^(p). The missing step is the categorical Tate diagonal (the algebra version is Lemma 5.16), so the repair is routine. Same text in arXiv v6.

issues.printed: The source cites [Don93, p. 46] for faithfulness of Rep(Ĥ) → Rep(T_Ĥ) and injectivity on tilting objects, explaining that characters determine tilting modules. issues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), §6.2.3, Proposition 6.3 and Corollary 6.4, case r = 0, pp. 46–47
issues.printed: The source selects a special vertex x ∈ B(G/F_v) in S_G’s apartment. It abbreviates K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r}, also writing U_r = K_r^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} ⊃ H(F_v)_{x,r}. Proposition 6.3 asserts injectivity of U_r\H_v/U_r → K_r\G_v/K_r for r ≥ 0. Corollary 6.4 asserts surjectivity of H(G,K_r;Λ)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} → H(H,U_r;Λ) under r ≥ 0.
issues.correction: State Proposition 6.3 and Corollary 6.4 for r > 0 and any x ∈ B(G/F_v) fixed by Gal(E_v/F_v), for example any x ∈ B(H/F_v). The paper's r > 0 argument proves exactly this, since it uses only that K_r is Gal-stable and pro-ℓ and never that x is special. The case r = 0 is used nowhere: Br needs plain K_r (Lemma 6.6 gives r > 0), Corollaries 6.13 and 6.14 are for r ≥ 1, and Definition 6.11 is a limit over cofinal r. It would need further hypotheses, at least that x be a special vertex of B(H/F_v), because the proof applies the Cartan decomposition of H at x. It is best dropped.
issues.reason: Counterexample at r = 0. Let E_v/F_v be totally ramified cyclic of degree p (tame, as p ≠ ℓ), H = SL_2 and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}SL_2. Then S_G = S_F is the diagonal torus. Take x = the vertex [O_E ⊕ ϖ_E O_E] of the tree of SL_2(E_v). It lies in the diagonal apartment, is special and Gal-fixed, and lies strictly inside the edge of the tree of SL_2(F_v) joining [O_E ⊕ O_E] and [O_E ⊕ ϖ_F O_E]. So H(F_v)_{x,0} = U_0 = K_0 ∩ SL_2(F_v) is the standard Iwahori subgroup I. Let t = diag(ϖ_F, ϖ_F^{-1}) and n = [[0, ϖ_E^{-1}], [−ϖ_E, 0]]. Then n has determinant 1 and preserves O_E ⊕ ϖ_E O_E, so n ∈ K_0, and n t n^{-1} = t^{-1}. Hence K_0 t K_0 = K_0 t^{-1} K_0. But I t I ≠ I t^{-1} I, since t and t^{-1} are distinct elements of the affine Weyl group (Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition). So Proposition 6.3 fails. Every K_0-biinvariant f has f(t) = f(t^{-1}), so 1_{ItI} is not a restriction and Corollary 6.4 fails too. The arXiv v6 text is the same. No erratum is listed on the Cambridge Core article page.

Then B(G/F_v)^{Gal} = B(H/F_v) is a single point, the barycentre of a chamber of B(SL_p/E_v), on which Frobenius acts by the order-p rotation of the affine Dynkin diagram. It is not a vertex. So §§6.3.3–6.4 as written do not construct ℨ_TV for this H, although Theorem 1.4 is stated for every H. The gap is filled because the r > 0 half of the proof of Proposition 6.3 does not use specialness.

issues.printed: The source claims that, for any abelian variety A of dimension 2g, every commutative Q-subalgebra of End(A)⊗Q has dimension at most g. It calls equality complex multiplication (CM), and asserts that End(A) must then be a CM order.
issues.correction: For a g-dimensional abelian variety A, every commutative semisimple Q-subalgebra of End(A) ⊗ Q has dimension at most 2g; A has CM when one of dimension 2g exists, and it is that subalgebra's intersection with End(A), not End(A), which is a CM order (when A is simple, End(A) itself is one).
issues.reason: The bound for a g-dimensional abelian variety is 2g (the subalgebra acts faithfully on H_1(A, Q), of dimension 2g); for the printed '2g-dimensional' A the bound would be 4g, not g. And End(A) need not be commutative: for A = E × E with E having CM by an imaginary quadratic K, End(A) ⊗ Q = M_2(K). The paper only uses abelian varieties L_R/L_Z with O_E-action, for which the intended statement is correct.

issues.locator: Published Invent. Math. 230 (2022), §3.4, splitting discussion pp. 254–255, especially the paragraph after (3.5); compare §3.5, proof of Theorem 3.5, p. 256
issues.printed: The source claims the sequence has a canonical splitting given by KSp(Z) → K(Z)[1/2]^{(+)} as a spectrum map arising from Sp_{2g}(Z) → GL_{2g}(Z).
issues.correction: With the standard unscaled hyperbolic first map H, use (1/2)c_B as retraction after inverting 2. Equivalently, with c_B as projection, take the explicitly rescaled inclusion (1/2)H. Identify the homotopy-orbit summand with the positive eigensummand via p_+ = (1 + ψ^{−1})/2 so the first-map normalization is explicit. The fibre sequence and existence of its splitting, the Witt-group computation and Theorem 3.5 are retained.
issues.reason: The underlying module of H(M) is M ⊕ M^∨, so c_B H = 1 + ψ^{−1}. This equals 2 id on K(Z)[1/2]^{(+)}, rather than id. Already in K_0(Z)[1/2] = Z[1/2], c_B(H([Z])) = 2[Z]. Inverting 2 makes 2 invertible, not equal to 1. The proof on p. 256 explicitly computes the hyperbolic/Betti–Hodge composite as (1 + ψ^{−1},0), corroborating the factor. The affected stated assertion is the map-level retraction in §3.4, not the existence of a splitting or the main Galois-action/universal-extension theorems.

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.6 (arXiv v4 p. 43), published version not re-read (see searched)
issues.printed: The source claims passing from κ to an algebraic closure reduces the proof to algebraically closed κ.
issues.correction: Argue directly: τ-fixed vectors that are F_q-linearly independent are κ-linearly independent (take a shortest relation, apply τ and subtract), so the fixed set has F_q-dimension ≤ dim_κ V_1; injectivity is not needed.
issues.reason: Base change need not preserve injectivity of τ when κ is imperfect: for κ = F_q(t) and τ(a, b) = (a^q + tb^q)e_1, τ is injective on κ² but its extension to κ̄ kills (−t^{1/q}, 1). In the paper's application τ is a Frobenius twist, so the reduction is valid there; Lemma 7.6 and Proposition 7.5 stand.

issues.locator: Lemma 10.5 and its proof (arXiv v4 p. 61), published version not re-read (see searched)
issues.printed: Lemma 10.5 asserts étaleness of w_1, u_1 and h_1. The proof writes j = (u_1, j′_{d−e}, j_e) : A_{d,e} → A_d ×_{X_d} (X′_{d−e} × X_e)^♡ and claims M_{d,e} ≅ M_d ×_{A_d} A_{d,e}, deducing étaleness of w_1 from that of u_1.
issues.correction: u_1 is étale only on the open locus where Div(s) ∩ σDiv(s) = ∅. w_1 and h_1 are étale by a different argument: M_{d,e} is an open substack of M_d ×_{X_d} (X_{d−e} × X_e)^{disj} (pairs of divisors with disjoint support), via the divisor D_{a′} of a point of M_d and E := the preimage in F of the part of F/⊕L_i over D_1; the addition map on disjoint pairs is étale, and requiring the legs to lie over D_2 is open and closed for Hk.
issues.reason: A very good framing only requires ν(D_s) ∩ D_a = ∅, so j′_{d−e} need not land in the ♡ locus. Counterexample for u_1: n = 2, x ∈ X(k) split into x′, σx′, x ∉ D_a, L_1 locally spanned by ϖe_1 and f_1, L_2 by e_2 and ϖf_2; then (⊕L_i)^∨/⊕L_i is k² at x′ and at σx′, and every line ℓ at x′ with ℓ^⊥ at σx′ gives a self-dual E with the same (L_i, a′), Div(s) and D_a. So the fibre of u_1 contains a curve. The isomorphism M_{d,e} ≅ M_d ×_{A_d} A_{d,e} fails even for n = 1 (2^{deg D′} Hermitian F ⊃ L against the single F = E). The only uses are Lemma 10.7 and the smoothness of M_{d,e}, Hk^1_{M_{d,e}}, which need only w_1 and h_1; Theorems 10.1, 10.2 and 1.1 stand.

issues.printed: Theorem 4.2 claims that D_r(G, K), for 1/p ≤ r < 1, is a noetherian Banach integral domain whose norm ‖ ‖_r is multiplicative.
issues.correction: D_r(G, K) has multiplicative norm, and so no zero divisors, for every real 1/p < r < 1 (ST03 Theorem 4.5(i)), and at r = 1/p by ST03 Remark 4.6. It is noetherian for r ∈ p^Q with 1/p < r < 1 (ST03 Theorem 4.5(ii)) and at r = 1/p. Noetherianity at real radii outside p^Q is not proved in the cited source.
issues.reason: The theorem cites 'the main result of [ST03, §4]'. ST03 Theorem 4.5 proves noetherianity only for r ∈ p^Q; the domain property at every interior real radius follows from the multiplicative norm of Theorem 4.5(i). Nothing downstream needs more: Theorem 5.7 uses only the graded ring of ST03 Theorem 4.5(i), and Theorem 5.1 uses the rational radii r = p^{−1/p^n}. The printed statement is therefore unproved as stated at irrational log_p r, although no counterexample is known.

For an arbitrary z (in particular λ^{A₀}_{n−1}z⁽⁰⁾, whose α equals α(z⁽⁰⁾)) pick μ ∈ Λ′ with α(μz) large; since Λ′μ ⊂ Λ′, M(z, a) ≥ M(μz, a − d_μ) with d_μ = log log(μz)_n − log log z_n, so c⋆(z) ≥ e^{−βd_μ}c⋆(μz) > 0, and then c > 0 in Theorem 3. issues.printed: (7.5) tr(Frob_z, V(Π,V)) = tr(Frob_z^n, V(Π,𝔳_1)) = Σ_j tr(Frob_z^n, L_j) = Σ_j tr(Frob_1^n, L_j)·tr(m_z^{−n}, L_j). … (7.6) tr(m_z, L_j) = μ(z)^{⟨α,β_j⟩} … 0 = Σ_{z∈k^×} μ(z)^{−2}·tr(Frob_z, V(Π,V)) = Σ_{z∈k^×} μ(z)^{−2}·Σ_j tr(Frob_1^n, L_j)·μ(z)^{⟨α,β_j⟩} = … = (q − 1)·Σ_{j : ⟨α,β_j⟩ ≡ 2 mod (q−1)} tr(Frob_1^n, L_j). (7.7)
issues.correction: By (7.6), tr(m_z^{−n}, L_j) = μ(z)^{−n⟨α,β_j⟩}, so constancy of z ↦ tr(Frob_z, V(Π,V)) gives Σ_j A_j ν(z)^{c_j} = const with ν = μ^{−n} and c_j = ⟨α,β_j⟩ ∈ {−2, …, 2}. Pairing with ν^{−2} isolates the highest-root term exactly when ν^2 differs from ν^c for c ∈ {−2, −1, 0, 1}, that is when d = (q − 1)/gcd(n, q − 1) ≥ 5 (always true for n = 1 and q > 5, where the printed argument works up to a sign). For d ≤ 4 another argument is needed, for example reducing a Weil restriction Res_{k_n/k} G′ to G′ over k_n((t)), or choosing χ_k on T(k) = T′(k_n) through a faithful character of k_n^× instead of μ ∘ α.
issues.reason: Over k_n, Lemma 4.7 applies to Frob_z^n and to the inertia element acting on T^{1/(q^n−1)} by z, which acts on T^{1/(q−1)} by z^n; so the exponent is −n⟨α,β_j⟩, as (7.5) itself records with tr(m_z^{−n}, L_j), but (7.7) substitutes μ(z)^{⟨α,β_j⟩}. The case n ≥ 2 is in scope: after the reduction of Theorem 7.1, G is k-simple, and the tensor induction over the W_k-orbit 𝔳_1, …, 𝔳_n is there precisely to handle n > 1. Example: q = 7, n = 2, G = Res_{F_49/F_7} SL_3. Then ν = μ^{−2} has order 3, and the values of c on 𝔳_1 are 2, 1, 1, 0, 0, −1, −1, −2. Since ν^{−1} = ν^2 and ν^{−2} = ν, constancy gives only A_2 + A_{−1} = 0 and A_1 + A_{−2} = 0 (A_c summing tr(Frob_1^2, L_j) over c_j = c), not A_2 = 0, and no contradiction follows. The theorem is not contradicted; its printed proof does not cover such G.

issues.printed: Theorem 7.12 takes F = k((t)), G reductive and unramified over F, and σ irreducible for G(F), and concludes that σ occurs irreducibly in a principal series that is unramified. issues.locator: Corollary 2.4(iii) and its proof p.7; published 2024 version
issues.printed: The source calls assertion three obvious.
issues.correction: Supply a torality argument using an additional property of these particular automorphic parameters, or an appropriate connectedness hypothesis. Abelian semisimple image alone does not imply containment in a maximal torus of a reductive group.
issues.reason: In PGL₂(ℂ), the classes of diag(1,−1) and [[0,1],[1,0]] commute (their lifts anticommute), generate a Klein four group, and are semisimple. In any faithful algebraic representation their finite abelian action is completely reducible into characters. They cannot lie in a rank-one torus, whose finite subgroups are cyclic. This refutes the general algebraic inference used as obvious; it does not construct a cuspidal automorphic Π with that parameter, so the verdict is a proof gap rather than a claimed counterexample to the automorphic corollary.

issues.citation: Gan–Ichino, "The Shimura–Waldspurger correspondence for Mp_2n", Annals of Mathematics 188 (2018), no. 3
issues.reviewReason: I read Gan–Savin (Compos. Math. 148 (2012), PDF from Cambridge Core). Prop. 7.3 (p. 1674) gives the J_r with GL(Y_{k−r}) acting by |det_{Y_{k−r}}|^{(k−r)/2}. The whole proof of Lemma 7.4 (p. 1675) reads: 'the center of GL(Y_{k−r}) acts by the character |det|^{−s+t_1} … whereas on S(Isom(Y′_r, X_r)) ⊗ Ω_{V_{n−k},W_{n−r}}, GL(Y_{k−r}) acts by |det|^{(k−r)/2} … Since −s + t_1 ⩽ 0 and k − r > 0, we deduce that the above Hom space must be 0.' Only the inequality −s + t_1 ≠ (k − r)/2 is used, and it holds as soon as s > −1/2. Gan–Ichino need exactly this range. After arranging π = Ind_P̃(τ̃_ψ ⊗ π_0) as a standard module, τ has blocks δ_i|det|^{s_i} with δ_i unitary square-integrable and 0 < s_i < 1/2. The embedding σ = Ind_Q(τ ⊗ σ_0) therefore puts Gan–Savin's s at −s_i ∈ (−1/2, 0), block by block, as in the proof of Gan–Savin Th. 8.1(iii). The remark 'which continues to hold for s > −1/2' is a correct and immediate observation, not a step without adequate proof. Even as a gap it would affect nothing: the paper proves the p-adic case of Lemma 5.2 by citing Atobe (Math. Ann. 371, Th. 3.13) and gives this argument only 'for the convenience of the reader'. The extraction's kind (gap) and affects (the proof) should therefore be withdrawn, along with the matching sentence in the lemma-5-2 note.

issues.reviewReason: Checked on the page image of p. 992 and against the sources. (1) F = R: Adams–Barbasch, Compos. Math. 113, §8 (read in the authors' preprint, whose Theorem 8.4 is 'Induction Principle I') works with 'an orthogonal space of signature (p, q) and W a symplectic space of dimension 2n, with no further restrictions' and arbitrary Levi decompositions. For any σ ⊗ σ′ that is a quotient of the Levi Weil representation ω_M it gives a nonzero Õ(V) × Mp(W)-map ω → Ind(σξ) ⊗ Ind(σ′ξ′). This literally covers the real stable-range pair (Mp_2n(R), O(r + 1, r)); the extraction's 'for the real metaplectic group' reading (equal rank only) is wrong. (2) F = C: Adams–Barbasch, J. Funct. Anal. 132, Cor. 3.21 (complex dual pairs; Mp_2n(C) is split). (3) F p-adic: Kudla's paper (read at GDZ) treats every dual pair (O(V_m), Mp(W_n)) of type (O, Sp), with its Jacquet-module filtration (Th. 2.8) and the cuspidal-support theorem (Th. 2.5), but it does not state the 'nonzero map to Ind ⊗ Ind' form. Adams–Barbasch say their proof 'is essentially the same as the proofs of ([Kudla], Theorem 2.5) and ([AB complex], Corollary 3.21)', and it carries over verbatim: a Levi-equivariant surjection ω ↠ ω_M ν from a mixed model (their Lemmas 8.5–8.6), a nonzero GL_k × GL_k-map S(M_k) → τ ⊗ τ^∨ (a Godement–Jacquet zeta integral), the quotient π_{η_0} ⊗ σ̃_{η′_0} of the smaller Weil representation, and Frobenius reciprocity. None of these steps uses the stable range, temperedness or A-packets. The passage from O(V) to SO(V) is (2.1). Consistency check: the matching τ̃_ψ = τ ⊗ χ_ψ against τ agrees with Kudla's Th. 2.5 ([π′] = [χ_V θ(σ_1), …], θ(σ) ≅ σ) and with the unramified correspondence (3.2). So 'easily extends' is accurate. What remains is at most an imprecise citation for p-adic F, which does not meet the protocol's definition of a gap (a step asserted without an adequate proof).

issues.reviewReason: The quotation is exact. I read Ichino–Lapid–Mao (arXiv:1404.2909v2; the Duke version GI cite is behind a subscription). Their Appendix A states the analogue explicitly on p. 27: 'We now treat the metaplectic group G̃ = Mp_n ... The above analysis works with obvious modifications. (See [BJ13] for the Langlands quotient theorem in this context.) In particular, the analogue of Lemma A.2 holds for G̃. (The half-integrality of R(δ) for generic square-integrable representations follows from the results of [GS12] and the corresponding statement for SO(2n+1).)' ILM's Cor. A.8 for Mp_n uses it. So GI cite a stated result, and the extraction's 'invoked without an argument' does not hold. The argument transfers. The proof of ILM Lemma A.2 uses Tadić's results on characters and the topology of the unitary dual (valid for finite central covers), the Langlands classification (Ban–Jantzen for covers), and half-integrality of cuspidal exponents of generic discrete series; this last holds for Mp, since the reducibility points for ψ-generic cuspidal data lie in {0, 1/2, 1, 3/2} (Bakić–Hanzer, arXiv:1902.07357, Prop. 3.5). With λ_m ∈ [−c, c]^k and c < 1/2 this forces λ_m → 0. Isolation of a square-integrable π_S is the case L = G of Lemma A.2, and the product over v ∈ S is immediate. So the recorded kind ('gap'), affects ('the proof') and correction are not right: there is no gap here. The same sentence's other input, {Π_{i,S}} ⊂ Irr_{≤c} via the cuspidality of Θ^aut_ψ(Π_i), does fail in the generality printed; that is recorded as the new issue.

issues.locator: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 978 (arXiv v3 p. 11; same text)
issues.printed: The source cites [93, Th. 9.1] for holomorphy of L^S_ψ(s, π) when Re s > n+1. Using (3.3), it claims holomorphy of L^S(s, θ^abs_ψ(π)) in Re s > r − n + 1/2, together with a pole located at s = r − n + 1/2.
issues.correction: Add that L^S_ψ(r − n + 1/2, π) ≠ 0. One route is absolute convergence of the Euler product L^S_ψ(s, π) = ∏_{v∉S} L(s, ϕ_v) for Re s > c + 1, where |Re s_{i,v}| ≤ c bounds the Satake exponents of the unitary unramified π_v uniformly in v; the bound c = n gives the printed range r > 2n + 1. A bound that avoids spherical-function theory on the cover: θ_{ψ_v}(π_v) to SO_{2r_0+1}, with r_0 = 2n + 2, is unitary (Li, Invent. Math. 97) and unramified with exponents {s_{i,v}} ∪ {r_0 − n − 1/2, …}. The unitarity bound for spherical representations of split groups then gives |Re s_{i,v}| ≤ r_0 − 1/2, and it is enough to run the proof with r > 3n + 2, which is allowed because the proof only needs some large r. If [93, Th. 9.1] in fact states absolute convergence, the fix is only to say so.
issues.reason: In (3.3), the factor ζ^S(s + r − n + 1/2 − j) with j = 2r − 2n has a simple pole at s = r − n + 1/2. The other ζ^S factors are evaluated there at 2, 3, …, 2r − 2n, so they are finite and nonzero. So L^S(s, θ^abs_ψ(π)) has a pole at r − n + 1/2 exactly when L^S_ψ(r − n + 1/2, π) ≠ 0. Holomorphy of L^S_ψ on Re s > n + 1, which is all the text invokes, does not exclude a zero at r − n + 1/2 > n + 1. The pole is essential: it is what shows that φ′ contains S_{2t} with t ≥ r − n. The rest of the argument is complete (see the status_comment on prop-3-1 for the dimension count behind the 'largest t' step), and Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 1.1 stand once the nonvanishing is supplied. [93] (Yamana, Invent. Math. 196) could not be consulted; the paper cites it for holomorphy only.
