issues.locator: Proposition 4.2.9, published p. 91; arXiv v4 p. 67
issues.printed: The source bounds the dimension of Ext¹_G(L(θ), L(λ)) by one. It asserts dimension one exactly when λ and θ are linked and occupy adjacent alcoves: some i₀ ∈ 𝒥 satisfies λ_i = θ_i whenever i ≠ i₀, while λ_{i₀} and θ_{i₀} belong to distinct alcoves with a common face.
issues.correction: Replace 'lie in different alcoves sharing a face' by the actual Ext¹ pattern (as in [And87, §4.1] and Table 6). In Table 5 labels the nonzero pairs among {A,…,G} are A–B, A–E, A–F, B–C, B–D, C–E, C–F, D–E, D–F, E–G, F–G. Alternatively, state only what is used: Ext¹ ≠ 0 forces λ_i = θ_i for i ≠ i₀, and dim Ext¹ ≤ 1.
issues.reason: Counterexample from the paper's own results. Take f = 1 and λ 6-deep in A, and let θ := w̃_E·λ = (12)t_{α₂}·λ, which lies in E and is 6-deep. By Lemma 4.2.6's proof and Table 5 (row E), L(θ) is a summand of gr₁Q₁(λ). By (4.8) (ξ = 0), Q₁(λ) is injective among p-bounded modules, so Ext¹_G(L(θ), L(λ)) ≅ Hom_G(L(θ), gr₁Q₁(λ)) ≠ 0. But A ⊂ (0,p)³ and E ⊂ (0,p)×(p,2p)×(2p,3p) (pairings with α₁^∨, α₂^∨, α₀^∨) share no face, not even a vertex. Table 6 likewise draws arrows A–E, A–F, C–F and D–E between non-adjacent alcoves. In the paper's defence, the proof of Proposition 4.2.12 (p. 94) uses the correct pattern ('λ_{i₀} ∈ D ⇒ θ_{i₀} ∈ E or F; λ_{i₀} ∈ F ⇒ θ_{i₀} ∈ C, D or G', matching Table 6), and the other uses (uniqueness of M, existence of i₀) only need dim ≤ 1 and the Künneth reduction, so the downstream results are unaffected. Independent check: Statement checked on p. 91. Encode an alcove by (⌊⟨x+η,α1^∨⟩/p⌋, ⌊⟨x+η,α2^∨⟩/p⌋, ⌊⟨x+η,α0^∨⟩/p⌋). Table 5 and Table 6 then give: A = (0,0,0), B = (0,0,1), {C,D} = {(1,0,1),(0,1,1)}, {E,F} = {(1,0,2),(0,1,2)}, G = (1,1,2). With Table 6's own weights, C = (1,0,1), D = (0,1,1), E = (1,0,2), F = (0,1,2); Table 5's permutation convention swaps the letters but not the geometry. Two of these alcoves share a face iff their triples differ in exactly one entry by 1. So A shares a face only with B, and A–E, A–F, C–F and D–E are non-adjacent pairs. The closures of A and E are disjoint (α0-pairings in (0,p) and (2p,3p)). The paper itself gives nonzero Ext¹ for these pairs. On p. 93, 'gr₁Q₁(λ⁰_{i₀}) is the direct sum of three irreducible modules in alcoves … B, E, and F if λ⁰_{i₀} is in alcove A'. Table 6 (second diagram) puts A = L(μ) in the socle of V(μ^op+pη′) ⊂ Q₁(μ) with E and F in the next layer, and the first diagram has edges A–E, A–F, C–F and D–E. Since Q₁(λ) has simple socle L(λ), each L(θ) ⊂ gr₁Q₁(λ) gives a nonsplit extension, so Ext¹_G(L(θ),L(λ)) ≠ 0. This holds for 6-deep λ ∈ A and θ = w̃_E·λ ∈ E, so the 'only if' direction is false. Every face-sharing pair in {A,…,G} is an edge of Table 6, so the 'if' direction and dim ⩽ 1 are not contradicted. The proof of Proposition 4.2.12 (p. 94) cites 4.2.9 for 'λ_{i₀} in D (resp. F) ⇒ θ_{i₀} in E or F (resp. C, D, or G)'. That is the Table 6 pattern, not face-sharing (D shares a face with only one of E, F, and F none with C), so the downstream arguments are unaffected. Versions: new in v4 (p. 67) with the same wording; v3 instead asserted existence of i₀ and uniqueness of M, citing [Hum06, §12.6].

For Q₁(λ⁰)⊗L(pω_λ), argue directly: (i) its G-socle is L(λ⁰+pω_λ) (the G₁-socle is L₁(λ⁰)⊗L(pω_λ)); (ii) the tensor filtration 𝓕 = soc_•(Q₁(λ⁰))⊗L(pω_λ) is semisimple with semisimple restrictions (Lemma 4.2.4(1)), and its restriction is a Loewy series of the rigid G-module ⊕Inj(F(λ⁰+ε)). Then 𝓕_k ⊆ soc_k and soc_k|_G ⊆ soc_k(−|_G) = 𝓕_k|_G give 𝓕 = soc_•.
issues.reason: Lemma 4.2.2 requires p-boundedness (⟨κ, α^∨⟩ < 2(h−1)p = 4p for GL₃). Q₁(λ⁰)⊗L(pω_λ) has highest weight 2(p−1)ρ + w₀λ⁰ + pω_λ, with α₀^∨-pairing 4(p−1) − ⟨λ⁰, α₀^∨⟩ + p⟨ω_λ, α₀^∨⟩. For λ⁰ in the lowest alcove (⟨λ⁰, α₀^∨⟩ < p−8) and ω_λ = ε′₁ or ε′₂ (λ in alcove C or D, which occur as socles of M in V_μ), this exceeds 4p+4, so the module is not p-bounded. issues.reason: Lemma 4.2.6 is stated for σ = F(μ) with μ 6-deep, via Corollary 4.2.3, which needs Q₁(μ) 3(h−1) = 6-deep. By Lemma 4.2.5, μ 6-deep only makes V_μ|_G 4-deep: e.g. the top-layer constituents F(μ^op + root) lose 2, and the gr₁/gr₂ constituents F(μ^op + minuscule) lose 1. So condition (3) for Γ(U) in the proof of Theorem 4.2.7(3), and the 'unique by Lemma 4.2.6' in Proposition 4.2.10, apply Lemma 4.2.6 to Serre weights that are only 4- or 5-deep. In the proof of Proposition 4.2.10, the modules M′_j have weights λ⁰ + pω_{λ,i₀} + wπε with ε ∈ L(ω^{i₀}), |⟨ε, α^∨⟩| ≤ 2, so they are 4-deep. Proposition 4.2.12 is then applied to them although its proof uses Lemma 4.2.2 and Corollary 4.2.3 (6-deep). In the paper's defence, every downstream use is under Theorem 4.1.9's hypothesis that R is 13-generic, which makes μ 13-deep and all constituents at least 11-deep, so the main theorems are unaffected. Only the depth thresholds stated in Theorem 4.2.7(3), Propositions 4.2.10 and 4.2.15 and Lemma 4.2.14 are not justified by the given proofs. Independent check: Checked on pp. 84–98. Lemma 4.2.6 needs σ = F(μ) with μ 6-deep, because its proof uses Corollary 4.2.3, which needs Q₁(μ) to be 3(h−1) = 6-deep. Lemma 4.2.5 only gives that the constituents of V_μ|_G (and of M|_G) are (n−2)-deep when μ is n-deep. This is sharp: the constituents F(w̃₊·μ+ω) with ω a root lose 2. (1) In the proof of Theorem 4.2.7(3) with μ 6-deep, condition (3) for Γ(U) is derived 'from Lemmas 4.2.5 and 4.2.6'. But Lemma 4.2.5 gives only 4-deep weights, below the threshold of Lemma 4.2.6. (2) In Proposition 4.2.10, λ and θ are 6-deep (p. 91), but F₀ = F(λ⁰+ε_λ) and F₁ can be only 4-deep. So 'unique up to isomorphism by Lemma 4.2.6' is not covered. In the proof of Proposition 4.2.12, the step (gr₁Q₁(λ′))|_G ≅ gr₁Inj(F₀) with λ′ = λ⁰+ε_λ uses Corollary 4.2.3, which needs 6-deep. The modules M′_j in the proof of 4.2.10 have weights shifted by πε^{i₀} (|⟨ε,α^∨⟩| ⩽ 2), so they are only 4-deep, and Proposition 4.2.12 (Lemmas 4.2.11 and 4.2.2) is applied to them. (3) Proposition 4.2.15 uses Theorem 4.2.7(3) (the length 9^f), so it inherits the gap. Lemma 4.2.14 is not affected: its proof uses only Theorem 4.2.7(2), U from Lemma 4.2.8 (2-deep) and Theorem 4.2.1. Downstream, Theorem 4.2.16 assumes the hypotheses of Theorem 4.1.9 (R 13-generic). So τ'_S may be only (13−2)-generic. Lemma 5.1.3 uses Proposition 4.3.7 and Theorem 4.1.9 for σ(τ'_S), both stated for 13-generic representations, and the proof of Theorem 4.1.9 through Prop. 4.3.7 needs 13 to produce an auxiliary 10-generic ρ̄ (13 − 3). This δ lies in the root lattice mod X⁰, because Adm(η) ⊂ t_ηW_a and η ≡ η′ = α0 mod X⁰. A nonzero element of the A2 root lattice pairs with some coroot to absolute value at least 2. So whenever the parameter moves, a 13-generic τ_S only guarantees that τ′_S is 11-generic (take μ exactly 13-deep on the relevant wall). The parameter does move in cases the proof needs. Example: in the n = 0 case of Lemma 5.1.4 with w̃*_i = id and σ_i = (ε1,1), a finite w′ of length ⩾ 2 cannot work, because (ε1,1) ∈ w′^{−1}(Σ0) forces w′(ε1) ∈ {0,ε1,ε2} ∩ Wε1 = {ε1}, hence w′ ∈ {1,β}. The readers' enumeration (checked by rerunning it and against the definitions on pp. 18–20, including that W̃ acts only on the first factor of Λ_W×A) gives γβ, βγ, βγβ with shift of spread 2, and for (5.5) with w̃* = α it forces γα with spread 2. issues.locator: §5.1, proofs of Lemma 5.1.4 (n = 0) and Lemma 5.1.5, published pp. 113–114; arXiv v4 pp. 85–86
issues.printed: The source invokes (5.5) and Theorem 4.1.9 to assert that the surjection σ̄(τ_S)^σ ↠ V persists.
issues.correction: V is defined as a quotient of σ̄(τ_S)^σ. To apply Lemma 5.1.3 (resp. the induction) for another type τ'_S one needs V to be isomorphic, as a G-module, to a quotient of σ̄(τ'_S)^σ. Theorem 4.1.9 and Proposition 4.1.1 only give that the quotient of σ̄(τ'_S)^σ with Jordan–Hölder set JH(V) exists and has the same pointing graph. An argument that the two multiplicity-free modules (same cosocle, constituents and extension graph, coming from lattices in different Deligne–Lusztig representations) are isomorphic is missing.
issues.reason: Two multiplicity-free modules with the same constituents and the same Γ need not be isomorphic in general (e.g. a 'diamond' σ over κ1 ⊕ κ2 over κ carries a gluing parameter when the relevant Yoneda products in Ext^2 vanish). So 'by Theorem 4.1.9' does not suffice as stated. Defence: the claim is very plausibly true for these specific modules, for instance via multiplicity-one statements in projective envelopes as in Lemma 4.2.14, or via the Weyl-module embedding of §4.2.4. EGS15 handles the analogous GL2 step at the level of patched modules (proof of their Lemma 10.1.12). Independent check: Checked on pp. 111–114. Lemma 5.1.3 (applied to τ′_S in the n = 0 case of Lemma 5.1.4) and the induction after the type change in Lemma 5.1.5 both need V itself to be a quotient of σ̄(τ′_S)^σ. V is given as a quotient of σ̄(τ_S)^σ. Theorem 4.1.9 with Propositions 4.1.1–4.1.2 yields only a quotient V″ of σ̄(τ′_S)^σ with JH(V″) = JH(V) and the same graph Γ. I found nothing in the paper showing that a multiplicity-free module with cosocle σ is determined by JH and Γ; a search for such a uniqueness statement came up empty. In general it is not: in a 'diamond' σ over κ1⊕κ2 over κ with vanishing Yoneda products in Ext², the two extension classes glue with a free parameter. Lemma 3.6.2 does not rescue the argument either. It makes M∞(V) ≅ R∞/I(V) depend only on JH(V) once M∞(V) is cyclic, but cyclicity is the point at issue, and two MCM modules with the same reduced support need not both be cyclic. For f = 1 the small V's in the n = 0 case are determined (Ext¹ is one-dimensional), so the problem arises from f ⩾ 2 or larger V. EGS15 (Lemma 10.1.12) identify the lattice explicitly for the analogous GL2 step, but only in length 2. The claim is very plausible, but the justification 'by (5.5) and Theorem 4.1.9' is incomplete.

issues.locator: §5.1, proof of Lemma 5.1.5 (n > 0), published p. 115; arXiv v4 p. 86
issues.printed: The proof asserts the existence of V^2 ⊂ V with #Σ_{V^2,i'} = #(Σ_{V^2,i'} ∩ r(Σ_0)) = 2 and, whenever i ≠ i', Σ_{V^2,i} = Σ_{V,i}. It says that induction verifies the cyclicity of M_∞(V^2).
issues.correction: V^2 is a quotient of σ̄(τ_S)^{σ''} with σ'' = cosoc(V^2), whose i'-component lies in the lower alcove (a = 0) although ℓ(w̃^*_{i'}) ⩽ 1. So σ'' violates (5.1), and the inductive hypothesis — Lemmas 5.1.4–5.1.5 for weights satisfying (5.1) — does not literally apply. The argument of Lemma 5.1.4 extends, because only the shape of Σ_{V^2,i'} ⊂ {(ω,1),(0,0),(ε1,0),(ε2,0)} is used, but this should be stated.
issues.reason: Checked by computer: in every case with #(Σ_{V,i'} ∩ r(Σ_0)) = 5, the admissible V^2 at i' are {(x,0), (w̃^*_{i'})^{−1}(ν4,1)} with x ∈ {0, ε1, ε2} and (x,0) pointing to the sink. Defence: the authors flag the step as 'one can check', and the extension is routine. Independent check: Checked on p. 115. The standing assumption (p. 111: 'we assume that the weight σ satisfies the conditions of Theorem 5.1.1', and p. 112) is that V is a quotient of σ̄(τ_S)^σ with σ satisfying (5.1), i.e. a_i = 1 whenever ℓ(w̃_i^*) ⩽ 1 (Proposition 2.1.3(1): Tr_μ(ω,a) lies in alcove π^{−1}(a)). The paper puts (w̃*_{i′})^{−1}(ν4,1) in Σ_{V²,i′} as a socle constituent, and Σ_{V²,i′} has exactly 2 elements. In the extension graph, adjacent vertices have different a. So the other i′-constituent, which must point to it for V² to have simple cosocle, has a = 0. But ℓ(w̃*_{i′}) ⩽ 1 (this is forced by #(Σ_{V,i′}∩r(Σ0)) = 5; ℓ ⩾ 2 rows of Table 3 have at most 4 predicted weights). So cosoc(V²) violates (5.1). If V² had non-simple cosocle it would not be a quotient of any σ̄(τ_S)^{σ″}, which is even further from the hypothesis. Either way, 'by the inductive hypothesis' does not literally apply. The argument of Lemma 5.1.4 plausibly extends, since only the shape of Σ_{V²,i′} matters, but this is not stated. A minor gap.

issues.locator: §5.3, ring homomorphism before (5.8), published p. 123; arXiv v4 p. 92
issues.printed: The source asserts a ring map R∞ = ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□[[x₁, …, x_h]] → 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪. Here 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺}) means the image of 𝕋^univ inside End_𝒪(S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W_{Σ₀⁺})). The notation 𝔪 also denotes the inverse image in R∞ of the target’s maximal ideal.
issues.correction: The target should be the Hecke algebra at tame level U^p acting on completed cohomology S̃(U^p, W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪 (or on all S(U^pU_p, W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ V)_𝔪), as in [CEG+16, §2.8]; in any case 𝔪 ⊂ R∞ is simply the maximal ideal of the local ring R∞.
issues.reason: As printed, 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺}) acts on forms of trivial weight at p. S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W̄_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪 ≠ 0 would mean that the trivial K-representation lies in W(r̄); by Theorem 5.3.3, W(r̄) = W?(ρ̄_𝒮), which for 10-generic ρ̄_𝒮 does not contain the trivial weight (F(0) is not 1-deep). Hence S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪 = 0 (Nakayama), the printed Hecke algebra is the zero ring and 'its maximal ideal' does not exist. Defence: only 𝔪 ⊂ R∞ is used later ((5.8), Theorem 5.3.4), and the pullback of the maximal ideal of any nonzero local quotient is the maximal ideal of R∞.

issues.locator: §5.3.1, proof of Theorem 5.3.1, published p. 124; cf. §6(16), published p. 130; arXiv v4 pp. 92, 98
issues.printed: The source claims that Theorems 5.3.3 and 3.5.3 allow the argument for [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] to be applied without modification.
issues.correction: The proof of Theorem 5.3.1 should be given (or a reference to a published proof), since by the authors' own §6(16) 'The proof of Theorem 7.4 [of LLHLM18], which was omitted, uses the same techniques' as the level-lowering Proposition 6.0.2.
issues.reason: Theorem 5.3.1 is proved only by reference to the proof of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4], which §6(16) states was omitted in [LLHLM18]. Theorem 5.3.5 also invokes Theorem 5.3.1 (for S̃(U^p,W)[λ] ≠ 0). Defence: the argument is the standard Taylor–Wiles–Kisin one (patching with M̃∞, irreducibility of the generic fibre from Theorem 3.5.3, nonvanishing from Theorem 5.3.3, level changing à la [Tay08]), and §6(16) indicates the techniques; experts can reconstruct it. Independent check: Checked on p. 124: the entire proof of Theorem 5.3.1 is 'Given Theorems 5.3.3 and 3.5.3, the proof of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] goes through unchanged.' On p. 130, §6(16) (the addendum to [LLHLM18]) says: 'The proof of Theorem 7.4, which was omitted, uses the same techniques' (as the level-lowering Proposition 6.0.2, based on [Tay08]). So the automorphy lifting theorem is proved by reference to a proof that, by the authors' own statement, does not appear in [LLHLM18]. Theorem 5.3.5 uses Theorem 5.3.1 (p. 125, 'S̃(U^p,W)[λ] is nonzero'). The argument is a standard Taylor–Wiles–Kisin one, and the needed local inputs (Theorems 3.5.3 and 5.3.3) are proved here, so the result is not in doubt. The written record has a missing proof, not a known error. Versions: the proof sentence is in v3 and v4 (v4 p. 92) and similar in v1/v2; the 'which was omitted' admission is in v4 (p. 98).

issues.printed: The source gives Lie G_n ≅ gl_n × gl_1, then defines ad r̄ : Γ → Aut_A(gl_n(A)) using the projection Lie G_n ↠ gl_n.

issues.printed: The source takes compact open U = U_p U^{∞,p} ≤ G(O_p) × G(A^{∞,p}_{F+}) and a finite O-module W with continuous U_p-action. It then takes W to be an O-lattice in ⊗_{v∈S_p} σ(λ_v, τ_v)^* ∘ ι_v and concludes that r(U,W)_mQ has type S, with D_v = D_ρ̄_v^{λ_v,τ_v} for v ∈ S_p.

The appendix's own application (§A.6, PDF201) is at level G(O_p), so its conclusions stand.

issues.reason: Over C let G=C2*C2=<s,t|s²=t²=1>. Put rho_a(s)=diag(1,−1) and rho_a(t)=[[a,1],[1−a²,−a]] for a=0,2. Both matrices are involutions with eigenvalues1,−1. issues.locator: Printed32/PDF36, remark(ii) following Theorem4.1; supplementary author notes, not a statement in LLHLM23. Published book text not independently matched.
issues.printed: The source claims the dimension would be n!.
issues.correction: Do not assert dimension n! for all irreducible admissible archimedean representations. A dimension theorem needs a restricted representation class and an exact algebraic Whittaker convention. For this application use the continuous functional constructed by the integral; no algebraic dimension count is needed.
issues.reason: Take the one-dimensional trivial irreducible admissible representation of GL_2(R). On its Harish–Chandra module the positive-root Lie algebra acts by zero. For ψ(x)=exp(2πix), an algebraic Whittaker functional λ would satisfy 0=λ(dπ(E12)v)=dψ(E12)λ(v)=2πiλ(v), so λ=0. Thus the dimension is zero, not 2!=2. The group-equivariant version likewise vanishes since ψ is nontrivial. This disproves the unqualified generality; it does not dispute a theorem for an appropriately restricted generic/principal-series class.

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma 8.4.11, fourth sentence, PDF 174 (page image)

By the Deligne–Lusztig character formula (R_T^θ·χ_V = R_T^{θ·χ_V|_T}), σ(τ) ⊗ V(λ) is a sum of Deligne–Lusztig representations whose parameters are shifted by the weights of V(λ). issues.locator: Proposition B.0.2(2) proof, PDF206 (page image checked); components of the special fibre listed on PDF206
issues.printed: The source seeks O-flatness of U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm, starting with its topological flatness over O. It later invokes [69, Proposition 8.2] to deduce normality of U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm from O-flatness and a reduced special fiber.
issues.correction: Supply two missing checks. Write U = U(z̃,λ,∇_{(a,b,0)}) and U^nm for its partial normalization. (a) Topological flatness. By the identification O(U(z̃,λ,∇)^nm) = O(U(z̃,λ,∇))[−t d21/c22] stated on PDF204, the element W is integral over the chart, with unit leading coefficient (a−1)(b−1)(a−b). Since O(U(z̃,λ,∇))[1/t] is a regular domain (proof of Proposition B.0.1), W lies in it, so U^nm[1/p] ≅ U[1/p]. Let Z be the closure of the generic fibre in U^nm. Z is O-flat and finite over U, and it maps onto U because U is O-flat (part (1)). Z_F is equidimensional of dimension 3 and dominates each of the seven components of U_F. The seven components of U^nm_F listed on PDF206 all have dimension 3 = dim U_F, and by Table 1 each is the only top-dimensional component over its image. So Z_F contains all of them, and Z_F = U^nm_F as sets. (b) Normal generic fibre, which the criterion of [69] also needs: U^nm[1/p] ≅ U[1/p] is the fibre over (−p,a,b) of U(z̃,λ,∇)|_{X^0×V}. That scheme is open in (P_λ\GL_n) × X^0 × A^2 by Proposition 3.3.4 (U19), the input already used in the proof of Proposition B.0.1, so the fibre is smooth over E.
issues.reason: Topological flatness is not formal here. U^nm → U is an isomorphism only where c22 ≠ 0, and four of the seven components of U^nm_F listed on PDF206 lie in V(c22): (c22, …), (d31, c22, d21, W), (c22, d21, c12, …) and (c22, c13, c12, …). The O-flatness step (a ϖ-power-torsion function would be nilpotent) rests on it. A scheme that is flat over O with reduced special fibre is normal only if its generic fibre is normal, and the proof never checks this. Both checks can be supplied as above, so the proposition stands. Reach: Corollary B.0.4 (Q10), Corollary B.0.5 (Q11) and Remark B.0.6 (Q12) use part (2).

issues.printed: For a dominant cocharacter λ ∈ X_*(T^∨), the theorem assumes h_λ-genericity of ā = a mod ϖ ∈ F^n. It asserts that w̃ ↦ closure(S°_F(w̃^*) ∩ Fl^{∇a}) naturally bijects Adm^reg(λ) with the irreducible components of maximal dimension in M^nv(≤λ,∇_a)_F.

issues.reason: Take GL_3 and λ = (1,0,0), which is dominant with h_λ = 1. Every element of Adm(λ) has length ≤ ℓ(t_λ) = 2. A regular element has the form w̃2^{-1}w0t_νw̃1, a reduced product (Proposition 2.1.5, Lemma 2.1.4), so its length is ≥ ℓ(w0) = 3. Hence Adm^reg(λ) = ∅. Yet M^nv(≤λ,∇_a)_F contains the nonempty affine spaces S°_F(w̃^*) ∩ Fl^{∇a} of Theorem 4.2.4 (e.g. w̃ = t_λ), so it has top-dimensional components, all of dimension < d. For regular λ, t_λ ∈ Adm^reg(λ), so the two readings agree. The only later use, Theorem 4.3.10, assumes λ regular.

(i) I = 1+v ∈ I_1(F) has φ(I) = 1+v^p ≢ 1 mod v^{m+1} for m ≥ p, contradicting Lemma 5.1.10(a), (b) with k = 1, and (d) with Y = v. With A_1 = 1 and A_2 = v^{p−1} (both in L^{[0,h]}GL_1 when h ≥ p−1) and I^{(j)} = v^{−1} for all j, A_2z̃_j = I^{(j)}A_1z̃_jφ(I^{(j−1)})^{−1} holds but I ∉ I_F(R), contradicting Lemma 5.4.4. (iii) For K = Q_p, τ trivial and h ≥ p−1, the rank-one Breuil–Kisin modules with Frobenius 1 and v^{p−1} are not isomorphic, but their étale φ-modules are (e ↦ ve). So ε_τ is not a monomorphism, contradicting Proposition 5.4.3. This is the same pattern as E84 and E88. The same example also disproves the final hooked arrow [Fltilde^{[0,h]}_{J,wtilde*(τ)}/T^{vee,J}-conj] → Φ-Mod_et in (7.17): take n=1, K=Q_p, trivial τ, h=p−1 and λ=h, with the compatible central character. Rank-one regularity and every stated root-depth condition hold. Scalar Frobenius matrices 1 and v^(p−1) give distinct bounded-height objects but isomorphic étale objects via e_1↦v e_0. A closed immersion of stacks is a monomorphism and hence cannot identify these two nonisomorphic objects. This concerns the full interval chart, not merely the fixed-Hodge subchart.

issues.locator: Proposition 5.5.9, last sentence of the proof, PDF125 (page image checked); relied on in the proof of Corollary 5.5.10, PDF125
issues.printed: The source obtains T^*_dd(M′) ≅ ρ̄^ss and invokes Proposition 5.5.7 to conclude additionally that M′ is semisimple.
issues.correction: Supply the missing implication by K56–K58. Repeat the presentation over an unramified splitting extension; the corrected K29 forces the unique lattice to be stable under the schematic scaling torus, yielding rank-one summands and a monomial basis (K57). Gauge uniqueness descends this property (K58), so K43 can apply it to the semisimple étale fibre at x=0. This adapts WE19 Theorem3.2.26, printed2465–2466, to the present arbitrary-height uniqueness theorem. The earlier reference to WE19 Theorem3.2.20 supplies a lattice from a lift, not semisimplicity by itself. The implication is now decomposed, but the source finding remains unreviewed; no independent-review verdict is assigned.
issues.reason: Proposition 5.5.7 (PDF123) says only this: for semisimple ρ̄, a semisimple M with T^*_dd(M) ≅ ρ̄ exists iff ρ̄ has such a presentation. It says nothing about an arbitrary M′ with T^*_dd(M′) semisimple. The proof of 5.5.9 produces M′ abstractly, as the point x = 0 of a closed locus, and never checks the criterion for ρ̄^ss. The proof of Corollary 5.5.10 ('By Proposition 5.5.7, M is semisimple of shape …') depends on this step.

issues.locator: Lemma7.2.10(2), published PDF146 (page image checked); Definition7.2.9 on the same page. Scope checked at PDF24,99–100,129,131.
issues.printed: The source claims cyclotomic freeness of ad(ρ̄) whenever ρ̄^ss|_{I_K} is 2-generic.
issues.correction: Require rank≥2 or p>2. For rank one and odd p over the standing unramified K/Q_p, ad(ρ̄)=1 and the nontrivial residual cyclotomic inertia character gives the required vanishing with M=K. Propagate this guard to G49, the generic-adjoint API of G22, and uses in G24/G52. The unramified splitting requirement in Definition7.2.9 is not changed. The same boundary is now recorded at the G35 labelling step and the G59 upper-bound proof. A unique rank-one flag may avoid this invocation, but does not fix the bounded-height collision in E102.
issues.reason: Take K=Q_2 and the trivial rank-one residual representation. GL_1 has no roots, so its inertia is 2-generic for every depth. But the mod-2 cyclotomic character is trivial; hence ad(ρ̄)⊗ε^{-1}=1 and H^0(G_M,1)=F̄_2≠0 for every unramified M/K. No witness of cyclotomic freeness exists. The p∤2n restriction on PDF129 explicitly lasts only for the remainder of Section6, while Section7 returns to the Section5.1 setup; it does not remove this case from the printed local lemma.

issues.locator: Proposition B.0.1(4), published PDF203; the equations of B.0.1(1) and the open V are on PDF202 (page image of the equations checked).
issues.printed: The source restricts to V = Spec Z[a, b][1/P(a,b)] ⊂ A², with P(a, b) = 7!b(b−1)(a−1)(a−2)(a−b)(a−b−1)(a−b−2). In (4), it defines H using the 3 × 3 minors of the Jacobian for presentation (1) relative to Z[t, a, b][1/P(a,b)], and asserts t³ ∈ H.
issues.correction: State (4) over Z[a,b][1/(aP)] (invert a as well). There t^3 ∈ H holds: 2·a·(a−2)^2·(a−b)·(b−1)·t^3 lies in the ideal of F1–F3 and six minors with integer cofactors (Q06, sourceData.appendixB.q06CertificateAP), and every factor except a divides P. The consumers are unaffected: every specialization used downstream has a a unit, so Proposition 3.3.9 and Corollary B.0.5 apply over Z[a,b][1/(aP)] with r = 3.
issues.reason: On the line a = 0, which lies in V whenever b(b−1)(b+1)(b+2) ≠ 0, the point t = 1, c12 = c13 = c22 = d21 = d33 = 1, d31 = (b−1)/(b+1) satisfies the three printed equations of (1), and the 3×6 Jacobian relative to Z[t, a, b] has rank 2 there. A power t^k in H would force rank 3 wherever t is invertible, so no power of t lies in H and (4) fails. The fibre of Spec R[1/t] → V over (0, b) is singular at this point too (rank 2 with the t column). The full Jacobian including the a and b columns has rank 3, so R ⊗ Q is regular there and the regularity step in the proof of (3) is not contradicted by this point. Checked exactly with SymPy at b = 5, −3, 7 and for symbolic b; the printed equations were re-read on the page image. Downstream (cc-39fac3, 29 September 2026): a is never ≡ 0 at the specializations used. At (−p, a, b) in Theorem 7.3.2 and Corollary B.0.5 the chart coordinate is a = a_{τ,1} − a_{τ,3} (Remark 3.3.2, PDF62), and a_τ ≡ s^{-1}(μ+η) mod ϖ (Lemma 7.3.1, PDF150). So a ≡ ±⟨μ+η, α∨⟩ for a positive root α, which is prime to p whenever μ is m-deep in C0 with m ≥ 0 (Definition 2.1.10, PDF33). The failure is therefore confined to the printed statement of (4) over V, and does not reach Corollary B.0.5.

issues.locator: Proof of Proposition B.0.2(2), published PDF205 (page image checked); the 8th Gröbner basis element is displayed on the same page, and the 6th generator of the ideal on PDF204.
issues.printed: The source says each polynomial’s first term is its leading monomial, except that vanishing of (a − b)((a − 1) − 1) makes the 8th generator’s first monomial zero and its second monomial leading.
issues.correction: except when (a − b)(a − 1) − 1 vanishes. The first coefficient of the 8th element is b((a − b)(a − 1) − 1) = b(a(a − b) − a + b − 1).
issues.reason: The displayed 8th element begins b((a−b)(a−1)−1)W d21 d33, and the 6th generator of the ideal on PDF204 has the same coefficient b(a(a−b)−a+b−1). The printed condition equals (a−b)(a−2), a factor of P, so read literally the exception never occurs on V. Yet the actual coefficient vanishes on the curve (a−b)(a−1) = 1, which meets V (for example (a,b) = (3, 5/2), with P ≠ 0). On that curve the left-most monomial is absent, and the leading term is the second monomial d21 d31 d33. So the proof's conclusion stands; only the stated exceptional locus is wrong.

With the sign of E114, the monodromy condition solves the six coefficients as c11 = c12·c31; d11 = c12·d31 + t/(a − 1); c23 = ((a − b − 2)·c22·d33 − (a − b)·t)/(a − 2); c21 = ((1 − b)·t·d21 + (b + 1)·c22·d31)/a; c33 = ((a − b − 1)/(b − 1))·(c12·d31·d33 − c13·d31) − ((a + b − 1)/((b − 1)(a − 1)))·t·d33; c31 = −b((a − b)(a − 1) − 1)/((a − b)(a − 1)a)·t·d21·d33 + b(a − b − 1)/((a − b)a)·c22·d31·d33 + (2a − b − 2)/((a − b)(a − 1))·t·d31. The formulas for c21 and c31 need a to be invertible, and a does not divide P. Items (2) and (3), certified for R over all of V (q04q05Certificate), are statements about U(z̃, λ, ∇) only where aP is invertible.

In those six unknowns the equations generate the unit ideal, for either sign of the parameter, at b = 5, −3 and 7 (Singular). issues.locator: Proof of Corollary 8.5.2, last paragraph, published PDF176 (page image checked); arXiv v2 PDF130 prints the same text.
issues.printed: The source obtains i^*_x(Z_σ) ≤ i^*_x(Z_{η,τ′}) for every x ∈ P_ss from Theorem 8.4.10(2). If all i^*_x(Z_{η,τ′}) vanish, Lemma 8.2.2 gives Z_σ zero. Otherwise, Theorem 7.4.2(1) gives i^*_x(Z_{λ+τ}) nonzero for some x ∈ P_ss, and Lemma 8.5.1 yields (λ+η, τ) ∈ S_{P,Λ,t}, producing a contradiction.
issues.correction: Argue at ρ̄ itself; only i^*_ρ̄(Z_σ) = 0 is needed. If i^*_ρ̄(Z_σ) ≠ 0, then ρ̄ lies on a component of the support of Z_σ, and so does ρ̄^ss (the component is closed and contains the semisimplifications of its points). ρ̄^ss ∈ P_ss, since m ≥ 6n−2. For a minimal patching functor M_∞ for ρ̄^ss and S_{Λ,t}, Theorem 8.4.10(2) gives i^*_{ρ̄^ss}(Z_σ) = Z(M_∞(σ)) ≠ 0. By exactness M_∞(σ°(λ,τ)) ≠ 0, and it is supported on X_∞(λ,τ) (Definition 6.2.1(1)), so R^{λ+η,τ}_{ρ̄^ss} ≠ 0. This contradicts the vanishing proved in the preceding paragraphs of the proof.
issues.reason: Lemma 8.5.1 needs the residual type to be P^η_{P,Λ,e}-generic. The corollary assumes this of ρ̄, but a point x ∈ P_ss is only (6n−2)-generic, so the lemma cannot be applied at x. Theorem 7.4.2(1) likewise needs τ to be max{2(h+1), 4n+h}-deep, which is not known here. The first case never occurs: Z_{η,τ′} ≥ C_σ because C_σ is a component of X^{η,τ′}_F (Theorem 7.4.2, (η,τ′) ∈ S_{{0},t}), and P_ss meets C_σ (Lemma 8.4.9). issues.locator: §A.4, the paragraph after Theorem A.4.1 defining pr, published PDF198 (arXiv 2007.05398v2 PDF144, the same sentence). Its source: Thorne, arXiv:1107.5989v1, proof of Theorem 6.8, claim (ii), PDF38–39, which derives it from Lemma 6.4 (PDF33–35).
issues.printed: LLHLM23 asserts freeness of pr(S(U1(Q), W)mQ) over O[ΔQ]. Thorne’s (ii) asserts, for every N, freeness of H1,QN over O[ΔQN] together with H1,QN/aQN ≅ H0,QN, and attributes the conclusions respectively to Proposition 5.9, Lemma 6.4 and Proposition 5.12.
issues.correction: Add that pr S(U_1(Q),W)_mQ is an O[Δ_Q]-direct summand of S(U_1(Q),W)_mQ. On that space each V^j satisfies P_j(V^j) = 0: on every characteristic-zero constituent its characteristic polynomial divides P_j (Thorne, remark after Proposition 5.8, PDF24), and the space is O-torsion-free. Since Q_j and R_j are comaximal, aQ_j + bR_j = 1 gives commuting idempotents e_j = a(V^j)Q_j(V^j) with Q_j(V^j)S = e_jS. So pr S = eS for e = ∏_j e_j, which commutes with the diamond operators. A direct summand of a free module over the local ring O[Δ_Q] is free, and e(S/a_QS) ≅ pr S(U_0(Q),W)_mQ gives the coinvariant statement.
issues.reason: Lemma 6.4(ii) proves that the whole space S(V, O) is free over O[U/V]; it says nothing about the image of the polynomial operator pr = ∏_j Q_j(V^j), which is not an idempotent, and a submodule of a free O[Δ]-module need not be free. CHT prove the analogous step for their projector explicitly: 'H1,QN is a direct summand of … over T … lemma 3.3.1 now tells us that H1,QN is a free O[∆QN]-module' (author manuscript PDF115). With the step supplied, the claim holds (A18, A33).

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, p.9 (published version)
issues.printed: The source sets t_i := Σ_{v|w_i} x_v. From |x_{v_{i,j}} − x_{v_{i,j′}}| ≤ 2 it deduces x_{v_{i,j}} = t_i/k_i + O_k(1). Since u, α_r, and α_s have norm 1, it obtains Σ_i t_i = 0, then asserts Σ_{i,j} max(x_{v_{i,j}}, 0) = Σ_i t_i + O_k(1) = O_k(1).
issues.correction: Normalise the α_i first. Their relative norms η_i = Nm_{L/K}(α_i) are units of K, since the ideal (α_i) has trivial relative norm. Pigeonhole the α_i by the class of η_i in O_K^*/(O_K^*)^d, which has at most d^{[K:ℚ]} = O_{[L:ℚ]}(1) classes. Within one class, η_i = η₀e_i^d with e_i ∈ O_K^*; replace α_i by α_i/e_i, which leaves the ideal unchanged. Then Nm_{L/K}(uα_r/α_s) = 1, so every t_i = log|Nm_{L/K}(uα_r/α_s)|_{w_i} vanishes, and the stated height bound follows. The loss is a factor O_{[L:ℚ]}(1) in N + 1, so (2.1) is unchanged.
issues.reason: The boxes control only PUL(α_i), i.e. the differences of coordinates within each block, because P drops the block sums t_i. Units u ∈ O* = ker(Nm_{L/K}) have t_i = 0, but an arbitrary generator α_i of ℘_i^{ℓa_i}℘̄_i^{−ℓb_i}℘₀^{−ℓa₀}℘̄₀^{ℓb₀} has t_i(α_i) = log|Nm_{L/K}(α_i)|_{w_i}, the logarithm of a unit of K, which need not be bounded. "Norm 1" in the absolute sense gives only Σ_i t_i = 0. The step Σ max(x_v, 0) = Σ_i t_i + O(1) needs each t_i = O(1) (for example t₁ = T, t₂ = −T gives Σ max ≈ T). So the claimed bound on H(uα_r/α_s) is not justified as written, though the repair costs only a constant depending on [L : ℚ].

issues.reviewReason: Confirmed on p.9. The boxes control only differences within each block of places above w_i, not the block sums t_i = log|Nm_{L/K}(uα_r/α_s)|_{w_i}; the paper's 'Σt_i = 0, since u, α_r and α_s all have norm 1' gives Σ_i t_i = 0 but not Σ max(x_v, 0) = O(1), and the height is unbounded once K has two or more infinite places, which is the case in the application (K = F₁). Rescaling by units of K alone does not suffice (it moves t only by d·Log of a unit). The proposed repair works: pigeonhole Nm_{L/K}(α_i) in O_K^*/(O_K^*)^d (at most d^{[K:ℚ]} classes), rescale, so that α_r/α_s has relative norm 1 and every t_i = 0, at the cost of a constant.

issues.printed: 𝓕(f)(y, w) = ∫_V f(x, u) ψ(Nm_{E/F}(⟨u, w⟩)) du
issues.correction: 𝓕(f)(y, w) = ∫_V f(y, u) ψ(Tr_{E/F}(⟨u, w⟩)) du
issues.reason: A Fourier transform needs a pairing that is F-bilinear in u, and Nm_{E/F}⟨u, w⟩ is quadratic in u. The Weil representation attached to q(y, w) = ⟨w, w⟩_V uses its polarization Tr_{E/F}⟨u, w⟩, as the linear side uses ψ(w*(v) + v*(w)). Beuzart-Plessis, whose Proposition 1 is Proposition 5.1 here, defines the unitary transform with ψ ∘ Tr_{E/F}. The first argument must be y, the variable on the left.

issues.locator: Lemma 2.8, p. 394
issues.printed: Lemma 2.8 assumes irrational θ1, …, θN ∈ R that are Q-linearly independent, together with M ∈ N and an integer b satisfying 0 ≤ b ≤ M − 1. It claims that every choice α1, …, αN ∈ R admits an infinite subsequence {ni} ⊂ N with lim e((Mni + b)θj) = e(αj), simultaneously for 1 ≤ j ≤ N.
issues.correction: Assume that 1, θ1, …, θN are Q-linearly independent.
issues.reason: As printed the lemma is false. θ1 = √2 and θ2 = 1 − √2 are irrational and Q-linearly independent, but e(nθ1)e(nθ2) = 1 for every n, so (e(1/2), e(0)) is never approached. The proof cites Kronecker's theorem (Apostol, Thm. 7.10), which needs the stronger hypothesis. The only application, in the proof of Lemma 2.9, chooses θj with 1, θ1, …, θN linearly independent, so nothing downstream is affected.

issues.locator: Lemma 2.9, p. 394
issues.printed: Lemma 2.9 takes αi, ci ∈ C indexed by i ∈ N. It assumes absolute convergence of φ(s) := Σ αi ci^s at s = s0 ∈ R and vanishing at all but finitely many s ∈ Z_{>s0}, and concludes Σ_{ci = c} αi = 0 whenever c ∈ C^×.
issues.correction: Add: for every ε>0, only finitely many indices have |c_i|≥ε. Group equal nonzero bases, start at an integer exponent in the absolute-convergence range, remove successive finite maximal-modulus blocks, and use dominated convergence on the remaining terms. Applications must explicitly provide absolute convergence at a positive integer exponent.
issues.reason: Confirmed by an exact entire-function construction, not a numerical check: a_n=(−1)^n/∏_{j=1}^n(2^j−1), a₀=1. The series F(x)=Σa_n x^n is entire, satisfies F(2x)=(1−x)F(x), and F(2^s)=0 for all positive integers s. With c_n=2^n the asserted coefficient cancellation fails. Finite superlevel sets of |c_n| justify the largest-modulus argument and dominated convergence. The applications use unit coefficients and absolute convergence in a positive-power range.

issues.locator: Theorem 4.1 proof, p. 403, and Proposition 4.2 proof, p. 404
issues.printed: The proof concludes that O_X̃(−E) = O_X̃(1) is ample relative to π. Its cited justification is the discussion together with Lemma 31.32.4(3) of [Stacks, Tag 01OF] and Lemma 29.38.2 of [Tag 01VL].
issues.correction: Use D=V(I O_X̃), including its multiplicities a_σ, in the ample bundle O(−D)⊗π*L^k. For cusp weight k′ choose k>k′ max a_σ and n₀ as in Serre vanishing, then ℓ₀=n₀k and n=n₀k′ have matching weights and ℓ₀E≥nD. Smooth extension of the actual differential form remains the separate obligation E17/G1.
issues.reason: The cited Stacks 01OF statement concerns the exceptional ideal divisor. If E means the usual reduced toroidal boundary, its equality with that divisor is not established. On a boundary cycle with E_σ²=−b_σ one has (−E)·E_σ=b_σ−2, illustrating why an arbitrary reduced boundary cannot simply replace a relatively ample exceptional divisor. No assertion that the original reduced-boundary vanishing theorem has been fully repaired is made.

issues.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.1 (§5.3), p. 416, and Example 2.7, p. 392
issues.printed: For even r, the source derives the result from Example 2.7 together with Theorem 1.7. For odd r and fundamental d1, it invokes Theorem 7.13 of [BEY21] for algebraicity, then claims that the remaining steps of Theorem 1.7’s proof establish Theorem 1.1.
issues.correction: Treat separately the case where d1d2 is a perfect square, i.e. E1 = E2. Then (z1, z2) is a small CM point (F = Q, Remark 1.4), and the statement is Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang, Theorem 6.1: for CM points in the same imaginary quadratic field, |D|^r G_{r+1,f}(z1^σ, z2^σ) = −(1/t) log|α^σ| with α in the ring class field H_D (deduced from their Theorem 5.5 and Corollary 5.6, which is the F = Q case of Conjecture 1.6 quoted in §1.2). This strengthens Viazovska (arXiv:1110.4654), who obtained α ∈ Q̄. First require nonsingular ordinary evaluations (E12). Write d_i=t_i²D₀ and D=lcm(t₁,t₂)²D₀. If H_D is larger than H₁H₂, equivariance makes log|α^σ| constant on Gal(H_D/H₁H₂); its norm has logarithm [H_D:H₁H₂] times that value. Absorb this degree and the rational ratio (t₁t₂/lcm(t₁,t₂)²)^r into κ and an integer power/inverse of the norm.
issues.reason: Example 2.7 and Theorems 1.3 and 1.7 require F = Q(√(d1d2)) to be a real quadratic field, while Theorem 1.1 is stated for all negative discriminants. issues.locator: §4.1, inclusion (4.2), p. 403, and Proposition 4.2 proof, p. 404
issues.printed: The source gives H⁰(X̃,E^{0,0}⊗L̃_{κ,ρ}) ⊃ A_{κ,ρ}(Γ), claiming that a bounded f and the order to which g vanishes make the differential form smooth globally as a section.
issues.correction: Add and prove the smooth weighted boundary-extension hypothesis, or supply a valid weighted ∂̄/cohomology argument for the actual theta data. Do not identify all bounded real-analytic automorphic forms with smooth sections on the compactification.
issues.reason: Bounded real analyticity on a punctured cusp does not imply C∞ extension. Already for F=Q, the invariant real-analytic weight-zero function f(τ)=1/log(e+|j(τ)|²) is bounded on H; at q=0 it behaves as 1/(−2log|q|), so it is not smooth there. Multiplication by any finite cusp power q^a still has derivatives of sufficiently high order failing to extend. Passing to a neat subgroup only changes the cusp width. The paper’s argument needs more than an order-of-vanishing estimate; this review does not claim the theta-specific existence theorem is false.

issues.correction: Proposition 9.1 rests on [LZ, Thm. 10.5.1], which Li–Zhang prove assuming their Conjecture 10.4.1 on the auxiliary space Ñ¹_n → N¹_n × Z(x_0). The paper cites it without that hypothesis, so as published Proposition 9.1, Lemma 11.1, Theorems 1.5 and 1.7 and Corollary 1.9 (which always involve a place above S_π ≠ ∅, since |S_π| is odd) depended on it. Cite in addition Li–Rapoport–Zhang, arXiv:2404.02214v2, Theorem 14.6.2 with Corollary 16.1.5, which prove every part of the conjecture that Li–Zhang §§10.4–10.5 use; with that citation the results hold as stated.
issues.reason: Li–Zhang state before Theorem 10.5.1: "Note that the result is conditional on Conjecture 10.4.1"; arXiv 1908.01701v3 says "In [KRSZ19] the authors will prove this conjecture, which from now on we assume to hold", and their final version (KRProof.pdf, compiled 31 October 2021) says the same of [LRZ21]. Conjecture 10.4.1 asserts (i) π₁ finite flat of degree q + 1, étale away from N^{1,ss}_n and totally ramified along it; (ii) π₂ the blow-up of Z(x_0) along the zero-dimensional Z(x_0)^ss; (iii) π₁^{−1}(N^{1,ss}_n) exactly the exceptional divisor; Li–Zhang deduce that Ñ¹_n is regular with exceptional divisors P_Λ ≅ P^{n−1}. The uses in §§10.4–10.5 were checked one by one against Li–Rapoport–Zhang Theorem 14.6.2 (pp.60–61): Lemma 10.4.2 needs Ñ¹_n regular (14.6.2(i)) and injective maps on local rings, which hold because π₁ is finite flat (14.6.2(ii), which is Conjecture (i) verbatim) and π₂ is an isomorphism on the dense non-special locus (14.6.2(iii)); Theorem 10.4.3 compares π₁^*Y(x) with π₂^*Z(x) up to the P_Λ and uses (ii), (iii), the description of the exceptional locus as a reduced Cartier divisor ⊔_Λ P_Λ with P_Λ ≅ P^{n−1} (14.6.2(iv)), and Conjecture (iii) only through supports, which Corollary 16.1.5 gives as Ñ^{exc} = π₁^{−1}(N^{[1],•}_n)_red (p.69); Theorem 10.5.1 uses the projection formulas for the finite flat π₁ and the proper π₂, which is an isomorphism off the zero-dimensional centre, and in (10.5.3.3) the intersection numbers χ(P_{Λ_1} ∩^L ⋯ ∩^L P_{Λ_n}) = (−1)^{n−1} or 0 of (14.6.1). The blow-up ideal of Conjecture (ii) and the scheme structure of π₁^{−1}(N^{1,ss}_n) are never used beyond these consequences. The sequel (Forum Math. Pi 2022, Prop. 4.27(2), "as [LL21, Props. 8.1, 9.1]") inherits the same dependence.

issues.printed: The source sums over i ≥ −2N and writes = C_{γ,δ}·q^{Nn(γ−δ)/(2−δ)} (∫_{A^m_0 × A^m_i × B^{n−2m}_{−N}} |f(x)|^{2−δ} dx)^{(2−γ)/(2−δ)}. issues.reason: The index i is summed out in the previous line, so it cannot appear on the right. The estimate needs the bound of each shell integral by the integral over the union, and Σ_{i≥−2N}(i + 2N + 1)q^{−im(γ−δ)/(2−δ)} ≍ q^{2Nm(γ−δ)/(2−δ)}, which together with q^{N(n−2m)(γ−δ)/(2−δ)} gives the stated power. issues.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.9(2), p.31, and proof of Lemma 8.3, p.37 (authors' final version; the same in arXiv v5, pp.31 and 37)
issues.printed: Proposition 6.9 claims injectivity of H^{2r}(X_{L_R L^R,u}, Q_ℓ(r)) → H^{2r}(X_{L_R L^R,u} ⊗_{E_u} Ē_u, Q_ℓ(r)) outside finitely many u ∈ V^fin_E \ V^{(ℓ)}_E. Lemma 8.3 likewise claims injectivity of H^{2r}(X′_L, Q_ℓ(r)) → H^{2r}(X′_L ⊗_K Q̄_p, Q_ℓ(r)) and H^{2r−2}(𝒳_L ⊗_{O_K} k, Q_ℓ(r − 1)) → H^{2r−2}(𝒳_L ⊗_{O_K} F̄_p, Q_ℓ(r − 1)). Both passages invoke Hochschild–Serre and the Weil conjecture.
issues.correction: Over the p-adic fields E_u and K the restriction to the geometric fibre is not injective in general; only the map over the finite field k is. In Proposition 6.9(2), take instead s ∈ (S^R_{Q^ac})^0_{L_R} \ m^R_π: it annihilates H⁰(E_u, H^{2r}(X_{L,u} ⊗ Ē_u, Q_ℓ(r))) and H²(E_u, H^{2r−2}(X_{L,u} ⊗ Ē_u, Q_ℓ(r))) by the de Rham comparison, while H¹(E_u, H^{2r−1}(X_{L,u} ⊗ Ē_u, Q_ℓ(r))) = 0 by weights, so s² ∉ m^R_π annihilates H^{2r}(X_{L,u}, Q_ℓ(r)) at every u of good reduction. In Lemma 8.3, use that H^{2r}(𝒳_L, Q_ℓ(r)) itself injects into H^{2r}(X′_L ⊗_K Q̄_p, Q_ℓ(r)) (see E13).
issues.reason: Let X be smooth projective of dimension 2r − 1 over a p-adic field E_u with good reduction, p ≠ ℓ. In the spectral sequence E_2^{a,b} = H^a(E_u, H^b(X_{Ē_u}, Q_ℓ(r))) ⇒ H^{a+b}(X, Q_ℓ(r)), the terms E_2^{0,2r−1} and E_2^{1,2r−1} vanish because H^{2r−1}(X_{Ē_u}, Q_ℓ(r)) is pure of weight −1, and E_2^{a,b} = 0 for a ≥ 3, so the kernel of H^{2r}(X, Q_ℓ(r)) → H^{2r}(X_{Ē_u}, Q_ℓ(r)) is E_∞^{2,2r−2} = H²(E_u, H^{2r−2}(X_{Ē_u}, Q_ℓ(r))). It is nonzero: for h the class of an ample divisor and β a generator of H²(E_u, Q_ℓ(1)) ≅ Q_ℓ, α = π^*β ∪ h^{r−1} restricts to zero over Ē_u, while α ∪ h^r = π^*β ∪ h^{2r−1} maps to deg(h^{2r−1})·β ≠ 0 under the trace isomorphism H^{4r}(X, Q_ℓ(2r)) ≅ H²(E_u, Q_ℓ(1)). The Weil conjectures kill only the weight −1 term. Over a finite field the Galois cohomological dimension is 1 and the kernel is H¹(k, H^{2r−3}(Q_ℓ(r − 1))), of weight −1, which vanishes, so the second map of Lemma 8.3 is injective. The rest of the proof of Proposition 6.9(2) already uses (1) to kill H⁰ and H² after localization; Disegni–Liu (arXiv v3, Lemma 4.7, p.43) likewise use the Hochschild–Serre filtration over E with only [LL21, Prop. 6.9(1)].

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma 8.3, p.37, with Definitions 6.2(2) and 6.3, p.29 (authors' final version; the same in arXiv v5, p.37)
issues.printed: The source says that, by definition, H^{2r}(X′_L ⊗_K Q̄_p, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗_Q Q^ac is annihilated by each element of (S^R_{Q^ac})^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R}. It then uses Poincaré duality together with smooth proper base change to claim annihilation of H^{2r−2}(𝒳_L ⊗_{O_K} F̄_p, Q_ℓ(r − 1)) ⊗_Q Q^ac by these same elements.
issues.correction: Definition 6.2(2) does not give this, so Lemma 8.3 ("If s is a product of two elements in (S^R_{Q^ac})^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R}, then it gives an ℓ-tempered Q^ac-étale correspondence of 𝒳_L") is not proved as stated. It holds for every s ∈ (S^R_{Q^ac})^0_{L_R}, and so for the product of such an element with an element of (S^R_{Q^ac})^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R}; Definition 6.3 should take each s_i to be such a product, which keeps s_i in (S^R_{Q^ac})^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R}. Proposition 6.9 supplies such products outside m^R_π (m^R_π is prime), so Proposition 8.1 and the main theorems go through with this choice.
issues.reason: Definition 6.2(2) asks s to annihilate the arithmetic cohomology H^{2r}(X_{L_R L^R,u}, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗_Q Q^ac over the local fields E_u. By the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence this sees only H⁰(E_u, H^{2r}(X_{L,u} ⊗ Ē_u, Q_ℓ(r))) and a quotient of H²(E_u, H^{2r−2}(X_{L,u} ⊗ Ē_u, Q_ℓ(r))): a Hecke-isotypic part of the geometric H^{2r} with no Frobenius-invariants at any u ∤ ℓ is invisible to it, and X′_L ⊗_{E′} K lives over the larger field K (Notation 5.6), which has more invariants. The next sentence transfers the same claim to H^{2r−2}(𝒳_L ⊗ F̄_p) by Poincaré duality and inherits the gap. The repair: H^{2r}(𝒳_L, Q_ℓ(r)) ≅ H^{2r}(𝒳_L ⊗_{O_K} k, Q_ℓ(r)) by proper base change; this injects into H^{2r}(𝒳_L ⊗_{O_K} F̄_p, Q_ℓ(r)), since the kernel H¹(k, H^{2r−1}(𝒳_L ⊗ F̄_p, Q_ℓ(r))) vanishes by weights; and H^{2r}(𝒳_L ⊗ F̄_p, Q_ℓ(r)) ≅ H^{2r}(X′_L ⊗_K Q̄_p, Q_ℓ(r)) by smooth proper base change, Hecke-equivariantly. Elements of (S^R_{Q^ac})^0_{L_R} annihilate the last group by the comparison with H^{2r}_dR(X_L/E) used in the proof of Proposition 6.9(2), since 2r ≠ 2r − 1; so they are ℓ-tempered, without (8.1) or absolute purity.

issues.locator: Proof of Corollary B.15, p.64 (authors' final version; the same in arXiv v5, p.63)
issues.printed: For (1), the source infers that H^{2r}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗_Q L is finitely generated over S_L from finite dimensionality of H^{2r}(𝒳, Q_ℓ(r)) over Q_ℓ, then invokes Definition B.12. For (2), it claims finite generation over S_L of two modules: H^{2r}(X, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗_Q L; ⊕_{i<2r−1} ⊕_j H^i(Y°_j ⊗_k F̄_p, Q_ℓ) ⊗_Q L.
issues.correction: These modules are not finitely generated over S_L when S is countable, as the Hecke algebras used in §§7–9 are; the conclusions still hold. S acts Q_ℓ-linearly on the finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-space H, so for a Q_ℓ-basis h_1, …, h_d the S_L-submodule generated by the h_i ⊗ 1 is finitely generated, has zero localization at 𝔪 (a submodule of a module with zero localization), and is therefore killed by some t ∈ S_L \ 𝔪; since h ⊗ λ = Σ_i (c_i ⊗ λ)(h_i ⊗ 1) and S_L acts (Q_ℓ ⊗_Q L)-linearly, t kills H ⊗_Q L.
issues.reason: Q_ℓ ⊗_Q L has uncountable dimension over a countable field L such as Q^ac, while a finitely generated module over S_L = S ⊗ L has countable L-dimension when S is countable. So H ⊗_Q L is not finitely generated as soon as H ≠ 0, and the step that deduces an annihilator outside 𝔪 from the vanishing of the localization needs the argument in the correction instead.

issues.printed: The source assigns to every open compact L ⊆ H(A^∞_F) a Shimura variety X_L for Res_{F/Q} ^uH at level L. It describes X_L as smooth and quasi-projective over E, of dimension n − 1, with E embedded in C by ι.

issues.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.2.1, p.59
issues.printed: The source assumes L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ integral, chooses a basis (e′_1, …, e′_n) with val(e′_i) = a′_i, and sets L′^♭ = ⟨e′_1, …, e′_{n−1}⟩. For x′ = e′_n it claims Int_{L^♭,V}(x) = Int_{L′^♭,V}(x′) and ∂Den_{L^♭,V}(x) = ∂Den_{L′^♭,V}(x′).
issues.correction: Replace the two claimed equalities by the equality of differences: with φ = Int_{L^♭,V} − ∂Den_{L^♭,V} and φ′ = Int_{L′^♭,V} − ∂Den_{L′^♭,V}, Theorem 6.1.3 cancels the horizontal parts, so φ(x) = Int(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩) − ∂Den(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩) = Int(L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩) − ∂Den(L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩) = φ′(x′). The induction hypothesis φ′ = 0 then gives φ(x) = 0 for x ∉ M(L^♭), which is all the rest of the proof uses.
issues.reason: Only the full functions Int_{L^♭}(x) = Int(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩) and ∂Den_{L^♭}(x) depend on the lattice L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ alone. Their horizontal and vertical parts depend on the hyperplane L^♭_F. By Definition 6.1.2, ∂Den_{L^♭,H}(x) and ∂Den_{L′^♭,H}(x′) are sums over integral L″ ⊇ L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩ with the different conditions t(L″ ∩ L^♭_F) ≤ 1 and t(L″ ∩ L′^♭_F) ≤ 1; geometrically, Z(L^♭)_H ≠ Z(L′^♭)_H. So the two stated equalities do not follow from what precedes them. The step is repaired in one line and the theorem stands.

issues.correction: A lift g̃ ∈ J(F) of g ∈ SO(V)(F) has spinor norm η(g̃) = sn(g) in F^×/(F^×)², so η(g̃) = 1 forces sn(g) = 1. What the argument needs is only val η(g̃) = 0, since g̃ carries RZ^{(ℓ)}_G to RZ^{(ℓ + val η(g̃))}_G (§4.5) and N = RZ^{(0)}_G; that is available exactly when some isometry carrying L′ to L has spinor norm of even valuation, which the remark does not establish. Do not replace the component-preserving rational subgroup by all SO(V′)(Q) in Theorem12.9.1. Supply the needed component comparison and orbit/multiplicity accounting separately.
issues.reason: The square class of η(g̃) is fixed by the SO image; changing a lift by a scalar changes η by a square. Thus η=1 is possible only for trivial spinor norm, and a p-unit lift only for even valuation. For m even≥4, ε=−1, V≅ϖH_m^− is isotropic and has Hasse−1. Write H_m^−=M⊥⟨w⟩ with M unimodular rank m−1 and take L to be its scaled sublattice. The stabilizer of L in SO(V) has even valuation spinor norm: O(M) is generated by unit-norm reflections, each acquiring valuation1 after scaling, and the complementary-line reflection also has valuation1; determinant1 forces an even number. Here the integral reflection-generation step has an elementary proof: for a unit vector v and its image w, at least one of Q(v−w),Q(v+w) is a unit because their sum is4Q(v); use one or two reflections to match v,w and induct on the unimodular orthogonal complement. A hyperbolic plane in V represents1 andϖ, so a product of two reflections has odd spinor valuation. Set L′=hL for such h: every isometry carrying L′ to L has odd spinor valuation. No J(F) element doing so preserves N. This confirms the faulty lift argument, not falsity of Int-isometry invariance; a semilinear/component-comparison repair remains possible but unproved here. Howard–Pappas§6.3 explicitly relates η to spinor square class, and§7.2.6 defines I(Q)^0 by val_pη=0. The later assertion on p.1457 that G′(Q)^0 surjects onto SO(V′)(Q) has the same obstruction: take the positive definite rational form V′=diag(3,3,1,2), p=3. Its local discriminant is2 and Hasse invariant−1, an allowed rank4 nearby space. The rational isometry diag(−1,1,−1,1), the reflections in the first and third basis vectors, has spinor norm3 and cannot be the image of a p-unit-similitude lift. The global proof must retain the subgroup/orbit distinction.

issues.reviewReason: Checked at the locator and recomputed. Lemma 2.1 of v1 reads verbatim 'The number of degree 2g monic integer polynomials p(x) all of whose roots have absolute value sqrt(q) is at most (2g)^g q^{(1/4)g(g+1)}', and at g = 1, q = 2 the bound is 2 sqrt 2, about 2.83, while X^2 - aX + 2 has all roots of absolute value sqrt 2 for every a with -2 <= a <= 2, which is five polynomials, and X^2 - 2 is a sixth. issues.printed: The source derives the bound for bad A using Conjecture 5.2 together with Proposition 5.10.
issues.correction: Assume in addition the analogue of Conjecture 5.2 for isogeny classes with factors B0 (Frobenius ±√p, End⁰ the definite quaternion algebra over Q(√p)), and conclude that a large factor E^h or B0^(h/2), h ≥ 0.99g, occurs with probability tending to 1. issues.printed: The source describes the centralizer of F as an algebra that is not a division algebra.
issues.correction: A Frobenius centralizer can be a division algebra (a field). Use the preceding local-invariant calculation to prove splitting over each local center; being a Q_p-centralizer or merely not being a division algebra does not establish that splitting.
issues.reason: Take E/F_5: y²=x³+1. Its discriminant is nonzero mod 5 and it has six rational points, so P_E=X²+5 and Q(π)=Q(√−5) has no real place. On the two-dimensional prime-field rational realization F has this characteristic polynomial; it is irreducible over Q_5 by Eisenstein. Hence the commutant is Q_5[F]≅Q_5[X]/(X²+5), a field and therefore a division algebra. In companion coordinates F=[[0,−5],[1,0]], every commuting matrix is xI+yF with determinant x²+5y²; unequal parity of valuations prevents a nonzero zero determinant. The proposition is not disproved: the preceding invariant proof is valid, and a field is split over its own center.

The proof considers (g^{−1}Ψ)h_γ ∈ Gal(F_S/F) = Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ⋊ Gal(F^{(m)}/F). It uses the prime-to-ℓ order of γ to claim a lift γ̃ ∈ Gal(F̃_S/F⁺) whose power γ̃^{[F:F⁺]} ∈ Gal(F̃_S/F) maps to (g^{−1}Ψ)h_γ in Gal(F_S/F).
issues.correction: Replace the equality by the inclusion G_{S,γ} ⊆ θ_S^{−1}Hom_{O_λ}(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}). Exactly, G_{S,γ} = q(N^α), where N = Gal(F̃_S/F₊^{(m)}), α is conjugation by a lift σ₀ of γ of prime-to-ℓ order, and q is restriction to F_S. Equality holds if [F:F⁺] = 1. For [F:F⁺] = 2, the statement Proposition 2.6.6 actually needs is that the O_λ-span of θ_S(G_{S,γ}) contains λ^c Hom(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) with c independent of m. It holds with c = 𝔣(r_S)r_{Ind R} when R_ℚ ≇ R_ℚ^𝔠. When R extends to R₊ over F⁺, it holds for S inside a 𝔠-eigenspace ε exactly when γ acts on (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} ⊂ R̄₊^{(m)} by ε, and it fails otherwise (then G_{S,γ} = {1} if S lies in the other eigenspace).
issues.reason: Take F+=Q(√5), F=F+(i), ell=3, m=1, R=Z3(1), j=2 and the identity polarization (muΦ=1). Let u=(1+√5)/2 and S be its one-dimensional mod-3 Kummer class, coming from the integral finite unit class. F(m)=F(m)+=F(ζ3); its degree over F+ is four, so u remains a noncube (use the fundamental-unit description of Q(√5)). FS=F(m)(cuberoot(u)) has cyclic cubic kernel. Choose γ induced by complex conjugation, of order two; hγ=1. Complex conjugation fixes the real cuberoot and inverts ζ3, so every lift of γ has square one. All associated-prime evaluations are consequently zero, while the right side is the full cubic kernel. The Kummer/Bloch–Kato unit identification is an explicit external input to this arithmetic witness, not claimed newly formalized. Re-checked on the page image (2026-09-23): confirmed — checked on the page image of p. 134 (Lemma 2.6.4 and its proof) with the definitions on p. 133; the counterexample was re-derived independently, and the exact replacement formula G_{S,γ} = q(N^α) was re-proved. The lemma is correct when [F:F⁺] = 1 and false in general when [F:F⁺] = 2. Counterexample to the printed lemma (all hypotheses of Proposition 2.6.6 also hold). F⁺ = ℚ(√5), F = ℚ(√5, i) (ℓ = 3 unramified), E_λ = ℚ₃, R = ℤ₃(1), j = 2, Ξ the identity ℤ₃(1)^𝔠 = ℤ₃(1)^∨(2), μ_Ξ = 1, B = 1, so ρ₊(𝔠) = (1, 1, 𝔠). Fix m ⩾ 1; u = (1+√5)/2. S := ℤ/3^m·κ(u) ⊆ H¹(F, μ_{3^m}) (Kummer class) lies in H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}) (u is a unit) and is free of rank one (u is not a cube in F: units of F are μ₄ × ⟨η⟩ with η = u or η² = ζu). ρ̄₊^{(m)}|_{Γ_F} = (ε̄, ε̄², 1), so F^{(m)} = F₊^{(m)} = F(ζ_{3^m}); Res is injective by Lemma 2.3.5(a) (ε̄(Γ_F) = 𝔽₃^× ∋ −1 as ζ₃ ∉ F), so K = Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ≅ ℤ/3^m with F_S = F(ζ_{3^m}, u^{1/3^m}), which is Galois over F⁺. γ := ρ̄₊^{(m)}(𝔠) = (1, 1, 𝔠) has order 2 and h_γ = 1, so the printed right-hand side is all of K. Every lift σ of γ to Gal(F_S/F⁺) is τ·𝔠 with τ ∈ K, and 𝔠τ𝔠^{−1} = τ^{−1} (𝔠 fixes the real root u^{1/3^m} and inverts ζ_{3^m}); hence σ² = 1 and Ψ_{w^{(m)}} = σ^{2g} = 1 for every γ-associated place: G_{S,γ} = {1} ≠ K. Direct check: such places lie over primes v of F⁺ with ‖v‖ ≡ 2 mod 3, where every element of 𝔽_{‖v‖}^× is a 3^m-th power, so Frobenius fixes u^{1/3^m}. Mechanism in general: for [F:F⁺] = 2 the Frobenius at the inert place is σ^{2g}, and squares of lifts in the 𝔠-coset are constrained (σ² = (1+α)(n)·σ₀²). The step 'it is easy to see' asserts the opposite. (The displayed splitting Gal(F_S/F) = Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ⋊ Gal(F^{(m)}/F) is also unjustified, though only a prime-to-ℓ lift of ⟨h_γ⟩ is needed.) Relevance to the main theorems: in Theorem 1.1.1 R = R₀ ⊗ R₁ is restricted from F⁺, so H¹(F, R̄) splits into 𝔠-eigenspaces; for S in one eigenspace F_S is Galois over F⁺, σ₀ acts on K ⊆ Hom(S, R̄) through the action of the lift of γ on R̄, and G_{S,γ} = θ_S^{−1}Hom(S, (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ, γ=+1}); if γ acts by −1 on the h_γ-fixed line, G_{S,γ} = {1} and loc_w(S) = 0 at every γ-associated place, so no abundant element exists. Case for the defence: the inclusion ⊆ is correct; the lemma is correct for [F:F⁺] = 1, the setting of [46, Lemmas 5.7–5.8] that v1/v2 cited; in the Rankin–Selberg application with R ≇ R^𝔠 the needed disjointness may well hold, and in the base-change case one can probably choose γ with the right sign using the large image — but none of this is in the paper, which applies the lemma as stated. Reach: a stated result (Lemma 2.6.4, and Proposition 2.6.6 which relies on it, are false when [F:F⁺] = 2); the proofs of Theorems 8.2.2 and 8.3.2 (hence Theorems 1.1.1, 1.1.5, 1.1.7, 1.1.9) invoke Proposition 2.6.6 with [F:F⁺] = 2 and need repair). O_λ-submodule of H¹_{f,R}(F, R̄^{(m)}); F_S/F^{(m)} and the injective equivariant θ_S from §2.3 with ρ = ρ̄^{(m)}; γ-associated places (Def. 2.6.3): places of F₊^{(m)} not over ∞ℓ, unramified over F⁺, with underlying place of F^{(m)} unramified in F_S, and Frobenius γ in Gal(F₊^{(m)}/F⁺); G_{S,γ} = their Frobenii Ψ_{w^{(m)}} in Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}). Lemma 2.6.4 adds only: order of γ prime to ℓ. THE EXAMPLE SATISFIES ALL OF THEM. F = ℚ(√5,i) ⊂ ℂ, 𝔠|_F ≠ 1, F⁺ = ℚ(√5), 3 unramified (disc 400). R = ℤ₃(1), Ξ = id (R^𝔠 = ℤ₃(1) = R^∨(2)); in rank one BᵗB^{−1} = 1 forces (−1)^{μ_Ξ+j+1} = 1 (μ_Ξ = 1), ρ₊(𝔠) = (1,1,𝔠), and ρ₊(𝔠g𝔠) = ρ₊(𝔠)ρ₊(g)ρ₊(𝔠) checks. S = ℤ/3^m·κ(u) ⊂ H¹_{f,R}(F, μ_{3^m}) (u = (1+√5)/2 a unit), free of rank one because u is not a cube in F (μ_F = μ₄, unit index ≤ 2) and F has no 3-power roots of unity. F^{(m)} = F₊^{(m)} = F(ζ_{3^m}); F_S = F(ζ_{3^m}, u^{1/3^m}) is Galois over F⁺ and K := Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ≅ ℤ/3^m (Res injective by Lemma 2.3.5(a): −1 ∈ ε̄(Γ_F) as √−3 ∉ F). γ = ρ̄₊^{(m)}(𝔠) has order 2, h_γ = 1, so the right-hand side of the lemma is all of K. RECOMPUTATION OF G_{S,γ}. A γ-associated place lies over v with Frob_v = complex conjugation on F(ζ_{3^m}), i.e. ‖v‖ ≡ 3 mod 4 and ‖v‖ ≡ −1 mod 3^m (so v has degree 1 over ℚ and is inert in F); w^{(m)} has residue field 𝔽_{‖v‖²} and Ψ_{w^{(m)}} acts on u^{1/3^m} by u^{(‖v‖²−1)/3^m} = (u^{‖v‖−1})^{(‖v‖+1)/3^m} ≡ 1, since u mod v lies in 𝔽_{‖v‖}. So G_{S,γ} = {1} ≠ K (smallest case m = 1, p = 11: u ∈ 𝔽₁₁, u^{40} = 1 in 𝔽₁₂₁). Group-theoretically: every lift of γ is τ𝔠 with 𝔠τ𝔠 = τ^{−1}, so (τ𝔠)² = 1. FAILING STEP. 'It is easy to see that there is γ̃ lifting γ with γ̃^{[F:F⁺]}|_{F_S} = (g^{−1}Ψ)h_γ' is false for [F:F⁺] = 2: squares of the coset σ₀N are (1+α)(N)·σ₀², a constrained set. Re-proved general formula: G_{S,γ} = {σ^{2g}|_{F_S} : σ ∈ σ₀N} = q(N_{2g}(N)) = q(N^α) (σ₀^{2g}|_{F_S} is a prime-to-ℓ element of the ℓ-group K, hence 1; q∘α^{2g} = q; on N^{α^{2g}}, N_{2g} is 2g/k times the norm of a cyclic group of order k prime to ℓ). For [F:F⁺] = 1, F₊^{(m)} = F^{(m)} (the perfect pairing R̄×R̄ → O/λ^m(j) forces ker ρ̄ ⊂ ker ε̄^j), N = K, α acts through h_γ, and the lemma holds; the inclusion ⊆ (first paragraph of the proof) always holds. The displayed ⋊ splitting is also unjustified but harmless (Schur–Zassenhaus gives a prime-to-ℓ lift of ⟨h_γ⟩). STRUCTURE FOR [F:F⁺] = 2. With M := Ind_F^{F⁺} R̄^{(m)}, Shapiro gives a Gal(F₊^{(m)}/F⁺)-equivariant injection θ̃: N ↪ Hom(S, M) (ker ρ̄_M = ker ρ̄₊), M^γ ≅ R̄^{h_γ} via the first projection, and θ_S(G_{S,γ}) = pr₁(θ̃(N)^γ). (i) If R_ℚ ≇ R_ℚ^𝔠, M_ℚ is absolutely irreducible and Res for M is injective (H¹(Gal(F₊^{(m)}/F), R̄) = 0 because Gal(F₊^{(m)}/F^{(m)}) is central and R̄^{Γ_F} = 0 under Lemma 2.3.5). Lemmas 2.3.3–2.3.4 for (F⁺, M) then show that the O_λ-span of θ_S(G_{S,γ}) contains λ^{𝔣(r_S)r_M}Hom(S, R̄^{h_γ}). The printed equality can still fail, but this span statement is what Prop. 2.6.6 uses. (ii) If R = R₊|_{Γ_F} and S lies in the ε-eigenspace H¹(F⁺, R̄₊⊗η^{(1−ε)/2}) while γ acts on the line R̄^{h_γ} ⊂ R̄₊ by −ε, then H¹_ur(F⁺_v, R̄₊⊗η^{(1−ε)/2}) ≅ (R̄₊⊗η^{(1−ε)/2})^{φ_v} = 0 at every γ-associated v. So loc_w(S) = 0 and G_{S,γ} = {1}. The polarization sign plays no role: γ only fixes a Galois coset, and the sign is that of ρ̄_{R₊}(σ) on ker(ρ̄(σ²) − 1). VERSIONS: v1/v2 Lemma 2.5.4(2) (hypothesis: order of h_γ prime to ℓ) is proved only by reference to [Liu16, Lemmas 5.7–5.8] (a setting with [F:F⁺] = 1); v3 is identical to the published text. Independent check 2: Quote checked on the page images: p. 134 (PDF 28) for the lemma and proof; pp. 132–133 for Def. 2.5.3, Constr. 2.5.4, Not. 2.6.1–2.6.2 and Def. 2.6.3; pp. 121 and 129 for the standing assumptions of §2. v3 is identical. v1/v2 have Lemma 2.5.4(2), proved by citing [46, Lemmas 5.7–5.8], which treat the case [F:F⁺] = 1. Defence attempted; it fails at every point. (i) Scope. §2 asks only that ℓ be odd and unramified in F (p. 121) and that F ⊂ ℂ be 𝔠-stable (p. 129). ℓ = 3 and F = ℚ(√5,i) qualify. Any odd ℓ unramified in F with ζ_ℓ ∉ F works the same way (e.g. ℓ = 7). (ii) j and the polarization. Def. 2.5.3 allows any integer j. The map Ξ = id: ℤ₃(1)^𝔠 = ℤ₃(1) → ℤ₃(1)^∨(2) is Γ_F-equivariant. Also B·ᵗB⁻¹ = 1 = (−1)^{μ_Ξ+j+1} with μ_Ξ = 1. So ρ₊(𝔠) = (1,1,𝔠), and ρ₊ is a homomorphism: 𝔠(g,μ)𝔠 = (μ·ᵗg⁻¹,μ) gives ε²·ε⁻¹ = ε = ρ(𝔠g𝔠). (iii) γ and h_γ. γ := ρ̄₊^{(m)}(𝔠) lies in the image and in the 𝔠-coset, and has order 2. h_γ is the first component of γ², which is 1, so (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} = R̄^{(m)} is free of rank 1. The paper itself takes γ to be the image of g^{[F′:F⁺]}𝔠 in Prop. 2.7.2. (iv) The class S. Any finitely generated submodule of H¹_{f,R}(F,R̄^{(m)}) is allowed; no 𝔠-condition is imposed, and 𝔠 does not even act on H¹(F,R̄) in general. κ(u) lies in H¹_{f,R} because u is a unit. u is not a cube in F: if u = x³ then (x/𝔠x)³ = 1 and ζ₃ ∉ F, so x ∈ F⁺, but u is the fundamental unit of ℚ(√5). So S ≅ ℤ/3^m. (v) The field F_S. F^{(m)} = F₊^{(m)} = F(ζ_{3^m}). Res is injective by Lemma 2.3.5(a), since −1 ∈ ε̄(Γ_F). So F_S = F(ζ_{3^m}, u^{1/3^m}) and K := Gal(F_S/F^{(m)}) ≅ ℤ/3^m, with θ_S bijective. Recomputation of G_{S,γ}. A γ-associated place lies over a place v of F⁺ whose Frobenius σ ∈ Gal(F_S/F⁺) restricts to 𝔠 on F(ζ_{3^m}). w^{(m)} has residue degree 2 over v, so Ψ_{w^{(m)}} = σ². Write σ = τ𝔠 with τ ∈ K. Since 𝔠 fixes the real root u^{1/3^m} and inverts ζ_{3^m}, 𝔠τ𝔠 = τ⁻¹ and σ² = 1. Hence G_{S,γ} = {1}, whereas θ_S⁻¹Hom(S,(R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) = K ≅ ℤ/3^m. Direct check. Such v have ‖v‖ = q ≡ −1 mod 3^m; for m = 1, v | 11 gives u ≡ 8, a cube in 𝔽₁₁. Since 3 ∤ q−1, u is a 3^m-th power in 𝔽_q, and all roots of X^{3^m} − u lie in 𝔽_{q²}. So w^{(m)} splits completely in F_S. General mechanism, re-derived. Let N := Gal(L/F₊^{(m)}), where L is the Galois closure of F_S·F₊^{(m)} over F⁺. Take σ₀ a lift of γ of order d prime to ℓ (Schur–Zassenhaus), α conjugation by σ₀, and q: N → K the restriction. Every lift is nσ₀, and σ₀^{2g}|_{F_S} = 1, so Ψ = q(Σ_{i<2g} α^i n). This gives G_{S,γ} = q(N)^α = q(N^α): the invariants of α, not of α² = h_γ. The step 'it is easy to see that there is an element γ̃ … lifting γ' asserts the opposite. What stands. The inclusion ⊆ (first paragraph of the proof) is correct, and the lemma is correct when [F:F⁺] = 1. The first reading's formula and correction are right. On reach, I refine the first reading's 'case for the defence'. When R ≅ R^𝔠, the failure is not confined to a badly chosen γ. For a rank-2 S with one class in each 𝔠-eigenspace, Proposition 2.6.6 fails for every γ. So Theorem 8.3.2 needs two γ's of opposite signs, not merely a well-chosen one. Reach to the main theorems: Lemma 2.6.4 reaches §8 only through Proposition 2.6.6. That proposition is invoked in the proof of Theorem 8.2.2 (r_S = 1, p. 310) and of Theorem 8.3.2 (r_S = 2, p. 317), with R = R₀⊗R₁, Ξ = Ξ₀⊗Ξ₁ (j = 1), [F:F⁺] = 2. In both proofs γ comes from an arbitrary (γ₀,γ₁,ξ) supplied by (L5-2)/Lemma 2.7.1, satisfying (a)–(e), and is chosen without reference to S. If R_ℚ ≇ R_ℚ^𝔠, the span version above (constant r_{Ind R} instead of r_R) rescues Proposition 2.6.6, and the proofs go through with changed constants. If R_ℚ ≅ R_ℚ^𝔠 the application inherits the failure. This covers every instance of Theorem 1.1.1 (R = (Sym^{n₀−1}H¹(A₀)⊗Sym^{n₁−1}H¹(A₁))(n)|_{Γ_F}) and base-change pairs in Theorems 1.1.5, 1.1.7 and 1.1.9. There H¹_f(F,R) = H¹_f(F⁺,R₊) ⊕ H¹_f(F⁺,R₊⊗η). Concretely, in the setting of Theorem 1.1.1 with ℓ large, suppose σ gives a γ satisfying (a)–(e). Then so does στ, for τ ∈ Gal(F̄/F_rflx) with ρ_{A₀}(τ) ≡ −1, ρ_{A₁}(τ) ≡ 1 and ε(τ) ≡ 1 mod ℓ^m (such τ exists by Serre's open image theorem): h_γ and ξ are unchanged, and the sign flips because n₀−1 is odd. For the hypothetical S that the proof by contradiction must exclude, lying in one eigenspace, one of these two admissible choices of γ gives loc_𝔭(S) = 0 at every γ-associated 𝔭. Then no abundant Ψ exists, ⟨s₁,c₁⟩_𝔭 = 0, and no contradiction follows. So the proofs of Theorems 8.2.2 and 8.3.2, and hence of Theorems 1.1.1, 1.1.5, 1.1.7 and 1.1.9, have a gap in the self-conjugate case. For Theorem 1.1.1 the gap is repairable for all but finitely many ℓ: take S in one eigenspace and γ of matching sign. In rank one, if the Selmer group meets both eigenspaces, no single γ gives an abundant pair, so use γ at 𝔭₁ and γτ at 𝔭₂ (conditions (PI)/(PII) depend only on h_γ and ξ). For general admissible λ (Definition 8.1.1) and base-change pairs, (L5-2) supplies only one γ, and nothing in (L1)–(L7) guarantees one of the opposite sign. There the proofs of Theorems 1.1.5, 1.1.7 and 1.1.9 are incomplete as written. No main theorem is shown false. The defect only makes a particular γ useless, and the statements remain consistent with BBK: e.g. a rank-one configuration with Selmer rank one in each eigenspace would violate parity. Theorems 8.2.2 and 8.3.2 apply Proposition 2.6.6, and so this lemma, with [F:F⁺] = 2, R = R₀⊗R₁ and j = 1. The γ comes from (L5-2) via Lemma 2.7.1 and is chosen after S, with no condition tying it to S (page images pp. 310, 317–319). Nothing in the Rankin–Selberg setup, the 1-polarization or Definition 8.1.1 rules out the failure. Case R_ℚ ≅ R_ℚ^𝔠. This covers all of Theorem 1.1.1 (A and A′ are over F⁺: Lemma 8.1.3, Prop. 2.7.2) and base-change instances of 1.1.5, 1.1.7 and 1.1.9. The lattice R is then Γ_{F⁺}-stable (call it R⁺), ℓ is odd, and H¹(F,R̄^{(m)}) = H¹(F⁺,R̄⁺) ⊕ H¹(F⁺,R̄⁺⊗η), with the local conditions preserved. For S in the χ-eigenspace, F_S is Galois over F⁺, and a cocycle computation gives θ_S(σ₀xσ₀⁻¹) = χ(σ₀)ρ⁺(σ₀)∘θ_S(x). Hence G_{S,γ} = θ_S⁻¹Hom(S,(R̄^{(m)})^{χ(σ₀)ρ⁺(σ₀)=1}). The module (R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ} is a line (Lemma 2.7.1(c)), and ρ⁺(σ₀) acts on it by a sign ε₀. So G_{S,γ} is either all of θ_S⁻¹Hom(S,(R̄^{(m)})^{h_γ}) or {1}. In the second case θ_S(Ψ_w)(s) = 0 at every γ-associated w. Restriction from F_w to F^{(m)}_{w^{(m)}} has degree g, which is prime to ℓ, so loc_w(s) = 0 in H¹_ns(F_w,R̄^{(m)}) ≅ R̄^{(m)}/(h_γ−1). Consequence for 8.2.2. The prime 𝔭 is γ-associated, so ⟨s₁,c₁⟩_𝔭 = 0 and no contradiction arises: the argument does not bound that eigenspace. Nothing controls the sign. For example, with n = 2 and the element g^{[F′:F⁺]}𝔠 of Prop. 2.7.2 (taking ρ̄(g) to commute with ρ⁺(𝔠)), one finds ε₀ = −c₁, where c₁ = ±1 is the eigenvalue of 𝔠 on the a-eigenvector of ρ̄_{A₀}(g). The paper leaves this free, and both choices satisfy (a)–(e). Consequence for 8.3.2. Suppose the hypothetical rank-2 S is ⟨s₊,s₋⟩, with one class in each eigenspace. Then every element of θ_S(G_{S,γ}) kills s₋ or kills s₊, for every γ, so no abundant pair exists. The paper uses a single γ for both 𝔭₁ and 𝔭₂. Repair. In rank 0, choose γ according to the eigenspace of S. In rank 1, use γ's of opposite signs at 𝔭₁ and 𝔭₂, as Bertolini–Darmon do when they choose ε_p. Changing the sign keeps h_γ and ξ, so conditions (a)–(e) and (PI)/(PII) are unaffected, since those are stated through Satake parameters at inert primes. For Theorem 1.1.1 both signs exist when ℓ ≫ 0: choose g in Prop. 2.7.2, or multiply by ρ̄₊(τ) with ρ̄(τ) = (−1)⊗1, which lies in the image since the image contains SL₂×SL₂ (Serre). So Theorem 1.1.1 survives with a modified proof. Not covered. For 1.1.5 and 1.1.9 at an arbitrary admissible λ, Definition 8.1.1 guarantees only one element satisfying (a)–(e). For 1.1.7, Lemma 8.1.4 supplies only ρ̄₊(φ_𝔭) at one prime 𝔭. So in the base-change case those proofs are incomplete unless a γ of the other sign is shown to exist, by an added hypothesis or a large-image argument. Case R_ℚ ≇ R_ℚ^𝔠. F_S and its 𝔠-conjugate should be linearly disjoint over F^{(m)} up to bounded index, because Hom_{Γ_F}(R,R^𝔠) = 0. A version of the lemma that loses only a bounded power of λ is then plausible, but the paper does not prove it. No main theorem is shown false. What fails is a proof by contradiction about a hypothetical Selmer class, and the statements are what Bloch–Kato predicts.
