issues.citation: Xinyi Yuan–Shou-Wu Zhang, "On the averaged Colmez conjecture", Annals of Mathematics 187 (2018), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: Confirmed on the page image; the kind should be 'gap' and affects 'the proof', not 'misprint' and 'nothing'. Counterexample for τ ∈ Hom(E,K): let w | p be ramified over v with F_v = Q_p, p odd, E_w = Q_p(ϖ), ϖ^2 = pu, and let A2 have type Φ2 ∌ τ1. Then Ω(A2)_w ≅ O_K with ϖ acting by τ̄1(ϖ), so Ω(A2,τ1) ≅ O_K/(τ1(ϖ) − τ̄1(ϖ)) = O_K/(2ϖ) ≠ 0, and Ω(A1×A2,τ1) = O_K ⊕ O_K/(2ϖ). Counterexample for the O_F version with F ramified at p: take F_v = Q_p(√p), E_w = F_v ⊗ Q_{p^2} and local type {(id,τ),(Frob,τ′)}. Then Lie is O_K ⊕ O_K with √p acting as (√p, −√p), and its τ-quotient is O_K ⊕ O_K/(2√p). With torsion the printed formula ord_σ(det f*) = ℓ_σΩ(Q,τ) does not hold for torsion-free determinants. In the first example both torsion-free τ1-parts are O_K and are matched by a unit, so the order is 0 while ℓ_σΩ(Q,τ1) = v_σ(2ϖ). The conclusion may still hold, since in this example the τ and τ^c torsion terms are symmetric, but the printed argument does not show it. The root cause is §2.2 of the paper, which calls N(A,τ) a line bundle without making W(A,τ) locally free (range 1). Theorem 1.1 (the averaged Colmez formula itself) is proved independently in [AGHMP18].

issues.locator: §2.2, proof of Theorem 2.2, pp. 545–546 (the display on p. 545; c_p defined at the top of p. 546)
issues.printed: The proof asserts ∏_{σ:K→Q̄_p} |α_{στ}|/|α_{στc}| = ∏_{σ:K→Q̄_p} |α_{στ}|/|α_{c_pστ}| = 1. It takes c_p in Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p) to act as complex conjugation on E under every embedding E → Q̄_p.
issues.correction: For x in K⊗Q_p, the product of |σ(x)|_p over σ: K → Q̄_p is |N_{K⊗Q_p/Q_p}(x)|_p. With x = τ(α) and x = τ(ᾱ), both products equal |N_{E⊗Q_p/Q_p}(α)|_p^{[K:E]}, since complex conjugation is a Q_p-algebra automorphism of E⊗Q_p and so preserves the norm. It asserts that O_{E_v}^× ⊂ U_v implies O_{E_v} ⊂ O_{𝔹_v} (p. 591), and recalls a chosen maximal order O_𝔹 in 𝔹_f containing O_Ê (p. 576).
issues.correction: In Theorems 1.6 and 1.7 (and §§1.2–1.3), take U = Ô_𝔹^× for a maximal order Ô_𝔹 of 𝔹_f containing Ô_E. This follows from 'U maximal ⊇ Ô_E^×' unless some place v | 2 of F with residue field F_2 splits in E. Theorem 1.1 is unaffected, since such a U can always be chosen.
issues.reason: At a split place v with residue field F_2, O_{E_v}^× = O_v^× × O_v^× spans only {(a, b) : a ≡ b mod ϖ_v}. Counterexample to the p. 591 inference: F = Q and E = Q(√−7), so 2 splits; embed E_2 = Q_2 × Q_2 diagonally in M_2(Q_2) and let L = {(x, y) ∈ Z_2² : x ≡ y mod 2}. U_2 = GL(L) is maximal compact and contains every diag(a, b) with a, b ∈ Z_2^×, but End(L) ∌ diag(1, 0), which sends (1, 1) to (1, 0) ∉ L. Part I needs O_E ⊂ O_B (p. 576; the O_E-action on the CM abelian variety; Erratum §1's Λ1 = O_E ⊂ Λ0 = O_B), and Part II needs it on p. 591, so neither theorem is proved for such U. There P_U corresponds, via X_U ≅ X_{g^{-1}Ug}, to a CM point whose order at v is O_v + ϖ_v O_{E_v}. The right side of Theorem 1.7 does not see this conductor, while CM heights do change with it (g = 1: at a split prime the conductor-2 CM elliptic curve's Faltings height differs by ½ log 2, Nakkajima–Taguchi), so the literal statement is not expected to hold. issues.locator: §4.3, before Theorem 4.10, p. 569
issues.printed: The source defines M_℘ = D(H_℘) as the covariant Deudonné crystal, citing [Ill85], [Mes72], and sets W_℘ = Lie(H)^∨, W^t_℘ = Lie(H^t)^∨; H^t_℘ denotes the Cartier dual of H_℘. It claims that passage to determinants gives the determinant morphism det W^t_℘ → det W^∨_℘ ⊗ ω^{⊗2}_{X_℘}.
issues.correction: Take M_℘, W_℘ and W^t_℘ to be the τ-parts for O_℘ ⊗_{Z_p} O_X → O_X, or the O_℘-relative Dieudonné crystal of the strict special formal O_{B,℘}-module ℋ_℘ with its Hodge filtration. These have ranks 4, 2 and 2, as §5.2 implicitly uses. If F_℘/Q_p is ramified, the τ-quotient of Lie(ℋ^t_℘)^∨ has torsion, and one must use its image in M_℘ or the relative theory.
issues.reason: ℋ_℘ has height 4d and dimension 2 (Theorem 4.9(1): Lie is locally free of rank 1 over O_X ⊗_{O_℘} O_{K_0}), where d = [F_℘:Q_p]. So the absolute crystal M_℘ has rank 4d, W_℘ has rank 2 and W^t_℘ has rank 4d − 2. For d > 1, 'taking determinants' of W^t → W^∨ ⊗ ω gives no map det W^t → det W^∨ ⊗ ω^{⊗2}, and the proof of Theorem 4.10 in fact computes only with the rank-2 pieces (the idempotents e_i, and the eigenlines L_i, N_i). Theorem 4.10 as intended is unaffected.

issues.locator: §5.2, before Proposition 5.4, p. 575
issues.printed: The source asserts W(I_y) = 0 and says W(I^t_y) has rank 1 and is free over O_{E,K} := O_{E,℘} ⊗_{O_℘} O_K, from which it derives Proposition 5.4.
issues.correction: True when F_℘/Q_p is unramified. Then O_{F,p} ⊗_{Z_p} O_L is a product, the τ-quotients are exact direct summands, and Proposition 5.4 follows from Proposition 5.3 by taking τ-components. When e(F_℘/Q_p) > 1, W(I_y) is a nonzero torsion module, the τ-quotient sequences 0 → W(G^t) → M(G) → W(G)^∨ → 0 displayed on p. 575 need not be left exact, and Proposition 5.4 and Corollary 5.5 need a separate integral argument. For example, W(−) could be redefined as the image in the generic fibre and the identities re-proved at the level of determinants. The paper gives no such argument.
issues.reason: Let τ′ ≠ τ be an embedding of F_℘ with the same residue embedding; one exists iff e(F_℘/Q_p) > 1. Ψ contains an embedding of E above τ′, so Ω(I_y) has a nonzero part on which O_℘ acts through τ′. Its τ-quotient is nonzero by Nakayama over the local ring O_℘ ⊗_{W(k_℘),ι_0} O_L. Explicitly, for F_℘ = Q_p(√p) with ℘ split in E, Ω(I_w) ≅ O_L with √p acting as −√p, so W(I_y) ⊇ O_L/(2√p) ≠ 0. W is defined on p. 575 as the τ-quotient for 'τ : O_{F,p} ⊗_{Z_p} O_K → O_K'. Theorem 1.1 (the averaged Colmez formula itself) is proved independently in [AGHMP18].

issues.locator: §5.2, deformation display and Corollary 5.5, pp. 575–576
issues.printed: The source writes Hom_{O_{E,p}}(Ω(H^t_{x″}), Ω(H_{x″})^∨) = Hom_{O_{E,p}}(W(H^t_{x″}), W(H″_{x″})^∨) = Hom_{O_{E,℘}}(W(H^t_x), W(H_x)^∨) ⊗_{O_K} O_{K′} = Hom_{O_{𝔹,℘}}(W(H^t_x), W(H_x)^∨) ⊗ O_{K′} = … . It attributes identity (3), the third equality, to an explicit calculation, calls the completion 𝒳̂″_{1,x″} of 𝒳″_{1,℘′} at x″ universal for deformations of the p-divisible group ℋ″_{x″}, and identifies two O_K-lattices in ω^{-2}_{X″_{1,℘′},x″}.
issues.correction: Identity (3) is false. Consequently 𝒳̂″_{1,x″} is not the universal deformation of ℋ″_{x″} as a p-divisible O_{E,p}-module; it can be at most the universal deformation with extra structure, such as the polarization from X′, and the claim is not used later. Corollary 5.5 follows directly without this chain. By Proposition 5.4 the W(I^t_y)-twists cancel in det W(ℋ″) ⊗ det W(ℋ″^t), which gives det W(ℋ_x) ⊗ det W(ℋ^t_x) ⊗ O_{K′} = N_{1,℘,x} ⊗ O_{K′} (E8 convention). The lattices lie in the generic fibre of N″ ≅ ω^{⊗2}, not ω^{-2}. In the first line, H should be H″ throughout.
issues.reason: At τ, W(H^t_x) and W(H_x)^∨ each have O_K-rank 2 and are free of rank 1 over O_{E,K}. They carry the standard 2-dimensional representation of O_{𝔹,℘} ⊗ K ≅ M_2(K), in which E acts with types τ1 and τ2 once each. So Hom over O_{E,K} has O_K-rank 2 and Hom over O_{𝔹,℘} has rank 1; the first two lines of the chain also have rank 2. In complex terms, deformations of (A, O_E) of Lie type Φ1+Φ2 move the τ1- and τ2-lines independently (P^1 × P^1), and only the polarization cuts this down to the curve X′.

issues.correction: For v ∈ S2, u ∈ O_{F_v}^×: c_{ψ1}(1,y,u) = 0, but c_{ψ2}(1,y,u) = 2 log N_v when y ∈ ϖ_v^{−1}O_{E_v} and q(y) ∈ O_{F_v}^× (0 otherwise). Hence c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −(2 log N_v/(1+N_v+N_v²))·1_{ϖ_v^{−1}(O_{B_v})_2}(y)·1_{O_{F_v}^×}(u), not 0, and Lemma 7.6(2)'s 'split: 0' fails at S2. Theorems 9.1 and 1.7 still hold. Prop. 9.2(2) at S2 needs only d_{φ_v} = 2n_{φ_v}log N_v − c_{φ_v} + log|uq(y)|φ_v = 0, and Lemma 8.7(2) at S2 is off by the compensating amount (next issue).
issues.reason: With X = N_v^{−s}, the ψ2 sum for n ≥ 1 is (1−X)²/(1−X/N)·Σ_{n≥1}X^n(1+(1−N^{−1})(n+2)), using vol{z′ ∈ O²: z′1z′2 ∈ p^k} = N^{−k}(1+(1−N^{−1})k). The ψ1 sum Σ_{n≥1}X^n(1+(1−N^{−1})n) has s-derivative 0 after multiplication. The ψ2 sum has the extra 2(1−N^{−1})X/(1−X), which is only a simple pole, so the product 2(1−N^{−1})X(1−X)/(1−X/N) has s-derivative 2 log N_v at s = 0. Equivalently, the substitution turns the sum into N_v^{2s} times a ψ1-type tail, and the factor N_v^{2s} contributes 2 log N_v. Directly for y = 1: the extra region x2 ∈ ϖ^{−1}O_E𝔧 − O_E𝔧 with z1z2 ∈ p^n has volume 2(1−N^{−1})N^{−n}. Checked by exact counting mod 3^6 (volumes for n = 1, 2, 3 match) and by sympy (derivative 0 for ψ1, 2 log N for ψ2). Searched: Annals 2018 article and the 2023 erratum (author revision Erratum5.pdf, 18 Dec 2022), which treats only §2 (Theorem 2.7); no correction to §§6–7 found. Independent second check (checker 4): After the substitution the n-th volume is N^{-n}(1+(1−N^{-1})(n+2)); the ψ1 case has n in place of n+2. With X = N^{-s}, c̃_{ψ2} = (1−X)²/(1−X/N)·[V0 + (1+2b)X/(1−X) + bX/(1−X)²], b = 1−N^{-1}. Its X-derivative at X = 1 is −2, so c = 2log N_v; the same formula with shift 0 gives 0 for ψ1. Checked in exact arithmetic for N = 2, 3, 5 and numerically by direct series summation (slopes 1.3863 and 2.1972 = 2log2 and 2log3). This confirms checker 3's entry on Lemma 7.6(2); record it once. issues.locator: §6.2, local identity and (6.2.1), p. 581; used in the proof of Lemma 6.1, pp. 582–583
issues.printed: The source asserts r_V(g)φ_w(x,u) = δ_w(g)^{(d−d1)/2} r_{V1}(g)φ_w(x,u) for w ∤ ∞, and gives (6.2.1) as A(g) = ρ∞(g)^{(d−d1)/2}δ(g)^{(d−d1)/2}θ_{A,1}(g) − ρ∞(g)^{(d−d0)/2}δ(g)^{(d−d0)/2}θ_{A,0}(g).
issues.correction: Insert the unramified quadratic characters of the complements. At finite w ∉ S′, r_V(g)φ_w = χ_{V1^⊥,w}(a_w)δ_w(g)^{(d−d1)/2}r_{V1}(g)φ_w, and (6.2.1) becomes A(g) = χ_{V1^⊥}(a(g))(ρ∞δ)^{(d−d1)/2}θ_{A,1} − χ_{V0^⊥}(a(g))(ρ∞δ)^{(d−d0)/2}θ_{A,0}, with χ_W(a(g)) = ∏_{w∉S′}χ_{W,w}(a_w). In the proof of Lemma 6.1 these characters are constant along g ∈ Γ (gg0 ∈ g0GL2(Ô)). So (1) holds (V_{ℓ,1}^⊥ = 0), while (2) follows only when, in each codimension, all the complements have the same discriminant character. §9 meets this: codimension 2 complements E·j with character η; codimension 4 quaternionic complements with trivial character. The main results are unaffected.
issues.reason: For even dim V the Weil representation has r(m(a))φ(x) = χ_V(a)|a|^{dim V/2}φ(ax), with χ_V the discriminant character; this is forced by the relations among r(n(b)), r(w) and the Weil index. Take V = B (χ_B = 1), V1 = E (χ_E = η) and z = diag(ϖ_w,ϖ_w) at an inert w ∉ S′. Then δ(z) = ρ∞(z) = 1, r_B(z)φ(y,u) = φ(ϖy, ϖ^{−2}u), but r_E(z)φ(y,u) = η_w(ϖ)φ(ϖy, ϖ^{−2}u) = −φ(ϖy, ϖ^{−2}u). So the nontruncated case of (6.2.1) gives A(z) = θ_{A,1}(z), whereas in fact A(z) = −θ_{A,1}(z). Equivalently: binary theta series have nebentypus η and quaternionic ones do not. issues.locator: §8.3, Lemma 8.7(2) and its proof, case v ∈ S2, pp. 617 and 619
issues.printed: Lemma 8.7(2) asserts n_{φ_v}(y,u) = φ_v(y,u)·½v(q(y)) for every non-archimedean place v of F and every (y,u) ∈ E_v^×× F_v^×. Its proof on p. 619 says that the analogous computation for v ∈ S2 yields 0 everywhere.
issues.correction: For v ∈ S2, write φ_v = ψ1 − (1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}ψ2 with ψ1 = 1_{O_{𝔹_v}^×}⊗1_{O^×} and ψ2 = 1_{ϖ_v^{-1}(O_{𝔹_v})_2}⊗1_{O^×}. Then n_{φ_v}(y,u) = −(1+N_v+N_v²)^{-1}ψ2(y,u) on E_v^××F_v^×, which is not 0; for example n_{φ_v}(1,1) = −1/(1+N_v+N_v²). The printed value is φ_v(1,1)·0 = 0. The lemma is correct for v ∉ S2. Prop. 9.2(2) and Theorem 9.1 still hold, because Lemma 7.6(2) fails at S2 by exactly the compensating amount: c_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = −(2log N_v/(1+N_v+N_v²))ψ2(y,u). Hence d_{φ_v}(1,y,u) = 2n_{φ_v}log N_v − c_{φ_v} + log|uq(y)|_vφ_v = 0 = −log|d_vq(𝗃_v)|_vφ_v(y,u). The proof of Prop. 9.2(2) at S2 must use both corrected values.
issues.reason: Use the formula of Prop. 8.5 with U_v = GL2(O_{F_v}) (Assumption 7.1), r = 0, so m_ν̄1(n(b)) = 1/(N_v^{−v(b)−1}(N_v−1)) and each shell v(b) = −i contributes 1. For b ∉ O, y·n(b) ∉ GL2(O), so the ψ1 part is 0. For y = diag(a,d), y·n(b) ∈ ϖ^{-1}(O_{𝔹_v})_2 if and only if v(a),v(d) ≥ −1, v(a)+v(d) = 0 and v(ab) ≥ −1. So the upper sum is 1+v(a), the lower 1+v(d), and n_{ψ2} = ½(2+v(ad)) = 1 on supp ψ2|_E. A brute-force enumeration for p = 2 and p = 3 (y = 1, diag(p^{-1},p), diag(p,p^{-1})) gives n = −1/7 and −1/13, against 0 printed. Checked on the page image. Checker 3 found the same error independently (as an out-of-range entry); merge the two. Unchanged in arXiv 1507.06903v3 (checked); not addressed by Erratum5 (Dec 2022), which concerns only Theorem 2.7. Independent second check (checker 3): Apply Prop. 8.5 with U_v = GL2(O_v) (r = 0): m_{ν1}(n(b)) = 1/(N^{−v(b)−1}(N−1)), so each shell v(b) = −i ≤ −1 contributes 1. ψ1(y n(b)) = 0 for b ∉ O. For y = diag(a,d) with a, d ∈ p^{−1} and ad ∈ O^×, ψ2(y n(b)) = 1 iff v(ab) ≥ −1, which gives v(a)+1 shells; the lower-triangular sum gives v(d)+1; the total is 2 + v(ad) = 2. So n_{ψ2} = 1, and n_{φ_v} = −1/(1+N+N²).

issues.locator: Proposition B.1, p. 902, and §B.2, p. 903 (published; also arXiv v3) — both verified on rendered page images, since a text layer drops the superscript
issues.printed: Proposition B.1 writes φ^{(r)}(0) := (d/ds)|_{s=0}φ(s) ≥ 0, while §B.2 defines Λ^{(r)}(π, 1/2) := (d/ds)|_{s=1/2}Λ(π, s).
issues.reason: The superscript (r) on the left-hand side is the r-th derivative — this is the whole point of "super-positivity", and both statements quantify over all r ≥ 0 and compare φ^{(r_0)} with φ^{(r_0+2i)}. As printed, the definitions say that every φ^{(r)}(0) is the first derivative. The proofs use the genuine r-th derivative (the Taylor coefficients of the product expansion in the proof of Proposition B.1, and the even-degree coefficients of A_i(s) in Remark B.4).

issues.locator: Proposition 2.4 (2.18), p. 787, and its proof, p. 788; Corollary 2.5, p. 788; Theorem 1.8, p. 775; §9.1.1, p. 876 (published version; also arXiv v3 unless stated)
issues.printed: Equation (2.18) gives J(u, 1_K, s) = L(η, 2s) + L(η, −2s) for u ∈ {0, ∞}, with the proof treating u = ∞ as analogous. Corollary 2.5 states J_r(1_K) = … 2^{r+2}(d/ds)^r|_{s=0}L(η, s), r > 0 even. Theorem 1.8 asserts, for even r > 0, ⟨θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T], θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]⟩_{Sht′^r_G} = (2^{r+2}/(log q)^r)L^{(r)}(η, 0).
issues.correction: J(∞, 1_K, s) = 2L(η, 0), independent of s. Hence J_r(1_K) = 2^{r+1}L^{(r)}(η, 0) for r > 0 even, and Theorem 1.8 reads ⟨θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T], θ^μ_*[Sht^μ_T]⟩ = (2^{r+1}/(log q)^r)L^{(r)}(η, 0). The r = 0 value 4L(η, 0) + q − 2 (Corollary 2.5, Remark 9.3) is unchanged.
issues.reason: On the u = ∞ orbits (a = 0 or d = 0 in γ) the conditions g_{ij}²/det g ∈ O for g = diag(x,1)^{−1}γ diag(y,1) force xy ∈ O^×, so |xy|^s = 1 on the support. For γ = [[0,1],[1,1]] or [[1,1],[1,0]] the sum is Σ_{E ≥ 0}η(E) = L(η, 0), and the orbit of w contributes 0 (η is nontrivial on its stabilizer). Structurally, γ ↦ γw swaps u = 0 and u = ∞ but turns the weight |h_1h_2|^s into |h_1|^s|h_2|^{−s}, under which the n_± orbits give constants; the two cases are not analogous. The r = 0 case agrees: 2L(η, 0) + 2L(η, 0) + (q − 2). A worked example (y² = (x² − 2)(x⁴ + x + 1) over F_5, L(η, T) = 1 + 3T + 5T²) gives J_2(1_K)/(log q)² = 184, against 368 from the printed formula. Theorem 1.8 is (log q)^{−r}J_r(1_K) by Theorem 9.2 (§9.1.1), so it inherits the factor 2. Proposition 3.2(3), used by Theorem 8.1 at u = ∞, is still true. Also in arXiv v3.

issues.locator: §B.2, Theorem B.2 and its proof, p. 904 (published version; also arXiv v3 unless stated)
issues.printed: Theorem B.2 assumes π is a nontrivial cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A) and is self-dual. The source claims that cuspidality and nontriviality make the standard L-function L(π, s) entire for s ∈ C.
issues.correction: Add the hypothesis that L(π, s) is entire. It is automatic for n ≥ 2; for n = 1 over a function field it excludes the unitary characters factoring through the degree, such as (−1)^{deg}.
issues.reason: π = (−1)^{deg} on GL_1 over a function field (the quadratic character of the constant-field extension) is nontrivial, cuspidal and self-dual, but L(π, s) = Z_X(−q^{−s}) has poles. For X = P¹, Λ(π, 1/2 + t) = 1/(q^t + q^{−t} + q^{1/2} + q^{−1/2}), so Λ″(π, 1/2) = −2(log q)²/(2 + q^{1/2} + q^{−1/2})² < 0 (−0.1300 for q = 3), contradicting (1). Theorem 1.7 uses only GL_2 cuspidal L-functions and is unaffected. Also in arXiv v3.

For such φ the global distribution vanishes: J(φ⊗f′,s1,s2) = 0, by substituting h2 ↦ h2t (resp. h1 ↦ h1t) in (2.2) with t ∈ A(O_x), η_x(t) = −1, since the degree regularisation is A(O)-invariant. issues.correction: F†_i = E†_i(−Σ_{x∈Σ∞} Σ_{2≤j′≤j≤d_x} c_x^(j′) x^(j)), so that the coefficient of x^(j) is c_x^(2) + … + c_x^(j)

issues.printed: Part (2) is claimed to hold already under d ≥ 3g − 2 + N. The source reduces the proof to Rν̂^√R_{d′!}Q_ℓ ≅ ⊕K_{d′,i} under the bound d′ ≥ 2g′ − g = 3g − 2 + ρ, and describes the domain of ν̂^√R_{d′} as smooth, geometrically connected, and of dimension d′.
issues.correction: The argument proves (2) only when every d′ = d+ρ−N± satisfies d′ ≥ 2g′−1, for example under the stated hypothesis d ≥ 2g′−1+N. Drop the remark, or give another argument for 2g′−g ≤ d′ ≤ 2g′−2.
issues.reason: X̂′_{d′} (pairs (L′, a′) with a′ ∈ H^0(X′,L′), possibly zero) is smooth only if H^1(X′, L′) = 0 for every L′ of degree d′, i.e. d′ ≥ 2g′−1. Take L′ = ω_{X′}(−E) with E effective of degree 2g′−2−d′, so c = h^1(L′) ≥ 1. At (L′, 0) the deformations H^1(O) ⊕ H^0(L′) minus the automorphisms H^0(O) have dimension g′ + h^0(L′) − 1 = d′ + c > d′ = dim X̂′_{d′}. So the constant sheaf need not be the IC complex, and the smallness argument does not apply. For g ≥ 2 this range is reached: d = 3g−2+N with Σ = Σ+ gives d′ = 3g−2+ρ = 2g′−g. YZ17 Prop. 8.2 assumes d ≥ 2g′−1. The remark is never used, since Propositions 7.1–7.3 and Theorem 7.4 all assume d ≥ 2g′−1+N.

issues.citation: Wei Zhang, "Weil representation and Arithmetic Fundamental Lemma", Annals of Mathematics 193 (2021), no. 3
issues.reviewReason: Checked against Mihatsch–Zhang, fetched with the stated User-Agent (SHA-256 67c39ae1…, as in result.json). Their (7.6), p. 48, has φ′(x,y) = 2^{−1}(x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)} with ψ0(b) = exp(2πib). Footnote 5 reads: 'Here the Gaussian functions differ slightly from those in [35, Section 12]; the latter should be corrected accordingly' ([35] is this paper). Footnote 3, p. 18, says the same of the constants. Independent check: take ψ(t) = e^{2πit}, q(x,y) = xy, the pairing xy′ + x′y and the self-dual measure dx dy. Then e^{−c(x²+y²)} is Fourier-fixed only for c = π; the printed c = π/2 goes to 2e^{−2π(x²+y²)}. So the printed φ′ is not an eigenvector of w = κ_{π/2}. This falsifies the weight-1 claim before Lemma 12.5, and the SL2 formulas of Lemmas 12.5 and 12.11, for the stated ψ. The unitary side fails the same way. By (1.4), ⟨u,u⟩ = q(u) is the hermitian norm. For V = C, with pairing 2Re(z w̄) and self-dual measure 2 dx dy, the transform of e^{−πzz̄} is 2e^{−4πzz̄}; so 'φ̂ = φ' and (12.4) fail, and e^{−2πq} is the fixed Gaussian. The printed §12 is internally consistent with ψ(t) = e^{πit}, not with the stated ψ(t) = e^{2πit} and the Whittaker function (1.5): both orbital values are e^{−πξ}, and Lemma 14.3 inherits this. Suppose instead ⟨u,u⟩ in (12.1) is read as the bilinear form 2q(u), as in §11.1. Then the unitary side is right, but Lemma 12.6's matching fails, e^{−πξ} against e^{−2πξ}. On either reading a printed claim is false. The main theorems survive after the rescaling, and Mihatsch–Zhang redo the comparison in §§7–8. The author preprint has the same functions. Minor: Mihatsch–Zhang's text on p. 48 cites '[33, Section 12]' and '[33, Lemma 12.5]'; their [33] is Zhang's 2012 Invent. Math. paper, and the footnote's [35] is meant. Known: Mihatsch–Zhang §7.2 (7.6), Proposition 7.4 and footnote 5, p. 48; footnote 3, p. 18; §7.3, p. 49.

issues.reason: For n=2, t=diag(1,i), t′=diag(i,1), k=[[0,1],[-1,0]]∈SO2 give k⁻¹t′k=t. These are different diagonal parameters, not related merely by diagonal signs. An arbitrary torus cutoff need not be constant on this fibre. The author preprint contains the same assertion. (cc-442dc5) Verified: t = diag(1, i) and t′ = diag(i, 1) are regular in T_n, and with k = [[0, 1], [−1, 0]] ∈ SO(2), k^{−1}t′k = t. The fibre over t therefore contains (1, t) and (k, t′), which K ∩ A does not relate. One repair: support ϕ_{T_n} (and Ω) in a set meeting each Weyl orbit in T_n^rs at most once; the fibres are then K ∩ A-orbits, since an element of GL_n(R) conjugating one regular diagonal t into T_n is monomial.

Take γ = −(1 i; 0 1) ∈ S_2 (γγ̄ = 1, det(1−γ) = 4, (γ+1)² = 0, so γ is not semisimple), u1 = (1,2)^T, u2 = (3,1), e = 5i. Set y = c^{−1}(γ), y′ = (y, i·u1; i·u2(1−y²), e) ∈ s_3 and γ′ = c(y′) ∈ S_3. Computed exactly: 1−d ≠ 0 and det(1−γ′) ≠ 0; e is cyclic for γ′ and for its transpose, so γ′ is rs; the characteristic polynomial of γ′ has nonzero discriminant, so γ′ is srs. Yet r(γ′) = (γ,(u1,u2)), which is rs but not srs. Any g′ matching γ′ is srs, since it has the same characteristic polynomial, and r(g′) is not srs either. It uses q + 1 > n to choose ξ ∈ F^1 with det(1 − ξg′) ∈ O_F^×. The third equality of (4.5), together with integrality of det(1 − g), is then said to imply 1 − d ∈ O_F^×.
issues.correction: The residue class of ξ must also avoid ξ̄ = d̄^{−1} (when d̄ has norm 1), where 1 − ξd ∉ O_F^×. The integrality of g, the first component of r(ξg′), cannot be assumed: it depends on ξ and does not follow from either side of (a) being nonzero. For q ≥ n+1 (so q + 1 > n + 1) a good class exists and the rest of the proof applies verbatim. For q = n an extra argument is needed. As printed, Proposition 4.12(i) (and 2.7(i)) at q = n proves only (a)_n ⇒ (b)_{n−1}. So Theorem 13.9(a) at q = n and Theorem 15.1(a) at p = n lack a complete proof. issues.reason: FL counterexample to the reduction step (Proposition 2.7(i) at q = n = 3, whose proof is 'the same'). F0 = Q_3, F = Q_3(i) unramified, ε = −1. V♯_0 = ⊕ F v_i with orthogonal norms (1, 1, −1), Λ♯_0 = ⊕ O_F v_i self-dual, u0 = v1+v2+v3 of norm 1, so Λ♯_0 = Λ0 ⊕ O_F u0 with Λ0 = Λ♯_0 ∩ u0^⊥ self-dual. Take g′ = diag(1, −1, i) in the basis (v_i). Then g′ ∈ K♯_0 is srs (distinct eigenvalues, u0 cyclic), so Orb(g′, 1_{K♯_0}) > 0, and d = ⟨g′u0,u0⟩ = −i. F^1 reduces onto μ_4 = {±1, ±i}. det(1−ξg′) = (1−ξ)(1+ξ)(1−iξ) is a unit only for ξ ≡ i, and then 1 − ξd = 1 + iξ ≡ 0 (mod 3). No ξ satisfies both units, and for ξ ≡ i the element g_ξ has det(1−g_ξ) = det(1−ξg′)/(1−ξd) of negative valuation, although both sides of (a) are nonzero. AFL side: the same residue configuration occurs for n = p = 5 on the non-split V_5. Take g′ diagonal with eigenvalues lifting the five norm-one classes of F_25 other than 1, in an orthogonal basis with norms t ≡ (4,2,3,2) (mod 5) (units) and t_5 = 5; u0 = Σ v_i has norm Σ t_i = 1 and v(det) = 1, so V_5 is non-split; d ≡ 1 (brute-force search mod 5). The only class with det(1−ξg′) ∈ O_F^× is ξ ≡ 1, where 1−ξd ≡ 0. Whether Int(g′) ≠ 0 there was not checked, so on the AFL side the step is unproved rather than refuted. Mihatsch–Zhang (JEMS, §9.3) use this equivalence only for the group version for V_{n+1} with q ≥ n+1, so they do not correct it.

issues.locator: §5.2, Theorem 5.5 and its proof, p. 899
issues.printed: The proof assumes integral invariants for (g, u). It invokes the proof of Proposition 4.12(i) to obtain g′ = r̃^{−1}(g, u, e) ∈ U(V_{n+1})°(F0)_srs satisfying Int(g′) = Int(g, u).
issues.correction: State Theorem 5.5 under q ≥ n, which covers its only use (§15: F0 = Q_p, p ≥ n). For general q, cite Mihatsch [32], published as 'Local constancy of intersection numbers', Algebra Number Theory 16 (2022), 505–519.
issues.reason: The argument invoked first multiplies g by ξ ∈ F^1 so that det(1−ξg) ∈ O_F^×. This needs a norm-one residue class ξ̄ with ξ̄^{−1} not a root of the reduced characteristic polynomial of g (degree n), guaranteed only when q + 1 > n. Example: q = 3, n = 4, g with eigenvalues ±1, ±i; then no ξ works. Without det(1−g) ∈ O_F^× the construction does not make 1 − d = 2(1+e+ũ*(1+x)^{−1}ũ)^{−1} a unit, and Proposition 4.6 cannot be applied. Theorem 5.5 carries no hypothesis on q, and §§3–5 assume only p odd. Mihatsch–Zhang (JEMS, §1) describe [32] as proving local constancy for all regular semisimple elements.

issues.locator: §9.3, (9.12) and the sentence after it, p. 927; also (10.1)–(10.2), p. 930
issues.printed: The source defines Int♮_ν(ξ,Φ) := ⟨G^B_ν(ξ,φ), LCM(α,φ0)_{ν,C}⟩ log q_ν, assigning log q_ν = 2 at a complex place ν and 1 at a real place.
issues.correction: log q_ν = 1 for complex places ν (and ½ for a real place). Equivalently, a complex place contributes the value of the Green function on the complex 0-cycle once: ½ Σ over the two embeddings E → C in ν. Theorem 10.1, Corollary 10.3, Lemma 14.4 and the constant-term cancellation in the proof of Proposition 14.5 are stated and used in this normalization. Mihatsch–Zhang, JEMS 2023, (4.6) p. 25 and the factor [E:E0]/2 in Theorem 6.9(3) p. 39, use the same normalization without comment on this paper.
issues.reason: (i) The arithmetic Chow group of §8.4 (p. 923) has principal divisors (div f, (−log|f|²_w)_w), and the paper's own example gives V_p = (0, 2 log|p|) over Q. Pairing (V_p,0) with a horizontal section over Z gives log p from the finite part, so (0, 2 log p) must give log p: the weight is ½ per embedding (Gillet–Soulé's deg^ = Σ log#k(P) + ½Σ_σ g_σ), not 1 per real place as printed. (ii) Internal check: E has [E:F] complex places above a real v0. As in the proof of Theorem 9.4, each ν and each of the τ(ZQ) fibres of (8.4) contributes Σ_{(δ,u)} GK(u,h∞)(z_δ)·Orb((δ,u),Φ). So (10.1)–(10.2), with the printed log q_ν = 2, give Int^K_{v0} = 2Σ GK(u,h∞)(z_δ)·Orb, twice what (10.3) states. With the corrected weight, (9.14) holds and Theorem 10.1 is right as printed. issues.locator: Proposition 7.9(b), second sentence, and the last paragraph of its proof, pp. 911–912
issues.printed: Part (b) asserts properness of CM(α,g) → Spec O_E[1/𝔡] and says the morphism becomes finite étale upon restriction to Spec O_E[1/𝔡] \ Ram(α).
issues.correction: Keep 'proper, hence finite by (a), with generic fibre finite étale over E', which is all §9.1 uses. Drop the étaleness over Spec O_E[1/d] ∖ Ram(α), or assume in addition that F′/F is unramified above the places in question. Above places v ∉ Ram(α) where F′/F ramifies it fails.
issues.reason: Counterexample. F0 = Q, F = K imaginary quadratic, n = 2 (so E = E_Φ E_r = K). Let D > 1 be squarefree, p | D an odd prime with p ∤ d_K, F′ = K(√D) and F′_0 = Q(√D). Take ω ∈ O_K with ω − ω̄ a p-unit and δ = (1+ω√D)/(1+ω̄√D). This is a norm-one element for F′/F′_0, so its characteristic polynomial α over K is conjugate self-reciprocal and irreducible. δ − 1 = (ω−ω̄)√D/(1+ω̄√D) is a uniformizer at each prime of F′ over p, so O_{K,p}[δ] = O_{F′,p} and p ∉ Ram(α). Let d be the product of 2, the primes ramified in K and the primes dividing N(1+ω̄√D) (so p ∤ d). Let V = R_{F′/K}W with ⟨x,y⟩_W = xȳ/√D: signature (1,1), with O_{F′} self-dual away from d. Then (z_δ, h = 1) is a C-point of CM(α,δ_d). At any C-point, Lie A is a CM type Φ′ of F′ with Φ′|_K = {ϕ0, ϕ̄0} (Kottwitz condition), i.e. Φ′ = {ϕ0⊗s, ϕ̄0⊗(−s)} for a sign s of √D. An element of Gal(K̄/K) with √D ↦ −√D swaps the two types and so moves the point. The residue fields of the closed points of CM(α,δ_d)_K therefore contain K(√D), which is ramified over K above p. So CM(α,δ_d) is not étale over O_K[1/d] above p. The proof's appeal to [18, Prop. 3.1.2(3)] needs an O_{F′}-Kottwitz condition over a base containing the reflex field of (F′,Φ′), which Definition 7.8 does not impose (Remark 7.7). Only properness and the zero-dimensional generic fibre are used later (§9.1, p. 925), so no later result is affected.

Then (10.4) gives GK(u,h∞)(z_δ) = −Ei(−4πa_{v0}|ξ′|_{v′0}), and (10.8) becomes −ΣEi(−4πa_{v0}|ξ′|_{v′0})·Orb. This matches the corrected analytic side ½e^{−2πξ}Ei(−4πa|ξ|) (E12, E15) and is Mihatsch–Zhang's normalization ((3.15) with R = −2q(u_z); (6.4) and (6.6), with footnote 4, p. 37: 'we use Ei(−4πa_v|v(ζ)|) instead of Ei(−2πa_v|v(ζ)|)').
issues.reason: Kudla's Green function [23, §11] is ξ(√a x,z) = −Ei(−2πaR_K(x,z)) with R_K = −(x_z,x_z). It is the one attached to the Gaussian e^{−π(x,x)_z}, whose theta series is indexed by q^{Q(x)} with Q(x) = (x,x)/2. For the hermitian space, (1.2)–(1.4) give Q(x) = q(x) = ⟨x,x⟩ and (x,x) = tr⟨x,x⟩ = 2⟨x,x⟩, so R_K = −2⟨u_z,u_z⟩, and the Green function for Z(ξ) with coefficient q^ξ = e^{2πiξτ} ((8.2), (8.14), (8.17), W_ξ in (1.5)) is −Ei(4πaR(u,z)). The printed 2π belongs to the e^{−π⟨u,u⟩} (effectively q^{ξ/2}) normalization of §12 (E12). The archimedean comparison (Lemma 14.4) is consistent only because both sides carry the same factor. Theorem 8.4 is quoted from Ehlen–Sankaran [8], which uses Kudla's normalization, and does not apply to (8.11) as printed, so the proof of Proposition 14.5 needs the corrected (8.11) together with the corrected Gaussian. This is the geometric-side counterpart of E12; no existing sourceIssue records it. Known in effect: Mihatsch–Zhang, JEMS 2023, §3.6 and §6.2 (not presented as an erratum). The preprint has the same (8.11).

issues.locator: §11.4, p. 938 ('Let G′ = GL(V0) act on V′ by (std, std∨)') against §12.5, p. 945 ('g · (u1, u2) = (g^{−1}u1, gu2)'). The first convention governs (11.19)–(11.20) and matches the proof of Lemma 12.3 (p. 942, computed by (2.14)); the second governs (12.14)–(12.19) (pp. 945–946), (12.26)–(12.27) and Lemma 12.13 (p. 950). Also (12.9) (p. 944) against the proof of Lemma 12.6 (p. 945).
issues.printed: The source specifies the action (std, std∨) of G′ = GL(V0) on V′. In §12.5 it identifies SO(V′, q) with the F0-group G′ := GL1,F0 using g · (u1, u2) = (g^{−1}u1, gu2) on V′.
issues.correction: Fix one action throughout. With (std, std∨), g·(u1,u2) = (gu1, u2g^{−1}): (11.20) agrees with (2.14), and Lemmas 12.3 and 12.5 stand. But then the n = 1 formulas become Orb(0+,φ′,s) = ∫φ′(g,0)|g|^{−s}η(g)dg and Orb(0−,φ′,s) = ∫φ′(0,g)|g|^{s}η(g)dg, with L(∓s,η). Lemma 12.11 becomes a^{(1+s)/2}·2^{−s/2−1} (½a^{(1+s)/2} after E12). (12.27) is normalized by L(−s,η′_v) and converges for Re(s) < 0. With §12.5's action instead: (11.20) equals (2.14) at −s, so Lemmas 12.3 and 12.5, and the derivative of Lemma 14.3(b), must be read with s ↦ −s, and the derivatives change sign. In either case (12.9) should read (h,t,u′) ↦ (h^{−1}th, h^{−1}·u′) for the left action used in the proof of Lemma 12.6.
issues.reason: For n = 1, (std, std∨) is g·(u1,u2) = (gu1, g^{−1}u2), the inverse of §12.5's action. Under (std, std∨), (11.20) at u′ = (1,ξ) is ∫φ′(g^{−1}, gξ)|g|^s d^×g = ∫φ′(t, ξ/t)|t|^{−s} d^×t. This is the integrand t^{−s} of Lemma 12.3's proof, which cites (2.14) with h·(u1,u2) = (h^{−1}u1, u2h). Under §12.5's action, (12.14) is ∫φ′(g, ξ/g)|g|^s d^×g, the same function at −s. The nilpotent integrals (12.15), (12.18) and (12.27), and Lemma 12.13's half-plane Re(s) > 0, hold only for §12.5's action. Under (std, std∨) the 0+ integrand is Φ′(γ, g^{−1}u1, 0)|det g|^s, which tends to Φ′(γ,0,0)|det g|^s as |det g| → ∞ along T′, so it converges only for Re(s) < 0. So both conventions enter the single function J(h,Φ′,s): the regular terms through Lemmas 12.3 and 12.6, the nilpotent terms through Lemma 12.11. Their s-derivatives are then added in (12.38). Values at s = 0 are unaffected, and so are Theorems 12.9 and 12.14, which hold for every s and hence for −s. The relative sign of ∂Orb(0±) and the regular-orbit derivatives is affected. That sign enters the cancellation of the log|a|_v terms in Proposition 14.5, which the §14 reviewer should recheck in one convention. Unchecked lead from my own computation: with the printed (12.15)–(12.19) and the paper's Orb(0+) = −Orb(0−), I find the coefficient of log a in 2∂Orb(0±, ω(h)Φ′) to be −2n·Orb((γ,0+),Φ′), and its negative under (std, std∨). The factor n comes from |det(a^{1/2}1_n)|^{s} = a^{ns/2}. P. 964 states +2·Orb((γ,0+),Φ′). The preprint has both actions. Mihatsch–Zhang §§7.1–7.2 repeat the pairing: their global (7.1) uses §12.5's action, and their local integral uses φ′(u1t^{−1}, tu2)|t|^s, i.e. (2.14).

issues.printed: The source invokes Lemma 12.3 together with (12.2) to conclude that Φ′ qualifies as a partial Gaussian test function with respect to the compact set Ω.
issues.correction: For n ≥ 2 the transfer factor must be compensated. Either require ϕ_{T_n}(t) = η̃(det(t)^{−⌊n/2⌋}∏_{i<j}(t_j − t_i))^{−1} for t ∈ Ω, a smooth K∩A-invariant function on T_n^rs; or, since only the orbit of the fixed γ matters in §§12.6–14, multiply Φ′_v by the constant η̃(det(γ)^{−⌊n/2⌋}∏_{i<j}(t_j − t_i))^{−1}, where (t_i) are the entries of γ conjugated into T_n. With either change, Φ′ is a partial Gaussian test function.
issues.reason: Special values include the transfer factor, by (2.13) and the S_n × V′_n analogue of (2.17): Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = ω(γ,u′)·Orb((γ,u′),Φ′,0), with ω(γ,u′) = η̃(det(γ)^{−⌊n/2⌋}det(γ^iu1)_{0≤i≤n−1}). At C/R, η̃ extends sgn from R^× to C^×, so η̃(z) = (z/|z|)^m with m odd. For γ = diag(t_1,…,t_n) ∈ T_n^rs and u1 = (x_i), det(γ^iu1) = ∏x_i·∏_{i<j}(t_j − t_i). Hence ω(γ,u′) = sgn(∏x_i)·η̃(w(t)), with w(t) = det(t)^{−⌊n/2⌋}∏_{i<j}(t_j − t_i). Lemma 12.6 gives the raw value Orb(u′,φ′,0) = ∏_i sgn(x_i)·Orb((1,ξ_i),φ′_1,0), by the substitution t ↦ x_i t in each rank-one integral. This equals sgn(∏x_i)·e^{−2πΣξ_i} when all ξ_i = x_iy_i > 0, using the corrected Gaussian. Therefore Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = η̃(w(γ))·Orb((δ,u),Φ). For n = 2 and t = (1,i), w = (i−1)/i = 1+i and η̃(w) = e^{imπ/4} ≠ 1. In general w(t) is real or purely imaginary when n is odd, and for even n its phase varies continuously on T_n^rs. For n = 1 the factor is 1 (Remark 12.4), which is the only case the paper checks. FL and AFL survive, because only the fixed rational γ matters and the constant ∏_{v|∞}η̃_v(w_v(γ)) can be absorbed into Φ′_∞. With the printed choice, however, J(h,Φ′) and J(h,Φ) differ by that constant in Theorem 13.4. The preprint has the same text. Mihatsch–Zhang (p. 53, §8.2) say the transfer factor lies in {±1}, which cannot hold at C/R.

issues.locator: Appendix B.2, Lemma B.1 and its proof, p. 974 (with the inverse-limit K-groups of B.1, p. 973)
issues.printed: Lemma B.1 takes X to be a locally noetherian formal scheme of the previously specified type. Its proof claims an immediate reduction to noetherian X and thereafter assumes that condition.
issues.correction: State Lemma B.1 (and Lemma B.2(ii)) for noetherian X, or define the quotients for locally noetherian X as inverse limits of the noetherian cokernels. The paper uses nothing beyond this: Lemma B.2 is used only in its local form (i), in the proof of Lemma 4.4, p. 889.
issues.reason: For locally noetherian X, B.1 defines K′_0(X) = lim_i K′_0(X_i), and footnote 11 says the quotients in Lemma B.1 are cokernels. Cokernels do not commute with inverse limits: comparing coker(lim) with lim(coker) involves a lim^1 term. Moreover, for an element of lim_i K′_0(X_i), 'E ⊗ O_{X1}' is defined at each stage only modulo the image of K′_0(X1∩X2∩X_i). So the reduction to the noetherian case is not immediate, and a proof would need a Mittag-Leffler argument that the paper does not give. The noetherian case itself is proved correctly.

issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right. On the v2 page images (PDF pp. 47-48) the quoted passage is verbatim, including the malformed 'H x Y ≃ Y_{(Y/H')^{p^-∞}} Y'. The torsor claim 'I.e. Y -> (Y'/H')^{p^-∞} is an H-torsor' rests only on the isomorphism H x Y ≃ Y x_M Y (M the perfected coarse space). By the paper's own definition (A.1.3, p. 468) a torsor also needs an fpqc, in particular flat, projection, and nothing in the v2 argument gives flatness. The displayed isomorphism cannot give it on its own: with H trivial it only says Y -> M is a monomorphism, e.g. the perfection of Spec k ⊔ (A^1 minus 0) -> A^1, which is surjective but not flat. Coarse quotients by finite flat groupoids are not flat in general (A^2 -> A^2/{±1}). The conclusion is nevertheless true. The published proof (Theorem A.29 reduced to Theorem A.30, flatness from Lemma A.31, pp. 476-477, identical in v3 PDF pp. 53-54) proves it. The published argument is complete once one notes that A^{p^-∞} ⊗_{C^{p^-∞}} A^{p^-∞} = B^{p^-∞} is flat over A^{p^-∞}, since B is finite locally free over A, and that ∩ J_k^{p^-∞} = 0 because some power of each element lands in (∏ J_k)R, which lies in the nilradical. So the v2 step is unjustified, not false: a gap in the v2 proof, not an error. The published paper does not have it. I checked the arXiv record myself: v3 is dated 20 Jul 2016 and its comment reads 'Fix a gap in the proof of Theorem A.29. A few more details added'. The numbering correspondence (v2 Prop. A.28 = v3/published Theorem A.29, v2 Lemma A.27 = published Lemma A.28) matches the images.

issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The page image of p. 422 matches the quotation. The first two sentences of the proof of Lemma 1.14 write Gr^{p^{−∞}}(i, 𝓔_0/p) three times. The lemma on the same page concerns an arbitrary rank-n locally free crystal 𝓔 on a perfect k-scheme X and concludes Y ≅ Gr^{p^{−∞}}(i, 𝓔/p), where 𝓔/p is the vector bundle defined in the paragraph just above. The maps written in the proof (x^*𝓔/p → x^*𝓔/𝓕_x → 0, x^*𝓔/p → 𝒬 → 0) use x^*𝓔/p, so 𝓔/p is meant. The only meaning 𝓔_0 has nearby is W(R)^n (§1.2.1, §1.3.1). That would give the constant Grassmannian Gr(i,n) × X, which is wrong for the application in Prop. 1.13 to the tautological crystal 𝓔_N on Gr_{μ•} (p. 423). In arXiv v2 (Lemma 1.15 there) the crystal itself was called E_0 and Gr(i, E_0/p) was consistent. The published text renamed the crystal 𝓔 but left these three occurrences, and v3 matches the published text. The revision improves the ledger entry. The old 'printed' field was a paraphrase, and the old reason ('varying lattice' versus 'fixed initial lattice') misdescribed what is in fact a name left over from v2.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The quotation matches p. 424. The displayed chain is 𝓕_N ⇠ 𝓕_{N−1} ⇠ ⋯ ⇠ 𝓕_0 = 𝓔, so its maps are 𝓕_i ⇢ 𝓕_{i+1}, and the condition is Inv(𝓕_i ⇢ 𝓕_{i+1}) = μ_i^*. Re-derivation: (Gr_{μ•})_R consists of chains 𝓔 = 𝓔_N ⇢ ⋯ ⇢ 𝓔_0 with Inv(β_i : 𝓔_i ⇢ 𝓔_{i−1}) = μ_i. The next sentence takes the quasi-isogeny 𝓕_N ⇢ 𝓕_0 = 𝓔 ⇢ 𝓔_0 and cuts out X_{ω_0}, where it is an isomorphism, which forces 𝓕_i ↔ 𝓔_{N−i}. So 𝓕_i ⇢ 𝓕_{i+1} is β_{N−i}, of position μ_{N−i}, and 𝓕_i ⇢ 𝓕_{i−1} is β_{N+1−i}^{−1}, of position μ_{N+1−i}^*. The printed condition neither reverses the index (for i = 0 it asks for μ_0, which does not exist) nor matches the star to the displayed direction. By the definition on p. 416 (Inv(β) = ω_i iff β : E_1 → E_2 is an inclusion with pE_2 ⊂ E_1 and dim E_2/E_1 = i), when all μ_j = ω_1 one has 𝓕_i = 𝓔_{N−i} ⊂ 𝓔_{N−i−1} = 𝓕_{i+1} of colength one. So Inv(𝓕_i ⇢ 𝓕_{i+1}) = ω_1, not ω_1^*. The revised correction is right, its two forms agree, and the rest of the proof works once it is made. The revision also improves the ledger. The old 'printed' was a paraphrase. The old reason's 'incompatible displayed arrows' is inaccurate: the chain arrows and the arrow in the condition agree, and what is wrong is the index and the star attached to that direction. The same text is in v2 (Lemma 1.17) and v3.

issues.locator: p. 437, Lemma 2.12(ii) (statement), and p. 438, proof of Lemma 2.12
issues.printed: The source identifies s_{1+θ} with the affine reflection for 1 + θ. It also says that −θ − 1 is the sole affine root belonging to Q_{1/2} and absent from Q_{1/4}.
issues.correction: Read θ^∨ for θ in both affine roots: 's_{1+θ^∨} is the affine reflection corresponding to 1 + θ^∨' (Lemma 2.12(ii), p. 437) and 'the only affine root appearing in Q_{1/2} but not in Q_{1/4} is −θ^∨ − 1' (proof, p. 438).
issues.reason: Q_r is the parahoric of the point −rμ (explicit in arXiv v2). With the convention that α + k corresponds to U_α(ϖ^kO), U_α(ϖ^kO) ⊂ Q_r iff k ≥ ⌈r⟨μ,α⟩⌉. The only root subgroup at which Q_{1/2} and Q_{1/4} differ is U_{−θ^∨}(ϖ^{-1}O), i.e. the affine root −θ^∨ − 1; Q_{1/2} and Q_{3/4} differ only at θ^∨ + 1. Both affine roots vanish at −θ/2, the point of Q_{1/2}, and s_{1+θ^∨} = s_{−θ^∨−1}, so the sign causes no ambiguity. This reflection is the nontrivial Weyl element of the rank-one quotient of Q_{1/2}; it conjugates Q_{1/4} to Q_{3/4}, and Q_{1/4}sQ_{3/4}/Q_{3/4} is the Q_{1/4}-fixed point of P^1, which maps to Gr_0. arXiv v2 (p. 21, item (2)) writes 'the hyperplane H given by the affine root 1 + θ^∨', which confirms this reading. So this is a notational slip; the recorded 'affects: the proof' and the open 'wall sign' question are not warranted. The first occurrence is in the statement of 2.12(ii), not the proof.

issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right. The page images read 's_{1+θ} is the affine reflection corresponding to 1 + θ' (statement of Lemma 2.12(ii), p. 437) and 'the only affine root appearing in Q_{1/2} but not in Q_{1/4} is −θ − 1' (proof, p. 438). On p. 437 θ is the coroot μ and θ^∨ is the corresponding root. An affine root has a root as its linear part, so '1 + θ' is ill-typed. I recomputed from the definition on p. 437: U_α(ϖ^kO) ⊂ Q_r iff k ≥ ⌈r⟨θ,α⟩⌉, and ⟨θ,α⟩ ∈ {0,±1,±2}, with ±2 only for α = ±θ^∨. Q_{1/2} and Q_{1/4} differ only at α = −θ^∨ (k ≥ −1 against k ≥ 0), i.e. at the affine root −θ^∨ − 1. Q_{1/2} and Q_{3/4} differ only at θ^∨ (k ≥ 1 against k ≥ 2), i.e. at θ^∨ + 1. So the reductive quotient of Q_{1/2} has an A_1 factor with roots ±(θ^∨+1), and Q_{1/4} and Q_{3/4} map to opposite Borels of it. The reflection s_{θ^∨+1} = s_{−θ^∨−1} (so the sign is irrelevant) fixes −θ/2 and sends −θ/4 to −3θ/4. It conjugates Q_{1/4} to Q_{3/4} and sends ϖ^θ to the base point. Q_{1/4}sQ_{3/4}/Q_{3/4} is the Q_{1/4}-fixed point of Q_{1/2}/Q_{3/4} ≅ P^1, and Q_0 ×^{Q_{1/4}} (that point) = Q_0/Q_{1/4} = Ḡ/P̄_θ maps to Gr_0, as claimed. Only one reading makes sense and it is confirmed by arXiv v2 (p. 21, item (2): 'the hyperplane H given by the affine root 1 + θ^∨'), so the old 'affects: the proof' and the open 'wall sign' question are not warranted. The same text is in v2 and v3. The first occurrence is in the statement of 2.12(ii) on p. 437, the second in the proof on p. 438.

issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right. The quotation matches the image of p. 448. By (1.4.5) (p. 429), p is the map to Z/2 written multiplicatively, μ → (-1)^{(2ρ,μ)}, and Lemma 1.25 and p. 448 say its values are 1 or -1. That is what an additive reading of p in F_2 would give, and it is what the text announces ('by a Koszul sign change') and cites ([BD, 5.3.21], [MV07] after Remark 6.2). The sign bookkeeping works only together with E57: the Koszul change gives Proposition 2.21 exactly because H^*(c') is the Koszul-signed flip.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The sentence is an accurate, compressed description of LY13 (published version). The proof of Lemma 4.3 (arXiv 3.3) contains a single sign computation: τ_K^* acts by −1 on H^2 of the orbit's partial flag variety, which is the degree-2 case of the analogue of Zhu's Lemma 2.32 (Zhu, p. 451: 'essentially the same as [LY13, Lemma 3.3]'). With geometric Satake this gives g = (−1)^ρ, hence Lemma 4.3(3) (the analogue of Lemma 2.30), then §4.4/§7.4 (the analogue of Lemma 2.34) and Theorem 1.3/7.3. Zhu states the intermediate step through Lemma 2.30 and geometric Satake explicitly on p. 450 and p. 452, and Remark 2.33 explains why the Chern-class computation alone does not suffice without Satake, so there is no inconsistency. In any case a provenance remark cannot affect Zhu's proof, which uses Theorem 2.35 as a black box. The genuine defect nearby is the LY13 numbering, recorded as a separate new issue. Independent check: I agree with the first reading that this is not a mistake. The sentence on p. 453 matches the image. In LY13 (published version, checked; arXiv 1203.0521v1 is the only arXiv version), Lemma 4.3 (v1: 3.3) takes one geometric input, besides the Satake equivalence. That input is that τ_K^* acts trivially on H^0 and by -1 on H^2 of the partial flag variety K/(P_λ ∩ K) onto which the open orbit retracts. This is the degree <= 2 case of the equal-characteristic analogue of Zhu's Lemma 2.32, and Zhu (p. 451) says his proof of 2.32 is 'essentially the same as [LY13, Lemma 3.3]'. Using IH^i = H^i(open orbit) for i <= 2, and Tannakian arguments with geometric Satake, LY obtain g = (-1)^ρ and hence Lemma 4.3(3), the analogue of Lemma 2.30. Section 4.4 then gives the stalk sign (analogue of Lemma 2.34), and (3.5) gives Theorem 1.3. Section 7.4 reruns this chain for Theorem 7.3, which is Zhu's Theorem 2.35. So 'deduced ... from the equal characteristic analogue of Lemma 2.32' is a compressed but true description. It does not claim that the Chern-class computation suffices on its own. Zhu says explicitly on p. 450 that LY used the equal-characteristic geometric Satake, and Remark 2.33 explains why 2.32 alone does not give 2.30. The ledger's contrary claim, that the argument uses the IH sign theorem (analogue of 2.30), is also true, because that is an intermediate step of the same chain. It does not make Zhu's sentence false. In any case a provenance remark cannot affect Zhu's proof, which uses Theorem 2.35 as a black box, so the ledger's 'affects: the proof' is unfounded. The real defect nearby is the LY13 numbering (E59).

issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right. On the images of p. 459 (last lines) and p. 460, the paper applies the fibre bound for m^{-1}(ϖ^λ) to 'the preimage of X^H_≤λ((Nm b)σ_E)'. Read literally, the inference 'dim of preimage ≤ dim X_≤λ + (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ)' is not justified. Points of X_≤λ that lie in a smaller stratum X_λ' (λ' < λ) have fibres of dimension up to (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ'), which can exceed (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ). For λ = |μ•| the literal argument would bound the whole of X_≤μ• by dim X_≤|μ•| + 0. But the displayed bound is itself true, and the conclusion follows by the obvious stratified reading. Assume (3.1.3) for H. For each λ' ≤ |μ•|, the preimage of the exact stratum X_λ' has dimension ≤ (ρ_H, λ' − ν_{Nm b}) − ½def_H(Nm b) + (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ') = (ρ_H, |μ•| − ν_{Nm b}) − ½def_H(Nm b). This number does not depend on λ'. X_≤μ• is the finite union of these preimages, so the upper bound holds, and Lemma 3.7 converts it to (ρ_G, μ − ν_b) − ½def_G(b). Equality: for λ' < |μ•| we have (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ') ≥ 1, since |μ•| − λ' is a nonzero sum of positive coroots. So by (3.1.3) for H every closed stratum X_≤λ' has strictly smaller dimension than X_≤|μ•| (when the latter is nonempty). Hence the open stratum X_|μ•| is nonempty and of full dimension. Over it m is bijective (the fibre over ϖ^{|μ•|} is a point), which gives equality. So replacing '≤λ' by the exact stratum 'λ' (the text says 'for λ' and uses the fibre over ϖ^λ) makes the proof correct as written. The meaning is clear and nothing downstream changes, so the right classification is misprint/nothing, not error/'the proof'. I checked that arXiv v3 has the same wording. arXiv v2 (PDF p. 36) writes 'dim X^H_≤μ•(Nm(b)) = max_λ dim X^H_≤λ(Nm b) + (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ)', with the same looseness. issues.locator: A.3.3, p. 480 (first paragraph)
issues.printed: The source sets c_X = c_{X'} o (eps^*)^{-1}. For a morphism f : X' -> X'' between irreducible algebraic spaces, each of dimension d and of finite presentation, it asserts that the canonical isomorphism f^* : H^{2d}_c(X''_kbar, Qlbar(d)) = H^{2d}_c(X'_kbar, Qlbar(d)) respects both c_{X'} and c_{X''}. This is used to conclude that the definition of c_X is unambiguous.
issues.correction: For finite surjective f of generic degree δ between geometrically irreducible d-dimensional spaces, c_{X'}∘f^* = δ·c_{X''}. Comparison maps between models (X'^{(m)} -> X'', Prop. A.17) are universal homeomorphisms of p-power degree. So c_X = c_{X'}∘(ε^*)^{-1} depends on the model up to a factor in p^Z, and no model-independent normalization exists (the perfected Frobenius of (P^1)^{p^-∞} is a k-automorphism acting by p). Either fix a model, or regard c_X, [X] and cl(Z) (and the bases of Remark 2.4 and Cor. 2.9) as canonical only up to powers of p. For subspaces of Gr_μ, canonical classes could be restored relative to a fixed model of the ambient space, e.g. the canonical model Gr'_μ of §B.2 with reduced induced structures, but the paper does not do this.
issues.reason: (i) Read literally (any morphism) the claim fails. H^{2d}_c is contravariant only for proper maps, a constant map kills H^{2d}, and a degree-delta finite map multiplies the trace by delta. (ii) It also fails for the intended model comparisons. Let X = (P^1_k)^{p^-inf} and let phi be the perfection of the relative Frobenius of P^1; phi is a k-automorphism of X with phi^* O(1) = O(p) (cf. Remark A.24). So phi^* acts by p on H^2_c(X_kbar, Qlbar(1)), and the models (P^1, eps) and (P^1, eps o phi) give values of c_X differing by p. Any c_X natural under automorphisms would need p = 1. The existing correction's 'an independent normalization proof remains open' should therefore read: no such normalization exists. Downstream, the 'canonical basis' of Remark 2.4 (p. 432) and the 'canonical isomorphism' CT_lambda(IC_mu) = Qlbar[B_mu(lambda)] of Cor. 2.9 (p. 435) are canonical only up to rescaling each basis vector by a power of p. The index sets and the lines are canonical. The Satake equivalence and the dimension results do not use this normalization. Present verbatim in v2 and v3.

issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The quotation is verbatim on the p. 480 image, and v2 and v3 have the same. The revised argument is correct, and it strengthens the ledger's. Let X = (P^1_k)^{p^-∞} with model ε: X -> P^1, and let F: P^1 -> P^1, [x:y] ↦ [x^p:y^p], be the k-linear relative Frobenius (P^1 is defined over F_p). Its perfection φ is a k-automorphism of X, the perfection of a universal homeomorphism (cf. Cor. A.16), with ε∘φ = F∘ε. So (P^1, F∘ε) is another model in the paper's sense (p. 471). F is finite flat of degree p and F^*O(1) = O(p) (cf. Remark A.24), so F^* acts by p on H^2(P^1_k̄, Q̄_ℓ(1)), and the standard trace satisfies Tr∘F^* = p·Tr. So the paper's claim that model morphisms f^* are 'compatible with c_{X'} and c_{X''}' fails already for model comparisons, and the two models give values of c_X that differ by p. There is no way to repair this intrinsically. φ^* acts by p on the line H^2_c(X_k̄, Q̄_ℓ(1)), so an isomorphism c_X invariant under k-automorphisms of X would force c_X = p·c_X. The 'alternative' construction via Pic((P^1)^{p^-∞}) = Z[1/p] has the same ambiguity, because the generator is determined only up to p^Z (Remark A.24). In general, comparison maps between models are finite universal homeomorphisms of p-power degree, so c_X, [X] and cl(Z) are defined only up to factors in p^Z. The ledger's 'normalization proof remains open' should therefore become 'no model-independent normalization exists'. Reach: the canonicity assertions of A.3.3 are false as stated, and so is the word 'canonical' in Cor. 2.9 ('canonical isomorphism CT_λ(IC_μ) ≅ Q̄_ℓ[B_μ(λ)]', p. 435) and in Remark 2.4's 'canonical basis' (p. 432): each basis vector is determined only up to a power of p. The index sets, the lines, the basis property and all dimension statements (hence the Satake equivalence) are unaffected. Hence error / a stated result, with limited downstream effect.

The decomposition sought is X = Ag: see the definition of W on p. 487, the multiplication 'by X^* on the left and g^{−1} on the right' that gives X^*A, and the conclusion 'then X = Ag'. (B.3.3) returns x = 0, y = 1, z = 0, which is this A. But XA^* = (p²−p −1; p² p²+p), so XA^{−1} has entry −1/p². With the order corrected, the proof works. For p > 2, (B.3.2) is equivalent to X^*A ≡ 0 mod p²: the p^0 terms cancel exactly as Teichmüller sums, e.g. [d_0x] + [−b_0z] = 0 when d_0x = b_0z, and the p^1 terms give the second equation. For 2×2 matrices, adj(X^*A) = A^*X, so A^*X ≡ 0 mod p². Hence p^{−2}Ã^*X̃ is integral, with determinant det X̃/p² ∈ W(R)^*. Both expressions in the display must be changed.

issues.reviewReason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right on each point I checked. (1) Locator: the sentence 'Proofs are generally omitted in this section.' is on p. 482 (PDF p. 80), in the opening paragraph of Appendix B, not on p. 484. (2) The following have no proof at all: Prop. B.1, Lemma B.9, and the final paragraph of B.3 ('one can also verify Conjecture I in this case'). The following have only hints or sketches: Prop. B.2 (one sentence), Lemma B.4 ('We give a hint of the proof'), Lemma B.7 and Prop. B.8 ('Details are left to readers'). The unnumbered assertions are unproved: on p. 485, that conditions (3)–(4) cut out M_{N,h} as an irreducible component; on p. 486, that \mathring M_{N,h} ≃ Gr′_N; and in Remark B.6. (3) The existing entry is wrong to list Lemmas B.10–B.11 as unproved, and I rechecked their proofs. (B.3.1) is correct: for 2×2 matrices, X_1X_0^* + X_0X_1^* = tr(X_1X_0^*)·I. In (B.3.3), when a_1d_1 − b_1c_1 is a unit, the second equation of (B.3.2) forces m = X_1X_0^*/(b_1c_1 − a_1d_1). This m is traceless because 2·tr(X_1X_0^*) = 0 and p > 2, has det m = det X_0/det X_1 = 0, and satisfies X_0^*m = 0 because X_0^*X_1X_0^* = −det(X_0)X_1^* = 0. The step W = W̃G and the uniqueness of A are sound, since A ∈ W̃ with A_1 = A_2(g_2g_1^{−1}). The remaining 'argument as in Lemma 1.10' also goes through. For (E,β,ε̄) in V, the image X = Ag lies in W. Transporting along the unique α with β∘α = Ã gives (E_0, Ã, h) with Ah = X. That point is the image of (A, h), so the map is surjective. It is injective because A is unique and β∘α = β forces α = id. The only defects in these proofs are E32 and E33. (4) Prop. B.2's sentence tacitly needs \tilde L_det to be trivial on the fibres of π. That follows from base-point-freeness together with the second part of Prop. B.1 (degree 0 on fibre curves, itself unproved). The fibres are connected (Lemma 1.18), and π_*O = O (Lemma A.21). (5) The Lemma B.4 hint is sound: the stabilizer of diag(p^{m_i}) has dimension nΣm_i = nN, and so does that of every double-coset translate. Hence dim V_{N,h} = N(n−1) + n²h − nN = n²h − N. The main theorems do not use Appendix B. §§0–3 cite it only in remarks, footnote 5 and the introduction. So the gap affects only the appendix's own stated results. Footnote 21 records that Bhatt–Scholze proved Conjectures I–II.

issues.locator: §0.2, pp. 407–408 (setting of Theorem 0.3)
issues.printed: On p. 407, the source takes G reductive over O, the integer ring of a p-adic field F, and denotes its affine Grassmannian by Gr_G. It claims that the category is semisimple and monoidal, as in equal characteristic. Theorem 0.3 on p. 408 imposes no condition on k.
issues.correction: In §0.2 (p. 407) and Theorem 0.3 (p. 408), assume that the residue field k over which Gr_G is formed is algebraically closed (and that G is connected reductive), as in §2, p. 429. Equivalently, work with Gr_G ⊗_k k̄.
issues.reason: In the introduction k is the residue field of F (§0.1.1, p. 404; §0.1.3, p. 405), and for a p-adic field it is finite. Over a finite k the semisimplicity claim and Theorem 0.3 fail. For G = G_m, Gr_G is the discrete set X_• = Z, and P_{L+G}(Gr_G) is the direct sum over Z of the categories of continuous Q̄_ℓ-representations of Gal(k̄/k). That category is not semisimple (Frobenius can act by a unipotent Jordan block), and H* does not give an equivalence onto Rep(Ĝ_m) = Z-graded vector spaces. The body proves the theorem only for algebraically closed k (§2, p. 429), and item T07 correctly includes that hypothesis. Case for the defence: introductions are informal, geometric Satake is conventionally stated over an algebraically closed field, §0.3 sets k = F̄_p two pages later, and the body states the hypothesis explicitly. That is why I class it as a misprint affecting nothing.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotations match the images of pp. 407–408. The setting is 'Let G be a reductive group over O, the ring of integers of a p-adic field F, and let Gr_G denote its affine Grassmannian ... this is a semisimple monoidal category', and Theorem 0.3 imposes no condition on k. Gr_G lives over k, which §0.1.1 (p. 404) defines as the residue field of the local field F; for a p-adic field k is finite. Even §0.5 (p. 411) fixes only 'a perfect field k'. The hypothesis first appears in §2 (p. 429): 'we assume that k is algebraically closed and that G is a connected reductive group scheme over O in this section'. So the missing hypothesis is not a convention stated elsewhere. For finite k both claims fail, for every G. The base point Gr_0 = L^+G/L^+G ≅ Spec k is a closed L^+G-orbit on which the connected group L^+G acts trivially. L^+G-equivariant perverse sheaves supported there are the continuous finite-dimensional Q̄_ℓ-representations of Gal(k̄/k). That category is not semisimple: Frobenius can act by the unipotent Jordan block [[1,1],[0,1]], which extends continuously to Ẑ → GL_2(Z_ℓ). Moreover, on these sheaves H* only forgets the Galois action. It is not full, since two different Frobenius characters are non-isomorphic sheaves with isomorphic H* = Q̄_ℓ, so H* does not factor through an equivalence onto Rep(Ĝ). The first reading's G_m example is a special case. For a non-split G over finite k, 'Ĝ' is also not the right target. Case for the defence, which I accept for the classification: the introduction is informal, §0.3 takes k = F̄_p on p. 409, geometric Satake is conventionally stated over an algebraically closed field, and the body theorem (§2) carries the hypothesis. The ledger item T07 already includes it. Misprint, affects nothing.

issues.printed: The source cites [GHKR06] and [CKV15] for the assertion that adjoint G admits superbasic σ-conjugacy classes only in these cases: G = PGL_n; G = Res_{E/F} PGL_n, with E/F unramified (p. 410). The assertion recurs on p. 456 using G_F.
issues.correction: On p. 410 and p. 456 read 'if G is F-simple of adjoint type' (as on p. 457). Equivalently, for G of adjoint type, superbasic classes exist only when G_F is a product of groups Res_{E_i/F} PGL_{n_i} with E_i/F unramified.
issues.reason: Without simplicity the claim is false. Take G = PGL_2 × PGL_3 over O, which is adjoint. If b_i is superbasic in PGL_i (for example the class with Kottwitz invariant 1), then b = (b_1, b_2) is superbasic in G. A proper F-Levi of G has the form M_1 × M_2 with some M_i proper, and b_i does not meet a proper Levi of PGL_i. Yet G is neither PGL_n nor Res_{E/F} PGL_n. The proof on p. 457 first reduces to simple adjoint G, so nothing downstream is affected.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches the image of p. 410, and p. 456 repeats the sentence with G_F. The literal claim is false. Take G = PGL_2 × PGL_3 over O, which is unramified and adjoint. Parabolic subgroups, and hence Levi subgroups over F, of a product are products M_1 × M_2 of Levis of the factors, and σ-conjugacy is taken componentwise. Let b_i be superbasic in PGL_i, for example the basic class with Kottwitz invariant 1 in Z/i. If some σ-conjugate of b = (b_1, b_2) lay in a proper M_1 × M_2, then some M_i would be proper and b_i would meet it, a contradiction. So b is superbasic. Yet G_F is neither PGL_n nor Res_{E/F} PGL_n, being neither simple nor a restriction of scalars of PGL_n from a field. The same argument shows that for adjoint G, superbasic classes exist exactly when every F-simple factor is Res_{E_i/F} PGL_{n_i}. The paper's own proof (p. 457) says 'one can assume that G = G_ad is simple of adjoint type. Then it follows from [GHKR06], [CKV15] that superbasic b exists only when G_F = Res_{E/F} PGL_n'. The intended hypothesis is therefore clear, and the argument that is actually run is correct. The slip is confined to the paraphrases on pp. 410 and 456.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches pp. 412–413. §0.5 (p. 411) defines W_𝒪(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(k)} 𝒪 and W_{𝒪,n}(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(k)} 𝒪/ϖ^n only 'for a perfect k-algebra R'; it also notes W_h(R) = W(R)/p^hW(R) only for perfect R. §1.1.1 nevertheless applies these to all affine k-schemes. For L_p^+ the natural extension does no harm: W(R) ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ W(R)^e for any R, which gives (Res_{𝒪/W(k)}𝒳)(W(R)), a representable functor. For L_p^h it fails. Take 𝒪 = W(k), h = 1 and 𝒳 = 𝔸^1: the formula gives R ↦ W(R)/pW(R) = W(R)/VFW(R). Here V[t] ∉ VFW(k[t]), since that would need t to be a p-th power, but V[t] becomes 0 after the fpqc cover k[t] → k[t^{1/p}]. So this functor is not even fpqc-separated, let alone a finite-type scheme. The intended functor is Greenberg's, as the citation says. p. 419 confirms this: it writes L_p^hM_n = 𝔸^{n²h} and L_p^h𝔸^1 = 𝔸^h, which hold for W_h(R) and fail for W(R)/p^h. So this is a notational slip whose meaning is clear, and nothing downstream is affected. The proposed correction needs fixing, however. W_m(R) ⊗_{W_m(k)} 𝒪/ϖ^h with merely em ≥ h is not well defined: for e = 1, h = 1, m = 2 it gives W_2(R)/pW_2(R) ≠ R. Even with m = ⌈h/e⌉ it is wrong when e ∤ h. For 𝒪 = W(k)[√p] and h = 3 it contains W_2(R)/pW_2(R) ≅ R × R/R^p (as sets) as a summand, which is not representable, whereas Greenberg's functor is.

issues.locator: p. 414, proof of Lemma 1.3
issues.printed: The source asserts that an ε-trivialization required by the definition of L′G exists étale locally over R, deduces claim (a), and concludes Gr_G = Gr′_G.
issues.correction: Add that every fpqc L^+G-torsor P over an affine perfect Spec R is étale-locally trivial. Its push-out to L^hG, the perfection of the smooth group L_p^hG and hence pfp, is étale-locally trivial by Corollary A.27. The kernels of L^{h+1}G → L^hG are perfections of vector groups, whose torsors over affine perfect schemes are trivial. So a section of the push-out lifts step by step, and P = lim_h P ×^{L^+G} L^hG has a section. Hence the fpqc quotient [LG/L^+G] equals the étale quotient, which is Gr′_G by (a), (b) and étale descent along W_𝒪(R) → W_𝒪(R′). Alternatively, prove directly that Gr′_G is an fpqc sheaf: use descent on each W_{𝒪,n}(R), p-adic limits for the torsor, and bounded denominators for β. For GL_n this is Kreidl's theorem, cited in footnote 4.
issues.reason: Gr_G is defined (§1.1.2, §A.1.4) as the quotient in the fpqc topology: its R-points are pairs (P, φ) with P an fpqc L^+G-torsor. The proof only shows that ε exists étale-locally for (𝓔, β) ∈ Gr′_G. That identifies Gr′_G with the étale sheafification of the presheaf quotient LG/L^+G. Passing to Gr_G needs either that Gr′_G is an fpqc sheaf, i.e. fpqc descent of G-torsors on W_𝒪(R) with trivializations, which is not addressed, or that fpqc L^+G-torsors are étale-locally trivial. Corollary A.27 covers only pfp groups, and L^+G is not pfp. Both facts are true, so the lemma holds, but the argument as written is incomplete. Lemma 1.9 ('By the same proof of Lemma 1.3') and the moduli description of Gr̄_{N,h} inherit the omission.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quoted sentences are on p. 414, but in the opposite order: 'Then it follows that Gr_G = Gr′_G.' comes right after claims (a) and (b) and before 'Let 𝓔 be a G-torsor … In other words, étale locally … Claim (a) follows.' The substance is confirmed. Gr_G = [LG/L^+G] is the quotient in the fpqc topology on perfect k-algebras (§1.1.2, §§A.1.3–A.1.4), and its points are pairs (P, φ) with P an fpqc L^+G-torsor. The proof shows only that, for (𝓔, β) ∈ Gr′_G, a trivialization ε exists étale locally, and that LG ≅ L′G. From this, Gr_G = Gr′_G follows only if one of two facts holds. Either Gr′_G is an fpqc sheaf, in which case LG → Gr′_G is an L^+G-torsor in Sp^pf and Gr′_G is the quotient. Or every fpqc L^+G-torsor is étale-locally trivial. Neither is proved or cited. Corollary A.27 needs a pfp group, and L^+G is not pfp. Footnote 4 (p. 405) cites Kreidl for the fpqc-sheaf property, but only for GL_n, and the proof does not invoke it. arXiv v2 gave no proof at all and cited Kreidl. Both facts are true: the first reading's dévissage works, and fpqc descent can also be checked level by level on W_{𝒪,n}(R). So Lemma 1.3 holds and the gap is real but minor. The reach should be 'the proof', not 'nothing'. The first reading's own reason says the argument as written is incomplete, and that is what a gap in a proof affects. No stated result is affected. Lemma 1.9 ('By the same proof of Lemma 1.3') and the moduli description of Gr̄_{N,h} rest on the same step.

issues.locator: p. 417, end of the proof of Lemma 1.5
issues.printed: The source uses finite presentation of N to write it as (coker(A^m → A^n)) ⊗_A R for a subring A ⊂ R finitely generated over ℤ. It then claims reduction to the familiar noetherian case.
issues.correction: Choose A ⊂ R to contain elements c_j with Σ c_jδ_j = 1, where the δ_j are the minors generating Fitt_r(N). Or argue directly over R: constant fibre rank r and reducedness give Fitt_r(N) = R and Fitt_{r−1}(N) = 0, so the finitely presented module N is finite locally free of rank r by the Fitting-ideal criterion.
issues.reason: Constant fibre dimension on Spec R does not pass to Spec A for an arbitrary finitely generated A ⊂ R, since only points in the image of Spec R → Spec A are controlled. So the reduction, as written, does not transfer the hypothesis it needs. The fix is one line and the claim itself (a finitely presented module of constant fibre rank over a reduced ring is locally free) is true, so nothing downstream changes. This is a minor gap in a standard noetherian-approximation step, and the same text is in v2 and v3.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches p. 417. As written, the reduction carries over the conclusion but not the hypothesis. For an arbitrary finite-type subring A ⊂ R, N_A = coker(A^m → A^n) need not have constant fibre dimension on Spec A, since only points in the image of Spec R are controlled. An example within the paper's setting: R = k[x^{±1/p^∞}] (perfect and reduced), A = 𝔽_p[x] ⊂ R and N_A = A/xA. Then N = N_A ⊗_A R = 0 has constant rank 0, but N_A is not locally free. So the 'well known' noetherian statement cannot be applied until A is chosen suitably, and the text does not choose it. The fix is short. Over reduced R, constant rank r gives Fitt_r(N) = R and Fitt_{r−1}(N) ⊂ nilradical = 0. One can adjoin to A elements c_j with Σ c_jδ_j = 1; since A ⊂ R, the Fitting ideals of N_A then satisfy the same two conditions. Or one can apply the Fitting-ideal criterion for local freeness directly over R. Lemma 1.5 is therefore true, and nothing downstream changes. The reach should be 'the proof' rather than 'nothing': the printed argument is incomplete, but no stated result is affected. The same text is in v2 and v3.

issues.printed: The source asserts that the definition supplies a tautological chain 𝓔_N → 𝓔_{N−1} → ⋯ → 𝓔_0 over U, consisting of isogenies between finite projective W(R)-modules.
issues.correction: the tautological chain of quasi-isogenies 𝓔_N ⇢ 𝓔_{N−1} ⇢ ⋯ ⇢ 𝓔_0

issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches p. 423. By p. 416, β is an isogeny iff the last entry of Inv(β) is ≥ 0, and ω_j^* = ω_{n−j} − ω_n has entries −1. issues.locator: p. 423, last line of the proof of Proposition 1.13
issues.printed: The source invokes Corollary A.23 to assert perfect properness of Gr_{μ•}.
issues.correction: By Corollary A.23, Gr_{μ•,μ_{N+1}} is perfectly proper over Gr_{μ•}, hence over k. It is also a perfect scheme, being a perfected Grassmannian bundle over one. The induction hypothesis should likewise read 'represented by a perfect k-scheme, perfectly proper over k', as in the statement of Proposition 1.13; 'perfectly projective' is undefined and not needed.
issues.reason: Gr_{μ•} is perfectly projective by the induction hypothesis. The step to be proved concerns the longer sequence, which is the Grassmannian bundle Gr^{p^{−∞}}(i, 𝓔_N/p) or Gr^{p^{−∞}}(i, (𝓔_N/p)^*) over Gr_{μ•}. The induction hypothesis is stated as 'perfectly projective', so the conclusion should be carried in that form. The same text is in v2 (citing Corollary A.22) and v3.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches p. 423. The induction step is about the longer sequence: Gr_{μ•,μ_{N+1}} ≅ Gr^{p^{−∞}}(i, 𝓔_N/p) or Gr^{p^{−∞}}(i, (𝓔_N/p)^*) over Gr_{μ•}. Corollary A.23 (p. 474) says such a Grassmannian bundle over a pfp perfect X is perfectly proper over X, and is perfectly proper when X is. So the conclusion should concern Gr_{μ•,μ_{N+1}}; Gr_{μ•} is already perfectly proper by hypothesis. A related slip affects the proposed correction. The induction hypothesis says 'perfectly projective perfect k-scheme'. That term occurs nowhere else in the paper, it is stronger than the conclusion of Proposition 1.13, and Corollary A.23 returns only 'perfectly proper'. The first reading's correction closes the induction by asserting projectivity. That is true, but it does not follow from A.23. The simpler repair is to run the induction with 'perfectly proper', which is all that A.23 needs. v2 has the same text (citing Corollary A.22, hypothesis 'essentially projective'), and so does v3.

issues.locator: p. 425, proof of Lemma 1.18 (positive dimension of fibres); also p. 425, proof of Lemma 1.18 (last paragraph)
issues.printed: For λ < Nω_1, the source claims there is an i with dim_k(Λ_λ ∩ p^iΛ_0/Λ_λ ∩ p^{i+1}Λ_0) > 1. It deduces that π^{−1}(p^λ) contains at least a ℙ^{1,p^{−∞}} parametrizing line choices in (Λ_λ ∩ p^iΛ_0/Λ_λ ∩ p^{i+1}Λ_0). The repeated version writes the fiber as π^{-1}(p^λ) and the projective space as P^{1,p^{-∞}}.
issues.correction: Replace ∩ by +: for λ < Nω_1, dim_k((Λ_λ + p^iΛ_0)/(Λ_λ + p^{i+1}Λ_0)) > 1 for some i (e.g. i = 0). Every hyperplane 𝓔_1 ⊂ Λ_0 containing Λ_λ + pΛ_0 extends to a point of π^{−1}(p^λ), so the fibre surjects onto ℙ^{d−1,p^{−∞}} with d = #{j : l_j ≥ 1} ≥ 2. Also: Replace ∩ by + in both places: dim_k (Λ_λ + p^iΛ_0)/(Λ_λ + p^{i+1}Λ_0) > 1 (this holds at i = 0 when λ < Nω_1), and lines L in this space give the lattices Λ_λ + p^{i+1}Λ_0 + L̃, which extend to full chains. Equivalently, dim (p^{-1}Λ_λ ∩ Λ_0)/Λ_λ = #{j : m_j ≥ 1} ≥ 2, the fibre of π_2 from the preceding paragraph.
issues.reason: For λ = (l_1 ≥ … ≥ l_n ≥ 0) with Σ l_j = N, Λ_λ ⊂ Λ_0 and Λ_λ ∩ p^iΛ_0 = ⟨p^{max(l_j,i)}e_j⟩, so the printed dimension is #{j : l_j ≤ i}. For n ≥ 2 this exceeds 1 for every λ once i ≥ l_1, including λ = Nω_1, whose fibre is a single point by the first part of the lemma. Moreover these subquotients lie inside Λ_λ, while points of π^{−1}(p^λ) are chains of lattices between Λ_λ and Λ_0, so lines in them do not give points of the fibre. With + the dimension is #{j : l_j ≥ i+1}, which for i = 0 is at least 2 exactly when l_2 ≥ 1, i.e. λ ≠ Nω_1. The intended argument is then correct. The same text is in v2 (with 𝓔_λ) and v3. It is classified as a misprint (∩ for +); a verifier could argue for 'error', since the step fails as printed.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches p. 425 (zoomed image). Write λ = (l_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ l_n) with λ ≤ Nω_1 and Σ l_j = N. Then l_n ≥ 0, so Λ_λ ⊂ Λ_0. With ∩: Λ_λ ∩ p^iΛ_0 = ⊕ p^{max(l_j,i)}W(k)e_j, so the printed subquotient has dimension #{j : l_j ≤ i}. For i ≥ l_1 this is n ≥ 2 for every λ, including Nω_1, whose fibre is a point by the first part of the lemma, so the printed criterion does not single out λ < Nω_1. These subquotients also lie inside Λ_λ. Points of π^{−1}(p^λ) are chains Λ_λ = 𝓔_N ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ 𝓔_0 = Λ_0 with colength-one steps, so a line in such a subquotient is not a choice of chain. With +: Λ_λ + p^iΛ_0 = ⊕ p^{min(l_j,i)}W(k)e_j, and the dimension is #{j : l_j ≥ i+1}. At i = 0 this is d = #{j : l_j ≥ 1}, which is ≥ 2 iff l_2 ≥ 1 iff λ ≠ Nω_1. The first step 𝓔_1 of a chain can be any hyperplane of Λ_0 containing Λ_λ + pΛ_0. Each such 𝓔_1 extends to a full chain, since 𝓔_1/Λ_λ has a composition series of length N−1. So the fibre surjects onto ℙ^{d−1,p^{−∞}}, which has positive dimension. The chain 𝓔_i = 𝓔 + p^i𝓔_0 built with + is the one used a page earlier in the same proof, so the intended meaning can be recovered. 'Misprint' with reach 'nothing' is therefore right, though the step fails as printed. The same text is in v2 (with 𝓔_λ, 𝓔_0) and v3. The same place also has: The quotation matches p. 425. The fibre lives over Λ = Λ_λ = W(k){p^{m_j}e_j} ⊂ Λ_0 (1.2.3), with m_j ≥ 0 and Σm_j = N, and consists of chains Λ = 𝓔_N ⊂ … ⊂ 𝓔_0 = Λ_0 with one-dimensional steps. Then Λ_λ ∩ p^iΛ_0 = ⊕ p^{max(m_j,i)}We_j, so the printed quotient has dimension #{j : m_j ≤ i}. For every n ≥ 2 this equals n > 1 once i ≥ m_1, for every λ, including λ = Nω_1, whose fibre is a single point (the first part of the lemma). The printed condition therefore does not detect λ < Nω_1. The printed quotient is also a subquotient of Λ_λ, so its lines give sublattices of Λ_λ, not lattices between Λ_λ and Λ_0. With + in place of ∩ the quotient (Λ_λ + p^iΛ_0)/(Λ_λ + p^{i+1}Λ_0) has dimension #{j : m_j > i}. This is ≥ 2 at i = 0 exactly when m_2 ≥ 1, i.e. λ ≠ Nω_1. A line L gives Λ_λ + p^{i+1}Λ_0 + L̃, which extends to a full chain, and a P^1 of lines gives a P^{1,p^{-∞}} in the fibre. The intended argument is clear. The same text is in v2 and v3.

issues.locator: p. 433, Proposition 2.5 (second sentence)
issues.printed: The source gives the closure identity \overline{S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ}} = ∪_{λ′≤λ} S_{λ′} ∩ Gr_{≤μ}.
issues.correction: Replace the second sentence by S̄_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} = ∪_{λ′≤λ}(S_{λ′} ∩ Gr_{≤μ}), which follows from the first. Or restrict to λ a weight of V_μ (equivalently S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} ≠ ∅) and supply a proof of closure(S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ}) = S̄_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ}.
issues.reason: If S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} = ∅ but some λ′ ≤ λ has S_{λ′} ∩ Gr_{≤μ} ≠ ∅, the left side is empty and the right side is not. Example: G = GL_2, μ = (1,0), Gr_{≤μ} = P^1, λ = (2,−1) = (1,0) + α^∨. S_{(2,−1)} ∩ Gr_{≤μ} = ∅, since its lattices contain p^{-1}(xe_1 + e_2) ∉ Λ_0. The right side is S_{(1,0)} ∩ P^1 ∪ S_{(0,1)} ∩ P^1 = P^1. The proof only cites [Zhu16, Prop. 5.3.6], which I checked: it proves S̄_λ = ∪_{λ′≤λ} S_{λ′} and says nothing about closures of the intersections with Gr_{≤μ}. For weights λ the refinement is plausible (I checked GL_2, μ = (2,0) and GL_3, μ = (1,0,−1) by hand) but it is not proved. Later arguments (Corollary 2.10, (2.2.11)) only use S̄_λ. The same wording is in arXiv v2 (Lemma 2.5) and v3.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: Zoomed image of p. 433: the overline covers S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ}, so the sentence asserts closure(S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ}) = ∪_{λ′≤λ} S_{λ′} ∩ Gr_{≤μ} for all λ and μ. This is false whenever S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} = ∅ but some λ′ ≤ λ has S_{λ′} ∩ Gr_{≤μ} ≠ ∅. Simplest case: μ = 0, λ = α^∨ (α simple). Gr_{≤0} = {ϖ^0} ⊂ S_0, so the left side is closure(∅) = ∅, while the right side contains S_0 ∩ Gr_{≤0} = {ϖ^0}. The first reading's GL_2 example (μ = (1,0), λ = (2,−1)) is also valid. In general S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} ≠ ∅ forces ϖ^λ ∈ Gr_{≤μ}, by the G_m-contraction, so λ must be a weight of V_μ. Case for the defence: one could read the sentence as meant only for λ a weight of V_μ. Even so, it is not proved. The proof only cites [Zhu16, Prop. 5.3.6], and I checked arXiv:1603.05593: that proposition states only that S_{≤λ} = ∪_{λ′≤λ} S_{λ′} is closed with S_λ open dense in it. It says nothing about intersections with Gr_{≤μ}. The inclusion ⊃ for weights (every S_{λ′} ∩ Gr_{≤μ} lies in the closure of S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ}) is a genuine statement about MV cycles, which the equidimensionality of Cor. 2.8 does not give. It is plausible (it holds in the GL_2 and SL_3-adjoint cases I checked), but it is not established. So the stated equality is false as printed and unproved in its natural range. The trivially true reading S̄_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} = ∪_{λ′≤λ} S_{λ′} ∩ Gr_{≤μ} is not what is printed. No later argument uses the refinement: Cor. 2.10 uses only the stratifications. The wording is the same in v2 (Lemma 2.5) and v3.
