issues.reviewReason: The quotations match p. 434 (Cor. 2.8) and p. 439 (Cor. 2.14). S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} ≠ ∅ implies ϖ^λ ∈ Gr_{≤μ}, i.e. λ is a weight of V_μ. Otherwise the scheme is empty. For Cor. 2.14, by (2.2.3) S_{λ•} ∩ Gr_{≤μ•} is a twisted product, empty unless each λ_i is a weight of V_{μ_i}. In those cases the printed dimension (ρ,λ+μ) (resp. the displayed equation dim(…) = (ρ,|λ•|+|μ•|)) is false. Case for the defence: for Cor. 2.8, 'equidimensional' is vacuous for ∅ and the component count (0 = dim V_μ(λ)) is right, so only the dimension clause fails. The displayed equation in Cor. 2.14 fails outright. The intended nonempty case is clear and is what the proofs treat. Nothing later uses the empty case. This is consistent with the ledger's E19 (verified as misprint/nothing). Zhu's own notes [Zhu16, Th. 5.3.9(1)] include the hypothesis 'if t^λ ∈ Gr_{≤μ}'.

issues.locator: pp. 434–435, proof of Corollary 2.8
issues.printed: The source says G is already defined over the integer ring of a p-adic field and concludes that Gr has a model over a finite field.
issues.correction: Either restrict the point-count argument to (k,F) for which O = W(k) ⊗_{W(F_q)} O_E for a finite totally ramified E/W(F_q)[1/p] (e.g. k = F̄_p by Krasner's lemma, or F tame), or add a spreading-out step: define S_λ ∩ Gr_{≤μ} over a perfected finitely generated F_p-algebra A carrying an Eisenstein polynomial approximating that of O, and specialize to closed points, where (2.2.5) applies, before concluding the dimension and component count over k.
issues.reason: In §2, k is any algebraically closed field and F is any totally ramified finite extension of F_0 = W(k)[1/p] (§0.5). A split G is defined over Z_p, but Gr_G is built from W_O(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(k)} O, and O need not descend to a finite field. Example: k an algebraic closure of F_p(t), F_1 = F_0(ζ_p), π = ζ_p − 1, u = 1 + [t]π, and F = F_1(u^{1/p}), totally ramified over F_0 of degree p(p−1). Suppose F = F_0 ⊗_{E_0} E with E_0 = W(F_q)[1/p]. After an unramified enlargement, F = F_1(v^{1/p}) with v ∈ E_0(ζ_p). Kummer theory then equates the classes of u and v^a in U^{(1)}/U^{(2)}·(F_1^×)^p ≅ k; the level 1 lies below p·e(F_1/F_0)/(p−1) = p and is prime to p. This forces t ∈ F̄_p, a contradiction. For such (k, F), the reduction to (2.2.5) is not justified as written. The corollary is surely still true by spreading out, but that argument is not given. The sentence first appears in arXiv v3; v2 simply asserted the point count.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches pp. 434–435. In §2, k is any algebraically closed field (p. 429) and F any totally ramified finite extension of F_0 = W(k)[1/p] (§0.5). G is split, so it descends to Z_p. But Gr is built from W_O(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(k)} O, and descending Gr to a finite field requires O = W(k) ⊗_{W(F_q)} O_E, i.e. F = F_0 ⊗_{E_0} E. I rechecked the first reading's counterexample independently. Let K = W(F̄_p)[1/p], which is algebraically closed in F_0 (an algebraic element generates an unramified extension with residue field algebraic over F_p). So any descended F has the form F_0 ⊗_K L, and by Galois correspondence L ⊃ K(ζ_p) and L = K(ζ_p)(v^{1/p}). Now take F = F_1(u^{1/p}), with F_1 = F_0(ζ_p), π = ζ_p − 1, u = 1 + [t]π and t ∈ k transcendental. Kummer theory would give u ≡ v^a mod (F_1^×)^p. Since v(u) = 0 and Teichmüller units are p-th powers, we may take v ∈ U^{(1)}(K(ζ_p)). But (U^{(1)})^p ⊂ U^{(p)} ⊂ U^{(2)}, so comparing in U^{(1)}/U^{(2)} ≅ k gives t = a·c with c ∈ F̄_p, a contradiction. The same computation shows [F:F_0] = p(p−1). So the sentence 'Gr is in fact defined over some finite field' is unjustified for such (k,F), and the point count (2.2.5) is not available. Base change to a larger algebraically closed field does not help, because the minimal field of definition here is transcendental over F_p. For k = F̄_p (Krasner), F tame (F = F_0(p^{1/e})) or F = F_0 the step is fine. The corollary is surely true, e.g. by spreading out, but that argument is not given. The sentence first appears in v3; v2 simply asserted the point count.

issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches p. 435: 'form a basis of H^i_c(S_λ, IC_μ)', with i unbound. In arXiv v2 the corollary was stated by cases (H^i_c = Q̄_ℓ[B_μ(λ)] for i = 2(ρ,λ), 0 otherwise), which bound i. issues.locator: p. 436, proof of Corollary 2.10
issues.printed: The source sets Fil′_{<λ} H^*(A) = Im(H^*_{S^−_{<λ}}(A) → H^*(A)), with S^−_{<λ} = S̄^−_λ − S^−_λ. Citing (2.2.10), it claims the two filtrations complement one another and jointly yield H^* = ⊕_λ H^*_c(S_λ, −).
issues.correction: Use Im(H^*_{S̄^-_λ}(A) → H^*(A)), as in [MV07, Th. 3.6]. Fix k = (2ρ,λ). Parity and degree give H^k_{S̄^-_λ}(A) = H^k_{S^-_λ}(A) and H^k(S̄_λ,A) = H^k_c(S_λ,A). The composite H^k_{S̄^-_λ}(A) → H^k(A) → H^k(S̄_{λ′},A) is the isomorphism of (2.2.10) (hyperbolic localization at ϖ^λ) for λ′ = λ. It is zero for λ′ ≠ λ of the same degree, since a nonempty closed G_m-stable S̄^-_λ ∩ S̄_{λ′} contains some ϖ^η with λ ≤ η ≤ λ′. Hence H^k(A) = ⊕_{(2ρ,λ)=k} Im(H^k_{S̄^-_λ}(A) → H^k(A)), which gives H^* ≅ ⊕_λ H^*_c(S_λ,−).
issues.reason: By Proposition 2.5, S̄^−_λ − S^−_λ = ∪_{λ′>λ} S^−_{λ′}. By (2.2.10) and Proposition 2.7, H^k_{S^−_{λ′}}(A) = 0 unless k = (2ρ,λ′) > (2ρ,λ). So the printed Fil′_{<λ} vanishes in degree (2ρ,λ) and cannot split off the λ-piece. Morally it is ⊕_{λ′>λ}, which lies inside Fil_{≥λ} instead of complementing it. Counterexample to the claimed complementarity: GL_2, A = IC_{(1,0)} = Q̄_ℓ[1] on P^1, λ = (0,1). Here Fil_{≥λ} = H^*(A), because S_{<λ} ∩ P^1 = ∅. But Fil′_{<λ} is the image of H^*_{pt}(A) with pt = ϖ^{(1,0)}, which is H^1 ≠ 0. The corollary is right by the MV argument the proof cites. Same text in arXiv v3.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches p. 436. By Prop. 2.5, S^-_{<λ} := S̄^-_λ − S^-_λ = ∪_{λ′>λ} S^-_{λ′}. By (2.2.10) and Prop. 2.7, H^*_{S^-_{λ′}}(A) is concentrated in degree (2ρ,λ′), and (2ρ,λ′−λ) ∈ 2Z_{>0} for λ′ > λ. So the printed Fil′_{<λ} vanishes in degree (2ρ,λ), the only degree of the λ-piece. It consists of pieces λ′ > λ, which already lie in Fil_{≥λ}, so it cannot complement it. I verified the first reading's counterexample: GL_2, A = IC_{(1,0)} = Q̄_ℓ[1] on P^1, λ = (0,1). Here S_{<λ} ∩ P^1 = ∅, so Fil_{≥λ} = H^*(A). S^-_{<λ} ∩ P^1 = S^-_{(1,0)} ∩ P^1 = {ϖ^{(1,0)}}, and H^1_{pt}(A) → H^1(A) = H^2(P^1) is the (nonzero) point class. So Fil_{≥λ} ∩ Fil′_{<λ} ≠ 0 and the sum is not direct. The printed filtration is thus not complementary to Fil, and 'these two filtrations are complimentary by (2.2.10)' is a false step. Corollary 2.10 itself is correct by the argument of [MV07, Th. 3.6], which the proof cites, run with the images of H^*_{S̄^-_λ} instead of H^*_{S̄^-_λ − S^-_λ}. The same text is in v3.

issues.locator: p. 437, item (2) before Lemma 2.12
issues.printed: In part (2), the source declares Q_{1/2} to be a maximal parahoric.
issues.correction: Delete item (2), or state: Q_{1/2} is the parahoric of −θ/2, whose reductive quotient contains the SL_2 of the affine roots ±(θ^∨+1). It is maximal unless the simple factor containing θ is of type A_n with n ≥ 2.
issues.reason: Q_{1/2} is the parahoric of −θ/2 (v2: 'the point −μ/2 is a vertex'). The affine roots vanishing there are ±(θ^∨ + 1) and the roots orthogonal to θ. These have full rank only if the roots orthogonal to the highest root have rank r − 1, which fails in type A_n, n ≥ 2, where they have rank n − 2. For SL_3, θ = (1,0,−1) pairs to 1 or 2 with every positive root. So −θ/2 lies on the single wall θ^∨ + 1 = 0, inside an edge, and Q_{1/2} is properly contained in the parahorics of the edge's two vertices. Type A is covered by the paper: θ ∈ M (p. 439) and Lemma 2.11 includes it. The claim is not used in any proof.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches p. 437. Q_{1/2} is generated by T(O) and U_α(ϖ^{⌈⟨θ,α⟩/2⌉}O), i.e. it is the parahoric of the point x = −θ/2. The affine roots vanishing at x are ±(θ^∨+1) and the roots α with ⟨θ,α⟩ = 0. So x is a vertex (Q_{1/2} maximal) iff the roots orthogonal to the highest root θ^∨ have rank r − 1. That holds exactly when α_0 meets a single node of the extended Dynkin diagram, which fails in type A_n, n ≥ 2 (the roots orthogonal to e_1 − e_{n+1} form A_{n−2}). Concretely, for SL_3 and θ = (1,0,−1), every positive root pairs to 1 or 2 with θ. So x = (−1/2,0,1/2) lies only on the walls ±(e_1−e_3+1) and is interior to an edge. Q_{1/2} is then strictly contained in the parahoric of the vertex (−1/3,−1/3,2/3) of that edge. Type A is within the lemma's scope (M on p. 439 contains θ for SL_n and GL_n). arXiv v2 justified the claim by 'the point −μ/2 is a vertex', which is the false step. The claim is not used: Lemma 2.12(i) needs only the A_1 factor ±(θ^∨+1) of the reductive quotient. The use of R_{L̄Q_{1/2}} in Lemma 2.19 (p. 442) needs only W_{Q_{1/4}} ⊂ W_{Q_{1/2}} ⊂ W.

issues.locator: p. 439, proof of Lemma 2.11 (μ = θ): display for π^{-1}(S_0 ∩ Gr_{≤μ}) and (2.2.13)
issues.correction: With Y = ∪_{wμ<0} ŪwP̄_μ/P̄_μ, π^{-1}(S_0 ∩ Gr_{≤μ}) = [φ^{-1}(Y) \ π^{-1}(∪_{wμ<0} S_{wμ} ∩ Gr_{≤μ})] ⊔ [π^{-1}(Gr_0) ∩ φ^{-1}(Ḡ/P̄_μ − Y)], where π^{-1}(Gr_0) ≅ Ḡ/P̄_μ is the section at infinity. So (2.2.13) should read RΓ_c(π^{-1}(S_0 ∩ Gr_{≤μ}), Q̄_ℓ[d]) = RΓ_c(Y, Q̄_ℓ[d−2]) ⊕ RΓ_c(Ḡ/P̄_μ − Y, Q̄_ℓ[d]); the sequence splits since all terms are in even degrees. Comparison with (2.2.12) then gives H^i(𝒞) = H^i_c(π^{-1}(S_0 ∩ Gr_{≤μ}), Q̄_ℓ[d]) for i ≠ 0 and H^0_c(S_0, IC_μ) ≅ Q̄_ℓ^{|Δ_θ|}.
issues.reason: Cells of Ḡ/P̄_θ: for β = wθ > 0 the dimension is ht θ + ht β − 1; for β < 0 it is ht θ − ht(−β); and d = 2 ht θ. With the printed (2.2.13), H^i_c vanishes for i > 0, yet H^i(C) = H^{i+d}(Ḡ/P̄_μ) ≠ 0 whenever some positive β ∈ Wθ has height 1 + i/2. In degree 0 both sides have dimension |Δ_θ|, which would give H^0_c(S_0, IC_μ) = 0. Check for SL_3: Ḡ/P̄_θ is the flag variety and C = Q̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ Q̄_ℓ^2 ⊕ Q̄_ℓ[−2]. The printed (2.2.13) gives Q̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ Q̄_ℓ^2, so H^0_c(S_0, IC_θ) = 0 and the degree-2 term would be negative. The corrected formula gives H^0_c = Q̄_ℓ^2 = V_θ(0). The final conclusion (and the [NP01, §8] computation it defers to) is right. The same display is in arXiv v2 and v3.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The display and (2.2.13) on p. 439 match the quotation. By Lemma 2.12(ii), π^{-1}(Gr_0) is the whole section at infinity Σ_∞ = Q_0 ×^{Q_{1/4}} Q_{1/4}sQ_{3/4}/Q_{3/4} ≅ Ḡ/P̄_θ, and Gr_0 ⊂ S_0. The printed right side lies in φ^{-1}(Y), Y = ∪_{wθ<0} ŪwP̄/P̄, so it misses Σ_∞ over Ḡ/P̄ − Y (the cells with wθ > 0). The printed formula then contradicts (2.2.12). Write β = wθ. The cell dimension is #{α>0 : ⟨α,β⟩ > 0}, which equals ht θ + ht β − 1 for β > 0 and ht θ − ht(−β) for β < 0, and d = 2ht θ = dim Ḡ/P̄_θ + 1. With the printed (2.2.13), H^i_c(π^{-1}(S_0 ∩ Gr_{≤θ}), Q̄_ℓ[d]) = 0 for i > 0. But H^i(𝒞) = H^{i+d}(Ḡ/P̄_θ) ≠ 0 for i = 2ht β − 2 > 0 whenever some positive β ∈ Wθ has height ≥ 2 (e.g. β = θ, if ht θ ≥ 2). In degree 0 both sides have dimension |Δ_θ|, which forces H^0_c(S_0, IC_θ) = 0. SL_3 check: Ḡ/P̄_θ is the flag variety and 𝒞 = Q̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ Q̄_ℓ^2 ⊕ Q̄_ℓ[−2]. The printed (2.2.13) gives Q̄_ℓ[2] ⊕ Q̄_ℓ^2, which is impossible. With the missing piece added, the Ḡ/P̄ − Y term reproduces H^i(𝒞) for i ≥ 0 and the Y term reproduces it for i < 0. What remains is the |Δ_θ| top cells of Y in degree 0. This gives H^i_c(S_0, IC_θ) = 0 for i ≠ 0 and H^0_c = Q̄_ℓ^{|Δ_θ|} (2 = dim V_θ(0) for SL_3). So the lemma and the [NP01, §8] conclusion are right, but the displayed decomposition and (2.2.13) on which the comparison rests are wrong. The same display is in v2 and v3.

issues.locator: p. 449, Lemma 2.28 and the Θ-diagram; c_vect defined in Proposition 2.21, p. 443
issues.printed: Lemma 2.28 gives the bottom row H^*(A_1) ⊗ H^*(A_2) —c_vect→ H^*(A_2) ⊗ H^*(A_1) —δ⊗δ→ H^*(θ^*A_2) ⊗ H^*(θ^*A_1). Proposition 2.21 describes the bottom-row c_vect as the ordinary vector-space flip.
issues.correction: In Lemma 2.28 and in the Θ-diagram (p. 449), c_vect must denote the Koszul-signed commutativity of graded vector spaces, a⊗b → (-1)^{|a||b|} b⊗a. Only in Proposition 2.21 and Corollary 2.22 is c_vect the plain flip.
issues.reason: The right column of Lemma 2.28 uses θ^*(A_1⋆A_2) ≃ θ^*A_2⋆θ^*A_1, which comes from (θ×~θ)^*(A_1⊠~A_2) ≃ θ^*A_2⊠~θ^*A_1, i.e. from interchanging the factors of an external product. Under Künneth this interchange induces the Koszul-signed flip. There is also an internal check. By the Θ-diagram and Lemma 2.29, H^*(c') = c_vect, since the powers √−1^i·√−1^j/√−1^{i+j} cancel. If c_vect were the plain flip, then the Koszul change (2.4.4) (intended (−1)^{ε1ε2}, E15) would give H^*(c) = (−1)^{ε(A1)ε(A2)}·flip, contradicting Proposition 2.21 for two odd objects (e.g. G = PGL_2, A_1 = A_2 = IC_ω, whose cohomology sits in degrees ±1). With the Koszul flip, H^*(c) = (−1)^{ε1ε2}(−1)^{ij}·flip = flip, because H^j(A) = 0 unless j ≡ ε(A) mod 2 (Lemma 1.25 and the parity of IC stalks). In the paper's defence, the text calls (2.4.4) a 'Koszul sign change' and cites [BD] and [MV07], so the intended reading can be recovered. LY13 (published §3.3) use the non-Koszul flip only because all their objects are even (G simply connected). Read literally, Lemma 2.28 is false by the sign (−1)^{ij}. The same text is in v2 and v3.

issues.reviewReason: The quotations match the images of pp. 443 and 449. In Lemma 2.28 and the Θ-diagram, c_vect is not redefined, so it is literally the 'usual flip' of Proposition 2.21. I re-derived the sign. (1) Geometry: the right column of Lemma 2.28 comes from (θ x~ θ)^*(A1 ⊠~ A2) = θ^*A2 ⊠~ θ^*A1, where θ x~ θ sends (g1,g2) to (θ(g2), θ(g1)). This interchanges the factors, and under Künneth such an interchange acts by a x b → (-1)^{|a||b|} b x a. (2) Internal consistency: the Θ-diagram follows from Lemmas 2.27–2.28, and Lemma 2.29 gives Θ = √−1^j on H^j. On H^i(A1) ⊗ H^j(A2) the factors √−1^{i+j} cancel, so H^*(c') equals the c_vect of Lemma 2.28. If that c_vect were the plain flip, then c = c' would already satisfy Proposition 2.21, and the announced Koszul change (2.4.4) (E15) would destroy it for two odd objects. Example: G = PGL_2, A1 = A2 = IC_ω with Gr_ω = P^1, whose cohomology lies in degrees ±1; H^*(c) would be -flip. With the Koszul flip, H^j(A) = 0 unless j ≡ ε(A) mod 2 (Lemma 1.25 and parity vanishing), so H^*(c) = (-1)^{ε1 ε2}(-1)^{ij} flip = flip, as Proposition 2.21 requires. This is also the MV07 mechanism (§6, after Remark 6.2). LY13 (published §3.3) state that they use the unadjusted flip on Vec^gr, which is harmless there because G is simply connected and every object is even. So read literally, Lemma 2.28 is false by (-1)^{ij}, and the only consistent reading is the Koszul flip. The phrase 'Koszul sign change' signals this, so the meaning is recoverable (misprint, nothing). v2 and v3 have the same text.

issues.locator: p. 451, proof of Lemma 2.32, first paragraph
issues.printed: The source asserts that pullback gives a canonical ring isomorphism H^*(Ḡ/P̄_μ) ≃ H^*(Gr_μ) and concludes that H^2 generates H^*(Gr_μ). Since it calls Θ̊_μ a ring homomorphism, it claims that checking Θ̊_μ = −1 on H^2 suffices.
issues.correction: Delete 'Therefore, H^*(Gr_μ) is generated by H^2 ... it is enough to prove that Θ̊_μ = -1 on H^2' (false, e.g. Gr(2,4) for GL_4, μ = (1,1,0,0)). Conclude instead from the equivariant diagram: the equivariant Θ̊_μ is the restriction to R_{L_μ} ⊂ R_{T̄,ℓ} of the ring automorphism induced by χ → -χ on the degree-2 generators, hence acts by (-1)^j in degree 2j. Specializing along R_{Ḡ,ℓ} → Q̄_ℓ gives the lemma in all degrees.
issues.reason: The cohomology ring of a partial flag variety need not be generated in degree 2. Counterexample: G = GL_4 and μ = (1,1,0,0) (minuscule), for which Gr_μ = (Ḡ/P̄_μ)^{p^{−∞}} = Gr(2,4)^{p^{−∞}}. There H^2 is spanned by σ_1, H^4 is 2-dimensional (σ_2, σ_{1,1}) and σ_1² = σ_2 + σ_{1,1}, so H^4 is not spanned by products of degree-2 classes. The reduction as written therefore fails for such μ. LY13 (published Lemma 4.3) use only degrees ≤ 2, via IH^i ≅ H^i(Ω_λ) for i ≤ 2, so the claim is Zhu's own. Lemma 2.32 itself remains true, since the proof's own equivariant computation covers all degrees. The same claim is in v2 and v3.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The claim is real. The quotation matches the image of p. 451, and v2 and v3 have the same sentence. The rational cohomology of a partial flag variety need not be generated in degree 2. Take G = GL_4 and μ = (1,1,0,0), which is minuscule. P_μ, generated by the U_α with <α,μ> <= 0, has Levi GL_2 x GL_2, so Gr_μ = Gr(2,4)^{p^{−∞}} (Corollary 1.24; dim = (2ρ,μ) = 4). The Betti numbers are 1,1,2,1,1. Since H^2 is one-dimensional, Sym^2 H^2 cannot span the two-dimensional H^4. So the stated reduction 'it is enough to prove Θ̊_μ = -1 on H^2' is invalid for such μ. The case is used: Lemma 2.32 is needed in all degrees for Gr_λ in the proof of Lemma 2.30 and in Remark 2.33 (minuscule μ). LY13 (published Lemma 4.3) use only degrees <= 2, so this claim is Zhu's own. The lemma remains true, and the repair is in the same proof. θ^* and γ are ring maps, R_{L_μ} = R_T^{W_L} is contained in R_T, and the diagram shows the equivariant map is induced by χ → -χ on the polynomial ring R_T, which is generated in degree 2. So it is (-1)^j in degree 2j, and it descends to H^*(Gr_μ) = Q̄_ℓ ⊗_{R_G} R_{L_μ}. Reclassify the reach: the proof as written makes a false assertion and an invalid reduction, so it affects the proof. No stated result is affected, and 'nothing' understates a genuinely false step.

issues.locator: p. 452, proof of Lemma 2.30 from Lemma 2.34
issues.printed: The source gives the identity i^!_λ C_μ = (i^*_λ C_μ[2(2ρ, λ − μ)])^*.
issues.correction: i^!_λ C_μ ≅ (i^*_λ C_μ)^*[2(2ρ, λ - μ)] = (i^*_λ C_μ[2(2ρ, μ - λ)])^*, up to a Tate twist, with C_μ = IC_μ[-(2ρ,μ)] (E16).

The shift belongs outside the dual; inside it, its sign flips. Check with G = SL_2, μ = α^∨, λ = 0. Gr_≤μ is the rationally smooth quadric cone, so C_μ = Q̄_ℓ and i^!_0C_μ = Q̄_ℓ[−4], whereas the printed formula gives (Q̄_ℓ[−4])^* = Q̄_ℓ[4]. The printed formula is not consistent with the printed normalization of C_μ either. Only the parity of degrees is used afterwards, and (2ρ, μ−λ) is even, so the argument is unaffected. The same text is in v3.

issues.reviewReason: The quotation matches the image of p. 452, and v2 and v3 have the same text. Gr_λ is smooth of dimension d_λ = (2ρ,λ), and IC_μ is Verdier self-dual up to a Tate twist. So i_λ^! IC_μ = (i_λ^* IC_μ)^*[2d_λ] on stalks. For C_μ = IC_μ[s] this gives i^!C_μ = (i^*C_μ)^*[2d_λ + 2s]. With the intended s = -(2ρ,μ) (E16) this is (i^*C_μ)^*[2(2ρ,λ-μ)] = (i^*C_μ[2(2ρ,μ-λ)])^*. The printed formula has the shift inside the dual with the wrong sign. It is also wrong with the printed normalization s = +(2ρ,μ), which needs [2(2ρ,λ+μ)] against the printed [2(2ρ,μ-λ)]. Checks: SL_2, μ = α^∨, λ = 0, intended normalization: C_μ = Q̄_ℓ (rationally smooth cone), i^!_0 C_μ = Q̄_ℓ[-4], but the printed formula gives Q̄_ℓ[4]. λ = μ, printed normalization: i^!_μ C_μ = Q̄_ℓ[2(2ρ,μ)], but the printed formula gives Q̄_ℓ[-2(2ρ,μ)]. The argument uses only parity. The inverse dual of H^*Ψ on H^{2b}(i^!C) acts by (-1)^{b + (2ρ,μ-λ)} = (-1)^b, since μ - λ lies in the coroot lattice. So the conclusion gr Θ = (-1)^j on degree 2j stands.

issues.locator: pp. 453–454, §2.4.5 (Lemma 2.34 from Theorem 2.35)
issues.printed: The source asserts applicability of ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig theory [KL79], [KL80]. It cites [LV12, §3] for analogous interpretations of P^{σ,⋄}_{y,w}, claiming these imply P^{σ,⋄}_{dλ,dμ}(q) = Σ tr(H^{2j}_λΨ_μ | H^{2j}_λC_μ)q^j.
issues.correction: Prove, on the perfect Witt-vector affine flag variety and for ⋄ = Ad(ω)∘*, the Lusztig–Vogan trace realization of P^{σ,⋄}_{y,w} (the analogue of [LV12, §3] and [LY13, published (3.2), (3.5), §7.4 with (7.1)]), including the Kazhdan–Lusztig purity and parity input. Then show that the resulting stalk involution on H^{2j}_λ C_μ equals Zhu's Ψ_μ = (Cor. 2.26)∘N_μ, via an Iwahori-level analogue of Lemma 2.24 and Corollary 2.26 compatible with pullback along Fl → Gr.
issues.reason: [LV12, §3] proves the trace interpretation of P^σ_{y,w} only for finite Weyl groups (flag varieties over F̄_p). §7.1–7.2 of LV12 assert, without proof, that it extends to affine Weyl groups over k((ε)) and to twisted ⋄. LY13 (published §3.1) call their affine version 'an elaboration of this remark'. Zhu needs it for the mixed-characteristic affine flag variety and the ⋄-twisted parahoric setting, with his own Ψ_μ built from Gr^op and Corollary 2.26, and he asserts it in one sentence. This formula is the only link between Theorem 2.35 and Lemma 2.34, and through Lemmas 2.30 and 2.29 it carries Proposition 2.21 and Theorem 0.3. In the paper's defence, the LV argument is formal: it uses the sheaf-function dictionary, purity and parity vanishing, and rank-one P^1-computations. All of these hold for perfections of Schubert varieties, and étale cohomology does not see perfection. So the gap is very likely fillable, but it is not filled in the paper. Zhu presents §2.4.4–2.4.5 as a sketch ('We sketch it here and refer to loc. cit. for details').
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotations match the images of pp. 453–454. The trace formula is the only link from Theorem 2.35 (a statement about Hecke algebras) to Lemma 2.34, and through Lemmas 2.30 and 2.29 (p. 450) to Proposition 2.21 and the symmetric monoidal structure in Theorem 0.3. I checked the sources. LV12 (arXiv 1109.4606) proves the trace interpretation (§3, via B×B over F_p-bar, a Frobenius twisted by the swap, and [KL] purity) only for finite Weyl groups. §7.1–7.2 say only that the ⋄-twisted and affine versions hold 'with essentially the same proof' over k((ε)). LY13 (published §3.1) call their affine version 'an elaboration of this remark' and state (3.2), (3.5) and the §7.4 formula (through (7.1)) without detailed proof. Zhu needs a new setting: the perfect Witt-vector affine flag variety, with ⋄ = Ad(ω)∘*. His involution Ψ_μ is defined through Gr^op, N_μ and Corollary 2.26, because θ maps Gr to Gr^op and there is no loop-group sheaf theory (Remark 2.25). Relating it to the τ^*-involution of a Lusztig–Vogan realization requires an Iwahori-level analogue of Lemma 2.24 and Corollary 2.26 and compatibility with pullback along Fl → Gr. The paper supplies none of this, only 'similar interpretations were given ... Such interpretations in particular imply'. The preceding 'The usual Kazhdan–Lusztig theory ... works in our situation' is likewise only asserted. Case for the defence: the LV argument is formal (sheaf–function dictionary, purity and parity, rank-one computations), étale cohomology does not see perfection, and the gap is very likely fillable. It is still a load-bearing step asserted without proof, so 'gap' with reach 'the proof' is right; no stated result is shown false. One small inaccuracy in the first reading's reason: the explicit 'We sketch it here and refer to loc. cit. for details' is on p. 452 and concerns Lemma 2.34 ⇒ Lemma 2.30. It does not label §2.4.5 as a sketch.

issues.printed: The source chooses τ_0 ∈ Σ and sets τ_i = σ^i(τ_0), i = 0, 1, 2, …, d − 1. Its diagram has upper row (σ^d)^*E_{τ_0} → (σ^{d−1})^*E_{τ_{d−1}} → ⋯ → E_{τ_0} and lower arrows σ^{d−1}(b_{τ_{d−1}}), σ^{d−2}(b_{τ_{d−2}}), …, b_{τ_0}. It defines Nm b = b_{τ_0}σ(b_{τ_1})⋯σ^{d−1}(b_{τ_{d−1}}).
issues.correction: p. 458: put τ_i := σ^{-i}(τ_0), i = 0, …, d−1. Equivalently, keep τ_i = σ^i(τ_0) and write τ_{d−i} for τ_i in the diagram, in Nm b = b_{τ0}σ(b_{τ_{d−1}})⋯σ^{d−1}(b_{τ1}), and in μ• = (μ_{τ0}, σ(μ_{τ_{d−1}}), …, σ^{d−1}(μ_{τ1})) of Lemma 3.5.
issues.reason: Under the paper's isomorphism a ⊗ b ↦ (τ(a)b)_τ, the automorphism 1 ⊗ σ satisfies (σx)_τ = σ(x_{σ^{-1}τ}). Equivalently, the Frobenius of W_{O_E}(R) sends the idempotent e_τ to e_{στ}, so σ^* moves objects on the τ-component to the στ-component. With τ_i = σ^iτ_0, (σ^j)^*E_{τ_j} lives on the τ_{2j}-component. So for d ≥ 3 the top row does not consist of H ⊗_{E,τ_0}-torsors. Likewise, the τ_0-component of σ(b) is σ(b_{σ^{-1}τ_0}), so the label σ(b_{τ_1}) needs τ_1 = σ^{-1}τ_0. With τ_i = σ^{-i}τ_0 the diagram typechecks, Nm b is the τ_0-component of bσ(b)⋯σ^{d−1}(b), and Lemma 3.5 holds as stated. The phrase 'σ^i induces an isomorphism H ⊗_{E,τ_i} L ≃ H ⊗_{E,τ_0} L' also fits this convention. Case for the defence: for d ≤ 2 the two conventions agree. The relabelling i ↦ −i changes neither Lemma 3.7 (which sums over all i) nor the dimension count. arXiv v2 had the untwisted Nm b = b_{τ_0}⋯b_{τ_{d−1}}; v3 and the published version inserted the σ^i but kept τ_i = σ^i(τ_0).

Then F(x_0, x_1) = (pσ(x_1), σ(x_0)), so Lie(X_0)^* = ker(F mod p) is the τ_1-line, while Fil^1 = Λ^1 is the τ_0-line. T(k) preserves both lines, and G(W)p^μG(W) = p^μ T(W), so (2) fails for every representative and the framing X_0 does not satisfy (∗). A point g ∈ T(L)/T(W), with v(g) = (a, c), gives D = gΛ_W with Frobenius of type μ + σv(g) − v(g) = (1 + c − a, a − c). Its Hodge line is the τ_0-line, as (∗) demands, iff a = c + 1, i.e. g ∈ X_{σ(μ)}(b). So M(G, b, μ)(k) = X_{σ(μ)}(b)(k) = {v(g) = (a, a − 1)}, which is disjoint from X_μ(b)(k) = {v(g) = (a, a)}. This contradicts (3) as printed, because the GL_2-level bijection sends g to gΛ_W. The last step of the proof of Proposition 3.11 ('sends X_μ(b)(k) … to M̄_μ(b)^{p^{-∞}}(k) … follows from Theorem 3.10(3)') has the same defect. Case for the defence: the problem vanishes when {μ} is Q_p-rational, including GL_h and every use of Theorem 3.10(2). The dimension results survive: g ↦ bσ(g) is an isomorphism of perfect spaces X_μ(b) ≅ X_{σ(μ)}(b), and ⟨ρ, σ(μ)⟩ = ⟨ρ, μ⟩, so the statement of Proposition 3.11 (as an abstract isomorphism) and Corollary 3.12 remain true. Footnote 16 relates the conventions to [Kim13] only by Λ ↔ Λ^* and μ ↔ −μ, which does not account for the missing σ. The same text is in arXiv v2 and v3.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotations check on the images of pp. 460–463. Conventions, all from the paper: F = ρ(b)σ on the contravariant module (p. 461 (1); p. 463 F = β^{-1}(bσ)β); (Lie X)^* = Fil^1 = ker(F mod p), forced by the paper's 1 = D(Q_p/Z_p) with F(1) = 1 and Fil^1 1 = 0; X_μ(b) = {g : g^{-1}bσ(g) ∈ G(W)p^μG(W)} ((3.1.1), (0.3.1)); and (∗) asks the Hodge filtration to be a G-translate of the μ-filtration Fil^1 = Λ^1. General computation: for a point gΛ_W with g^{-1}bσ(g) = h'p^{μ'}h, the Hodge filtration in the frame g is σ^{-1}(h)^{-1}·σ^{-1}(Λ^1_{μ'}), of type σ^{-1}(μ'). A G(k)-translate carrying it to the μ-filtration forces σ^{-1}(μ') to be conjugate to μ: both cocharacters then lie in P_μ with the same image in P_μ/U_μ, so they are U_μ-conjugate. Hence (∗) at gΛ_W ⇔ μ' = σ(μ), and M(G,b,μ)(k) = X_{σ(μ)}(b)(k), not X_μ(b)(k). I verified the counterexample independently. G = Res_{Z_{p²}/Z_p}G_m = Aut_{Z_{p²}}(Λ), Λ = Z_{p²}, s = the Z_{p²}-action. Λ⊗W = W_{τ0} ⊕ W_{τ1}, and a⊗x ↦ (τ_0(a)x, τ_1(a)x) turns id⊗σ into (y_0, y_1) ↦ (σy_1, σy_0). With μ = (1,0) (n = 1, h = 2) and b = μ(p), F(x_0,x_1) = (pσx_1, σx_0). Then ker(F mod p) is the τ_1-line, while Fil^1 is the τ_0-line. G(W)p^μG(W) = p^μT(W), and T(k) preserves both lines, so (2) fails for every representative. For g with valuations (a,c) and M = p^aW ⊕ p^cW (the lattices stable under the tensors), F(M) ⊂ M ⇔ a ∈ {c, c+1}, and the Hodge line of M is the τ_0-line iff a = c+1. So M(G,b,μ)(k) = {(c+1,c)} = X_{σμ}(b)(k), while X_μ(b)(k) = {(a,a)}. These are disjoint inside the GL_2 set, where the map is g ↦ gΛ_W. Theorem 3.10(3), as a bijection compatible with the two embeddings, is therefore false here, and the last step of the proof of Proposition 3.11 (p. 464) fails the same way. Neither is rescued by the framing: X_0 (a = c = 0) is not itself in M(G,b,μ). Literature check. [HP15] (arXiv 1509.03914, which the paper cites on p. 462) has Def. 2.2.2(ii) b ∈ G(W)μ^σ(p)G(W), Lemma 2.2.5 (Hodge filtration induced by a conjugate of μ), and Thm. A(ii) RZ_G(k) ≅ X_{G,b,μ^σ}(k). Kim's final arXiv version (1308.5537v6, Lemma 2.5.8) states that the Hodge filtration is a {μ}-filtration iff b ∈ G(W)p^{σ*μ^{-1}}G(W), which is b ∈ G(W)p^{σ(μ)}G(W) after the footnote-16 dictionary μ ↔ −μ. One refinement to the first reading's remark on footnote 16: Kim13 v1 (2013, the version cited) does use G(W)μ(p^{-1})G(W) (Cor. 3.8.2), so the footnote matches it. But v1 also imposes, as the 'Hodge-type condition' (Def. 2.3.2), that the μ-filtration is the Hodge filtration Fil^1M_0 = F^{-1}(pM_0), which excludes this example. Zhu drops that hypothesis and asserts on p. 461 that it follows ('by our assumption and the classical Dieudonné theory'). Case for the defence, which I accept as limiting the damage: when {μ} is defined over Q_p (all GL_h cases, Theorem 3.10(2), and PEL/Hodge data with reflex field Q_p) nothing changes. Also, g ↦ bσ(g) is an isomorphism of perfect k̄-spaces X_μ(b) ≅ X_{σ(μ)}(b), since σ is the relative Frobenius of the F_p-structure, and ⟨ρ,σμ⟩ = ⟨ρ,μ⟩. So an isomorphism X_μ(b) ≅ M̄_μ(b)^{p^{-∞}}, the dimension equality in Proposition 3.11 and Corollary 3.12 survive. The map the proof constructs does not identify X_μ(b) with M̄. The same statements occur in the introduction: p. 409 'one identifies the set of k-points of M(G,b,μ) with the set X_μ(b)', and Proposition 0.4, p. 410. arXiv v2 (Theorem 3.10(4), citing [Kim, Prop. 3.8.4]; Proposition 3.12) and v3 have the same text.

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma A.2, p. 465
issues.printed: The source describes U x_{X,sigma_X} X -> U x_{Y,sigma_Y} Y as obtained by base change from X -> X x_{Y,sigma_Y} Y using U x_{Y,sigma_Y} Y -> Y as an étale cover.
issues.correction: ... the base change of X -> X x_{Y,σ_Y} Y along the étale cover U x_{Y,σ_Y} Y -> X x_{Y,σ_Y} Y (the base change of U -> X).
issues.reason: A map with target X x_{Y,sigma_Y} Y cannot be base-changed along a map to Y. Along the corrected cover, X x_{(X x_{Y,sigma_Y} Y)} (U x_{Y,sigma_Y} Y) = U x_{X,sigma_X} X, and the conclusion (being an isomorphism descends along an étale cover) goes through.

issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation is verbatim on the p. 465 image. The relative Frobenius is X -> X x_{Y,σ_Y} Y, x ↦ (σ_X(x), f(x)), and its target is X x_{Y,σ_Y} Y, so it cannot be base-changed along a map to Y. The cover that works is U x_{Y,σ_Y} Y -> X x_{Y,σ_Y} Y, the base change of the étale cover U -> X, so it is itself an étale cover. Computing directly: X x_{(X x_{Y,σ} Y)} (U x_{Y,σ} Y) = {(x,u) : σ_X(x) = g(u)} = U x_{X,σ_X} X, and the induced map to U x_{Y,σ_Y} Y is (u, x) ↦ (u, f(x)). So the sentence holds with the corrected cover, and 'being an isomorphism' descends along it. A slip in naming the target of the cover.

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma A.7(7), p. 467
issues.printed: For b in B, the source chooses a monic g(x) in A^{p^-inf}[x] with g(b) = 0. It claims that sufficiently large n puts every coefficient of h(x) := g(x)^{p^n} in A, and uses h(b) = 0 to conclude that b is integral over A.
issues.correction: Lift the coefficients of h to A to get a monic h̃ ∈ A[x]. Then h̃(b) ∈ ker(B -> B^{p^-∞}), so h̃(b)^{p^m} = 0 for some m, and b is a root of the monic polynomial h̃(x)^{p^m} ∈ A[x].
issues.reason: A -> A^{p^-inf} and B -> B^{p^-inf} need not be injective (the lemma allows non-reduced spaces), and g(b) = 0 holds only in B^{p^-inf}. The literal step 'h(b) = 0' fails in B for non-reduced B. The repair is one line.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation is verbatim on the p. 467 image. Lemma A.7 is stated for arbitrary algebraic spaces over k, which may be non-reduced, and then A -> A^{p^-∞} and B -> B^{p^-∞} need not be injective. 'All coefficients of h are in A' can then only mean 'in the image of A', and h(b) = g(b)^{p^n} = 0 holds only in B^{p^-∞}. For a lift h̃ ∈ A[x], h̃(b) lies in ker(B -> B^{p^-∞}), which consists of the elements killed by some power of Frobenius, and need not be 0. So 'Since h(b) = 0, b is integral over A' does not follow as written. For reduced A and B the argument is literally correct. The repair is short and correct: h̃(b)^{p^m} = 0, so b is a root of the monic polynomial h̃(x)^{p^m} ∈ A[x]. The lemma is true. So this is a gap, as the first reading says. But a gap means the written proof of (7) (direction 'f^{p^-∞} integral ⇒ f integral') is incomplete in the non-reduced case, so the reach is 'the proof', not 'nothing'. The applications of A.7(7) (Theorem A.30, Prop. A.32) use only the easy direction.

issues.locator: A.3.5(ii), display (A.3.4), p. 481
issues.printed: In part (ii), the source assumes connectedness of J_1 and triviality of its action on X. It calls (A.3.4) P_J(X) -> P_{J/J_1}(X) a forgetful functor and asserts that this functor is an equivalence.
issues.correction: Then the pullback (inflation) functor P_{J/J_1}(X) -> P_J(X) along J -> J/J_1 is an equivalence of categories.
issues.reason: J/J_1 is a quotient of J, not a subgroup. A J/J_1-equivariant structure pulls back to a J-equivariant one, and there is no forgetful functor in the printed direction. Since an equivalence is asserted, the content is unaffected. Same in v2 and v3.

issues.reviewReason: The p. 481 image reads '(ii) Assume that J_1 is connected and that the action of J_1 on X is trivial. Then the forgetful functor (A.3.4) P_J(X) -> P_{J/J_1}(X) is an equivalence of categories.' J/J_1 is a quotient of J, not a subgroup. The natural functor is inflation, pulling a J/J_1-equivariant structure back along J -> J/J_1, and it goes P_{J/J_1}(X) -> P_J(X), the same direction as (A.3.3) (q^*[dim J_1] : P_{J/J_1}(X̄) ≃ P_J(X)). A functor in the printed direction exists only as a quasi-inverse, obtained by descending the structure using connectedness of J_1, and it is not 'forgetful'. Since an equivalence is asserted, the content is unchanged. v2 and v3 have the same.

issues.locator: A.3.5, last paragraph, p. 482
issues.printed: The source assumes a finite-codimension closed normal subgroup J_1 of J acting trivially on X, with J_1 obtained by perfecting a pro-unipotent pro-algebraic group. It defines P_J(X) as P_{J/J_1}(X) and invokes (A.3.4) and (A.3.6) to claim that both definitions are unaffected by the choice of J_1.
issues.correction: Require J_1 to be connected (as for the congruence subgroups L^+G^{(h)} used in the paper). Two admissible choices J_1, J_1' are then compared through the connected, normal, pro-unipotent subgroup J_1J_1' (or through J_1 ∩ J_1'), applying (A.3.4) to the connected groups J_1J_1'/J_1 and J_1J_1'/J_1', and (A.3.6) for cohomology.
issues.reason: (A.3.4) is stated only for connected J_1, but the condition allows disconnected unipotent J_1 (finite p-groups are unipotent in characteristic p). Counterexample: J = Z/p (constant), X = Spec k. Both J_1 = J and J_1' = {1} satisfy the condition, but P_{J/J}(X) = Vect while P_{J/{1}}(X) = Rep_{Qlbar}(Z/p), which has p simple objects. This also conflicts with the earlier definition of P_J for pfp J. The cohomology half is fine, since (A.3.6) holds for any unipotent J_1 (l != p). In the paper J_1 is always a connected congruence subgroup, so nothing downstream is affected.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The quotation is verbatim on the p. 482 image. The mathematics is right. In characteristic p, unipotent groups need not be connected: the constant group Z/p ⊂ G_a is unipotent. So the condition admits disconnected J_1, and the independence claim then fails. Take J = Z/p, X = Spec k (k algebraically closed). Both J_1 = J and J_1' = {1} satisfy every stated condition, but P_{J/J}(X) = Vect while P_{J/{1}}(X) = Rep_{Q̄_ℓ}(Z/p), with p simple objects. The latter also agrees with the first-paragraph definition of P_J for pfp J, while the former does not. Connectedness of J alone does not rescue it either: G_a^{p^-∞} acting on X = G_a^{p^-∞} through the Artin-Schreier map has kernel J_1 = Z/p, and P_J(X) = Rep(Z/p) ≠ Vect = P_{J/J_1}(X). Classification: the defect is the omission of the word 'connected'. The sentence justifies independence 'By (A.3.4)', and (A.3.4) is stated only for connected J_1. Every J_1 the paper actually uses is a connected congruence subgroup L^+G^{(h)} = ker(L^+G -> L^hG) (§2.1.1, p. 429). So the intended hypothesis is fixed by the cited result and by every use, and with it the claim is true. This matches how missing hypotheses clear from context are classified elsewhere in this verification (misprint, affects nothing). 'Error' with 'affects nothing' is not coherent here: if the independence claim were counted as a genuine false assertion, it would affect a stated claim. The cohomology half ((A.3.6)) needs only unipotence. For two connected choices it gives the same answer as for the categories.

In §1.3.1 (p. 421), μ• = (μ_1, …, μ_N), and Gr_{μ•} classifies chains E_N ⇢ ⋯ ⇢ E_0 (1.3.1), one step for each μ_i. The line bundles L_i on p. 483 are indexed by these steps. issues.locator: p. 488, §B.3, final paragraph
issues.printed: The source restricts \tilde L_det to Gr_2 ⊂ \widetilde{Gr}_2 and then defines L_det = j_*(L_det|_{Gr_2}).
issues.correction: L_det = j_*(\tilde L_det|_{Gr_2}), where Gr_2 ⊂ \widetilde{Gr}_2 is identified with Gr_2 ⊂ \overline{Gr}_2 by Lemma 1.18.
issues.reason: L_det is the bundle being constructed, so the printed right-hand side is circular. The previous sentence restricts \tilde L_det to Gr_2 ⊂ \widetilde{Gr}_2, which identifies with Gr_2 ⊂ \overline{Gr}_2 by Lemma 1.18. Case for the defence: once L_det exists, L_det|_{Gr_2} = \tilde L_det|_{Gr_2}, so the printed identity is true but not a construction. The claim is plausible but left unproved. The complement of Gr_2 is the point pE_0, which is an A_1 cone point with class group Z/2 (not killed by perfection for p odd), so j_* of a line bundle need not be invertible. Here \tilde L_det restricted to the exceptional P^1 over pE_0 is (E_0/E_1)⊗(E_1/pE_0) = O(1)⊗O(−1) = O, which makes invertibility plausible.
searched: Crossref record of doi:10.4007/annals.2017.185.2.2, checked 2026-09-23: no update, correction or erratum relation
issues.citation: Xinwen Zhu, "Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic", Annals of Mathematics 185 (2017), no. 2
issues.reviewReason: The page image (p. 488) reads 'One can restrict \tilde L_det to Gr_2 ⊂ \widetilde{Gr}_2. Then L_det = j_*(L_det|_{Gr_2}).' The right-hand side has no tilde. As a definition of L_det it is circular. As an identity it holds for any line bundle on the normal surface \overline{Gr}_2, so it constructs nothing. The previous sentence shows the intent: restrict \tilde L_det, identify π^{−1}Gr_2 ≅ Gr_2 by Lemma 1.18, then push forward. arXiv v3 has the same text. The dropped tilde does not affect the meaning. (The unproved claim that this j_* is invertible belongs to E34. It is in fact easy: near pE_0, \widetilde{Gr}_2 → \overline{Gr}_2 contracts the (−2)-section of P(O(1)⊕O(−1)) to the A_1 point. \tilde L_det has degree (E_0/E_1)⊗(E_1/pE_0) = O(1)⊗O(−1), i.e. 0, on that curve. So its class in the local class group Z/2 is trivial.)

issues.locator: Lemma 6.9 proof, published p.292; also arXiv v3 printed p.51
issues.printed: The proof identifies a quotient of the entire eta term in degree n−1 with line-twisted I-torsion in H^n(C).
issues.correction: Use the good-truncation boundary quotient: if x=f^(n−1)y lies in eta and dy=fz, H^n(C)[f]=0 implies z=dw; hence dx=f^n dw maps to zero in the target boundary quotient. Do not identify the entire degree n−1 term quotient with H^n(C)[I].

issues.locator: Remark 11.16, p.307 (Publ. math. IHÉS 129)
issues.printed: The source claims globalization would give canonical descent of every smooth formal scheme X/O_K to W(k)[π^p] ⊂ O_K, the θ-image of 𝔖 → O_K. It calls this impossible, citing as a counterexample elliptic curves having good reduction and j invariant in O_K − W(k)[π^p].
issues.correction: A descent along φ of the projection for A=O_K is a quotient 𝔖/J with φ(J)𝔖=(E). If no such J exists, which is so whenever p does not divide the degree e of E (in particular for K unramified, where moreover W(k)[π^p]=O_K and no elliptic curve as described exists), there is no descent already for A=O_K, for a different reason. If it exists, J=ker θ, 𝔖/J≅W(k)[π^p], O_K is free of rank p over it, and the elliptic-curve argument applies.
issues.reason: K=Q_p, π=p, E=z−p: W(k)[π^p]=Z_p=O_K, so the set O_K−W(k)[π^p] is empty and the printed counterexample does not exist; and (z−p) is not generated by a power series in z^p, so the projection for A=O_K has no descent at all. For p∤e, e>1, O_K is not the base change along φ of any quotient of 𝔖, so 'descends to W(k)[π^p]' is not what a descent along φ would give. The conclusion of the remark, that no functorial descent exists, is true in every case.

issues.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.9, p.13 (with Lemma 3.4, p.11), arXiv:1710.06145v3
issues.printed: The source uses the trivial action of Δ on R and Lemma 3.7 to identify the last quotient as a finite direct sum of R-copies. Proposition 3.8 is then invoked to exclude nonzero 𝔪-torsion, and Lemma 3.4 is claimed to apply to the maps and yield the conclusion.

issues.reason: For M=H^i_cont(Δ,R)⊕H^i_cont(Δ,M_∞) the quotient M/M[ζ_p−1] is the image of the first summand, whereas M/(ζ_p−1)M is H^i_cont(Δ,R)/(ζ_p−1) plus the whole second summand; a module without 𝔪-torsion always has M/M[f] without 𝔪-torsion, so the check made is not the hypothesis of the lemma. issues.locator: Remark 11.16, p.307 (Publ. math. IHÉS 129)
issues.printed: The obstruction to functorial Frobenius descent is illustrated for general K by an elliptic j-invariant outside W(k)[π^p].
issues.correction: A descent along φ of the projection for A=O_K is a quotient 𝔖/J with φ(J)𝔖=(E). If no such J exists, which is so whenever p does not divide the degree e of E (in particular for K unramified, where moreover W(k)[π^p]=O_K and no elliptic curve as described exists), there is no descent already for A=O_K, for a different reason. If it exists, J=ker θ, 𝔖/J≅W(k)[π^p], O_K is free of rank p over it, and the elliptic-curve argument applies.
issues.reason: For K=Q_p and π=p, W(k)[π^p]=O_K, so the suggested j-invariant cannot exist. The ideal (z−p) cannot be extended from a series ideal in z^p. More generally p∤e obstructs coefficient-ideal descent already for O_K. The conclusion about absence of functorial descent survives with these separate cases.

issues.locator: §14, proof of Proposition 14.4(b), p. 62
issues.printed: The proof claims β′⁴ ≠ 0 and analogous nonvanishing for subsequent powers, treating this as a contradiction to β being nilpotent.

issues.locator: Compositio156(2020), Lemma9.1/proof, printed pp.2493–2494; PDF pp.26–27; also v6 pp.22–23
issues.printed: The source asserts generic finiteness.
issues.correction: Do not use the unrestricted pullback identity for degeneracy loci across jumping modular fibres. Control the exceptional fibres or prove a stratified global statement; retain this as a gap in the global closedness proof.
issues.reason: Take a constant abelian surface B, S=Bl₀(B), A=B×S, and X the graph of the blowdown S→B. The modular image is B in a fixed fibre and the map on X has generic relative dimension0. Its exceptional curve E≃P¹ is constant in B; its relative generically special closure over E has relative dimension0<dim E=1, so E⊂X^deg(0). But B in a fixed fibre has empty0-degeneracy locus. Generic finiteness does not imply dimension preservation for every subvariety. This refutes the unrestricted intermediate identity, not the ultimate closedness theorem.

issues.locator: §3.3, the sketch for the families j = n + in0, p. 651 (published version)
issues.printed: The source claims that, for f with degree at most d ≥ 1 separately in each variable, some n0 satisfying 0 ≤ n0 ≤ 2d³ + 1 makes j = n + in0 permissible. It says one may choose n0 ≥ 1 avoiding the obstacle with n0 − 1 bounded by the total degree of Gm, and bounds that degree by 2dψ(m)² ≤ 2d³ using resultant estimates.
issues.correction: The obstacle must be avoided for every m with ψ(m) ≤ d at once, so the sketch as written gives n0 − 1 ≤ Σ_{m: ψ(m) ≤ d} 2dψ(m)² ≤ 2d⁴ (there are at most d such m, as ψ(m) ≥ m), that is some 1 ≤ n0 ≤ 2d⁴ + 1. The bound 2d³ + 1 needs a further argument.
issues.reason: Permissibility needs Gm(n + in0, n − in0) ≢ 0 in n for every m ≤ M, as in the proof of Lemma 3.2. The sketch shows that the obstacle can occur only when ψ(m) ≤ d and, for one such m, excludes at most deg Gm ≤ 2dψ(m)² values of n0. For d ≥ 3 more than one m qualifies (m = 1, and m = 2 since ψ(2) = 3), and the excluded sets need not coincide: for d = 3 the union bound is 2·3·(1 + 9) = 60 > 54 = 2d³. The existence of some n0 bounded polynomially in d is unaffected; whether 2d³ + 1 itself holds is not settled here.

issues.correction: d_ℓp = e^{−2ρ_P(H_P(p))} d_rp, that is, left Haar measure is δ_P(p)^{−1} times right Haar measure.
issues.reason: For the upper triangular group of GL_2 with p = (a, u; 0, b), left multiplication rescales u by the upper-left entry and right multiplication by the lower-right entry, so left Haar measure is |a|^{−1}da* db* du (the formula Arthur himself gives on p. 21) and right Haar measure is |b|^{−1}da* db* du. Their ratio |b/a| equals e^{−2ρ(H_P(p))}, since α(H_P(p)) = log|a/b| for the unique root α and ρ = α/2.

issues.reason: Let X be the closed unit disc over an algebraically closed complete field of characteristic 0, V ⊂ X the annulus {|T| = 1} (an object of X_ét) and U = lim_n V_n → V the Kummer tower T^{1/p^n}. U → X is pro-étale with a countable presentation, so {U → V} is a covering of the printed Definition 3.9. A pullback along V_n → Z of a morphism Y → Z of X_fét is a union of components of the restriction to V_n of a finite étale cover of X; the closed disc over such a field has no nontrivial finite étale covers (Lütkebohmert's p-adic Riemann existence theorem, not read here), so the connected degree-p steps V_{n+1} → V_n are not of that form. Hence the countable case is unchanged only if steps may be finite étale surjections of X_ét.

issues.citation: Peter Scholze, Erratum to 'p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties', three-page author erratum (undated), SHA-256 identical to the copy read in RS-05
issues.reviewReason: Rejected as justified. The reason rests on the claim that the closed unit disc over an algebraically closed complete field of characteristic 0 has no nontrivial finite étale covers, which is false: over ℂ_p, ℂ_p⟨T⟩ → ℂ_p⟨U⟩, T ↦ U^p − U, is finite étale of degree p (the derivative pU^{p−1} − 1 is a unit) and connected (ℂ_p⟨U⟩ is a domain). So it is not shown that the Kummer steps over the annulus fail the X_fét form of the erratum's condition. This does not show that the packet's reading (steps pulled back from X_ét) is wrong: with it, the erratum's 'for countable limits, the definitions are unchanged' is immediate, and the packet keeps it as its chosen reading. Found by the checkpoint review of 2026-09-26 (finding F4) and confirmed here.

issues.locator: §8, proof of Proposition 8.5, p. 48 (arXiv:1205.3463v2)

The paper states only the absolute charts (Lemma 5.2). The relative charts follow from Huber 1.6.10 over the base V, Lemma 2.2.8 and the ball-into-torus embedding; they are AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-toric-charts.

issues.locator: §15, Lemma 15.3 (second assertion) and its proof, p. 90, arXiv v4 (14 April 2026)
issues.printed: The source claims that for a Tate Zp -algebra A, completing A∞ uniformly gives a perfectoid Â∞. It says x^{p^n} − ϖ0 x = ϖ0 defines a finite étale R-algebra, hence a solution exists in R with x = ϖ ∈ R.
issues.correction: Assume A complete (or, more generally, that A has a ring of definition henselian along a pseudouniformizer). For an arbitrary Tate ℤ_p-algebra A apply the lemma to the completion Â: Spa and Spd do not change, and the tower must be taken over Â. The proof's step 'finite étale over R = Â∞, hence a solution' needs FÉt(A∞) ≅ FÉt(Â∞), which holds when A is complete (the ring of definition colim A_i° is then henselian along ϖ) and fails in general.
issues.reason: ECD §3 defines a Tate ring without completeness. Take A = ℚ_p[T] with ring of definition ℤ_p[T] and the p-adic topology. Finite étale ℚ_p[T]-algebras are products of L[T] for finite extensions L/ℚ_p (the affine line over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 is simply connected), so every tower has A∞ = B[T] with B a colimit of finite étale ℚ_p-algebras; its uniform completion is B̂⟨T⟩, and at any point of Spa(B̂) with completed residue field K the element T ∈ K°⟨T⟩ is not a p-th power modulo the maximal ideal of K°, so Frobenius is not surjective modulo ϖ^p and B̂⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid. Here FÉt(A∞) → FÉt(Â∞) is not essentially surjective: B̂⟨T⟩[X]/(X^p − X − T/p) is finite étale but not split.

issues.printed: Definition 2.8.1 asserts equivalence, for a Banach ring A, of: (a) equivalence of its norm to some power-multiplicative norm; (b) equivalence of its norm to its spectral seminorm; (c) existence of c > 0 with |x2 | ≥ c |x|2 for every x ∈ A; and (d) boundedness of the subring A◦.
issues.correction: (a)-(c) are equivalent and define uniformity; they imply (d), and (d) implies that the spectral norm defines the topology; (d) implies (a)-(c) when A contains a topologically nilpotent unit z with |z|·|z⁻¹| = 1 (for instance for the norms of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm), but not in general.
issues.reason: On a complete nonarchimedean field K the norm |x| for |x| ≤ 1 and |x|(1 + log|x|) for |x| > 1 is submultiplicative, defines the topology of K (so K° is bounded) and is not equivalent to its spectral norm |·|; so (d) does not imply (b). The authors record this in the errata to the paper.

issues.locator: item (1), p. 1, in the three-page erratum (SHA-256 3cfa56b9…)
issues.printed: The source says an analogous condition belongs in the pro-étale covering definition, Definition 3.9, and also in Definition 3.4.
issues.correction: For Definition 3.9 the 'similar condition' is not displayed. The reading that preserves étale covers: each covering map U_i -> U is a composite of a transfinite composition of pullbacks of finite étale surjections (U_0 = W_i) and an étale map W_i -> U. Requiring U_i -> U itself to be such a transfinite composition, as a literal transfer of the Definition 3.3 condition, would exclude open covers.
issues.reason: A covering of X_proét by two open subspaces U_1, U_2 ⊆ X is a family of étale (open) immersions; an open immersion onto a proper open is not a transfinite composition of pullbacks of finite étale surjections (each such map is surjective on underlying spaces). So the Definition 3.3 condition cannot be transferred verbatim.

issues.locator: §3.1, proof of Corollary 3.4, p. 1725 (journal); same in arXiv v4
issues.printed: The source claims the object now exists and is sousperfectoid, because an étale algebra over a sousperfectoid algebra remains sousperfectoid, citing Proposition 6.3.3.(ii) op. cit.
issues.correction: Berkeley 6.3.3(2) concerns finite étale algebras only. The step holds in the following form: an étale map to the locally noetherian space B is locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale map (Huber Lemma 2.2.8); pulled back to the sousperfectoid X ×_L B, the finite étale pieces are sousperfectoid by 6.3.3(2) and their opens are covered by sousperfectoid rational subsets by 6.3.3(1). This proves that the fibre product is a sousperfectoid adic space (covered by sousperfectoid affinoids); the algebra-level statement 'étale algebras over sousperfectoid algebras are sousperfectoid' is proved only for composites of rational localisations and finite étale maps, since the sousperfectoid property is not known to be of local nature (Hansen-Kedlaya Definition 7.1).

issues.locator: §4, proof of Lemma 4.7, Stein case, printed p. 21 (arXiv v1)
issues.printed: The source claims strictness of the canonical surjections p_j : Ω^j_{A^n}(A^n) → Ω^j_X(X). From p_{i+1} ∘ d^i_{A^n} = d^i_X ∘ p_i, it concludes that reduction to X = A^n is valid.
issues.correction: The reduction does not follow as written (the image of a closed subspace under a strict surjection need not be closed). It is completed by finiteness: im(d^i_X) has finite codimension in the closed subspace ker(d^{i+1}_X) because H^{i+1}_dR(X) is finite-dimensional, and a finite-codimensional image of a continuous map of Fréchet spaces is closed; then the Banach open mapping theorem gives strictness. This is why the footnote's hypotheses are needed; for general smooth Stein X finite-dimensionality must be assumed or proved.
issues.reason: p_{i+1}(im d_{A^n}) = im d_X, and p_{i+1} maps the closed subspace im d_{A^n} = ker d_{A^n} onto a subspace whose closedness is exactly what is to be shown.

issues.printed: The source calls A Tate when A contains a topologically nilpotent unit z. For each c ∈ (0, 1), it claims A becomes a Banach ring under the norm given by α(x) = inf{cⁿ : n ∈ Z, z⁻ⁿx ∈ A0}.
issues.correction: Require z ∈ A0 (always achievable by replacing z with a power, or since every ring of definition of a Tate ring contains a topologically nilpotent unit, Wedhorn Proposition 6.14), and A complete and Hausdorff for 'Banach ring'. Then α is a submultiplicative nonarchimedean norm defining the topology.
issues.reason: Without z ∈ A0 the exponent set {n : z⁻ⁿx ∈ A0} need not be downward closed and α violates even the triangle inequality. Take A = ℚ_p(√p), A0 = {a + b√p : a ∈ ℤ_p, b ∈ pℤ_p} (an open bounded subring, i.e. a ring of definition), z = √p and c = 1/2. Then α(1) = 1 (allowed n: 0 and n ≤ −2), α(√p) = 1/2 (allowed n: 1 and n ≤ −1), but α(1 + √p) = 4 (allowed n: n ≤ −2 only), and 4 > 1 + 1/2. Checked on the page image.

issues.locator: Proof of Lemma 8.3.3, pp. 40–41, arXiv:2205.15352v4 (February 2025), author pagination; scoped to this accessed preprint, not to the journal version of record.
issues.printed: The proof seeks a smooth compactification with strict normal-crossings boundary. After strictifying the stable-moduli boundary by stratum blowups, it takes the normalization in the finite étale cover’s function field and proceeds to boundary monodromy without resolving that normalization.
issues.correction: A finite normalization of a smooth strict-SNC model need not be smooth. Resolve the normalized projective model and principalize its reduced boundary while preserving the given smooth cover. Use the resulting proper boundary morphism to pull back node-smoothing equations; their nonnegative exponents give the same commuting-meridian formula. Stack-to-scheme realization and comparison with the coarse model must retain their separate hypotheses.
issues.reason: Over a characteristic-zero field, the connected cover of the two-dimensional torus defined by z²=xy is finite étale. The normalization of the affine plane in its function field is Spec(k[x,y,z]/(z²−xy)): a normal quadratic cone, singular at the origin. Its local dimension is two but its cotangent dimension there is three. Thus normalization alone does not provide the smooth compactification needed at this step. Resolution preserving the cover supplies it, and the full-chart extending-unit argument computes the added boundary meridians. A stronger example survives the preceding boundary-stratum blowup: over C take z³=xy, then x=u and y=uv. The integral closure is C[a³,a²b,ab²,b³], with u=a³, v=b³, z=a²b and ab²=z²/u. It is the normal third-Veronese ring, finite over C[u,v], with the correct fraction field. Its vertex has dimension two and cotangent dimension four, so this normalized pivot chart is still singular.

issues.reason: A smooth proper curve can have only one rational special-fibre point, so every integral rational point lies in the same disc. issues.reason: Take c=0, ε=1/4 and F(x)=exp(x/4) for x<0, exp(−2x) for x≥0, F(0)=1. The printed weighted function is exp(x) on x<0 and exp(−5x/4) on x≥0, integrable/BV and continuous. Yet the transform at s=0 has negative-tail integrand exp(−x/4), so its ordinary improper integral diverges. The double class of [1 b; 0 n/m] depends only on b mod (1/m)ℤ, so as printed t_{1,2,1/2} = t_{1,2,0} = μ*_2. But e(1/2)μ*_2 = μ*_2 is impossible: its adjoint μ_2 e(−1/2) = μ_2, multiplied on the left by μ*_2, gives e(−1/2) = 1 by relation (a). With the corrected entry, (n, m, γ) ↦ X is a bijection onto the double cosets, which is the linear independence the proof asserts next.

issues.printed: The remark identifies continuous Mahler expansions on ℤ_p with convergent ordinary power series on the whole unit disc.

issues.reason: Take K=Q(sqrt(-31)), p=3 and S the complex place and the prime above 3. The three reduced forms (1,1,8),(2,-1,4),(2,1,4) give class number three. The source’s finite Poitou–Tate theorem remains the correct input; this finding does not reject its final duality statements.

issues.locator: Lemma 4.14, final proof paragraph, author p. 53; published journal p. 368, Inventiones 211 (2018)
issues.printed: The proof says G_(L,S) has finite image in G_(F,S), then invokes injectivity of inflation to descend splitting.

issues.locator: §31.2 Exercise, printed p.201 of the 2006 Springer edition, Grundlehren 335; the dimension-index notation is defined in §28.7, p.185.
issues.printed: The special-block length n also appears as the dimension index in the requirement ρ∈G_n^0(F). Thus the literal indexing restricts the irreducible Weil factor to dimension n.
issues.correction: Allow any finite-dimensional irreducible smooth Weil factor ρ, of dimension d≥1 independent of the special-block length n≥1: ρ∈G_d^0(F). The block has dimension dn.
issues.reason: The source defines G_d^0(F) as dimension-d irreducible Weil representations. Sp(2), with a one-dimensional trivial Weil factor, is an indecomposable Frobenius-semisimple object of dimension two and nonzero monodromy. Under the literal restriction d=n, n≥2 forces dimension n²≥4, while n=1 forces dimension one and zero monodromy. Hence the literal restriction excludes Sp(2); separating the indices repairs the intended classification.

issues.locator: Definition 2.19, p. 33, arXiv:0809.0415v2
issues.printed: The definition calls D split when some representation R −→ Md (k) has determinant D. It claims this is equivalent to R/ ker(D) being a finite product of matrix algebras with base field k.
issues.correction: The two conditions are not equivalent. 'R/ker(D) is a finite product of matrix algebras over k' implies 'D is the determinant of a representation R → M_d(k)', but not conversely, even for multiplicity-free D. In the notation of Theorem 2.16 with all k_i/k finite separable: D is the determinant of a k-representation iff the index of S_i divides m_i for every i; R/ker(D) is a product of matrix algebras over k iff moreover every k_i = k and every S_i is split. The two conditions agree when D is absolutely irreducible, and when k is algebraically closed. The second condition is the one used in the proof of Theorem 2.22 and in the sentence after the definition, and should be taken as the definition of 'split'.
issues.reason: (1) k = ℝ, R = ℂ, D = N_{ℂ/ℝ} (dimension 2, multiplicity free): D is the determinant of the regular representation ℂ → M_2(ℝ), ker(D) = 0, and R/ker(D) = ℂ is a field of degree 2 over ℝ, not a product of matrix algebras over ℝ. (2) k = ℝ, R = ℝ[Q_8], D = det of the 4-dimensional real representation of Q_8 on ℍ by left multiplication: D is the determinant of R → End_ℝ(ℍ) ≅ M_4(ℝ), but R/ker(D) ≅ ℍ, a division algebra (D = Nrd² on the ℍ factor, m = 2, index 2). With the first condition as definition, Theorem 2.22(ii) fails for A = k = ℝ, R = ℂ, D = N_{ℂ/ℝ}; with the second it is correct.

issues.locator: Proposition A.2.1 and its proof, Point 5 and Figure 1, pp. 30–34 of the preprint arXiv 1106.5586v1 (the only arXiv version); the published version, Math. Ann. 356 (2013), was not obtained, and this finding is against the preprint only
issues.printed: In the l = 5 case, the source places the projective image of G in a conjugate of PGL2 (F5 ) or of PSL2 (F5 ). For Ḡ equal to PGL2 (F5 ), it cites [CPS75, 2.3 (g)] to claim H 1 (G, gln (Fl )) 6= (0), concluding that G lacks adequacy.
issues.correction: In the preprint: for l = 5 only the projective image PSL₂(F_5) is excluded; if the image of G in PGL₂(F̄_5) is conjugate to PGL₂(F_5), then G is adequate. (The same is in print as Guralnick–Herzig–Tiep, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 19 (2017), Corollary 9.5, which does not mention the discrepancy.)
issues.reason: By Lemmas A.1.3–A.1.4 of the same appendix, G is adequate iff GL₂(F_5) is. GL₂(F_5) has no quotient of order 5, 5 ∤ 2, its semisimple elements span M₂(F_5), and H¹(GL₂(F_5), gl₂) = H¹(GL₂(F_5), F_5) ⊕ H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂) = 0: the first because the abelianisation is F_5^× of order 4; the second by a direct cocycle computation over the Cayley graph of GL₂(F_5) (a direct linear-algebra computation by this job), which gives dim H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂ ⊗ det^j) = 0, 0, 1, 0 for j = 0, 1, 2, 3, and dim H¹ = 1 for SL₂(F_5) and for {g : det g = ±1}. So the class in H¹(SL₂(F_5), sl₂) is moved by the outer action of diag(2,1) (it lives in sl₂ ⊗ det²), and inflation–restriction gives H¹(GL₂(F_5), sl₂) = H¹(SL₂(F_5), sl₂)^{GL₂/SL₂} = 0. This agrees with the Andersen–Jørgensen–Landrock description of Ext¹_{GL₂(F_p)}(1, Sym^{p−3} ⊗ det^b) (nonzero only for b ≡ 1 mod p − 1, while sl₂ = Sym² ⊗ det⁻¹), and with Gee–Newton Lemma 3.2.3.

issues.locator: §1.1 Notations, printed p. 180 (Duke Math. J. 54 (1987)); Collège de France PDF p. 2, read on the page image
issues.printed: The source denotes the finite image of ρ by G and realizes it as a subgroup of GL_2(F_q), with q a suitable power of p. It claims the field F_q may be generated by the traces in G whenever p ≠ 2 or ρ is irreducible.
issues.correction: The trace field is a field of definition if ρ is irreducible, or if p≠2 and ρ is semisimple.
issues.reason: For p ≠ 2 and ρ reducible but not semisimple the parenthesis fails. Take a Galois extension of Q with group (Z/p)² and let ρ send it isomorphically onto G = {(1 a; 0 1) : a ∈ F_{p²}} ⊂ GL_2(F̄_p). Every element of G has trace 2, so the field generated by the traces is F_p, but G has order p² and the p-part of |GL_2(F_p)| = p(p−1)²(p+1) is p, so G is not isomorphic to a subgroup of GL_2(F_p). The two cases that are true: for ρ irreducible (hence absolutely irreducible over F̄_p) the trace determines ρ, so ρ ≅ σ(ρ) for every automorphism σ fixing the traces and ρ descends because the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial; for ρ semisimple and p ≠ 2, det = (tr² − tr∘(g ↦ g²))/2 lies in the trace field, and Deligne–Serre Lemme 6.13 applies. For p = 2 and ρ = χ ⊕ χ with χ of order 3 the traces vanish, and ρ is not realisable over F_2 (its characteristic polynomials X² + χ(g)² are not in F_2[X]), so p ≠ 2 is needed in the reducible semisimple case when the sentence is read as realisability of ρ; the counterexample above contradicts the sentence under either reading.

issues.locator: §3 (Ramification groups), PDF p. 2, arXiv:1307.4525v4
issues.printed: The source identifies the union of the positive absolute upper ramification groups with wild inertia and calls that union pro-p.
issues.correction: Wild inertia P_F is the closure of the union of G_F^v over v>0. The closure cannot in general be omitted: for F=F_p((t)) that union is a proper dense subgroup of P_F.
issues.reason: Take F=F_p((t)) and fix v>0. Choose e prime to p with 1/e<v. For arbitrarily large f divisible by the multiplicative order of p modulo e, put L_0=F_{p^f}((s)), s^e=t. Adjoin solutions of y_a^p−y_a=a/s for an F_p-basis a of F_{p^f}. The pole of order one shows these Artin–Schreier classes are independent, so the resulting wild group has order p^f. Their span is stable under the tame s↦ζs action and constant-field Frobenius, hence the compositum is Galois over F. Its positive upper break is 1/e, by the tame Herbrand scaling. Thus G_F^v has trivial image whereas P_F surjects onto wild groups of unbounded order: G_F^v has infinite index and empty interior in P_F. If the union were P_F, the compact group P_F would be the countable union of the closed subgroups G_F^{1/n}, contradicting Baire. In every finite Galois quotient the union maps onto wild inertia, so its closure is P_F. The earlier argument using only a cyclic quotient of order p did not establish infinite index.

issues.locator: §7.5.16 'Representations Induced From Index Two Subgroups', the paragraph before Lemma 7.5.17, arXiv v3 pp. 201–202
issues.printed: For an absolutely irreducible G ⊂ Sp_4(k) whose W restricts reducibly to an index two subgroup H, the source writes W|_H = V ⊕ V^σ. It claims these G-equivariant decompositions, allowing reducible summands: W ⊗ W = W ⊗ W^∨ = k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ Ind_H^G(ad⁰(V)) ⊕ As(V) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ, ad⁰(W) = Sym²(W) = Ind_H^G(ad⁰(V)) ⊕ As(V), ∧²(W) = k ⊕ k(χ) ⊕ As(V) ⊗ χ.
issues.correction: Add the hypothesis that the symplectic form is non-degenerate on V (equivalently det V = 1, equivalently H lies in SL(V) × SL(V^σ) embedded as in §2.2). In the other case, V Lagrangian with V^σ ≅ V^∨, one has Sym²(W)|_H = Sym²V ⊕ Sym²V^∨ ⊕ (V ⊗ V^∨) and ∧²(W) ⊇ Ind_H^G(det V), and the displayed decompositions fail unless det V is trivial.
issues.reason: Take k = F_p with p ≥ 5, H the Siegel Levi subgroup {diag(g, g*)} ≅ GL_2(F_p) of Sp_4(F_p) and G its normaliser, generated by H and an element exchanging the two Lagrangians. Then W|_H = V ⊕ V^∨ with V ≇ V^∨, G is absolutely irreducible and H has index two. The scalar a ∈ F_p^× of GL_2 acts on Sym²V ⊂ Sym²(W) by a², but trivially on ad⁰(V), on ad⁰(V^σ) and on V ⊗ V^σ = V ⊗ V^∨, hence trivially on Ind(ad⁰(V)) ⊕ As(V); for a² ≠ 1 the second display is false, and likewise the first and third. With the form non-degenerate on V the three displays hold (checked over H, and V·V^σ ⊂ Sym² is the tensor induction, V∧V^σ its twist by χ). Lemmas 7.5.17–7.5.22 apply the paragraph only where V is non-degenerate: in Lemma 7.5.17 absolute irreducibility of As(V) excludes a character in V ⊗ V^σ, hence the Lagrangian case, and Lemma 7.5.18 is about SL_2(k) ≀ Z/2.

issues.locator: V.6.8, proof of Theorem 6.8, PDF p. 420 (book p. 412)
issues.printed: The proof combines the IV.1.13 computation of Kn(Fq) with finite generation of Kn(R), cited to IV.6.9, to conclude SKn(R) = 0 for even n > 0 and finiteness for odd n.

issues.locator: V.6.8, the remark after Proposition 6.8.1, PDF p. 420 (book p. 412)
issues.printed: The source declares that 6.8.1 fails at n = 1. It identifies the kernel of K0(R) → K0(F) with the finite group Pic(R), and infers that K1(F; Z/ℓ) → ⊕K0(R/𝔭; Z/ℓ) fails to be surjective.
issues.correction: The conclusion of 6.8.1 can fail for n = 1: the cokernel of ∂ : K₁(F; ℤ/ℓ) → ⊕K₀(R/𝔭; ℤ/ℓ) is Pic(R)/ℓ, so ∂ is onto exactly when Pic(R)/ℓ = 0.
issues.reason: The mod-ℓ sequence ends K₁(F; ℤ/ℓ) → ⊕ ℤ/ℓ → K₀(R)/ℓ = ℤ/ℓ ⊕ Pic(R)/ℓ → K₀(F)/ℓ = ℤ/ℓ → 0, so the image of ⊕ ℤ/ℓ is Pic(R)/ℓ. For R = ℤ, Pic = 0 and ℚ^×/ℓ → ⊕_p ℤ/ℓ is onto (p ↦ e_p); the remark's 'is false for n = 1' holds only when ℓ divides the class number, e.g. R = 𝓞 of ℚ(√−5), ℓ = 2.

issues.locator: V.6.8.1, proof, second paragraph, PDF p. 421 (book p. 413)
issues.printed: The proof cites IV.1.13 for multiplication by β^{i−1} giving the isomorphism ⊕Z/ℓ ≅ ⊕K1(R/𝔭)/ℓ → ⊕K2i−1(R/𝔭). It represents each target element as β^{i−1}a with a in ⊕K1(R/𝔭). Taking a lift s ∈ K2(F), it sets x = β^{i−1}s in K2i(F; Z/ℓ) and claims ∂(x) = β^{i−1}∂(x) = β^{i−1}a.
issues.correction: Multiplication by β^{i−1} is an isomorphism ⊕K₁(R/𝔭)/ℓ → ⊕K_{2i−1}(R/𝔭; ℤ/ℓ), every element of ⊕K_{2i−1}(R/𝔭; ℤ/ℓ) has the form β^{i−1}a, and ∂(x) = β^{i−1}∂(s) = β^{i−1}a.
issues.reason: β lies in K₂(R; ℤ/ℓ), so β^{i−1}a lies in K_{2i−1}(R/𝔭; ℤ/ℓ), which is the target in the diagram that follows; the integral group K_{2i−1}(𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ/(q^i − 1) is not ℤ/ℓ in general. '∂(x) = β^{i−1}∂(x)' is a slip for β^{i−1}∂(s), s being the lift. At primes 𝔭 over ℓ the identification ℤ/ℓ ≅ K₁(R/𝔭)/ℓ also fails (K₁(R/𝔭)/ℓ has order prime to the residue characteristic), though multiplication by β^{i−1} is still an isomorphism there.

issues.locator: V.6.8.2, Wild Kernels 6.8.2 (PDF p. 421; book p. 413), in the author-hosted combined draft of 29 August 2013
issues.printed: The source identifies divK2i(F) up to isomorphism with the wild kernel: the intersection, for every valuation v of F, of the kernels of K2i(F) → K2i(Fv). It cites [225] as proof.
issues.correction: div K_{2i}(F) is a subgroup of the wild kernel of index at most two; they are equal when i is even or F is not special, and div K_{2i}(F) has index two in the wild kernel when i is odd and F is special (Hutchinson's condition). For K_2, div K_2(F) ≠ WK_2(F) exactly when F is special.
issues.reason: The cited paper [225] (Weibel, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 206 (2006) 222–244; author's preprint of 23 July 2004) proves this in Theorem A and Theorem 5.5, and its Example 5.6 (after Hutchinson) gives F = ℚ(√d), d < 0, d ≡ 2 (mod 16), for instance ℚ(√−14), where {−1, −1} lies in K^w_2(F) but not in div K_2(F) and K^w_2(F) ≅ div K_2(F) ⊕ ℤ/2. Both groups are finite subgroups of K_2(O_F), so they are not isomorphic. For i = 1 the K-book's wild kernel is the classical one: K_2(F) is torsion and K_2(F_v) is μ(F_v) plus a uniquely divisible group (Moore), so the kernel of K_2(F) → K_2(F_v) is the kernel of the Hilbert symbol.
issues.known: Corrected in the reference the passage cites: Weibel, 'Higher wild kernels and divisibility in the K-theory of number fields', J. Pure Appl. Algebra 206 (2006), Theorem A (author copy https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/archive/papers-dir/wildkernel.pdf, read on its pp. 1–2 and 13–15); for K_2, Hutchinson [Hu1, 4.4] as quoted there. Not in the K-book errata list.

issues.locator: VI.2, the paragraph after Proposition 2.3, PDF p. 479 (book p. 471), author-hosted draft of 29 August 2013
issues.printed: The source calls R and Q_2 exceptional and extends that assertion to all their subfields.
issues.correction: Q_2 and its subfields are exceptional, and so is every number field embeddable in R; R itself is non-exceptional under the definition given (as is the infinite subfield Q(ζ_{2^∞})^+ of R).
issues.reason: The definition asks that Gal(F(ζ_{2^ν})/F) be non-cyclic for large ν. For F = R this group is Gal(C/R) ≅ ℤ/2, cyclic; for F = Q(ζ_{2^∞})^+ it is {±1}. For a number field F ⊂ R the group contains −1 (complex conjugation) and has order tending to infinity, and a subgroup of (ℤ/2^ν)^× containing −1 of order at least 4 is not cyclic, so the conclusion for real number fields stands. Nothing in the book uses the exceptionality of R: Proposition 2.3 gives an infinite 2-part for R in cases (c) and (d) alike.

issues.locator: V.6.8.1 remark, standalone Chapter V, printed p. 44
issues.printed: The source concludes that K₁(F; Z/ℓ) → ⊕K₀(R/p; Z/ℓ) fails to be surjective.
issues.correction: For n=1 the boundary can fail to be onto. Its cokernel is Pic(R)/ℓ, so it is onto exactly when Pic(R)/ℓ=0; finiteness of Pic(R) alone does not imply non-surjectivity.
issues.reason: In the finite-coefficient sequence, K₀(R; ℤ/ℓ)=K₀(R)/ℓ and K₀(F; ℤ/ℓ)=ℤ/ℓ. The kernel of their rank map is Pic(R)/ℓ, which is therefore the cokernel of the preceding boundary. For R=ℤ the class group is zero and the prime valuations make ℚ^×/(ℚ^×)^ℓ → ⊕_p ℤ/ℓ onto. The preceding sentence correctly says that the n=1 analogue of the general theorem fails; this finding concerns only the unconditional non-surjectivity assertion that follows it. For a finite class group, failure occurs exactly when gcd(ℓ,#Pic(R))>1, for example class number 2 with ℓ=2.

issues.locator: Lemma 4.4, preprint p.12, author PDF dated 23 July 2004; publication inaccessible and not collated.
issues.printed: The source quantifies over every m.
issues.correction: Prime ideal class and norm congruence cannot be prescribed independently. A simultaneous Chebotarev condition must agree on the intersection of the relevant class field and cyclotomic extension; only compatible pairs can be realised.
issues.reason: Take F=Q(i), m=4, a=3. Every prime of odd residue characteristic has norm congruent to 1 modulo 4: a split rational prime is 1 modulo 4, and an inert prime has squared norm. The dyadic prime has norm 2. Therefore no prime ideal has norm 3 modulo 4, in any ideal class. This disproves the unrestricted quantifier, without claiming that Theorem 4.5 or Theorem A is false.

issues.locator: §3.1, paragraph on neatness, p. 41, and Lemma 3.2(1), p. 42, of the published version (Forum Math. Sigma 4 (2016) e21); also Proposition 3.7(1), p. 48, which omits the orientation sheaf. arXiv:1511.04913v1 has the same text.
issues.printed: For neat U and arbitrary g∈G(𝔸_F^∞), the source calls Γ_{g,U}=G(F)∩gUg⁻¹ a neat arithmetic subgroup in G(F⊗_ℚℝ) and torsion-free. It claims the resulting X^G action is properly discontinuous, free, and preserves orientation.
issues.correction: Neat arithmetic groups act freely and properly discontinuously but need not preserve the orientation of X^G; X^U_G need not be orientable, and Verdier duality (Proposition 3.7(1)) must be twisted by the orientation local system o_U. The claim holds when G(F ⊗ ℝ) is connected, which covers the paper's applications (Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n with F CM, and U(n, n)).
issues.reason: G = PGL_{2,ℚ}, X^G = ℍ with det < 0 acting antiholomorphically. U = K(5)K(13)∏_{p≠5,13}PGL_2(Z_p) is neat (adjoint eigenvalues ≡ 1 at 5 and at 13, so torsion is 5-primary and 13-primary, hence trivial). The matrix (57, 455; 455, 3632) = 57·I + 65·(0, 7; 7, 55) has determinant −1 and lies in U, and its class reverses orientation, so the corresponding component of X^U_G is a nonorientable surface.

issues.locator: Theorem 1.2 ('that is'), with §1.0.2, printed p. 2 of arXiv:2506.03465v2 (the version read; the Annals version was not read)
issues.printed: Theorem 1.2 asserts the even parity Goldfeld conjecture for E : y2 = x3 − x, the congruent number elliptic curve: among positive square-free n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8, a subset of density one satisfies ords=1L(s, E(n)/Q) = 0.
issues.correction: The 'that is' identifies Goldfeld's statement, which §1.0.2 formulates for fundamental discriminants (both signs, ordered by |d|), with a density-one statement for positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) ordered by n. The implication needs a comparison of the two families and orderings: E^(d) ≅ E^(m) for m the positive squarefree part of |d| (twists depend on the squareclass and E^(−m) = E^(m)); |d| = m or 4m according to the sign and m mod 4; by ST.0/density-one-restricts-to-subfamilies-of-positive-lower-density and ST.0/piecewise-rescaling-of-a-height the classes 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) carry exactly half of the fundamental discriminants ordered by |d| and density one within them transfers; root number −1 elsewhere (footnote 2) gives odd analytic order. With this comparison the stated result is right.
issues.reason: Goldfeld's conjecture in §1.0.2 is stated for '50% of the fundamental discriminants n', a different family (both signs, n ≡ 1 mod 4 or n = 4m) with a different ordering; the paper does not give the comparison. The weights are not equal: for m ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 4) the two fundamental discriminants with squarefree part m have |d| ∈ {m, 4m}, {4m, 4m}, {4m, m}. Numerically, among fundamental discriminants with |d| ≤ 2·10⁶ the proportion with m ≡ 1, 2, 3 (mod 8) is 0.49999.

issues.locator: Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 3.19, pp. 22 and 33 (arXiv v3); independently collated with the corresponding published Annals 181 (2015), 191–242 passage (version receipt in this review).
issues.printed: Theorem 3.1 asserts that, in any large family of elliptic curves E, ordering by height yields mean 2-Selmer group size 3 for S2(E).
issues.correction: Add the hypothesis that Inv_p(F) has positive measure for every prime p (equivalently Π_p M_p(F) > 0, i.e. N(F; X) ≫ X^{5/6}); all families the source applies the theorem to satisfy it.
issues.reason: Largeness constrains only all but finitely many p, and a local set Σ_p may be closed with null boundary and still have measure zero. Example: Σ_5 = {(I, J) : −J/27 has 5-adic digits in {0, 1}} and Σ_p unrestricted (beyond minimality) for p ≠ 5. The integers with base-5 digits in {0, 1} meet every residue class modulo m for 5 ∤ m, so Inv_p(F) is everything at p ∤ 30 and F is large, but M_5(F) = 0 and N(F; X) ≍ X^{1/3 + (log 2)/(2 log 5)} = o(X^{5/6}). Then (72) and (73) are both o(X^{5/6}) and the proof of Theorem 3.19 gives no limit.

issues.locator: Author revision of 14 March 2021, proof of Lemma 7.1.1.4, printed p. 533, PDF page index 560
issues.printed: The source refers to submodules of it that are free.
issues.correction: For the finitely generated projective summand already obtained in the proof, split a finite free surjection and pass the natural cohomology comparison to that direct summand. Alternatively use a filtered colimit of finite free modules with general transition maps, not a filtered union of free submodules. The prime-filtration argument in this packet is a separate repair for injectivity, not a replacement proof of all refinement cohomology.
issues.reason: Flatness alone does not express a module as a filtered union of free submodules. A finitely generated module equal to such a directed union would be one of those submodules: put its finite generating set in a common member. It would therefore be free. A nonprincipal invertible ideal in a Dedekind domain is finite projective but not free. The source notation allows an infinite set of retained primes, so semilocality cannot simply be read into the standing notation. This tests the generic algebra inference, not a constructed PEL counterexample: no claim is made here that a particular nonprincipal ideal has been realized for a chosen PEL datum, or that Lemma 7.1.1.4 or the final expansion principle is false. A separately proved freeness hypothesis for a particular base would also repair that case.
