issues.locator: Published §5, proof of Theorem 5.2, p.386; related reflex-ideal/cardinality notation already occurs in arXiv 1506.01466v5, §5, pp.6–7. Both directly read, including page images.
issues.printed: The published source uses Norm_{K/Q}(I), |O_K/I|, and r_{K,φ}(I)·overline(r_{K,φ}(I)); v5 uses |O_K/I| and writes its ideal equalities using r′_{K,φ}.
issues.correction: Take the ideal norm from the reflex field: N_{K*/Q}(I). For an integral representative I, its cardinality expression is |O_{K*}/I|. For a fractional ideal use the positive rational ideal norm, not a quotient cardinality. Write the ideal-level identity as t_{K,φ}(I)·overline(t_{K,φ}(I)) = N_{K*/Q}(I) O_K, reserving r for the induced class-group map.
issues.reason: The input I belongs to the ideal group of K*, whereas t(I) is an ideal of K. Multiplying the reflex-type product by its complex conjugate includes every embedding of K* exactly once, giving N_{K*/Q}(I) after extension to the normal closure, hence the asserted ideal identity over K. If t(I)=(a), the ratio a·bar(a)/N(I) is a totally positive unit in the real subfield, and changing a by a unit changes it by a unit norm. Thus the intended unit-quotient argument is preserved. The old entry’s claim that the issue occurs only in publication is wrong: the reflex-field ideal I and |O_K/I| already occur together on v5 pp.6–7. The published version makes the incorrect norm subscript explicit. Integral class representatives may always be chosen; retaining a fractional I requires the norm notation instead of cardinality.

issues.locator: Published §2.2, p.382; arXiv 1506.01466v5 §2.2, p.3. Both directly read.
issues.printed: The source asserts equality between the regulators of E and E₀.
issues.correction: With the usual class-number-formula normalization, R_E = 2^{g−1} R_{E₀}/Q_E, where Q_E=[O_E^×:μ_E O_{E₀}^×]∈{1,2}. Thus the regulators are comparable by constants depending only on g, rather than equal. The ratio can vary with E through Q_E.
issues.reason: The unit rank is g−1 in both fields. On units from E₀ the logarithmic embedding for E doubles every coordinate, because a complex place has weight two. Its regulator determinant is therefore 2^{g−1}R_{E₀}; the full E-unit lattice contains this lattice with index Q_E, giving the formula. For completeness, u/bar(u) is a root of unity by Kronecker’s theorem. The map u↦u/bar(u) induces an injection O_E^×/(μ_E O_{E₀}^×)→μ_E/μ_E²: if u/bar(u)=ζ², then u/ζ is real. Hence Q_E is 1 or 2. For g=3 the ratio is 4/Q_E, always 2 or 4, so equality already fails for any sextic CM field, for example Q(ζ₇). Only fixed-degree comparability enters the relative Brauer–Siegel estimate, which is unchanged. This derivation verifies the correction without claiming to have directly consulted the Washington proposition cited by the original errata.

issues.reason: For E=Q(√−23), the three elliptic CM j-invariants are the roots of H_{−23}(X)=X³+3491750X²−5151296875X+12771880859375, recorded in the official Sage reference at https://doc.sagemath.org/html/en/reference/arithmetic_curves/sage/schemes/elliptic_curves/cm.html#sage.schemes.elliptic_curves.cm.hilbert_class_polynomial. The polynomial is irreducible modulo 2 (X³+X+1), and its discriminant is −5^18·7^12·11^4·17²·19²·23. It has one real root and two nonreal roots. The field of moduli of a complex elliptic curve with its canonical principal polarization is Q(j). For the real root this is a subfield of R, while for a nonreal root it is not; these are distinct subfields of C, although they have the same degree and are abstractly isomorphic. All these elliptic curves can be equipped with the fixed primitive CM type. The printed literal field equality therefore fails. The published detailed proof uses bounded field extensions instead and is not invalidated by this sketch error.

issues.reason: The proof gives 0≤deg(C_i|F)<2, hence degree zero or one, not positivity. The paper refers to Stacks for basic definitions at the start of §2; Stacks tag 004R excludes the empty space from connected spaces. Normal D_i has empty conductor. A compatible example is the blowup X of P²_R along a line in its special fibre, for a mixed-characteristic DVR R with perfect residue field. With exceptional divisor E, H the pulled-back hyperplane and m sufficiently large, L=mH, Δ=0 and D=E give L=A+E with A=mH−E relatively ample, L−K_X=(m+3)H−E relatively ample, and L|E pulled back from the line, of Iitaka dimension one. E is a smooth ruled surface, so its normalization conductor is empty. The subsequent gluing only needs at most one point.

issues.locator: Corollary 6.7 proof, published pp.700–701 (PDF 46–47), especially its paraphrase of Keel Lemma 5.2; v2 pp.42–43; Annals of Mathematics 195 (2022), 655–705, DOI 10.4007/annals.2022.195.2.4, compared with arXiv:2002.11915v2 (23 January 2022).
issues.printed: The source describes L as nef and Q-effective, and asserts ν(L)=1 ⇒ L semiample.
issues.correction: For the normal projective surface over an algebraically closed field, require h⁰(L^m)≥2 for some m>0, equivalently positive Iitaka dimension in this numerical-dimension-one setting. In the application, use h⁰(mL)≥χ(mL)−h²(mL)→∞, not mere existence of a section.
issues.reason: Let E be an elliptic curve over C and M∈Pic⁰(E) a non-torsion line bundle. On the smooth ruled surface P_E(O_E⊕M), the tautological quotient line bundle N=O(1) is nef, N²=0 and N has degree one on each ruling fibre. Moreover h⁰(N^m)=Σ_{j=0}^m h⁰(M^j)=1 for every m>0. Its unique section has zeros on every fibre, so no positive power is globally generated. This disproves the unqualified algebraically closed field assertion. The same construction works in characteristic p using an elliptic curve over F_p and its generic point over an algebraic closure of F_p(E) to obtain non-torsion M. Witaszek’s preceding Riemann–Roch estimate and the bounded h² in Keel Lemma 5.4 supply growing h⁰, so the stronger, valid surface criterion repairs this application. Keel’s published Lemma 5.2 p.281 itself prints h⁰>0; Witaszek repeats that incorrect form rather than misquoting a correct theorem.

issues.locator: Definition 3.12, arXiv 1702.04644v2 p.13 / published p.394; proof of Theorem 3.13, v2 p.14 / published pp.395–396. Both versions independently collated.
issues.printed: The source defines Γ as the tame quotient of G_{F̄_p(t)} for extensions ramified only in S, and claims it is free pro-prime-to-p with generators δ_1, …, δ_k. Each δ_i is said to generate tame inertia at a point in S∖∞.
issues.correction: Let Γ be the maximal prime-to-p quotient of that tame quotient. This Γ is free pro-prime-to-p on δ_1, …, δ_k with δ_1⋯δ_kδ_∞ = 1. Since |F| is prime to p, φ factors through it.
issues.reason: Independently checked both versions and SGA 1 XIII Corollary 2.12, including its proof: the single-relation free presentation is asserted for the maximal prime-to-p quotient, not an identification of the entire tame group with that quotient. A concrete tame quotient of order divisible by p is given by the characteristic-3 elliptic example in the review: E:y²=x³+x²+1 has a point P=(2,1) of order 3, and translations by P together with inversion give a tame S3-cover of P¹, branched at four points with inertia order 2. This also fits a branch set arising from a prime-to-3 quadratic cover. Replaced the inherited modular-cover assertion by this independently checked example. Since |F| is prime to p, both F and its reduced Schur cover have prime-to-p order (the Schur multiplier is finite and annihilated by |F|). Thus the homomorphisms used in the definition and lifting argument factor through the corrected quotient. Confirmed the slip without claiming a failure of the intended invariant.

issues.locator: Proposition 4.4 and proof, arXiv 1702.04644v2 pp.19–20 / published pp.402–403. Both versions independently collated.
issues.printed: For a global field Q with place ∞, finite G, G′ ⊂ G ≀ S_2, and c the order 2 elements of G′ mapping nontrivially to S_2, the source takes ramified φ: Gal(Q̄_∞/Q_∞) → G′ with image ⟨(1,σ)⟩. It claims a bijection from {(K,ρ) | … ρ ∈ Sur(G_K^{un,∞}, G) | ρ is type G′} to marked (G′,c) extensions (L,π,m) of Q, taken up to isomorphism, with infinity type φ. The proof obtains ρ by projecting a marked extension to its first factor and claims the two constructions are mutual inverses.
issues.correction: Assume G′ is admissible. For the inverse-construction issue, a weaker sufficient condition is (1,σ)∈G′ together with surjectivity of ker(G′→S2) onto the first factor G; the ramified infinity-type hypothesis already implies the former in the first bijection. The swap then also gives surjectivity onto the second factor, and the intersection of the projection kernels is trivial. The applications in Theorem 4.8 use admissible G′.
issues.reason: Read both bijections and their inverse construction in both versions. For G=C3 and G′=⟨(1,σ)⟩≅C2, the marked imaginary quadratic extension Q(√−3)/Q gives a point on the right of the first bijection, with the required infinity type and allowed finite inertia. The left side is empty because a C3-extension of a quadratic field has degree 6 over Q, so its Galois closure cannot have group of order 2. The inverse projection from ker(G′→S2)=1 is not surjective. Confirmed the missing hypothesis. The correction below includes (1,σ)∈G′ explicitly when giving the weaker alternative, rather than treating surjectivity of one projection alone as all the needed data. With those assumptions, the two projection kernels intersect trivially, so the two conjugate subextensions recover M; the inertia conditions give the required unramified extension.

issues.citation: Melanie Matchett Wood, "Nonabelian Cohen–Lenstra moments", Duke Mathematical Journal (2019)
issues.reviewReason: Read the real and imaginary paragraphs side by side in both versions. In the real case infinity splits and contributes zero to the different/discriminant. Every finite inertia group is tame of order 2, so the G′-cover contributes |G′|/2 times the finite branch degree Σn_i, and the quadratic cover contributes Σn_i. Thus both printed +1 terms must be removed. The subsequent count has dimension 2n and denominator q^(2n)−q^(2n−1), consistent with this correction. Confirmed a copied exponent slip; no correction to the imaginary +1.

issues.locator: Conjecture 5.1, arXiv 1702.04644v2 p.26 / published p.411; Lemma 3.11, v2 p.13 / published p.393. Both versions independently collated.
issues.printed: For h ∈ H_2(G′,c)|μ_Q| and u ∈ μ_{Q(μ_{4|G̃′_c|})}, the source claims that goodness of G′ implies lim_{X→∞} (Σ_{K∈IQ^t_X} #{ρ ∈ Sur(G_K^{un,∞}, G) | ρ is type G′, I_{G′,π,Q}(ρ,u) = h}) / (Σ_{K∈IQ^t_X} 1) = 1. It also claims the corresponding result for real quadratic fields.
issues.correction: Write h∈H_2(G′,c)[|μ_Q|] and take u to be a generator of the cyclic group μ_L, L=Q(μ_(4|G̃′_c|)). Equivalently formulate the conjecture by the Hom-valued invariant. This is a sufficient repair of the indexing: more generally, if u=ζ^a for a generator ζ, evaluation is h↦h^a on H_2(G′,c)[|μ_Q|], so it is enough that this power map be an automorphism. The average-one assertion after this repair remains conjectural.
issues.reason: Lemma 3.11 with exponent 0, or the homomorphism property immediately after Definition 3.1, gives I(ρ,1)=1. Thus u=1 and h≠1 make the numerator identically zero, contradicting the predicted average 1. The review independently constructs a good admissible F=PSL2(F5)≀C2 with nonzero H2(F,c)[2] using a stem central extension by C2 that kills the c-commutators; this does not rely on trusting the table's computed multiplier. A generator of μ_L is a sufficient clean repair, not a necessary choice in every case: writing u=ζ^a, evaluation is the a-power map on H2(F,c)[|μ_Q|]. issues.locator: Theorem 4.19, function-field case, p.101 (with the definition of maximal variation, §1.6, p.16); the same statement is Theorem 4.19 in arXiv v4, p.100, in the author manuscript dated 21 August 2024 (126 pp., the journal's revision date; SHA-256 b36f4860…813e)
issues.printed: Theorem 4.19 takes K to be a number field or a one-variable function field, S quasi-projective over K, π : X → S a smooth relative curve with maximal variation and genus g > 1, and α a line bundle of positive degree on the fibers of X. It asserts the relative Bogomolov conjecture for i_α^m : X^m_{/S} → J^m_{/S} whenever m ≥ dim S + 1. In §1.6, maximal variation requires the moduli morphism S → M_{g,R} to be generically finite.
issues.correction: For a function field K of a curve over k, the hypothesis must be maximal variation of a model over k (equivalently, as the proof says, bigness of the relevant adelic line bundles over k rather than over K), which excludes isotrivial families. With that hypothesis, or for K a number field, the statement stands.
issues.reason: Counterexample to the function-field case: k algebraically closed of characteristic 0, K = k(t), S = Spec K, X = C₀ ×_k K for a smooth projective curve C₀/k of genus > 1, and α of degree 1. The moduli morphism Spec K → M_{g,K} is a point, hence generically finite, so X → S has maximal variation in the sense of §1.6. But every point of C₀(k) has canonical height 0 in the constant Jacobian, and these points are Zariski dense in X, so part (1) fails for m = 1 = dim S + 1; constant products give the same failure for the other parts. The proof itself notes that "we need the bigness of the adelic line bundles over k instead of over K", which a constant family does not have. The main uniform Bogomolov theorem excludes isotrivial families and is unaffected. Found by the extraction (items 185–189, 262–266).

issues.reviewReason: Confirmed. Theorem 4.19 and the definition of maximal variation are both verbatim in the same author manuscript the errata names: I re-fetched it from http://faculty.bicmr.pku.edu.cn/~yxy/preprints/bigness_and_bogomolov.pdf on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is b36f4860cc0f098ef062523e8a5147e8172d1e4e357fc76a63cd7c0d782a813e, reproducing the recorded hash, with the date 'August 21, 2024' on its title page, on pages 101 and 16, and the counterexample stands. With S = Spec K for K = k(t), the moduli morphism S → M_{g,K} is a K-point, which is quasi-finite on the dense open U = S, so §1.6's definition of maximal variation is satisfied vacuously; for X = C₀ ×_k K with C₀/k of genus g > 1 and α of degree 1, every point of C₀(k) has canonical height zero in the constant Jacobian and C₀(k) is Zariski dense, so part (1) fails at m = 1 = dim S + 1. What settles the diagnosis is that the proof on the same page says so itself: 'Similar to Proposition 4.18, we need the bigness of the adelic line bundles over k instead of over K, where k = Z if K is a number field and k is the field of constants if K is a function field of one variable.' A constant family does not have it. So the function-field case is false as printed — 'a stated result' is right — and the correction, maximal variation of a model over k, is what the proof needs.

issues.locator: §1.6, definition of stable curves, p.16, in the author manuscript dated 21 August 2024 (126 pp., the journal's revision date; SHA-256 b36f4860…813e)
issues.printed: The source defines stability by semistability, arithmetic genus g > 1, and the requirement that every rational irreducible component of C_k̄ meet other irreducible components in at least three points.
issues.correction: Count special points on the normalization: every rational component must have at least three points of its normalization lying over nodes, counting both branches of a self-node (the Deligne–Mumford condition). Equivalently, a smooth rational component meets the other components in at least three points, and a rational component with a self-node meets them in at least one.
issues.reason: The printed condition ignores self-nodes. For example, a rational curve with one node attached at one point to a smooth genus-one curve is a stable curve of genus 2 in the usual sense, but its nodal rational component meets the other component in only one point. The paper uses stable reduction and the moduli of stable curves from the literature, so the intended (standard) notion is clear. Found by the extraction (item 1 and report §8).

issues.reviewReason: Confirmed, and the counterexample checks out. The definition is verbatim in the same author manuscript the errata names: I re-fetched it from http://faculty.bicmr.pku.edu.cn/~yxy/preprints/bigness_and_bogomolov.pdf on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is b36f4860cc0f098ef062523e8a5147e8172d1e4e357fc76a63cd7c0d782a813e, reproducing the recorded hash, with the date 'August 21, 2024' on its title page on page 16. The Deligne–Mumford condition counts special points on the normalisation, both branches of a self-node included, which the printed condition ignores. The recorded example is stable in the standard sense and fails the printed one: a nodal rational curve meeting a smooth genus-one curve at one point has arithmetic genus 1 + 1 + 1 − 2 + 1 = 2 > 1, its rational component carries three special points (two branches of the self-node and the attaching point), and it meets the other component only once. Since the paper uses stable reduction and the moduli of stable curves from the literature, the intended notion is the standard one and nothing depends on the printed wording.
